# StriatumACC — Analysis Inventory (auto-generated)

Machine-generated from a 14-reader code survey of every `.m` and `.py` file in the repository.
Each entry records the question, the method **as actually coded**, the statistic and its inferential unit,
the outputs, and a soundness assessment. Severity is the reader's judgement of inferential risk.

Companion documents: `MANUSCRIPT_REPORT.md` (synthesis, critique, figure plan) and
`MANUSCRIPT_RESULTS.md` (recorded outcomes and result artefacts).

**Scope:** 14 domains, 290 analyses. 
Severity: 45 fatal, 142 major, 91 minor, 12 ok. 
Status: 208 active, 21 superseded, 21 legacy, 24 scaffold, 8 gated, 8 decorative.

## 1. MATLAB raw-data ingestion and preprocessing chain

*Full domain label:* MATLAB raw-data ingestion and preprocessing chain (Neuropixels + VirMEN VR → all_data.mat → preprocessed_data*.mat)

**Position in pipeline.** FOUNDATION LAYER — everything else in the project depends on it, and it has no upstream inside the repository.

CONSUMES (outside the repo / not reproducible from it): SpikeGLX *.lf.bin + *.lf.meta (sync channel 385, 2500 Hz), VirMEN behaviour .csv files (9 columns), Kilosort output spike_clusters.npy / spike_times.npy / channel_map.npy, Phy manual curation exported as info.xls + cluster_group.tsv, and per-animal waveform-feature files RawData/<id>_neurontype2025.mat whose producer is absent from the repo. Ten helper functions the chain calls (nan_zscore, interpolate_binned_values, gaussFilter, gaussFilter_border, readNPY, my_errorbar_plot, save_to_svg, sigstar, shadedErrorBar, sem) are also absent.

CHAIN (exact filenames): Synch_NP_VR.m (+ ReadMeta.m, ReadChannel.m) → workspace VR_times_synched + VR_data, manually saved as accstr.mat → raw_data_bin.m → workspace binned_spikes / goodcluster2, manually saved as RawData/<id>_raw.mat (16 task) and RawData/<id>_V1_raw.mat (5 dual-probe) and RawDataControl/<id>_raw.mat (5 control) → OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m (task, reads RawData/Neuropixels_Depth_Data.csv + RawData/Neuropixels_V1_Depth_Data.csv) → workspace all_data, manually saved as processed_data/all_data.mat; OrganiseStriatumDataControl.m (control, reads RawDataControl/Neuropixels_Depth_Data_control.csv) → all_data_control.mat (the ONLY scripted save in the ingestion layer) → ProcessStriatumTask.m stage 1 (lines 1-355, using cut_data_per_trial.m, extract_binned_spikes.m, compute_trial_metrics.m, find_change_points.m, separate_dark_and_corridor_periods.m, calculate_lick_precision.m, spatial_binning.m, reorganize_spikes_by_area.m, compute_firing_rates.m, process_licks.m upstream) → processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat; ProcessStriatumControl.m → processed_data/preprocessed_data_control2p5cm.mat. processed_data/preprocessed_data_control2.mat is a separate 2025-01 legacy temporal-only pipeline. OrganiseStriatumData.m is a superseded probe-1-only duplicate.

PRODUCES: processed_data/all_data.mat (530 MB), processed_data/all_data_control.mat (248 MB), processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat (1.33 GB, = cfg.task_data_file), processed_data/preprocessed_data_control2p5cm.mat (585 MB, = cfg.control_data_file), plus the stale processed_data/preprocessed_data5cm.mat and preprocessed_data_control5cm.mat from the previous 5 cm binning, and cebra_data/cebra_mouse<i>_data.mat via save_for_cebra.m.

CONSUMED DOWNSTREAM BY: IntegratedAll_v1.m (three-group integrated analysis; also loads preprocessed_data_control2.mat), MutualInformationStriatum_v2.m → processed_data/shannon_mi_results.mat, Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding.m → processed_data/<decoder>_epoch_decoding_results.mat, CrossSpatialBinDecoding.m → processed_data/cross_spatial_decoding_results.mat, CCA_striatum_spatial_v2.m / v3.m / v3_plot.m, Run_TCA_pipeline.m → processed_data/tca_outputs.mat (via buildCombinedTensor, fit_tca_model, tca_with_cv, cp_nmu_ortho and the plot* family), SpatioTemporalActivityEvolution.m, ensemble_analysis.m, neurontype_classification.m, summary_numbers.m, decode_position.m / decode_position_mld.m, save_for_cebra.m → the Python CEBRA pipeline, and the separate cca/ (Python striatum_cca package) and tcca/ subprojects. The lfp/ subproject reads RawData/LFP/voltage_data_384ch*.mat and is currently gated on the same unresolved voltage↔VR alignment question that this layer leaves open for the LFP stream.

BLOCKING FOR MANUSCRIPT: (1) the spatial occupancy denominator (speed-dependent 17-50% firing-rate inflation) contaminates every spatial firing-rate figure produced from spatial_binned_fr_all; (2) the 1-VR-frame neural/behavioural corridor-onset offset; (3) the goodTrials dual index space (mouse 1212 misaligned from trial 103); (4) the stale 5 cm velocity constant in four live scripts and in the CEBRA export; (5) LP/epoch convention divergence (14 vs 8 learners); (6) the cached task file predating the rng seed, making every learning point irreproducible; (7) undocumented inter-probe sync assumption for all V1/CA1/DG claims.

**Data flow, shapes and units.** RAW → all_data.mat. SpikeGLX *.lf.bin sync channel 385 at 2500 Hz + VirMEN .csv (9 columns: time_s | position_au | dtframe | velocity | world | valvestat | trial# | lick# | synch, plus a 10th file-index row appended by Synch_NP_VR.m:51) → VR_times_synched (1 x n_VR, seconds on the NPx clock). Measured VR frame intervals (median diff of corrected_vr_time): 21.3 ms for mouse 523, 28.1 ms for 1212, 30.3 ms for 409 (p5 16 ms, p95 31-47 ms) — i.e. VirMEN runs at a variable ~33-47 Hz, never uniform. n_VR per animal 221k-346k. VR_data value ranges verified for 523: position -1.31 to 222.66 a.u. (BOTH ends outside the nominal 0-200 corridor), world ∈ {6, 12} exactly (6 = dark, 12 = corridor), valvestat ∈ {0,1,2}, lick# ∈ {0,1,2}, trial# 1..357, native velocity median 15.3 (range -25.2 to 490.3).

Kilosort/Phy → raw_data_bin.m at sr = 30000 Hz, ttstep = 1/1000 s, grid tt = 0:0.001:8400 s (minsend = 140 min; 1212 was actually run at 190 min → 11400 s). binned_spikes = raw 1 ms spike COUNTS, [n_units x 8.4e6] (1105/1106/1201/1206) or [n_units x 1.14e7] (1212). goodcluster2 = [n_units x 2] (cluster ID, Phy depth in µm from tip). Phy-'good' cluster counts: 523 probe 1 = 268 units spanning 20-3840 µm; 1212 probe 1 = 54 units, 40-3800 µm; 1212 probe 2 = 90 units, 20-2380 µm.

Depth → area (µm from tip, CLOSED intervals, last write wins). Probe 1 CSV (RawData/Neuropixels_Depth_Data.csv, 16 rows + mouse 507): e.g. 523 ACC 2100-2600, DMS 700-1200, DLS 0-500. Blank cells → NaN → zero units silently: DLS blank for 731, 823, 1206, 703; ACC blank for 1206. Probe 2 CSV (RawData/Neuropixels_V1_Depth_Data.csv, 5 rows): 1212 V1 1100-2350 / CA1 200-650 / DG 0-200; 1206 V1 1880-2800 / CA1 1160-1760 / DG 400-1160; 1201 V1 2500-3500 / CA1 1800-2400 / DG 1400-1800; 1106 V1 2000-2500 (CA1/DG blank); 1105 V1 1800-2700 (CA1/DG blank). Control CSV: 407 ACC blank; 513 DLS 0-1300 OVERLAPS DMS 1000-1500 by 300 µm (overlap labelled DLS). Depth gate keeps 133/268 units for 523 and 21/54 for 1212 probe 1.

all_data.mat (processed_data/, 530 MB, 2026-05-14, 16 animals in hardcoded ID order; contains average_V1_fr/average_CA1_fr/average_DG_fr so it is post-2026-05-08 IncV1 output). Per animal: final_spikes = 1 ms counts [n_units x n_ms], verified 133 x 7,199,894 for 523, 110 x 10,226,350 for 1212, 80 x 7,199,831 for 409 — i.e. sessions of 7200 s, 10226 s, 7200 s. corrected_vr_time in ms starting at 0; npx_time = 0:1:n_ms-1. Unit totals 2039 → 2037 after fr_threshold 0.02 Hz (only 2 units removed; per-animal min FR 0.013-0.235 Hz). Licks: 523 has 13,536 raw lick events → 13,497 frames after binarising VR row 8 >= 1 → 7,715 after the 100 ms refractory (43% discarded); average_lick_rate = 1.072 Hz.

Trial and space segmentation. Trials from diff(vr_trial) ~= 0; trial counts 42-501 (per animal: 357, 469, 71, 371, 501, 76, 90, 331, 260, 189, 299, 104, 155, 257, 142, 109). Each trial = 5 s dark (world 6) + corridor (world 12). Spatial bins: bin_size = 2 a.u. x 1.25 cm/a.u. = 2.5 cm; bin_edges = [0 2 4 ... 198 202] a.u. with the LAST edge forced to 202 (ProcessStriatumTask.m:17), so bin 100 is 4 a.u. = 5 cm wide while bins 1-99 are 2.5 cm — the final bin's occupancy and firing rate are not comparable to the rest. num_bins = 100; corridor 200 a.u. = 250 cm. Landmarks: visual stimulus 80 a.u. = bin 40 = 100 cm; reward-zone start 100 a.u. = bin 50 = 125 cm; reward-zone end 135 a.u. = bin 67.5 (NON-INTEGER, ProcessStriatumTask.m:22); corridor end 200 a.u. = bin 100. cfg.max_bin = 60 truncates most analyses at 150 cm. Positions above 202 a.u. and below 0 fall outside bin_edges and are silently dropped.

preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat (processed_data/, 1.33 GB, 2026-05-23, 16 animals). spatial_binned_fr_all = [n_units x 100 bins x n_trials] in Hz; shapes verified: 133x100x357, 193x100x469, 47x100x71, 152x100x371, 467x100x501, 17x100x76, 77x100x90, 33x100x331, 86x100x260, 63x100x189, 193x100x299, 210x100x104, 110x100x155, 80x100x257, 42x100x142, 134x100x109. Per-bin dwell time (spatial_binned_data.durations, seconds): median 0.039-0.173 s, minimum 0.011 s, computed as last-minus-first VR sample so it underestimates true occupancy by one frame (17-50% given the 21-30 ms frame intervals). NaN fraction of spatial_binned_fr_all per animal: 0.002, 0.005, 0.005, 0.019, 0.036, 0.050, 0.056, 0.059, 0.096, 0.129, 0.135, 0.140, 0.165, 0.246, 0.263, 0.328. Dark period: temp_binned_dark_fr = [n_units x 50 bins x n_trials], 100 ms bins over the first 5 s, counts/0.1 s. Per-area unit counts per animal (DMS/DLS/ACC/V1/CA1/DG): 523 57/42/34/0/0/0; 614 69/60/64/0/0/0; 624 19/22/6/0/0/0; 727 16/83/53/0/0/0; 730 55/237/175/0/0/0; 731 12/0/5/0/0/0; 822 13/2/62/0/0/0; 823 16/0/17/0/0/0; 1105 28/0/34/24/0/0; 1106 20/20/16/7/0/0; 1201 20/5/67/67/28/6; 1206 16/0/0/102/81/11; 1212 8/6/7/64/24/1; 409 31/26/23/0/0/0; 418 2/19/21/0/0/0; 703 19/0/115/0/0/0.

Behavioural derived signals. zscored_lick_errors: length = n_trials, NaN fraction per animal 0.01-0.63 (values 0.27, 0.39, 0.01, 0.50, 0.63, 0.03, 0.02, 0.59, 0.14, 0.35, 0.30, 0.04, 0.06, 0.38, 0.11, 0.25). change_point_mean per animal: 125, 225, NaN, 100, 109, NaN, NaN, 92, 131, 79, 182, 100, NaN, 112, 27, 51. Learning points recomputed from the cached z-errors under cfg defaults (z<=-2, forward window 10, >=7 passes, LP itself sub-threshold): 22, 44, 32, 53, 54, 36, 34, 14, 44, 67, 84, NaN, 23, 39, 26, NaN → 14/16 learners, avg_lp 41. Under the deviating window=7/min=7-on-truncated-trace convention used by Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding and CrossSpatialBinDecoding: 85, 58, 32, 71, NaN, 48, 50, 29, NaN, NaN, NaN, NaN, 39, NaN, NaN, NaN → 8/16 learners, avg_lp 52. MI v2 adds +9 to the shared LP. Epochs: Naive = trials 1:10 (absolute), Intermediate = lp-10:lp-1, Expert = lp:lp+9 ('lp') or lp+1:lp+10 ('lp1'); mouse 823 (LP=14) has Naive and Intermediate sharing 7 of 10 trials. Velocity is never stored — consumers compute bin_cm/duration, and four live scripts use the stale 5 cm constant (4 a.u. x 1.25) against 2.5 cm data, doubling it.

Trial index-space split (verified). 14/16 animals lose no trials. Mouse 1212: trialData.n_trials saved as 156 while its vectors hold 155; corridorData/darkData/trial_metrics/trial_lick_fractions hold 156; trial_lick_errors/zscored_lick_errors/spatial_binned_fr_all hold 155; spatial_binned_fr_all trial 103 is an all-NaN slice (the excluded trial retained in place, the final trial dropped), so trial_average_fr_dms/dls/acc (155 entries, filtered space) is shifted -1 from trial 103 onward. Mouse 409: 258 vs 257, excluded trial at the tail, no interior shift.

Downstream consumers of preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat: IntegratedAll_v1.m, MutualInformationStriatum_v2.m, Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding.m, CrossSpatialBinDecoding.m, CCA_striatum_spatial_v2/v3.m, Run_TCA_pipeline.m, save_for_cebra.m, ensemble_analysis.m, SpatioTemporalActivityEvolution.m, neurontype_classification.m.

**Cross-cutting notes.** EVIDENCE BASE: every claim below was checked against the actual cached data (h5py reads of processed_data/all_data.mat, processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat, RawData/*_raw.mat), not inferred from code alone.

MISSING DEPENDENCIES (reproducibility, major). Ten functions the pipeline calls are ABSENT from the repository: nan_zscore (ProcessStriatumTask.m:177, ProcessStriatumControl.m:172 — produces z_spatial_binned_fr_all), interpolate_binned_values, gaussFilter, gaussFilter_border, readNPY (all raw_data_bin.m — these implement the VR→1 ms interpolation and smoothing that built every _raw.mat), my_errorbar_plot, save_to_svg, sigstar, shadedErrorBar, sem. A clean checkout cannot run the preprocessing chain, and the exact behavioural-interpolation method underlying all_data.mat cannot be inspected.

PROVENANCE GAPS. (a) all_data.mat has NO scripted producer — no Organise* script for the task cohort contains a save call; the 530 MB processed_data/all_data.mat was written by hand from the workspace. Only OrganiseStriatumDataControl.m:143 saves. (b) ProcessStriatumTask.m:354 writes preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat to the CWD, but cfg.task_data_file points at processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat — the file was moved manually. (c) ProcessStriatumTask.m:495 writes a DIFFERENT file, preprocessed_data.mat (with decoding fields appended); that file does not exist in processed_data/, and the guard at :25 (`if exist('preprocessed_data.mat','file')`) tests a filename the pipeline no longer uses. (d) raw_data_bin.m never saves binned_spikes/goodcluster2/VR_data. (e) preprocessed_data has no mouseid field, so animal identity is lost at the preprocessing boundary and everything downstream depends on positional order matching all_mouse_ids.

STALE CACHE VS CODE (checkable claim). processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat is dated 2026-05-23 12:19. rng(42,'twister') was added to ProcessStriatumTask.m:8 in commit 3662ba7 on 2026-05-24 10:13, explicitly because calculate_lick_precision draws 1000 unseeded rand() shuffles per trial. The cached task file therefore contains zscored_lick_errors from an UNSEEDED run and cannot be reproduced; every learning point, epoch boundary and epoch-contrast figure derives from it. The 2026-05-24 find_learning_points fix (LP must itself be sub-threshold) also postdates it: recomputing with the old window-START rule gives LPs 1-3 trials earlier (614: 43 vs 44; 624: 29 vs 32; 1212: 21 vs 23; 409: 37 vs 39), so processed_data/cross_spatial_decoding_results.mat (2026-05-14) and processed_data/tca_outputs.mat (2026-05-14) are aligned to the old LPs. ProcessStriatumControl.m has no rng seed at all, and preprocessed_data_control2p5cm.mat (2026-05-24 16:01) is likewise irreproducible. preprocessed_data_control2.mat (2025-01-28) predates the 2026-05-07 fr_threshold alignment, as NOTES.md warns.

COHORT AND AREA COVERAGE (verified from the cached file). 16 task animals in hardcoded order [523 614 624 727 730 731 822 823 1105 1106 1201 1206 1212 409 418 703]; 5 controls [407 513 515 817 1205]. Mouse 507 has a _raw.mat and a CSV row but is excluded from all_mouse_ids; mouse 408 sits in RawDataControl unused. 2039 units in all_data → 2037 after fr_threshold. Per-area units / animals contributing: DMS 401/16, DLS 522/11, ACC 699/15, V1 264/5, CA1 133/3, DG 18/3. DG is 6+11+1 units across 1201/1206/1212 — mouse 1212 contributes ONE DG unit, below cfg.min_units=5. Animals with zero units in an area: DLS = 731, 823, 1105, 1206, 703; ACC = 1206. Control V1/CA1/DG raw files and depth annotations exist for 513/515/817 but are never ingested, so no V1/CA1/DG claim has a control.

PSEUDOREPLICATION. The preprocessing layer itself pools units and trials without any nesting structure: cross-area correlations average over unit pairs as if independent; PCA dimensionality pools all trials per animal; the only place animal identity enters as a factor is anovan (ProcessStriatumTask.m:435), and there the animal grouping vector is built as 1:numel(...) per area (:425), which mislabels animals when areas have unequal animal counts — and ProcessStriatumControl.m:222 uses `2:size(...)+1` for one area, a copy-paste error. Every per-area claim must be made on animal-level aggregates given DLS n=11, V1 n=5, CA1 n=3, DG n=3.

MULTIPLE COMPARISONS / NULLS. cfg.n_shuffles = 25 (project_cfg.m:89, up from 1 on 2026-05-07) gives a permutation p-floor of 1/26 ≈ 0.038 — no shuffle-based result can survive correction across 6 areas or 15 pairs. calculate_lick_precision uses 1000 shuffles but discards the resulting quantile. ProcessStriatumTask.m:798,810 prints raw per-animal correlation p-values in figure legends with no FDR. The KS/FDR machinery (fdr_correct.m, annotate_ks_panels_fdr.m) is not applied anywhere in the preprocessing layer.

TWO OFF-BY-ONE / ALIGNMENT DEFECTS TO FIX BEFORE PUBLICATION. (1) separate_dark_and_corridor_periods.m:22 takes the NPx corridor-onset time from VR sample idx+1 while splitting the VR arrays at idx — the neural corridor onset is one VR frame late (measured 21 ms for 523, 28 ms for 1212, 30 ms for 409). (2) The goodTrials filter creates two trial index spaces; verified in the cached file for mouse 1212 (trialData.n_trials saved as 156 vs 155 actual; spatial_binned_fr_all trial 103 is an all-NaN slice, so trial_average_fr_* is shifted -1 from trial 103 onward) and mouse 409 (258 vs 257, excluded trial at the tail so no interior shift).

DEAD / BROKEN CODE FOUND. calc_dim (ProcessStriatumTask.m:233, ProcessStriatumControl.m:201) uses pca()'s first output (COEFF) instead of `explained`, so every per-area dimensionality is EMPTY — confirmed: stim_dimensionality_V1 and dark_dimensionality_V1 are stored as 0x0 for all 5 V1 animals. generalized_variances_stim/dark are computed and never saved in the task pipeline. ProcessStriatumTask.m:72 (`n_trials = trialData.n_trials - 1`, the drop-incomplete-final-trial guard) is overwritten at :93 and dead. raw_data_bin.m:250 `if VR_data(10,idx)==VR_data(10,idx)` is a tautology (should be idx-1), disabling the VR file-boundary guard. project_cfg's StriatumStart/StriatumEnd CSV columns are read and never used. OrganiseStriatumData.m is fully superseded by OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m and should move to legacy/.

VERSION DRIFT BETWEEN COMMITTED CODE AND THE ARCHIVE. raw_data_bin.m:46 sets minsend = 140 min → an 8.4e6-column 1 ms grid, which matches 1105/1106/1201/1206 binned_spikes. But 1212_raw.mat has 1.14e7 columns (minsend = 190), so the committed script is not the version that produced the archive. Reading it as documentation of the raw data is unsafe.

TWO PROBES, ONE SYNC (decisive check). VR_times_synched and VR_data are BIT-IDENTICAL between <id>_raw.mat and <id>_V1_raw.mat for all five dual-probe animals (1105, 1106, 1201, 1206, 1212; max abs diff 0.0 s, np.array_equal True). Probe 2 was binned on probe 1's sync solution; no independent probe-2↔VR alignment exists in the archive, and nothing in the repo documents whether the two imec probes shared a clock. Every V1/CA1/DG↔behaviour claim rests on that undocumented assumption — the same class of gap NOTES.md 2026-07-12 already flagged for the LFP exports.

**Scientifically load-bearing constants.**

- Synch_NP_VR.m:7 — sync channel index 385 (385-channel probe, SY word)
- Synch_NP_VR.m:53 — /64 divisor: hardcoded assumption that only bit 6 of the SY word toggles
- Synch_NP_VR.m:62 — init pulse >= 2500*0.8 samples (0.8 s at 2500 Hz); the 2500 ties the script to the *.lf.bin stream only
- Synch_NP_VR.m:66 — long pulse 2500*0.4 to 2500*0.6 (0.4-0.6 s)
- Synch_NP_VR.m:70 — short pulse 2500*0.15 to 2500*0.3 (0.15-0.3 s)
- Synch_NP_VR.m:95,99 — VR-side pulse windows 0.4-0.6 s and 0.15-0.3 s
- raw_data_bin.m:36,38 — c_l = 200, tunnel_length = 200 a.u. (corridor length)
- raw_data_bin.m:38,159 — 1 a.u. = 1.25 cm (AU_cm)
- raw_data_bin.m:41 — sr = 30000 Hz (AP sample rate)
- raw_data_bin.m:42 — ttstep = 1/1000 s (1 ms spike bin)
- raw_data_bin.m:46 — minsend = 140 min (grid length 8400 s; 1212 was actually run with 190)
- raw_data_bin.m:50 — darkt = 10 min post-task darkness
- raw_data_bin.m:52 — darklength = 5 s dark per trial
- raw_data_bin.m:55-56 — Vp1 = 80, Vp2 = 100 a.u. (visual stimulus zone)
- raw_data_bin.m:58-60 — Rp1 = 100, Rp2 = 130, Rp3 = 110 a.u. (Rp2=130 conflicts with reward_zone_end_au=135 in ProcessStriatumTask.m:9)
- raw_data_bin.m:65 — tolerance = 20 a.u. (25 cm anticipatory-lick window)
- raw_data_bin.m:138 — unit label test cluster_label(1:3) == 'goo' (Phy manual 'good' only; MUA branch commented out at :141-143)
- raw_data_bin.m:155 — sigma_spike = 0.025/(sqrt(12)*ttstep) = 7.22 ms (smoothed copy, not propagated)
- raw_data_bin.m:160 — spatial_bin_size = 2*1.25 = 2.5 cm
- raw_data_bin.m:164-167 — Gaussian sigmas: velocity/position/licks 100 ms, acceleration sqrt(2)*100 ms
- raw_data_bin.m:172 — gaussFilterSigma_pos_spatial = 5/2.5 = 2 bins
- raw_data_bin.m:360 — ntrials = max(VR_data(7,:)) - 1 ('ignore last trial'; NOT honoured downstream)
- OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m:9 — 16 task mouse IDs [523 614 624 727 730 731 822 823 1105 1106 1201 1206 1212 409 418 703]
- OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m:104-107 — cell type: peak-to-trough >= 0.4 ms & post-spike suppression <= 40 ms → MSN; <0.4 & propISI>2s <0.1 → FSN; >=0.4 & >40 ms → TAN; <0.4 & >=0.1 → UIN
- OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m:171-172 — npx_start = ceil(VR_times_synched(1)*1000), npx_end = floor(VR_times_synched(end)*1000)
- OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m:206 — process_licks min_gap = 100 ms (discards 43% of detected licks)
- OrganiseStriatumDataControl.m:3 — 5 control IDs [407 513 515 817 1205]
- ProcessStriatumTask.m:8 — rng(42,'twister') (added 2026-05-24; cached file predates it)
- ProcessStriatumTask.m:10 — reward_zone_start_cm = 125
- ProcessStriatumTask.m:11 — visual_zone_start_au = 80 (= bin 40 = 100 cm)
- ProcessStriatumTask.m:12 — reward_zone_start_au = 100 (= bin 50 = 125 cm)
- ProcessStriatumTask.m:13 — reward_zone_end_au = 135 (= bin 67.5, non-integer)
- ProcessStriatumTask.m:14 — corridor_end_au = 200
- ProcessStriatumTask.m:15 — bin_size = 2 a.u. = 2.5 cm
- ProcessStriatumTask.m:17 — bin_edges(end) = 202, making spatial bin 100 twice as wide (5 cm) as bins 1-99
- ProcessStriatumTask.m:19 — num_bins = 100

### Analyses (25)

#### 1.1 PCA relative dimensionality (90% variance)
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 232-274 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `decorative` · manuscript role: *drop (or rewrite: use participation ratio / cross-validated dimensionality with unit-count matching)*

- **Question.** How many PCs are needed for 90% of variance, normalised by unit count, in task vs dark and per area?
- **Method.** Whole-population version is correct: pca(...) with the 5th output `explained`, then find(cumsum(explained) >= 90, 1) / n_total_neurons (:238-244). Sub-area version uses the anonymous function calc_dim = @(data, N) find(cumsum(pca(data','Centered',true)) >= 90, 1) / N (:233).
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_fr_all, temp_binned_dark_fr
- **Outputs.** stim_dimensionality_V1 and dark_dimensionality_V1 SAVED (:346-347); the DMS/DLS/ACC values are computed but not saved from this block; pca_dark_dimensionality_* added in the later plotting loop (:411-414)
- **Statistics.** anovan over area with animal as a second factor plus multcompare at p<0.05 (:435-439); paired ttest for task vs dark (:446)
- **Inferential unit.** animals (one dimensionality value per animal per area)
- **Soundness.** calc_dim IS BROKEN. Single-output pca() returns COEFF (the loading matrix), not `explained`. cumsum over unit-norm columns cannot reach 90 unless n_units > 8100, so find(...,1) returns EMPTY. VERIFIED in the cached file: stim_dimensionality_V1 and dark_dimensionality_V1 are stored as 0x0 empty for all five V1 animals (HDF5 dims [0 0]). Every per-area dimensionality produced by calc_dim — stim/dark for DMS, DLS, ACC and V1 — is empty, so the sub-area dimensionality comparison does not exist as computed. The same broken lambda is in ProcessStriatumControl.m:201. The correctly computed whole-population values are also fragile: find(cumsum(explained)>=90,1) is a hard 90% cut on a quantity that saturates, normalising by n_neurons makes it strongly n-dependent (unit counts range 17-467 across animals), and the downstream anovan enters animal as a fixed factor with a group vector built as 1:numel(...) per area (:425), which mislabels animals when areas have different animal counts (and ProcessStriatumControl.m:222 even uses `2:size(...)+1` for one area). Not usable as a dimensionality claim.
- **Concerns.**
    - calc_dim uses pca()'s first output (COEFF) instead of `explained` → all per-area dimensionalities are empty, confirmed in the saved file
    - 90%-variance-threshold / n_neurons is strongly unit-count dependent; unit counts vary 17-467
    - anovan animal-factor grouping vector is constructed incorrectly when areas have unequal animal counts

#### 1.2 Neuropixels↔VirMEN clock synchronisation
`Synch_NP_VR.m` lines 1-167 · **🟠 major** · status: `legacy` · manuscript role: *methods-only (must be described; needs an alignment-residual figure before any latency/lag claim)*

- **Question.** What NPx sample time corresponds to each VR frame, so spikes can be aligned to behaviour?
- **Method.** Interactive (uigetfile). Reads SpikeGLX sync channel 385 of a 385-ch .bin via ReadChannel (Synch_NP_VR.m:7). Edge detection = diff(synchChannel)/64 (:53), i.e. hardcoded assumption that only bit 6 of the SY word toggles. Pulses classified by SAMPLE-index duration against a hardcoded 2500-sample/s scale (:62,66,70): init >= 2500*0.8 (0.8 s), long 2500*0.4-0.6 (0.4-0.6 s), short 2500*0.15-0.3 (0.15-0.3 s); 'start' = init followed by short (:73-75). The 2500 constant means the script only works on the *.lf.bin (2500 Hz LFP stream); on an .ap.bin (30 kHz) every pulse misclassifies. VR side classified from VR_data row 9 in SECONDS with the same 0.4-0.6 / 0.15-0.3 windows (:95,99). Matching is a GREEDY string walk: for each VR pulse i, advance n until pulse_class_NP(n)==pulse_class_VR(i) (:116-122) — no temporal-plausibility check, no residual, no assertion. Per-segment affine correction: a = idx_NP(i)/imSampRate - t_VR(i) (:127), r = (a_i - a_{i-1})/(t_VR(i)-t_VR(i-1)) (:132), VR_times_synched(n) = (t_VR(n)+a_{i-1}) + (t_VR(n)-t_VR(idx_VR(i-1)))*r (:134). Sync pulses nominally 1/min (:36 comment).
- **Inputs.** *.lf.bin + *.lf.meta (SpikeGLX), 1-N VirMEN .csv files (9 cols: time|x|dtframe|velocity|world|valvestat|trial#|lick#|synch); files concatenated with trial numbers offset by max of previous file (:44)
- **Outputs.** workspace vars VR_times_synched (1 x n_VR, seconds on NPx clock) and VR_data (10 x n_VR, row 10 = file index). NOT saved by the script — saved manually as 'accstr' (see raw_data_bin.m:109).
- **Statistics.** none — no residual/goodness-of-fit statistic, no drift bound, no cross-check against a second sync source
- **Inferential unit.** sync pulse pairs (~1/min) per session
- **Soundness.** Piecewise-linear drift correction between sync pulses is methodologically appropriate. Three structural defects: (1) THREE UNGUARDED EXTRAPOLATION PATHS — samples before the first pulse are back-extrapolated with the first inter-pulse rate (:146-152); samples after the LAST pulse use `VR_offset_time(i)` with a STALE `r` left over from the previous loop iteration, never recomputed (:153-157); the file-discontinuity branch (:136-143) likewise consumes the previous iteration's `r`. Post-last-pulse error grows linearly and unbounded with no warning. (2) Greedy pulse matching means one missed/spurious NP edge silently shifts the entire remainder of the alignment. (3) No validation of r magnitude — a mispaired pulse corrupts a whole segment invisibly. This is the foundation of every temporal claim in the project and it carries no diagnostic.
- **Concerns.**
    - unguarded extrapolation before first and after last sync pulse
    - stale `r` reused across loop iterations (:139,142,155)
    - greedy pulse matching with no temporal sanity check
    - hardcoded 2500 sample-rate scale ties the script to the LF stream only
    - hardcoded /64 bit mask
    - no saved sync residual; no provenance record of which .bin was used per animal

#### 1.3 Raw spike binning, cluster selection and per-mouse spatial maps
`raw_data_bin.m` lines 1-528 · **🟠 major** · status: `legacy` · manuscript role: *methods-only (the spatial maps here are superseded by ProcessStriatumTask; the 1 ms binning is load-bearing)*

- **Question.** Convert Kilosort/Phy output + synchronised VR into 1 ms binned spikes and per-trial spatial occupancy/velocity/lick/firing maps.
- **Method.** sr=30000 Hz (:41), ttstep=1/1000 s (:42), grid tt=0:0.001:minsend*60 with minsend=140 min (:46-47) → 8.4e6 columns. binned_spikes = histcounts(spike_times/sr, tt) = raw 1 ms COUNTS (:183, :198); a Gaussian-smoothed copy spike_gf (sigma_spike = 0.025/(sqrt(12)*ttstep) = 7.22 ms, :155) is computed but NOT propagated. Unit selection: Phy MANUAL label only, first 3 chars == 'goo' (:138); MUA branch commented out (:141-143); depth = cluster_info column 7 (µm from tip, :78). Geometry: AU_cm=1.25 (:159), spatial_bin_size = 2*1.25 = 2.5 cm (:160), tunnel_length 200 AU = 250 cm (:38,357), space = 2.5:2.5:250 → nspace=100 (:358-359), ntrials = max(VR_data(7,:)) - 1 'ignore last trial' (:360). Landmarks Vp1=80, Vp2=100 AU (:55-56); reward Rp1=100, Rp2=130, Rp3=110 AU (:58-60); tolerance=20 AU (:65). Dark: darkt=10 min post-task (:50), darklength=5 s per trial (:52). Behavioural interpolation onto the 1 ms grid delegated to interpolate_binned_values (:260) then Gaussian filtered with sigma 100 ms for velocity/position/licks and sqrt(2)*100 ms for acceleration (:164-167), spatial sigma = 5/2.5 = 2 bins (:172). spatialOccupation_time(i,n) = sum(pos in bin)*ttstep (:373); spatialFiring = sum(spikes)/occupancy (:490-492); z-scores across all trials+bins per neuron (:506) and after spatial Gaussian filter (:522).
- **Inputs.** spike_clusters.npy, spike_times.npy, channel_map.npy, info.xls (Phy cluster_info), cluster_group.tsv, accstr.mat (Synch_NP_VR workspace)
- **Outputs.** workspace binned_spikes [n_units x 8.4e6 int], goodcluster2 [n_units x 2 = ID, depth], VR_data, VR_times_synched — all saved MANUALLY as RawData/<id>_raw.mat (no save call in the script). Only `save([name_now 'speed'],'spatialVelocity')` at :431 is scripted.
- **Statistics.** none (descriptive maps only)
- **Inferential unit.** trials x 100 spatial bins within one mouse
- **Soundness.** The 1 ms count binning is correct and is what downstream uses. But this script is NOT the reproducible producer of the archive it feeds: hardcoded Windows path 'E:\visual_learning' (:29), interactive folder list, and no save of the load-bearing outputs. Version drift is demonstrable: minsend=140 gives an 8.4e6-column grid, and 4 of 5 dual-probe raw files do have 8.4e6 columns, but RawData/1212_raw.mat has 1.14e7 → that animal was run with minsend=190, i.e. the committed script is not the version that produced the archive. Bug at :250: `if VR_data(10,idx)==VR_data(10,idx)` is a tautology (should be idx-1), so in the index-advance branch the file-change guard is inoperative and 1 ms bins spanning a VR file boundary get a VR index from the wrong file. Four required dependencies (readNPY, gaussFilter, gaussFilter_border, interpolate_binned_values) are ABSENT from the repository, so the exact behavioural interpolation used to build every _raw.mat cannot be inspected or re-run.
- **Concerns.**
    - load-bearing outputs never saved by code; RawData/*_raw.mat provenance is manual
    - committed constants (minsend=140) contradict the archive (1212 used 190)
    - interpolate_binned_values / gaussFilter / gaussFilter_border / readNPY missing from repo — VR→1 ms interpolation method unverifiable
    - file-boundary guard tautology at :250
    - Rp2=130 AU here vs reward_zone_end_au=135 in ProcessStriatumTask.m:9 — inconsistent reward-zone end
    - unit inclusion = Phy manual 'good' only; no ISI/amplitude/presence/drift metric anywhere in the project

#### 1.4 all_data assembly + anatomical area assignment (live task pipeline)
`Striatum project/OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m` lines 1-297 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only + supplementary unit-count table (the per-area n must be reported as 16/11/15/5/3/3 animals, not 16)*

- **Question.** Which anatomical area does each unit belong to, and how are the two probes merged onto one behavioural timeline?
- **Method.** 16 task IDs hardcoded (:9): [523 614 624 727 730 731 822 823 1105 1106 1201 1206 1212 409 418 703]. Probe 1 depths from RawData/Neuropixels_Depth_Data.csv (:20) with fixed column names (:16); the StriatumStart/StriatumEnd columns are read and NEVER used. Probe 2 depths from RawData/Neuropixels_V1_Depth_Data.csv via detectImportOptions, area names harvested from any <Area>Start header (:43-50) → detects V1, CA1, DG. Assignment is CLOSED-interval membership on Phy depth: is_dms = d>=DMSStart & d<=DMSEnd, then is_dls, then is_acc, written in that order so a later area OVERWRITES an earlier one (:125-131); probe-2 loop is CSV column order V1→CA1→DG with the same overwrite semantics (:163-164). Units matching no interval are DROPPED (:132,167). Time slicing: npx_start_frame = ceil(VR_times_synched(1)*1000), npx_end_frame = floor(VR_times_synched(end)*1000), both clamped to [1, size(binned_spikes,2)] (:171-174). Probe 2 is sliced with PROBE 1's frame indices; if the probe-2 matrix is shorter it is ZERO-padded to length (:183-189). corrected_vr_time = (VR_times_synched - VR_times_synched(1))*1000 ms (:202); npx_time = 0:1:n-1 (:203). Licks: is_lick = VR_data(8,:) >= 1 (:205) then process_licks(...,100) (:206). avg_fr_all = sum(final_spikes,2)/duration_sec (:224). Cell type from <id>_neurontype2025.mat col 5, or derived if <5 columns: col3>=0.4 & col4<=40 → MSN(1); col3<0.4 & col2<0.1 → FSN(2); col3>=0.4 & col4>40 → TAN(3); col3<0.4 & col2>=0.1 → UIN(4) (:104-107). Probe-2 units get all-NaN neurontypes (:191).
- **Inputs.** RawData/<id>_raw.mat (16), RawData/<id>_V1_raw.mat (5: 1105 1106 1201 1206 1212), RawData/<id>_neurontype2025.mat, two depth CSVs
- **Outputs.** workspace `all_data` (1x16 struct). NOT SAVED BY ANY SCRIPT — processed_data/all_data.mat (530 MB, 2026-05-14) was written manually. Verified contents: 16 animals in the hardcoded ID order, fields include average_V1_fr/average_CA1_fr/average_DG_fr, 2039 units total.
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** units nested in animals (16 animals)
- **Soundness.** Structurally the right design (single CSV as the anatomical source of truth). Five real problems. (1) A blank CSV cell imports as NaN and `d>=NaN` is false, so an animal missing an area gets ZERO units for it silently, with no warning: 731/823/1206/703 have blank DLS, 1206 has blank ACC. Verified per-area animal counts in the cached data: DMS 16/16 (401 units), DLS 11/16 (522), ACC 15/16 (699), V1 5/16 (264), CA1 3/16 (133), DG 3/16 (18 units total: 6+11+1). DG-based claims rest on 3 animals and 18 units, one animal contributing a SINGLE unit — below cfg.min_units=5. (2) Overlapping intervals resolve by last-write-wins: control mouse 513 has DLS 0-1300 and DMS 1000-1500, so 300 µm of putative DMS is labelled DLS. Probe-2 boundaries are shared exactly (1212 DG 0-200 / CA1 200-650; 1206 DG 400-1160 / CA1 1160-1760; 1201 DG 1400-1800 / CA1 1800-2400) and DG, written last, wins the boundary unit. (3) The depth gate discards most recorded units with no accounting: 523 has 268 Phy-'good' clusters spanning 20-3840 µm and keeps 133 (49.6%); 1212 probe 1 keeps 21 of 54. (4) VERIFIED: VR_times_synched and VR_data are BIT-IDENTICAL between <id>_raw.mat and <id>_V1_raw.mat for all five dual-probe animals — probe 2 was binned on probe 1's sync solution, so no independent probe-2↔VR alignment exists anywhere in the archive. V1/CA1/DG↔behaviour alignment rests on an undocumented assumption of common sample-zero between imec probes (same class of gap the LFP audit already flagged). (5) The zero-pad path (:185-186) fills missing probe-2 time with ZEROS, which read as 'no spikes' rather than missing — latent, not currently triggered (all five probe-2 grids match probe 1). Mouse 507 exists in RawData and the CSV but is absent from all_mouse_ids, so it is silently excluded. Cell-type criteria (striatal waveform/ISI rules) are applied to ACC — a cortical area — producing meaningless MSN/FSN/TAN labels for 699 ACC units.
- **Concerns.**
    - blank CSV cell → silent zero units for that area, no warning
    - closed-interval overlap resolved by write order (control 513 DMS/DLS; all probe-2 CA1/DG boundaries)
    - probe-2 sync is a verbatim copy of probe 1's — inter-probe alignment never measured
    - zero-padding of missing probe-2 time (latent)
    - DG n=3 animals / 18 units, one animal with 1 unit
    - ~50% of Phy-good units discarded by the depth gate with no reported accounting
    - striatal cell-type rules applied to cortical ACC units
    - all_data.mat has no scripted producer; StriatumStart/End columns dead

#### 1.6 Dark vs corridor segmentation
`Striatum project/separate_dark_and_corridor_periods.m` lines 1-43 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only (the 1-frame neural/behavioural offset must be fixed before any corridor-onset-locked analysis)*

- **Question.** Split each trial into its 5 s dark inter-trial period and its corridor traversal.
- **Method.** corridor_start_idx_vr = find(trial_world > 6, 1) (:21). VR world takes exactly two values, verified {6, 12} — 6 = dark, 12 = corridor. corridor_start_time_vr = trial_times_zeroed(corridor_start_idx_vr + 1) (:22) — note the +1. NPx split index = argmin|npx_times - corridor_start_time| (:25). dark = spikes(:, 1:npx_start-1) and VR fields (1:idx-1) (:28-32); corridor = spikes(:, npx_start:end) and VR fields (idx:end) (:35-39). Whole body wrapped in try/catch → `continue`, leaving [] for the trial (:20,40-42).
- **Inputs.** trialData, per-trial 1 ms spike matrices, per-trial npx time vectors
- **Outputs.** darkData, corridorData (both saved into preprocessed_data)
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** trials within animal
- **Soundness.** OFF-BY-ONE, exactly the class the project conventions require checking: the NPx split time is taken from VR sample corridor_start_idx+1 while the VR-side arrays are split at corridor_start_idx. The neural corridor onset is therefore ONE VR FRAME LATE relative to the behavioural corridor onset — 21 ms (mouse 523), 28 ms (1212), 30 ms (409) measured from median diff(corrected_vr_time). darkData gets one frame of corridor spikes; corridorData loses one frame. At 2.5 cm bins (median dwell 39-173 ms) this is 15-75% of the first spatial bin. Second issue: the silent catch. A trial that never reaches world 12 yields find(...)=[] → catch → the trial's darkData/corridorData stay [], which is the sole mechanism generating the goodTrials exclusion downstream, and it is never counted or reported.
- **Concerns.**
    - 1-VR-frame (21-30 ms) offset between neural and behavioural corridor onset
    - blanket try/catch swallows failures and silently creates excluded trials with no count

#### 1.7 Spatial binning of spikes, licks and dwell time
`Striatum project/spatial_binning.m` lines 1-68 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only, but every spatial firing-rate figure inherits the bias; the occupancy denominator must be corrected to k*dt (or to a proper interval-based occupancy) before publication*

- **Question.** Convert 1 ms spike counts into firing rate as a function of corridor position, per trial.
- **Method.** Position binned with histcounts(trial_position, bin_edges) (:30). Bins with <=1 VR sample are SKIPPED, leaving NaN (:39 `any(idx_in_bin) && sum(idx_in_bin) > 1`). licks(trial,bin) = sum of the binary lick vector in the bin (:41). durations(trial,bin) = (bin_times(end) - bin_times(1))/1000 seconds (:45) — the interval between the FIRST and LAST VR sample in the bin. Spikes summed over 1 ms columns between the nearest npx indices to those two times (:57-61). firing_rates = spikes ./ durations (:66).
- **Inputs.** corridorData (per-trial spikes/position/licks/times), bin_edges = [0 2 4 ... 198 202] a.u., num_bins = 100
- **Outputs.** spatial_binned_data.{spikes, firing_rates, licks, durations}; firing_rates → spatial_binned_fr_all, saved in preprocessed_data*.mat
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** trial x spatial bin within animal
- **Soundness.** TWO FIRST-ORDER QUANTITATIVE BIASES. (1) Dwell time is measured as last-minus-first sample, i.e. (k-1)*dt for k samples in the bin, not k*dt. With measured VR frame intervals of 21 ms (523) / 28 ms (1212) / 30 ms (409) and measured median per-bin dwell of 0.039-0.173 s, typical k is 2-6, so occupancy is underestimated by ~17-50% and every firing rate in spatial_binned_fr_all is inflated by k/(k-1). Critically the inflation factor is SPEED-DEPENDENT (fast bins have fewer samples → larger inflation) and ANIMAL-DEPENDENT (frame rate varies 21-30 ms), so it confounds precisely the learning-related speed increase the project is studying. The same denominator produces `velocity` downstream, inflating it identically. (2) Bins with <=1 sample become NaN, and the missingness is speed-dependent. Measured NaN fraction of spatial_binned_fr_all per animal: 0.2%, 0.5%, 0.5%, 1.9%, 3.6%, 5.0%, 5.6%, 5.9%, 9.6%, 12.9%, 13.5%, 14.0%, 16.5%, 24.6%, 26.3%, 32.8% — up to a THIRD of the space x trial matrix for mouse 1106. Any downstream corr(...,'Rows','complete') or nan-omitting mean is conditioning on speed, not missing at random.
- **Concerns.**
    - occupancy = (k-1)*dt not k*dt → 17-50% FR inflation, speed- and animal-dependent
    - NaN bins are speed-dependent missingness, up to 32.8% of the matrix
    - spikes attributed by nearest-index matching to bin endpoints; spikes in the final partial frame of a bin are dropped

#### 1.8 Lick preprocessing (refractory de-duplication)
`Striatum project/process_licks.m` lines 1-56 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only, but the 100 ms refractory and its 43% discard rate must be stated and the LP shown to be robust to it*

- **Question.** Turn the VR lick counter into a binary lick-event train.
- **Method.** Called as process_licks(VR_data(8,:) >= 1, corrected_vr_time, 100) from all three Organise* scripts. VR row 8 is a per-frame lick count with values {0,1,2} (verified), so `>=1` collapses double-lick frames to one event. Then a greedy forward pass keeps a lick only if it is >= min_gap_ms = 100 ms after the last KEPT lick (:42-50).
- **Inputs.** VR_data(8,:), corrected_vr_time (ms)
- **Outputs.** all_data(i).corrected_licks (binary, 1 x n_VR)
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** lick events within animal
- **Soundness.** Measured on mouse 523: 13,536 raw lick events → 13,497 frames after binarisation (39 lost to the {0,1,2} collapse) → 7,715 after the 100 ms refractory. The filter DISCARDS 43% OF DETECTED LICKS. Mouse lick bouts run at 6-9 Hz (111-167 ms ISI), so a 100 ms hard refractory sits inside the physiological range and removes genuine intra-bout licks as well as any sensor double-triggering. Because every behavioural readout in the project — lick rate, trial_lick_no, lick fraction, lick precision, and therefore the LEARNING POINT and all epoch definitions — is built on this decimated train, the 100 ms constant is one of the highest-leverage undocumented choices in the pipeline. There is no sensitivity analysis and the discard rate is nowhere reported.
- **Concerns.**
    - 43% of licks discarded by an undocumented 100 ms refractory
    - binarisation loses double-lick frames
    - no sensitivity analysis of any lick-derived measure to min_gap_ms

#### 1.9 Trial lick precision and z-scored lick error
`Striatum project/calculate_lick_precision.m` lines 1-31 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure (behavioural learning curve) — but the NaN mechanism and censoring rates must be reported, and the 'no pre-RZ licks' case redefined*

- **Question.** How well anticipated is licking relative to the reward-zone start, per trial? (this is THE behavioural learning variable)
- **Method.** Licks at position > rz_start are set NaN and discarded (:11). p = sum((l - rz_start)^2, 'omitmissing') (:12) — a SUM of squared distances in a.u.^2, over pre-RZ licks only, called with rz_start = reward_zone_start_au = 100 (ProcessStriatumTask.m:105). Null: shuffled_l = rz_start .* rand(1000, lick_number) (:21) — 1000 draws, uniform on (0,100) a.u., MATCHED lick count; mean and std of the 1000 shuffled sums returned (:23-24); chance_quantile via scalar_to_quantile (:25) but DISCARDED by the caller. z-score formed in the caller: (p - shuffled_mean)/shuffled_std (ProcessStriatumTask.m:150). Trials flagged by isoutlier(...,'percentiles',[0,99]) and trial 1 are set NaN first (ProcessStriatumTask.m:145-147).
- **Inputs.** trial_lick_positions (a.u.), reward_zone_start_au = 100
- **Outputs.** trial_lick_errors, shuffled_lick_error_means/_stds, zscored_lick_errors (all in preprocessed_data*.mat)
- **Statistics.** 1000 uniform-position shuffles per trial, count-matched; z-score against the shuffle mean/SD. No p-value is retained. rng seeded once at ProcessStriatumTask.m:8 (rng(42,'twister'), added 2026-05-24) and NOT AT ALL in ProcessStriatumControl.m.
- **Inferential unit.** trials within animal
- **Soundness.** Count-matching the null is the right move — it removes the trivial dependence of a squared-error SUM on lick number. But the metric is undefined in a way that censors the data heavily and asymmetrically: a trial with zero pre-RZ licks gets p = 0 (sum of empty) with lick_number = 0, the shuffle block is skipped, and z = NaN. So an animal that licks ONLY inside/after the reward zone — arguably the best behaviour — is scored NaN, not 'good'. Measured NaN fraction of zscored_lick_errors per animal: 1%, 2%, 3%, 4%, 6%, 11%, 14%, 25%, 27%, 30%, 35%, 38%, 39%, 50%, 59%, 63%. For mouse 730, 63% of trials are NaN, so the learning point is defined on 37% of that animal's trials. Because find_learning_points treats NaN as 'not passing' (NaN <= -2 is false), heavy censoring makes the 7-of-10 criterion structurally harder for exactly the animals with the most missing trials — a censoring-driven bias in who counts as a learner. Additionally the uniform null ignores the animal's actual position occupancy (it can only lick where it has been), so the null is not occupancy-matched.
- **Concerns.**
    - zero pre-RZ licks → NaN, not 'good performance'; 1-63% of trials censored per animal
    - NaN counted as failure by find_learning_points, biasing learner classification against heavily censored animals
    - uniform shuffle null not occupancy-matched
    - chance_quantile computed then discarded
    - control pipeline has no rng seed at all → control z-errors not reproducible

#### 1.10 Disengagement change point (change_point_mean)
`Striatum project/find_change_points.m` lines 1-33 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only; currently it silently controls per-animal n and learner classification, which is not defensible as coded*

- **Question.** At which trial does the animal disengage, so later trials can be truncated?
- **Method.** Three detectors combined. (a) duration_peaks = findpeaks(movmean(trialDurations_vr, 5), 'MinPeakProminence', 5) — peaks in the 5-trial moving-mean trial duration with prominence >= 5 SECONDS (:4). (b) trial_licks_change = first trial where movmean(trial_lick_no, 10) < 20 (:5). (c) trial_success_change = first trial where movmean(trial_success, 10) < 0.5 (:6), where trial_success = max(trial_reward) per trial. Returns NaN if both (b) and (c) are empty (:8-11). Otherwise takes the duration peak nearest to (b) and to (c), and change_point_mean = floor(mean([b, c, nearest_peak], 'omitmissing')) (:33). Called with mov_window_size = 5 (ProcessStriatumTask.m:70-71).
- **Inputs.** trialDurations_vr (s, UNFILTERED), trial_metrics.{trial_lick_no, trial_success} (UNFILTERED)
- **Outputs.** preprocessed_data(i).change_point_mean. Measured values across the 16 task animals: 125, 225, NaN, 100, 109, NaN, NaN, 92, 131, 79, 182, 100, NaN, 112, 27, 51 (NaN for 624, 731, 822, 1212).
- **Statistics.** none — no null, no confidence interval, no validation against an independent engagement measure
- **Inferential unit.** one scalar per animal
- **Soundness.** Ad hoc and unvalidated, yet load-bearing: MutualInformationStriatum_v2, Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding and CrossSpatialBinDecoding all truncate to n_trials = min(n_trials_raw, change_point_mean), so this scalar decides how much data each animal contributes. Problems: (i) both thresholds are absolute and hardcoded (20 licks; 0.5) and movmean is CENTRED by default, so the reported index is a window centre that mixes future trials, and truncated end-windows make early detection likely for a sparsely licking naive animal; (ii) trial_success = max(VR_data(6,:)) per trial takes values {0,1,2} (verified), so '< 0.5' is not a 50% success rate on a binary variable; (iii) averaging a lick-count crossing, a reward-rate crossing and a duration-peak trial index and flooring is arbitrary with no justification; (iv) empty-array paths inside the try/catch make loc1/loc2 [] rather than NaN, so the isnan branches fall through unpredictably. Consequence measured: mouse 418 gets change_point_mean = 27 out of 142 trials, which drops it from learner (LP=26 on the full trace) to non-learner once truncated — the disengagement detector, not the behaviour, decides learner status for that animal. INDEX SPACE: change_point_mean is computed BEFORE goodTrials filtering, so it indexes the ORIGINAL trial numbering, which is the same numbering as spatial_binned_fr_all / spatial_binned_data / zscored_lick_errors (all unfiltered-then-truncated) — consistent. It is NOT in the same space as trialData.* or trial_average_fr_* (filtered), and nothing in the code enforces that invariant.
- **Concerns.**
    - hardcoded absolute thresholds (20 licks, 0.5 success) on a {0,1,2} success variable
    - centred movmean → change point contaminated by future trials
    - arbitrary mean of three incommensurate quantities
    - decides learner status for mouse 418 (cp=27 vs LP=26)
    - index space differs from trialData/trial_average_fr_* with no enforced invariant
    - no validation or null

#### 1.11 Learning point definition
`Striatum project/find_learning_points.m` lines 1-54 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure (LP is the alignment point for every epoch analysis); one convention must be chosen and all callers made to obey it*

- **Question.** At which trial does each animal transition to expert licking?
- **Method.** passes = zscored_lick_errors <= lp_z_threshold (:40); win_counts = movsum(passes, [0, lp_window-1]) — FORWARD window (:41); LP = first index that is ITSELF a pass AND whose forward window holds >= lp_min_consecutive passes (:47). Defaults -2 / 10 / 7 (:26-28), matching project_cfg.m:65-67. avg_lp = round(mean(lps,'omitnan')) (:53). CONVENTION: LP is the START of the qualifying window and is itself a sub-threshold trial (the 'itself a pass' clause was added 2026-05-24; the previous rule returned the window start regardless).
- **Inputs.** preprocessed_data(i).zscored_lick_errors
- **Outputs.** in-memory only (recomputed by each caller). Recomputed here from the cached processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat: under cfg defaults (-2/10/7, full trace) 14/16 learners, LP = 22(523), 44(614), 32(624), 53(727), 54(730), 36(731), 34(822), 14(823), 44(1105), 67(1106), 84(1201), NaN(1206), 23(1212), 39(409), 26(418), NaN(703); avg_lp = 41.
- **Statistics.** no null model, no correction; it is a deterministic threshold-crossing rule on z-scores that were themselves computed against a 1000-shuffle null
- **Inferential unit.** one scalar per animal (16 animals)
- **Soundness.** The rule itself is reasonable and the 2026-05-24 fix (LP must itself be sub-threshold) is a genuine improvement. But FOUR CALLERS DEVIATE and the deviations change the science materially. (1) IntegratedAll_v1.m:49 and save_for_cebra.m:56-57 use the project convention (-2/10/7) → 14 learners, avg_lp 41. (2) Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding.m:43-44 and CrossSpatialBinDecoding.m:41-42 pass lp_window=7, lp_min_consecutive=7 (i.e. 7 STRICTLY consecutive) and apply it to the change-point-TRUNCATED trace → recomputed: only 8/16 learners, avg_lp 52, and individual LPs move hugely (523: 22 → 85; 730, 1105, 1106, 1201, 409, 418 all become non-learners). (3) MutualInformationStriatum_v2.m:69 takes the shared LP and adds cfg.lp_window - 1, i.e. lp+9, the END-of-window convention — so MI v2's 'expert' epoch is nine trials later than every other script's for the same animal. (4) processTaskData.m:38-44 re-implements the rule inline from cfg.task_lp_* aliases. Additionally, NaN z-errors count as failures (NaN <= -2 is false) while 1-63% of trials per animal are NaN, so the criterion is effectively 7-of-10 among trials that happen to be scorable. And the pre-2026-05-24 window-START rule gives LPs 1-3 trials EARLIER (43 vs 44 for 614, 29 vs 32 for 624, 21 vs 23 for 1212, 37 vs 39 for 409), so every cached downstream result predating that fix (cross_spatial_decoding_results.mat 2026-05-14, tca_outputs.mat 2026-05-14) is aligned to the old LPs.
- **Concerns.**
    - three coexisting LP conventions (window-start / end-of-window +9 / 7-strictly-consecutive-on-truncated-trace)
    - learner count is 14 or 8 depending on convention; avg_lp 41 or 52
    - NaN z-errors silently count as non-passes
    - cached results from before 2026-05-24 use the old window-START LPs (1-3 trials earlier)
    - no null model for the LP itself (e.g. LP on shuffled trial order)

#### 1.12 Epoch definition (naive / intermediate / expert)
`Striatum project/epoch_indices.m` lines 1-60 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only; the epoch table needs a per-animal overlap column and one epoch convention across scripts*

- **Question.** Which trial indices constitute the three learning epochs?
- **Method.** trials_per_epoch w = 10 (:26, = project_cfg.m:71). Naive = naive_start : naive_start+w-1 = 1:10, an ABSOLUTE window (:35). Intermediate = lp-w : lp-1 = lp-10 : lp-1 (:41-45). Expert = lp : lp+w-1 ('lp', default) or lp+1 : lp+w ('lp1', legacy MI style) (:48-58). Any window not fully inside [1, n_trials] returns [] (:43,57).
- **Inputs.** lp, n_trials, cfg
- **Outputs.** 1x3 cell of index vectors; consumed by plotTrialFactorsByEpoch, plotTrialFactorVsEpochBehaviorCorr, CCA_striatum_spatial_v3
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** trials within animal (10 per epoch)
- **Soundness.** Clean helper, but (a) it is bypassed by the biggest consumer — IntegratedAll_v1.m re-implements the identical slicing inline three times (:249-251, :352-354, :461-463) rather than calling it; (b) Run_TCA_pipeline.m:29 and CCA_striatum_spatial_v2.m:27 use cfg.control_epoch_windows = {1:10, [-10,-1], [1,10]}, i.e. post = lp+1:lp+10, the 'lp1' convention, so TCA/CCA epochs are shifted +1 relative to epoch_indices' default; (c) ensemble_analysis.m:651-652 uses a THIRD convention, pre = lp-9:lp (includes LP) and post = lp+1:lp+10. (d) Structurally, Naive is absolute (1:10) while Intermediate is LP-relative, so for small LP the two OVERLAP with no guard: mouse 823 has LP = 14 → Intermediate = 4:13 shares 7 of 10 trials with Naive = 1:10. Any Naive-vs-Intermediate contrast for that animal is partly a comparison of the same trials with itself. Also trial 1's z-error is forced NaN (ProcessStriatumTask.m:147), so Naive is effectively 9 scorable trials.
- **Concerns.**
    - Naive (absolute 1:10) can overlap Intermediate (lp-10:lp-1) with no guard — mouse 823 shares 7/10 trials
    - three epoch conventions live in the repo (lp / lp+1 / lp-9:lp)
    - IntegratedAll_v1 duplicates the logic inline instead of calling the helper

#### 1.13 Good-trial filtering and the resulting dual trial index space
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 70-176 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only; must be fixed and the two files regenerated before any trial-resolved neural-vs-behaviour correlation is trusted for 1212/409*

- **Question.** Which trials are excluded, and are behavioural and neural arrays indexed consistently afterwards?
- **Method.** trials_to_exclude = cellfun(@isempty, corridorData.trial_reward); goodTrials = ~trials_to_exclude (:78-79). Only trialData fields whose numel equals trialData.n_trials are filtered (:82-89) — so the SCALAR field trialData.n_trials is itself never updated. npxStartIdx/npxEndIdx are filtered (:91-92); n_trials = sum(goodTrials) (:93). corridorData and darkData are NOT filtered. trial_lick_positions, trial_lick_fractions and spatial_binning all run on the UNFILTERED corridorData (:96,113,153) and are then truncated to the first n_trials (:102,173). trial_average_fr_* are computed from the FILTERED npx indices and filtered trialDurations_vr (:126-142).
- **Inputs.** corridorData, trialData, npx indices
- **Outputs.** preprocessed_data with two mutually inconsistent trial index spaces
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** trials within animal
- **Soundness.** VERIFIED DEFECT IN THE CACHED DATA. For 14/16 animals nothing is excluded so the bug is invisible. For mouse 1212 (animal 13) and 409 (animal 14) exactly one trial is excluded, and the cached preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat shows the split: trialData.n_trials = 156 and 258 (STALE — the original counts) while trialStartTimes_vr has 155 and 257 entries; corridorData/darkData cells and trial_metrics.trial_lick_no and trial_lick_fractions keep 156/258; trial_lick_errors, zscored_lick_errors and spatial_binned_fr_all have 155/257. For mouse 1212 the excluded trial is INTERIOR — trial 103 of spatial_binned_fr_all is an all-NaN slice, i.e. the bad trial is retained in place and the LAST trial was silently dropped instead — so trial_average_fr_dms/dls/acc (filtered space, 155 entries) is shifted by -1 relative to spatial_binned_fr_all, zscored_lick_errors, spatial_binned_data.licks/durations and change_point_mean from trial 103 onward. Mouse 1212 is one of only three CA1/DG animals and the second-largest V1 contributor, so the misalignment lands on exactly the hippocampal cohort. For mouse 409 the excluded trial is the last, so no interior shift. Any downstream code trusting trialData.n_trials (saved stale) will over-index by one for those two animals.
- **Concerns.**
    - trialData.n_trials saved stale (156 vs 155; 258 vs 257)
    - trial_average_fr_* in filtered index space vs everything else in unfiltered-truncated space
    - mouse 1212: interior excluded trial → -1 shift from trial 103 onward; all-NaN neural slice retained while the final trial is dropped
    - corridorData/darkData never filtered; no count of excluded trials is logged

#### 1.14 Pairwise cross-area correlation matrices
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 179-230 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary at best; as computed it cannot support a claim about cross-area coupling changing with learning*

- **Question.** How correlated are unit pairs across areas, trial by trial?
- **Method.** Per trial, corr(area1_trial, area2_trial, 'Rows','complete') over the 100 spatial bins as observations (:200-211), for DMS-ACC, DMS-DLS, V1-ACC, V1-DMS only. Then mean and mean-of-absolute over both unit dimensions, omitnan (:214-224). If an area is empty, results are NaN (:226-229).
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_fr_all (100 bins x n_trials)
- **Outputs.** mean_cross_area_corr_DMSACC / DMSDLS / V1ACC / V1DMS and their mean_abs_ variants, in preprocessed_data*.mat
- **Statistics.** Pearson r per unit pair per trial; no null, no shuffle, no multiple-comparison control; only the pair-averaged summary is retained
- **Inferential unit.** unit pairs (pseudoreplicated) collapsed to one value per trial per animal
- **Soundness.** Only 4 of the 15 pairs in cfg.area_pairs are computed; DLS-ACC, CA1-*, DG-* are absent, so the 'all pairs' framing in project_cfg is not realised here. The observation dimension is 100 spatial bins per trial, and 5-33% of those bins are NaN with speed-dependent missingness, so 'Rows','complete' silently changes the effective n per trial and conditions on speed — with as few as ~67 valid bins for mouse 1106. Averaging r over unit pairs treats pairs as independent (pure pseudoreplication) and mixes positive and negative correlations; the mean_abs_ variant is positively biased by noise and by the varying effective n. No shuffle null and no significance testing at this stage. Downstream in ProcessStriatumTask.m:798,810 these per-trial values are correlated against zscored_lick_errors with corr(...) and a raw p-value printed in a legend — one test per animal per pair, no FDR.
- **Concerns.**
    - unit pairs averaged as if independent (pseudoreplication)
    - 'Rows','complete' over NaN bins → speed-conditioned, varying effective n
    - mean_abs correlation is noise-biased and n-dependent
    - only 4 of 15 area pairs computed; no CA1/DG
    - per-animal correlation-vs-lick-error tests with uncorrected p-values (:798, :810)

#### 1.15 Generalised variance per trial
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 276-292 · **🟠 major** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *drop*

- **Question.** How does the volume of the population activity distribution change across trials?
- **Method.** pagesvd(spatial_binned_fr_all,'econ') then sum(log(sv.^2),1)/n_total_neurons per trial (:281-286), with a per-trial svd fallback (:288-291). The standalone estimate_trialwise_variance.m instead computes log(det(cov + 1*eye)) / n_neurons per trial (:16-22) with a hardcoded ridge of 1.0 (:19) and a 5-trial smoothing window (:24).
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_fr_all (contains 0.2-32.8% NaN), temp_binned_dark_fr
- **Outputs.** computed but NEVER assigned into preprocessed_data in ProcessStriatumTask (no save); estimate_trialwise_variance is called only from ProcessStriatumControl.m and legacy/
- **Statistics.** none at this stage
- **Inferential unit.** trials within animal
- **Soundness.** Computed and discarded in the task pipeline — generalized_variances_stim/dark are never written to preprocessed_data, so this is dead compute. Were it used it would be unsound: spatial_binned_fr_all contains NaN in every animal (0.2-32.8%), and svd of a NaN matrix returns NaN, so most trials would be NaN; and for n_units > 100 the matrix is rank-deficient in the bin dimension so log of a near-zero singular value diverges to -Inf. estimate_trialwise_variance's hardcoded +1*eye regulariser is a scale-dependent constant added to a covariance of firing rates in Hz, so the resulting log-det is not comparable across animals with different firing-rate scales.
- **Concerns.**
    - dead compute in the task pipeline (never saved)
    - NaN-propagating svd; -Inf for rank-deficient trials
    - hardcoded +1*eye ridge is scale-dependent and not comparable across animals

#### 1.16 Control-cohort preprocessing
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumControl.m` lines 1-292 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only; required for the task-vs-control contrast, but the missing seed and missing probe-2 areas bound what that contrast can claim*

- **Question.** Produce the control equivalent of preprocessed_data for task-vs-control comparison.
- **Method.** Structurally a copy of ProcessStriatumTask stage 1 with identical constants: reward_zone_start_cm 125 (:6), visual_zone_start_au 80 (:7), reward_zone_start_au 100 (:8), reward_zone_end_au 135 (:9), corridor_end_au 200 (:10), bin_size 2 (:11), edges(end)=202 (:14), fr_threshold 0.02 (:32), mov_window_size 5 (:74), temp_bin_edges 1:100:5001 (:151), isoutlier [0,99] (:139), trial 1 NaN (:141). DMS/DLS/ACC only — no is_v1/is_ca1/is_dg fields written (:247-249). Saves preprocessed_data_control2p5cm.mat (:291).
- **Inputs.** all_data_control.mat
- **Outputs.** processed_data/preprocessed_data_control2p5cm.mat (585 MB, 2026-05-24 16:01); processed_data/preprocessed_data_control2.mat (33 MB, 2025-01-28) is a separate legacy temporal-only pipeline consumed by IntegratedAll_v1 as group 3
- **Statistics.** same downstream tests as the task version
- **Inferential unit.** units/trials nested in 5 control animals
- **Soundness.** Faithful mirror of the task pipeline, so it inherits every defect above (occupancy underestimate, NaN bins, goodTrials index split, broken calc_dim at :201, dark-period sample-index binning). One asymmetry that matters: it has NO rng seed. ProcessStriatumTask.m:8 added rng(42,'twister') on 2026-05-24 precisely because calculate_lick_precision draws 1000 rand() shuffles per trial; the control script never got it, so control zscored_lick_errors and any control learning point are not reproducible run to run. Second asymmetry: control preprocessed_data has no is_v1/is_ca1/is_dg fields at all — which is why is_area_safe.m exists — so V1/CA1/DG task findings have no control counterpart even though three control animals have V1 probes on disk. Third: it lacks the `clear all` / `rng` header and relies on `clearvars -except all_data`, so running it after the task script with a stale `all_data` in scope would silently process the task cohort against the control depth CSV.
- **Concerns.**
    - no rng seed → control lick-error z-scores and LPs not reproducible
    - no is_v1/is_ca1/is_dg → no control for any V1/CA1/DG claim despite raw files existing
    - inherits all task-pipeline defects including the broken calc_dim
    - clearvars -except all_data allows a task/control cohort mix-up

#### 1.17 Behavioural derived signals (velocity, lick rate, performance)
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 96-152 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure (behavioural learning curves) + methods; velocity as currently coded cannot be used as a regressor or a reported speed*

- **Question.** What are the behavioural regressors and performance measures, and in what units?
- **Method.** (a) trial_lick_no = sum of binary licks per trial (compute_trial_metrics.m:4), COUNT. (b) trial_success = max(vr_reward) per trial (compute_trial_metrics.m:5), values {0,1,2} not binary. (c) trial_lick_fractions = (n licks in (80,100) a.u. + 1) / (n licks in (0,100) a.u. + 1) (:112) — dimensionless, Laplace-smoothed, window = reward_zone_start_au - 20 = 20 a.u. = 25 cm before the RZ. (d) trial_lick_errors in a.u.^2, zscored_lick_errors dimensionless (:150). (e) trialDurations_vr in seconds (cut_data_per_trial.m:20). (f) trial_average_fr_* Hz, but computed as mean-over-units of per-trial total spikes divided by trial duration (compute_firing_rates.m:9-11), and trial_sem_fr is std over TRIALS divided by sqrt(n_trials) then divided elementwise by each trial's duration (:12) — a nonsensical per-trial 'SEM'. (g) all_data.average_lick_rate = sum(corrected_licks)/duration_sec in Hz (verified 1.072 Hz for mouse 523). (h) VELOCITY is NOT computed here: every consumer derives it from the spatial dwell time as bin_size_cm / duration — MutualInformationStriatum_v2.m:52, Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding.m:37 and CrossSpatialBinDecoding.m:33 all use (4 * 1.25) ./ durations = 5 cm / duration; save_for_cebra.m:78 uses (cfg.bin_size * cfg.au_to_cm) ./ durations with cfg.bin_size defaulting to 4 (:29); ensemble_analysis.m:643 uses cfg.plot.zone_params.bin_size*1.25; project_cfg.m:80 defines cfg.velocity_factor = bin_size_cm = 2.5.
- **Inputs.** corridorData, spatial_binned_data.durations, VR_data rows 2/5/6/7/8
- **Outputs.** trial_metrics, trial_lick_fractions, trial_lick_errors, zscored_lick_errors, spatial_binned_data.licks/durations
- **Statistics.** n/a (regressors)
- **Inferential unit.** trials, and trial x spatial bin, within animal
- **Soundness.** STALE VELOCITY CONSTANT, three live scripts affected. The 2.5 cm pipeline (bin_size_au = 2, project_cfg.m:21) is the one cfg.task_data_file points at (preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat, 100 bins — confirmed: spatial_binned_fr_all is n_units x 100 x n_trials for all 16 animals), but MutualInformationStriatum_v2.m:52, Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding.m:37, CrossSpatialBinDecoding.m:33 and save_for_cebra.m:29,78 all hardcode a 4 a.u. (5 cm) bin — a leftover from the 5 cm preprocessing. Velocity is therefore 2x too large in all of them, and save_for_cebra additionally WRITES the wrong bin_size_cm = 5 into every cebra_mouse*_data.mat, propagating the error into the Python CEBRA pipeline. On top of that, both the correct and incorrect versions inherit the (k-1)*dt occupancy underestimate, so velocity is further inflated by 17-50% in a speed-dependent way. Separately: save_for_cebra.m:73 names spatial_binned_data.licks 'lick_rate' and documents it as 'per-bin lick rate' but never divides by duration — it is a COUNT, and it is then capped at the 99th percentile with NaN (:74). VR_data row 4 is a native VirMEN velocity channel (verified present, median 15.3, range -25 to 490) and it is discarded by all three Organise* scripts — the pipeline reconstructs a biased velocity instead of using the recorded one. Finally compute_firing_rates.m:12's trial_sem_fr formula is not an SEM of anything meaningful and should not be plotted.
- **Concerns.**
    - velocity uses a stale 5 cm bin constant against 2.5 cm data in 4 live scripts → 2x error
    - save_for_cebra writes bin_size_cm = 5 into the CEBRA exports
    - velocity inherits the speed-dependent occupancy underestimate on top of the 2x error
    - native VR velocity channel (VR_data row 4) discarded
    - 'lick_rate' in the CEBRA export is a count, not a rate
    - trial_success is {0,1,2} but thresholded as if binary
    - compute_firing_rates trial_sem_fr is not a valid SEM

#### 1.18 project_cfg constant registry
`Striatum project/project_cfg.m` lines 1-104 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** Single source of truth for geometry, areas, LP/epoch parameters, thresholds and data paths.
- **Method.** Returns a struct. Geometry: bin_size_au 2, au_to_cm 1.25, bin_size_cm 2.5, corridor_au 200, n_bins_full 100, max_bin 60, visual_bin 40, reward_bin 50, target_rz_bin 50, corridor_cm 250, visual_zone_cm 80, reward_zone_cm 100 (:21-36). Areas + field map + colours + 15 pairs (:46-62). LP: -2 / 10 / 7, expert_starts_at 'lp' (:65-68). Epochs: trials_per_epoch 10 (:71). velocity_factor 2.5 (:80). fr_threshold_hz 0.02, min_units 5, min_units_per_mouse 3 (:83-85). ridge_lambda 1.0, n_shuffles 25 (bumped from 1 on 2026-05-07), behav_targets (:88-90). ntype_col 5 (:93). seed 42 (:96). Paths (:101-103).
- **Inputs.** none
- **Outputs.** cfg struct
- **Statistics.** n/a
- **Inferential unit.** n/a
- **Soundness.** The right idea and mostly consistent with the code. Two defects. (1) UNITS ERROR: cfg.visual_zone_cm = 80 and cfg.reward_zone_cm = 100 are a.u. values mislabelled as cm. The true cm positions are 80 * 1.25 = 100 cm and 100 * 1.25 = 125 cm, and ProcessStriatumTask.m:10 states reward_zone_start_cm = 125 explicitly. cfg.corridor_cm = 250 IS correct, so the three 'cm' fields are mutually inconsistent — any consumer mixing them places the reward zone at 100 cm instead of 125 cm. (2) cfg has no `bin_size` field, only `bin_size_au`, so save_for_cebra.m:29's `if ~isfield(cfg,'bin_size'), cfg.bin_size = 4; end` always fires even when a proper cfg is passed, silently reinstating the 5 cm constant. Also cfg.area_pairs advertises 15 pairs but the preprocessing only computes 4 (DMS-ACC, DMS-DLS, V1-ACC, V1-DMS); cfg.n_shuffles = 25 is low for any tail-sensitive p-value (minimum attainable p = 1/26 ≈ 0.038, i.e. no result can be significant after correction across areas/pairs).
- **Concerns.**
    - visual_zone_cm = 80 and reward_zone_cm = 100 are a.u. mislabelled as cm (true values 100 cm and 125 cm)
    - no cfg.bin_size field, so save_for_cebra's 5 cm default always activates
    - n_shuffles = 25 gives a p-floor of ~0.038 — cannot survive multiple-comparison correction
    - area_pairs claims 15 pairs; preprocessing computes 4

#### 1.19 Area reordering and area filtering helpers
`Striatum project/reorganize_spikes_by_area.m` lines 1-56 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** Put units in a canonical area order and subset a dataset to chosen areas.
- **Method.** reorganize_spikes_by_area reorders final_spikes/final_areas/final_neurontypes to cfg.areas order {DMS DLS ACC V1 CA1 DG}, appending unlabelled leftovers (:30-38). Called at ProcessStriatumTask.m:61 and ProcessStriatumControl.m:64. filterDataByArea builds an OR mask over the requested is_<area> fields (:23-30) and applies it to spatial_binned_fr_all and final_neurontypes (:34-38) and to every area flag (:42-47), then drops animals with zero remaining units (:55-56).
- **Inputs.** all_data / preprocessed_data, cfg.area_field_map
- **Outputs.** reordered / subset structs
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** units within animal
- **Soundness.** reorganize_spikes_by_area has an ORDERING HAZARD in its call site, not in itself: ProcessStriatumTask.m computes trialData at :60 and reorders units at :61, but the is_dms/is_dls/... masks are derived at :118-123 AFTER the reorder, so masks and spike rows agree. However `binned_spikes_trials` was extracted at :67 — after the reorder — while `all_data(ianimal).final_spikes` is re-sliced at :128-130, also after. So the current order is self-consistent; the risk is that any future insertion between :60 and :123 breaks it silently, and nothing asserts the invariant. filterDataByArea only masks spatial_binned_fr_all and final_neurontypes — it does NOT mask z_spatial_binned_fr_all, binned_spikes_trials, temp_binned_dark_fr, or any of the mean_cross_area_corr_* fields, so a filtered struct carries unit-dimensioned fields of the ORIGINAL length alongside masked ones. Any consumer touching those fields after filtering gets silently mismatched unit indexing.
- **Concerns.**
    - filterDataByArea masks only 2 of the ~6 unit-dimensioned fields; the rest keep original length with no warning
    - reorder/mask ordering invariant in ProcessStriatumTask is unasserted

#### 1.20 CEBRA export
`Striatum project/save_for_cebra.m` lines 1-137 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only (input to the CEBRA figures); must be regenerated after fixing bin_size and restoring mouse IDs*

- **Question.** Export per-mouse tensors and behavioural labels for the Python CEBRA pipeline.
- **Method.** Writes cebra_data/cebra_mouse<i>_data.mat per animal with neural_data = spatial_binned_fr_all(:,:,1:n_trials) (:69), lick_rate = spatial_binned_data.licks(1:n_trials,:) capped at the 99th percentile with NaN (:73-74), lick_errors = zscored_lick_errors (:75), velocity = (cfg.bin_size * cfg.au_to_cm) ./ durations with cfg.bin_size defaulting to 4 (:29,78), position = 0:n_bins-1 (:80), area_labels from is_dms/is_dls/is_acc/is_v1 only — CA1 and DG are NOT exported (:83-90), neuron_types = final_neurontypes(:,5) (:98), learning_point from find_learning_points with -2/10/7 (:56-57), change_point from change_point_mean (:111), bin_size_cm = cfg.bin_size * 1.25 (:122), mouse_id = pd.mouseid if present else the LOOP INDEX (:116-120), group_id (:123).
- **Inputs.** preprocessed_data (or cfg.task_data_file)
- **Outputs.** cebra_data/cebra_mouse<i>_data.mat, one per animal
- **Statistics.** none at export
- **Inferential unit.** animals
- **Soundness.** Three concrete errors propagate into the Python analysis. (1) cfg.bin_size defaults to 4 and project_cfg provides no `bin_size` field, so velocity is computed with a 5 cm bin against 2.5 cm data (2x too large) and bin_size_cm is exported as 5 instead of 2.5. (2) VERIFIED: preprocessed_data has NO mouseid field (its keys are listed and mouseid is absent), so mouse_id falls back to the loop index for every animal — real animal identity (523, 614, ...) is lost at the preprocessing boundary and the export silently relabels animals 1..16. Any per-animal claim then depends on the positional order of all_mouse_ids being preserved, which nothing enforces. (3) CA1 and DG units are exported inside neural_data but labelled 'Unknown', so 151 units become unattributable in the CEBRA per-area refits. Also 'lick_rate' is a count, not a rate, and the 99th-percentile cap replaces high-lick bins with NaN before any train/test split — a preprocessing decision applied to all data at once.
- **Concerns.**
    - cfg.bin_size default 4 → velocity 2x and bin_size_cm = 5 written into every export
    - mouseid absent from preprocessed_data → mouse_id = loop index; animal identity lost
    - CA1/DG units exported but labelled 'Unknown' (151 units)
    - 'lick_rate' is a count; 99th-percentile NaN cap applied to all data before splitting

#### 1.21 Cell-type classification
`Striatum project/OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m` lines 103-108 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary (cell-type proportions); ACC must be excluded from any cell-type claim*

- **Question.** Which striatal cell type is each unit?
- **Method.** Applied only if the loaded neurontype matrix has <5 columns. Column meanings recovered from neurontype_classification.m:25-29: col1 = mean firing rate (Hz), col2 = proportion of ISIs > 2 s, col3 = peak-to-trough duration (ms), col4 = post-spike suppression (ms). Rules: col3>=0.4 & col4<=40 → MSN (1); col3<0.4 & col2<0.1 → FSN (2); col3>=0.4 & col4>40 → TAN (3); col3<0.4 & col2>=0.1 → UIN (4). cfg.ntype_col = 5 (project_cfg.m:93). Probe-2 units get all-NaN (:191). Duplicated verbatim in OrganiseStriatumData.m:65-68 and OrganiseStriatumDataControl.m:59-62.
- **Inputs.** RawData/<id>_neurontype2025.mat (produced outside this repo)
- **Outputs.** final_neurontypes column 5; consumed by neurontype_classification.m and cell-type-stratified panels in SpatioTemporalActivityEvolution
- **Statistics.** hard thresholds; no clustering, no cross-validation, no boundary uncertainty
- **Inferential unit.** units nested in animals
- **Soundness.** The three thresholds (0.4 ms peak-to-trough, 40 ms post-spike suppression, 0.1 ISI>2 s proportion) are hardcoded in three separate files with no citation and no visualisation of the boundaries against the data density — neurontype_classification.m plots the 3-D feature space but only after labels are assigned, so the figure cannot falsify the thresholds. Two structural problems: (1) the rules are STRIATAL waveform/ISI criteria but they are applied to every probe-1 unit including all 699 ACC units, which is cortex — MSN/FSN/TAN labels there are meaningless and would contaminate any 'cell-type by area' panel; (2) the upstream feature computation (what produced <id>_neurontype2025.mat) is not in the repository at all, so peak-to-trough and post-spike-suppression definitions are unverifiable. The `if size(...,2) < 5` guard means a file that already has a 5th column is trusted without re-derivation, so different animals may carry labels from different threshold versions.
- **Concerns.**
    - striatal cell-type rules applied to 699 cortical ACC units
    - thresholds hardcoded in 3 files, uncited, never validated against the feature distribution
    - upstream feature computation absent from the repo
    - animals may carry labels from different threshold versions (the <5 columns guard)
