#### 1.23 Trial segmentation from the VR trial counter
`Striatum project/cut_data_per_trial.m` lines 1-35 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** Where does each trial start and end in VR-sample space?
- **Method.** changeIdx_vr = [find(diff(vr_trial)~=0), n_vr_datapoints] (:7); n_trials = numel(changeIdx_vr) (:9); trialStartIdx = [1, changeIdx(1:end-1)+1] (:11). Boundary is placed at the LAST sample of the outgoing trial — correct. trialDurations_vr = (end-start)/1000 s (:20). Per-trial cells for times (zeroed to trial onset, :17), licks, position (raw VR a.u.), reward, world; trial_lick_positions = position at lick frames (:27).
- **Inputs.** all_data(i).{corrected_vr_time, vr_trial, vr_position, vr_reward, vr_world, corrected_licks}

- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** trials within animal

(1) trialDurations_vr = (t_end - t_start)/1000 omits the final frame's dwell, a systematic ~1-frame (21-30 ms) underestimate of trial duration; this feeds compute_firing_rates directly. (2) The last trial is retained even though it is typically incomplete — raw_data_bin.m:360 explicitly dropped it (`ntrials = max-1`), and ProcessStriatumTask.m:72 sets `n_trials = trialData.n_trials - 1` but that assignment is DEAD (overwritten at :93), so the intent to drop the incomplete final trial was lost in the refactor.

#### 1.24 Unit inclusion gate (fr_threshold)
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 33-51 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only; the methods text must not present 0.02 Hz as a meaningful quality gate, and the absence of any spike-sorting quality metric needs stating*

- **Question.** Which units enter every downstream analysis?
- **Method.** fr_threshold = 0.02 Hz (:33, = project_cfg.m:83, aligned across Task and Control 2026-05-07). keep_neurons = all_data(i).avg_fr_all >= 0.02 where avg_fr_all = total spikes over the whole VR-covered session / session duration (:39). Applied to final_spikes, final_areas, avg_fr_all, final_neurontypes (:40-50). Identical code in ProcessStriatumControl.m:32-52.
- **Inputs.** all_data(i).avg_fr_all
- **Outputs.** filtered all_data in workspace; unit counts propagate into preprocessed_data
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** units nested in animals
- **Soundness.** MEASURED AS EFFECTIVELY INERT: across the cached all_data.mat, 2 of 2039 units fall below 0.02 Hz (both in mouse 730; per-animal minimum firing rates are 0.013-0.235 Hz). 2039 → 2037 units. So the complete unit-inclusion criterion set for this project is: (1) Phy MANUAL label 'good' (raw_data_bin.m:138; MUA branch commented out at :141-143); (2) cluster ID >= 0 (raw_data_bin.m:150); (3) Phy depth inside a CSV [Start, End] interval for one of DMS/DLS/ACC/V1/CA1/DG (OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m:132,167) — this is the gate that actually bites, discarding ~50% of good clusters (523: 268 → 133); (4) fr >= 0.02 Hz (removes 0.1%). There is NO ISI-violation, amplitude, presence-ratio, contamination or drift criterion anywhere in the pipeline, and no waveform-based exclusion. Downstream soft gates: cfg.min_units = 5 per area for plotting (project_cfg.m:84) and cfg.min_units_per_mouse = 3 (:85) — DG violates the former for mouse 1212 (1 unit).
- **Concerns.**
    - 0.02 Hz removes 2/2039 units — presenting it as a quality criterion would be misleading
    - no ISI-violation / amplitude / presence-ratio / drift metrics anywhere
    - real gate is manual Phy label + depth-interval membership, which discards ~50% of good units unaccounted

#### 1.25 Dark-period temporal binning
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 155-170 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary (dark-period control)*

- **Question.** What is population activity during the 5 s dark inter-trial interval?
- **Method.** temp_bin_edges = 1:100:5001 → 50 bins of 100 SAMPLES (= 100 ms at 1 kHz) covering the first 5 s (:157-158). Binning uses histcounts over the SAMPLE INDEX 1:length(darkData.binned_spikes{itrial}), not time (:161). temp_binned_dark_fr = counts / 0.1 s (:169). z_temp_binned_dark_fr = zscore(..., [], [2,3]) — per neuron across bins AND trials, i.e. whole-session statistics (:170); computed but NOT saved. Identical in ProcessStriatumControl.m:151-165.
- **Inputs.** darkData.binned_spikes (1 ms), darklength = 5 s (raw_data_bin.m:52)
- **Outputs.** preprocessed_data(i).temp_binned_dark_fr [n_units x 50 x n_trials], Hz
- **Statistics.** none at this stage
- **Inferential unit.** neuron x 100 ms bin x trial
- **Soundness.** Correct in effect because the spike matrix is at 1 kHz, so sample index == ms. Two fragilities: `length()` on an n_units x n_time matrix returns the LARGER dimension, which happens to be time here (n_units <= 467) but would silently break for a wider array; and trials whose dark period is shorter than 5 s leave trailing bins as preallocated NaN with no record. The [2,3] z-score uses whole-session statistics, which is unsupervised and therefore not leakage, but it means dark z-scores are not comparable across animals or epochs in an absolute sense.
- **Concerns.**
    - length() on a matrix rather than size(...,2)
    - short dark periods leave silent NaN bins
    - whole-session z-score (unsupervised, but limits cross-epoch interpretation)

## 2. Per-session processing and its embedded analyses

*Full domain label:* Per-session processing and its embedded analyses — ProcessStriatumTask.m (Task cohort), ProcessStriatumControl.m (Control 1 cohort), processTaskData.m (learning-point definition and epoch alignment), processControlData.m (control inclusion and yoked epoch definition)

**Position in pipeline.** CONSUMES: RawData/<id>_raw.mat and RawData/<id>_neurontype2025.mat → all_data.mat (via OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m, which labels DMS/DLS/ACC/V1/CA1/DG from RawData/Neuropixels_V1_Depth_Data.csv); RawDataControl/<id>_raw.mat → all_data_control.mat (via OrganiseStriatumDataControl.m — note the on-disk cache contains V1/CA1/DG firing-rate fields that the repo's version of that script does not produce, so its provenance does not match the checked-in code). Control 2 comes from RawDataControl2/ via legacy/OrganiseStriatumDataControl2.m and is never touched by either file under review.

PRODUCES: ProcessStriatumTask.m → processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat (16 animals, 43 fields, 1.33 GB, mtime 2026-05-23 12:19); its later decoding cell would write preprocessed_data.mat, which does not exist on disk. ProcessStriatumControl.m → processed_data/preprocessed_data_control2p5cm.mat (5 animals, 32 fields, 585 MB, mtime 2026-05-24 16:01); its TCA and decoding cells would write preprocessed_data_control.mat, which also does not exist. Both scripts save with bare relative filenames (CWD-dependent) while consumers read via project_cfg.m paths under processed_data/. Retired siblings still on disk: preprocessed_data5cm.mat and preprocessed_data_control5cm.mat (2026-05-14, 40-bin variants), preprocessed_data_control2.mat (2025-01-28, 4 animals, 5 fields, legacy temporal pipeline at 0.1 Hz).

CONSUMED DOWNSTREAM BY: IntegratedAll_v1.m (the canonical three-group figure script; loads task_data_file = preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat, control_data_file = preprocessed_data_control2p5cm.mat, control2_data_file = preprocessed_data_control2.mat and calls processTaskData.m / processControlData.m to define learning points and yoked epochs), SpatioTemporalActivityEvolution.m (Task vs Control, group labels 1/2), Run_TCA_pipeline.m (via buildCombinedTensor → runTCAAnalysis → ensemble_analysis; this is where TCA actually lives now, superseding the TCA cells inside ProcessStriatumControl.m), CCA_striatum_spatial_v3.m and the tcca/ Python port, CrossSpatialBinDecoding.m, Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding.m, MutualInformationStriatum_v2.m, save_for_cebra.m (group_id 1=task, 2=control, 3=control2), summary_numbers.m. Everything downstream depends on exactly four fields from these caches — spatial_binned_fr_all, z_spatial_binned_fr_all, temp_binned_dark_fr and zscored_lick_errors — plus the is_* area masks, so the defects that matter most for the manuscript are the ones in those four (dwell-time-unfloored rates, whole-session z-scoring, the 5 s dark truncation, and the unseeded/unreproducible lick shuffle baked into the Task cache), not the ~1660 lines of plotting that follow.

**Data flow, shapes and units.** RAW → all_data.mat (Task, 16 mice, 2039 units after the 0.02 Hz filter) and all_data_control.mat (Control 1, 5 mice, 1120 units) via OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m / OrganiseStriatumDataControl.m. Spikes are 1 ms binned (`binned_spikes` sliced from ceil(VR_times_synched(1)*1000) to floor(VR_times_synched(end)*1000); npx_time = 0:1:N-1 in ms). VR is resampled to the same ms clock (corrected_vr_time = (VR_times_synched - VR_times_synched(1))*1000). VR channel map: position = VR_data(2,:), world = VR_data(5,:), reward = VR_data(6,:), trial = VR_data(7,:), lick = VR_data(8,:) >= 1 debounced by process_licks(..., 100).

UNIT FILTER: avg_fr_all >= 0.02 Hz. Empirically removes 2/2039 task and 0/1120 control units (0.05 Hz would remove 12 and 5; the legacy Control 2 pipeline's 0.1 Hz would remove 28/1120).

CORRIDOR GEOMETRY: 1 a.u. = 1.25 cm. visual zone onset 80 a.u. (100 cm), reward zone 100-135 a.u. (125-169 cm), corridor end 200 a.u. (250 cm). bin_size = 2 a.u. = 2.5 cm; bin_edges = 0:2:200 with the last edge forced to 202 → num_bins = 100. reward_zone_start_bins = 50, reward_zone_end_bins = 67.5, visual_zone_start_bins = 40 in the a.u./bin_size convention used in the scripts (note the lick heatmaps instead annotate bins 20 and 25, a stale 5 cm-pipeline convention).

TRIAL SPLIT: dark period = trial start up to the first sample with world > 6; corridor = that sample to trial end. Both periods are stored per trial. Trials whose corridor split fails are marked by an empty corridorData.trial_reward and excluded from trialData only.

MAIN TENSORS (shapes read off the caches, MATLAB order):
- spatial_binned_fr_all and z_spatial_binned_fr_all: [n_units × 100 bins × n_trials]. Task animal 1 = [133 × 100 × 357]; animal 5 = [467 × 100 × 501]; animal 12 = [210 × 100 × 104]. Control animal 1 = [105 × 100 × 209]; animal 2 = [474 × 100 × 109].
- temp_binned_dark_fr: [n_units × 50 bins × n_trials], bins = 100 ms each, covering only the first 5 s of the dark period (temp_bin_edges = 1:100:5001, counts / 0.1 s).
- spatial_binned_data.licks and .durations: [n_trials × 100] (durations in seconds; rate = spikes ./ durations, no dwell-time floor).

COHORT NUMBERS: Task n = 16 animals; trials per animal 71, 76, 90, 104, 109, 142, 155, 189, 257, 260, 299, 331, 357, 371, 469, 501 (sorted); units per animal 17, 33, 42, 47, 63, 77, 80, 86, 110, 133, 134, 152, 193, 193, 210, 467 (total 2039). Per-area unit counts (DMS / DLS / ACC / V1 / CA1 / DG): animal 1 57/42/34/0/0/0; a2 69/60/64/0/0/0; a3 19/22/6/0/0/0; a4 16/83/53/0/0/0; a5 55/237/175/0/0/0; a6 12/0/5/0/0/0; a7 13/2/62/0/0/0; a8 16/0/17/0/0/0; a9 28/0/34/24/0/0; a10 20/20/16/7/0/0; a11 20/5/67/67/28/6; a12 16/0/0/102/81/11; a13 8/6/7/64/24/1; a14 31/26/23/0/0/0; a15 2/19/21/0/0/0; a16 19/0/115/0/0/0. Several animals have 0 DLS or 0 ACC units, which is what makes the area ANOVAs drop animals silently.
Control 1 n = 5 animals; trials 209, 109, 132, 137, 145; units 105, 474, 180, 169, 192 (total 1120). DMS/DLS/ACC: 27/78/0, 2/81/172, 9/7/65, 11/23/7, 30/87/75 — leaving 0, 219, 99, 128, 0 units in V1/CA1/DG that the script never labels but that are included in every all-unit computation.
Control 2 n = 4 animals (316, 317, 1011, 1103), cache holds only firing_rates_per_bin (50 temporal bins), is_dms/dls/acc and trialData.

KEY DERIVED VECTORS, per animal, length = n_trials: trial_lick_errors and zscored_lick_errors (1000-shuffle z), trial_lick_fractions (Laplace-smoothed pre-zone lick fraction), trial_metrics.trial_lick_no and .trial_success, trial_average_fr_dms/dls/acc/v1, mean_cross_area_corr_DMSACC / DMSDLS / V1ACC / V1DMS and the four mean_abs_ variants. Index-space caveat: trial_average_fr_* and trialData.* are goodTrials-filtered (155/257 for task animals 13/14) while the rest are unfiltered-order (156/258 for trial_lick_fractions and trial_metrics, first-155/257 for the tensors and lick errors).

DOWNSTREAM (not persisted by these scripts): avg_neuron_corrs [n_units × 50 trials in Task, × n_trials in Control], avg_population_corrs [3 areas × trials], avg_lick_corrs and avg_occupancy_corrs [1 × trials], decoded_positions {n_counts × n_bootstraps} each [100 bins × n_trials], decoder_performance (rmse/r2/mae/position_errors, plus per_trial_accuracy and overall_accuracy for the MLE variant).

All load-bearing helpers read in full: cut_data_per_trial.m, separate_dark_and_corridor_periods.m, spatial_binning.m, compute_firing_rates.m, calculate_lick_precision.m, compute_trial_metrics.m, find_change_points.m, extract_binned_spikes.m, decode_position.m, decode_position_mld.m, tca_with_cv.m, estimate_trialwise_variance.m, plot_decoder_accuracy_vs_chance.m, plot_striatum_pca(_new).m heads, visualize_performance_correlations.m. The Task cache on disk (mtime 2026-05-23 12:19) PREDATES the seed line, so its shipped shuffled_lick_error_means/stds — and therefore every learning point derived from them — came from an unseeded run and cannot be reproduced bit-for-bit today.

RECURRING STATISTICAL PATTERNS, ranked by how much they threaten a manuscript claim:
1. Min-over-restarts as a fit-quality metric, used three times: best-of-20 bootstraps by lowest RMSE (Task L565-611, Control L840-860), max-R² bootstrap in visualize_performance_correlations.m L30, and min-over-initialisations twice inside tca_with_cv.m (5 per fold, 10 for the final fit). In the decoding-by-condition analysis the selection statistic (mean RMSE over all trials) overlaps the quantity being compared across conditions.
2. Overlapping sliding windows treated as independent observations. Every stability measure uses stride 1 with width 5 (or 10 for behaviour in Task, 5 in Control), so consecutive values share 80-90% of their data; the scatter cells then report Pearson p-values over these points, and the pooled lick-vs-occupancy scatter additionally pools across animals. Effective n is 5-10× smaller than plotted n.
3. Uncorrected multiplicity at scale: 32 cross-area-vs-lick-error tests, 64 stability-vs-behaviour tests, 64 stability-vs-performance tests, 48 population-stability tests in Task alone, all with p printed in a legend and none corrected. The repository has fdr_correct.m and CLAUDE.md mandates BH-FDR for test grids — it is used nowhere in these two files.
4. Soft circularity: trial conditions (First3 / Precise z<=-2 / Imprecise z>-1) are defined from zscored_lick_errors and then compared on quantities correlated with the same behaviour; the behaviour-stability-vs-behaviour-precision analysis is circular outright (both computed from the same lick timestamps).
5. Future leakage in the predictor: stability at trial t is a window over t-2..t+2, so it contains behaviour and neural data from trials after t, yet is correlated against the single-trial lick error at t.
6. Saturated fixed-effects ANOVAs: anovan(y, {area, animal}) with exactly one observation per area×animal cell, animal entered as a fixed factor. This is not a nesting correction, and animals with zero units in an area silently drop, desynchronising the grouping vectors (Control's animal_groups is also literally off by one: [1:n, 1:n, 2:n+1]).
7. Small-n paired t-tests: n = 5 control animals for the generalised-variance and stability comparisons, giving a coarse p-value floor.
8. No null models anywhere in these two files. No shuffle baseline for decoding, no trial-permutation null for cross-area correlations, no null for stability. The only shuffle in the entire pipeline is the 1000-draw uniform lick null inside calculate_lick_precision.m.

UNIT/AXIS BUGS THAT WILL APPEAR IN FIGURES: decoder bin_size is hard-coded to 5 cm in both decode_position and decode_position_mld while the live preprocessing produces 100 bins of 2.5 cm, so every RMSE/MAE 'in cm' is 2× the truth; plot_decoder_accuracy_vs_chance is called with 2 arguments so its chance line is drawn at 1/50 instead of 1/100; lick heatmaps are labelled 'spatial bin (x5cm)' with reward-zone xlines at bins 20 and 25, correct only for the retired 40-bin pipeline (the true zone is bins 40-54).

ACTUALISED (not hypothetical) INDEX MISALIGNMENT: the goodTrials filter is applied to trialData fields and npxStart/EndIdx but not to darkData/corridorData/spatial_binned_data or to the lick/metric vectors, leaving two index spaces in the saved struct. I checked all 21 animals: 19 lost zero trials, task animal 14 lost the last trial (harmless), and task animal 13 lost trial 103 of 156 — a mid-session drop, so for that animal every filtered field (trialData.*, trial_average_fr_*) is shifted one trial relative to every unfiltered field (spatial_binned_fr_all, temp_binned_dark_fr, zscored_lick_errors, trial_lick_fractions, trial_metrics) for 53 trials. Downstream scripts that pair spatial_binned_fr_all with zscored_lick_errors are internally consistent; anything pairing trial_average_fr_* with lick error is not.

MOST LOAD-BEARING SINGLE DEFECT: the `calc_dim` anonymous function (Task L233, Control L202) cumsums pca's FIRST output (the coefficient/loading matrix) rather than the explained-variance vector, so every per-area 'relative dimensionality' number — DMS, DLS, ACC and V1, stim and dark — is not the 90%-variance dimension and has no interpretation. The all-unit values a few lines below use `explained` correctly, so all-unit and per-area figures plot two different statistics on the same axis. Compounding it, the metric is divided by n_neurons, which makes it monotone in unit yield (8 to 237 units per area here), and the Task/Control cohorts differ systematically in what 'all units' means. Any dimensionality claim needs the formula fixed, neuron-count matching by subsampling, and a proper participation ratio.

### Analyses (35)

#### 2.1 Relative dimensionality (PCA 90% variance / n_neurons) — in-loop, stim and dark
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 232-274 (Control: 201-227) · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *drop as coded; recompute with a proper participation ratio and neuron-count matching (subsample to a common n) before any figure*

- **Question.** Is population activity lower-dimensional during the corridor (stim) than during dark, and does dimensionality differ between DMS, DLS, ACC (and V1)?
- **Method.** Data reshaped to [n_units × (bins·trials)]; pca(X','Centered',true); dimensionality = find(cumsum(explained)>=90,1) / n_neurons_in_that_set. Computed for: all units (stim, dark), DMS, DLS, ACC (stim, dark) and, in Task only, V1 (stim, dark). The anonymous helper `calc_dim = @(data,N) find(cumsum(pca(data','Centered',true))>=90,1)/N` uses pca's FIRST output (the coefficient matrix), not `explained` — cumsum over coefficients, thresholded at 90.
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_fr_all, temp_binned_dark_fr
- **Outputs.** Only stim_dimensionality_V1 and dark_dimensionality_V1 are ever written to preprocessed_data — confirmed by inspecting the saved HDF5 field list. stim/dark dimensionality for all/DMS/DLS/ACC are computed and discarded every iteration.
- **Statistics.** none in-loop
- **Inferential unit.** animals (one scalar per animal per area)
- **Soundness.** Two separate defects. (1) `calc_dim` is wrong: it cumsums pca's coefficient matrix (loadings), not the explained-variance vector, so the DMS/DLS/ACC/V1 'relative dimensionality' numbers are not the 90%-variance dimension at all — they are the first index at which a running sum of loadings crosses 90, which has no interpretation. The all-unit values (lines 236-244 / 204-211) use `explained` correctly, so all-unit and per-area numbers are not even the same statistic. (2) Normalising the participation dimension by n_neurons makes the metric strongly n-dependent (unit counts range 8-237 per area here), so any area or group difference is confounded with yield: Task unit counts are fully area-labelled (2039 units) while Control animals 2/3/4 carry 219/99/128 units in V1/CA1/DG that are counted in n_total_neurons but in no area mask.
- **Concerns.**
    - calc_dim cumsums PCA coefficients instead of explained variance → per-area dimensionality is meaningless
    - 90%-variance dimension is sample-size and trial-count dependent; dividing by n_neurons does not fix it, it inverts it
    - in-loop values for all areas except V1 are never saved (dead computation)
    - Task/Control asymmetry in what 'all units' means (Control includes unlabelled V1/CA1/DG units)

#### 2.2 Stim vs dark dimensionality paired t-test
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 443-450 (Control: 399-406) · **🔴 fatal** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *drop until the stim dimensionality is actually computed, saved and matched for neuron count*

- **Inferential unit.** animals
- **Soundness.** BROKEN as coded: `dimensionality_stim_all` is never defined in ProcessStriatumTask.m (the loop's per-animal scalar `stim_dimensionality_all` is never collected and never saved; the saved struct has no pca_stim_* field — confirmed on disk). In Control the corresponding cell (lines 297-317) reads pca_stim_dimensionality_all/dms/dls/acc, fields that nothing in the repository ever writes, so that cell errors on a fresh run and the t-test cell inherits the failure. Any figure of this comparison in circulation was produced from a stale workspace, not from this code path.
- **Concerns.**
    - undefined variable / never-written struct field → cell cannot run
    - if it ran, it would compare a correctly-computed dark value against a value from the mis-specified calc_dim path

#### 2.3 TCA factor clustering across animals (Control script)
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumControl.m` lines 437-676 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `superseded` · manuscript role: *drop (superseded by the TCA pipeline)*

- **Question.** Do tensor-component spatial profiles cluster into a small number of stereotyped corridor patterns shared across control animals, and do their trial loadings differ between the first 3 trials and the rest?
- **Method.** num_clusters = 3. Reads preprocessed_data(ianimal).tca_best_mdl; collects U{2} (spatial) and U{3} (trial) factors; spatial patterns normalised to unit norm; similarity = corrcoef(patterns); distance = 1 - r; Z = linkage(squareform(D),'average'); cluster(Z,'maxclust',3); dendrogram colour threshold = median of the last two merge heights. Trial factors normalised by their max; per-factor mean loading for trials 1:3 vs rest; per cluster, anovan(loading, {condition, animal}) + multcompare + sigstar.
- **Inputs.** tca_best_mdl (field) — NEVER written by this script or by any other file in the repository; absent from preprocessed_data_control2p5cm.mat on disk (verified field list)
- **Outputs.** figures only
- **Statistics.** per-cluster two-way ANOVA (condition, animal as fixed factor) with FACTORS as the observations, multcompare, sigstar at p<0.05; 3 clusters tested with no correction across clusters
- **Inferential unit.** TCA factors (multiple per animal) treated as independent observations
- **Soundness.** Cannot run: the required field does not exist in the cache. Even if it did, the inference is pseudoreplicated by construction — the observations are individual factors, several per animal, entered into an ANOVA with animal as a fixed covariate rather than a random/nested factor, and clusters are then tested for a condition effect using the same factors that defined the clusters. num_clusters = 3 is fixed with no stability or gap-statistic justification. TCA now lives in Run_TCA_pipeline.m; this cell is dead code.
- **Concerns.**
    - reads a struct field nothing ever writes → dead cell
    - factors-as-observations with animal as a fixed factor → pseudoreplication
    - cluster count fixed at 3 without justification or stability check
    - clusters defined and then tested on the same data
    - trial factors normalised by their maximum (an order statistic) before averaging

#### 2.4 Area-specific TCA fitting (Control script)
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumControl.m` lines 678-729; tca_with_cv.m · **🔴 fatal** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *drop from this file (TCA belongs to Run_TCA_pipeline.m); if revived, fix the call, seed cvpartition, and stop excluding rank 1*

- **Question.** What are the DMS-, DLS- and ACC-specific tensor components of corridor activity in control animals?
- **Method.** Calls tca_with_cv(spatial_binned_fr_all(is_area,:,1:n_trials), zscored_lick_errors(1:n_trials), 'cp_nmu', 'min-max', 5, 10, 50) — SEVEN arguments. tca_with_cv.m accepts SIX (data, tca_type, normalisation, cross_validation_fold, maxNumFactors, max_iterations) with tca_type validated as a member of {cp_als, cp_nmu, cp_orth_als}, so the lick-error vector is passed where a method string is expected. Inside tca_with_cv (if called correctly): min-max normalisation per unit over the flattened bins×trials matrix with NaN→0; cvpartition(n_trials,'KFold',5); for each rank 1:10 and each fold, 5 random initialisations keeping the one with the lowest TRAIN error; test trial loadings solved by lsqnonneg against the Khatri-Rao product of the train-fold A and B; CV error = relative reconstruction error; best rank = argmin of mean CV error over ranks 2:10 (rank 1 excluded); final model refit on ALL trials with 10 initialisations keeping the lowest total error; components reordered by variance explained.
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_fr_all per area, zscored_lick_errors
- **Outputs.** tca_best_mdl_dms / _dls / _acc would be written into the struct and saved to preprocessed_data_control.mat (line 729) — but the calls error first, and no such fields exist in any cache on disk
- **Statistics.** 5-fold CV over trials for rank selection (held-out, and genuinely so), but the within-fold and final model selection are both min-over-initialisations (order statistic); no null model; cvpartition is unseeded
- **Inferential unit.** trials nested in animals
- **Soundness.** BROKEN: the call signature does not match the function (7 args vs 6; argument 2 fails mustBeMember validation). This cell errors for every animal. The CV design underneath is actually the better part of the codebase — rank chosen on held-out folds — but rank 1 is excluded from selection without justification, min-over-5-inits within each fold biases the fold's train error downward, the final model is refit on all trials with min-over-10-inits and its reconstruction error is therefore an in-sample optimum, and min-max normalisation with NaN→0 turns missing bins into hard zeros (a value with a different meaning from 'low rate').
- **Concerns.**
    - call signature mismatch → cell cannot run
    - min-over-initialisations used as fit quality (both in-fold and final)
    - rank 1 excluded from CV selection
    - NaN→0 after min-max scaling conflates missing with silent
    - cvpartition unseeded

#### 2.5 Per-trial mean firing rate per area
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 126-142 (Control: 127-136); compute_firing_rates.m · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary (or drop the SEM)*

- **Question.** How does mean firing rate per area evolve across trials?
- **Method.** slice_spikes over FILTERED npxStart/EndIdx; per trial total_spikes = mean over units of summed 1 ms bins; trial_average_fr = total_spikes ./ trialDurations_vr (whole trial, dark+corridor). V1 guarded by any(is_v1) in Task; Control computes DMS/DLS/ACC only.
- **Inputs.** all_data.final_spikes, trialData.trialDurations_vr
- **Outputs.** trial_average_fr_dms/dls/acc(/v1), trial_sem_fr_* (saved; length = filtered n_trials)
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** trials nested in animals
- **Soundness.** The SEM is wrong: trial_sem_fr = std(total_spikes)./sqrt(num_trials)./trialDurations_vr — it is the SD ACROSS trials divided by sqrt(n_trials), broadcast back per trial, not a within-trial SEM across units. Reporting it as a per-trial error bar is not defensible.
- **Concerns.**
    - trial_sem_fr_* is an across-trial quantity mislabelled as a per-trial SEM
    - this is the only field computed in the FILTERED index space alongside the neural tensors in unfiltered space (animal 13 shift)

#### 2.6 Per-trial cross-area neuron-pair correlations (DMS-ACC, DMS-DLS, V1-ACC, V1-DMS)
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 179-230 (Control: 174-199, DMS-ACC and DMS-DLS only) · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary at best; needs a null and a spatial-tuning control before it can carry a claim*

- **Question.** Does trial-by-trial coupling between striatal and cortical units track learning/behaviour?
- **Method.** Per trial, corr(area1_trial, area2_trial,'Rows','complete') where each column is a unit and each row one of the 100 spatial bins → full [n1 × n2] Pearson matrix per trial. Summaries: mean over all pairs, and mean of |r| over all pairs (squeeze(mean(...,[2,3],'omitnan'))). V1 branch returns NaN vectors when n_V1 = 0.
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_fr_all
- **Outputs.** mean_cross_area_corr_DMSACC / DMSDLS (+ V1ACC / V1DMS in Task), and mean_abs_ variants — all saved
- **Statistics.** none — no null, no test; r is later correlated against lick error (see behaviour-plotting entry)
- **Inferential unit.** unit pairs nested in trials nested in animals
- **Soundness.** Correlating two units over only 100 position bins within a single trial gives a very noisy r per pair (and both units share the same position signal, so this is dominated by shared spatial tuning, not by trial-specific coupling). Averaging signed r over pairs cancels opposing signs; the mean-|r| version is biased upward by noise and is monotone in the noise level, so a difference in mean|r| between conditions can be produced purely by a firing-rate/SNR difference. No shuffle or trial-permutation null anywhere.
- **Concerns.**
    - shared position tuning is not removed → 'coupling' is largely common spatial drive
    - mean|r| is noise-biased and SNR-dependent
    - no null model, no test
    - NaN bins handled by 'Rows','complete' per pair, so different pairs use different bin subsets

#### 2.7 Dark relative dimensionality across areas — post-loop recomputation + 2-way ANOVA
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 366-441 (Control: 320-397) · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure candidate but the model must become a proper mixed/nested design and the metric must be neuron-count matched*

- **Question.** Does dark-period dimensionality differ between DMS, DLS and ACC?
- **Method.** Recomputes per animal from the saved temp_binned_dark_fr (trials 1:n_trials), this time correctly using `explained`: dim = find(cumsum(explained)>=90,1)/n_neurons for all/DMS/DLS/ACC; writes pca_dark_dimensionality_all/dms/dls/acc into the in-memory struct. Then anovan(y, {area_groups, animal_groups},'varnames',{'area','animal'}) with animal_groups = 1:n repeated per area (Control miscodes the third block as 2:numel(...)+1), multcompare, sigstar on comparisons with p<0.05, my_errorbar_plot, save_to_svg('area_dark_dimensionality' / '..._control').
- **Statistics.** two-way ANOVA (area, animal as a fixed factor), Tukey-type multcompare via multcompare defaults; significance thresholded at 0.05; cell2mat over a struct field that must be non-empty for every animal
- **Inferential unit.** animals (one value per animal per area)
- **Soundness.** Treating animal as a fixed crossed factor with exactly one observation per area×animal cell means the model is saturated: there is no replication, the residual df come only from the missing interaction, and the 'animal' factor absorbs between-animal variance in a way that is not a random-effect correction. Animals with zero units in an area yield empty pca_dark_dimensionality (find on an empty cumsum) → cell2mat either errors or silently drops that animal, so the three area vectors can have different lengths while area_groups/animal_groups are built assuming they do not (Control's animal_groups is additionally off by one). The dimensionality metric itself carries the n-dependence flagged above. Neither of these fields is saved to disk.
- **Concerns.**
    - saturated fixed-effects ANOVA with n=1 per cell; animal-as-fixed-factor is not a nesting correction
    - animals with 0 units in an area silently drop, mismatching the grouping vectors
    - Control animal_groups = [1:n, 1:n, 2:n+1] is a coding error
    - metric confounded with unit count
    - recomputes what the loop already computed (duplicate work, and the two versions use different formulas)

#### 2.8 Generalised variance per trial (pagesvd log-det proxy)
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 276-292 (Control: 229-243) · **🟠 major** · status: `decorative` · manuscript role: *drop (superseded by estimate_trialwise_variance, which at least ridge-regularises)*

- **Question.** How does the total volume of population activity change trial by trial, in corridor vs dark?
- **Method.** sv = pagesvd(tensor,'econ') on [n_units × bins × trials]; generalized_variances = sum(log(sv.^2),1)/n_total_neurons per trial, for stim and dark; try/catch falls back to a per-trial svd loop.
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_fr_all, temp_binned_dark_fr
- **Outputs.** NOTHING — generalized_variances_stim/dark are never assigned into preprocessed_data and never plotted in either file; absent from both caches on disk
- **Statistics.** none here
- **Inferential unit.** trials nested in animals
- **Soundness.** Dead computation. Mathematically it is also fragile: with 100 bins and up to 467 units the matrices are rank-deficient, so the smallest singular values are ~0 and log(sv^2) → -Inf; any NaN bin makes svd error (which the catch swallows into an equally broken fallback). Dividing by n_total_neurons again makes the value non-comparable across animals.
- **Concerns.**
    - rank deficiency → log(0) = -Inf contamination
    - result never saved or used
    - try/catch hides failures
    - normalisation by n_neurons is not a fix for dimension dependence

#### 2.9 Generalised variance: first 3 trials vs rest (Control only)
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumControl.m` lines 408-434; estimate_trialwise_variance.m · **🟠 major** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *drop or rebuild with a fixed common n and >3 early trials*

- **Question.** Is population activity volume different on the first 3 trials of a control session than on the remainder?
- **Method.** estimate_trialwise_variance(z_spatial_binned_fr_all): per trial, cov of the [100 bins × n_units] matrix, genVar = log(det(cov + 1*eye(n_units))), divided by n_units. Then mean over first_idx (trials 1:3) vs rest_idx, paired ttest across animals, sigstar.
- **Inputs.** z_spatial_binned_fr_all
- **Outputs.** figure only; nothing saved
- **Statistics.** paired t-test, n = 5 control animals, uncorrected
- **Inferential unit.** animals
- **Soundness.** Cannot run as ordered: this cell uses first_idx / rest_idx at lines 415-423 but they are only defined at lines 443-451 (the next cell). On a fresh top-to-bottom run it errors. Statistically: the ridge term is a hard-coded 1*I on a covariance of z-scored rates, so for animals with many units (474) the determinant is dominated by the ridge, not the data, and log(det)/n is then largely a function of unit count; first-3-trials vs rest with n=5 animals has almost no power and 'first 3 trials' is a proxy for novelty that is confounded with dark-adaptation and lick count.
- **Concerns.**
    - variables used before definition → cell errors
    - ridge = 1 hard-coded, dominates det for high-unit animals
    - n=5 paired t-test, 3 trials per condition
    - estimate_trialwise_variance still contains a commented-out plotting call (processing/plotting mixed)

#### 2.10 Position decoding — linear ridge-free readout, leave-one-trial-out
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 453-495 (Control: 747-787); decode_position.m · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure, after fixing bin_size and the negative-prediction handling and adding a shuffle baseline*

- **Question.** How well is corridor position decoded from population activity, and how does that scale with neuron count?
- **Method.** options = struct('bin_size',5,'model_type','linear','area','all','n_bootstraps',20,'neuron_counts',[50]). decode_position.m: X = reshape(spatial_binned_fr_all(selected,:,:), n_sel, [])' i.e. one sample per (bin, trial); target true_positions = repmat((1:n_pos_bins)',n_trials,1) * options.bin_size. Neuron subsampling: randperm(n_neurons, 50), repeated 20× (1 iteration if 50 == n_neurons). Inner loop = leave-one-TRIAL-out over all n_trials folds; fitrlinear('Learner','leastsquares','Solver','lbfgs') with NO regularisation for 'linear' (the 'ridge' branch would use Lambda=1). Predictions < 0 are set to NaN (twice). Metrics: rmse, r2 = 1 - SS_res/SS_tot, mae, per-position mae, all pooled over held-out samples.
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_fr_all (raw rates, NaN bins retained)
- **Outputs.** Task line 495 writes decoded_positions / decoding_options / decoding_performance into preprocessed_data and saves 'preprocessed_data.mat'; Control lines 779-787 do the same into 'preprocessed_data_control.mat'. NEITHER file exists in processed_data/ and neither cache on disk contains any decoding field — so no decoding result in the repository was produced by this code path.
- **Statistics.** held-out (LOO over trials) — this part is correct; no null/shuffle baseline; no test at this stage
- **Inferential unit.** held-out trials nested in animals; bins are the samples
- **Soundness.** Cross-validation scheme is genuinely held-out and trial-wise, which is the right unit. Three real problems. (1) UNITS: bin_size is hard-coded to 5 (cm) while the live preprocessing produces 100 bins of 2.5 cm — every RMSE/MAE printed 'in cm' by visualize_decoding_results is 2× the true error, and true_positions spans 5-500 instead of 2.5-250. (2) Setting negative predictions to NaN and then computing metrics only over ~isnan removes the worst-predicted samples, biasing RMSE down and R² up — selection on the prediction. (3) No shuffle/chance baseline, so an R² is reported with nothing to compare it to. Also unseeded randperm inside decode_position (Task's file-level rng(42) covers a single top-to-bottom run; Control has no seed at all).
- **Concerns.**
    - bin_size=5 cm hard-coded against a 2.5 cm pipeline → 2× unit error in all reported cm values
    - y_pred<0 → NaN then dropped from metrics = selection on predictions
    - no chance/shuffle baseline
    - neuron subsampling unseeded (Control)
    - output never actually written to any cache on disk

#### 2.11 Position decoding — Gaussian naive-Bayes / MLE decoder
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 480-483 (Control: 774-777); decode_position_mld.m · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure, after fixing the chance level and per-fold standardisation*

- **Question.** How accurately can the exact position bin be classified from population activity, versus chance?
- **Method.** options_mle = struct('bin_size',5,'area','all','n_bootstraps',100,'neuron_counts',[100]). Uses z_spatial_binned_fr_all. Leave-one-trial-out: tuning curves mu = mean over training trials, sigma = std over training trials with a floor epsilon = 1e-6; per test bin, log-likelihood = -0.5*sum(log(2*pi*sigma^2) + diff^2/sigma^2) assuming independent Gaussian units; decoded bin = argmax. Metrics: rmse/r2/mae plus exact-bin per-trial accuracy and overall accuracy. plot_decoder_accuracy_vs_chance(decoder_performance_mle, 100) is then called with only 2 arguments, so the helper's default n_pos_bins = 50 applies and the chance line is drawn at 1/50 = 0.02.
- **Inputs.** z_spatial_binned_fr_all
- **Outputs.** decoded_positions_mle / decoder_performance_mle stay in the workspace; the write-back into preprocessed_data is commented out (Task lines 491-493); nothing on disk
- **Statistics.** held-out LOO for the tuning curves (correct); chance level drawn as a yline, no test against it; 100 bootstrap neuron subsets unseeded
- **Inferential unit.** held-out trials nested in animals
- **Soundness.** Tuning curves are fit on training trials only, which is correct, but the input is z_spatial_binned_fr_all — z-scored across all trials INCLUDING the held-out trial, so the per-unit mean/std leak. The chance line is wrong by 2× (1/50 plotted where the true chance is 1/100 for the 2.5 cm pipeline), which makes above-chance decoding look worse and below-chance look impossible. Independence across units is assumed with no justification. RMSE again in 5 cm units.
- **Concerns.**
    - z-scoring fit on all trials (mean/std leakage into held-out trial)
    - chance level plotted at 1/50 while n_pos_bins = 100
    - bin_size = 5 cm unit mismatch
    - no statistical test against chance, only a reference line
    - independent-Gaussian likelihood not validated

#### 2.12 Decoding performance across behavioural conditions (First 3 / Precise / Imprecise)
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 498-771 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary at best; needs bootstrap averaging instead of min-selection, exhaustive non-overlapping conditions, and a speed/dwell control*

- **Question.** Is position decoded better on behaviourally precise trials than on imprecise or naive trials?
- **Method.** Trial labels from zscored_lick_errors: first_idx = trials 1:3; precise_idx = z <= -2 (comment says -3), imprecise_idx = z > -1, both with trials 1:3 excluded — note the two sets are NOT exhaustive (-2 < z <= -1 is dropped) and 'imprecise' is defined by a different threshold from 'precise'. For each animal, selected_neuron_count = 50; the bootstrap with the LOWEST mean RMSE across trials is selected (min over 20 random neuron subsets), then per-trial RMSE and R² are recomputed from that single best bootstrap and averaged per condition. Repeated-measures ANOVA via fitrm('First3,Precise,Imprecise~1') + ranova, post-hoc multcompare with 'bonferroni', separately for RMSE and R²; sigstar on p<0.05 using comparison_pairs = [1 3; 1 2; 2 3] indexed against multcompare rows 1..3.
- **Inputs.** decoded_positions, decoder_performance, zscored_lick_errors
- **Outputs.** figures only (Decoding RMSE / R² across conditions); nothing saved
- **Statistics.** rmANOVA (n = animals with all three conditions non-empty) + Bonferroni post-hoc; two independent families (RMSE and R²) not corrected against each other; sigstar row-to-pair mapping is hand-wired and does not match multcompare's row order (multcompare on a 3-level within factor returns 6 ordered rows; this cell indexes rows 1:3 while the analogous stability cells index rows [1,2,4])
- **Inferential unit.** animals (means of trials within condition within animal)
- **Soundness.** Two structural problems. (1) min-over-bootstraps: choosing the best of 20 random neuron subsets by its own mean RMSE and then reporting per-trial metrics from that subset is an order statistic used as a fit-quality measure — it biases performance upward and, worse, the selection criterion (mean RMSE over ALL trials) is correlated with the per-condition means being compared. (2) Circularity risk: conditions are defined by z-scored lick error and compared on a decoder whose input trials differ systematically in running speed and dwell time (precise trials are behaviourally different traversals), so a decoding difference is not evidence about neural coding without a movement control. Condition sets also overlap in coverage gaps (trials with -2 < z <= -1 excluded from both) and the 'Precise' comment/threshold disagree (-3 vs -2).
- **Concerns.**
    - min-over-20-bootstraps selection then reporting from the winner
    - selection statistic overlaps the compared quantity
    - precise/imprecise thresholds asymmetric (-2 vs -1) and non-exhaustive; comment says -3, code says -2
    - sigstar pair↔multcompare row mapping is hand-wired and likely mislabels which comparison is starred
    - RMSE and R² families uncorrected against each other
    - trial-count imbalance across conditions not addressed (First3 has exactly 3 trials)

#### 2.13 Per-animal behaviour plotting: cross-area correlation vs lick error
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 774-818 (Control: 975-1018) · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary; requires BH-FDR across animals/pairs and detrending or a null preserving trial autocorrelation*

- **Question.** Does trial-by-trial cross-area coupling predict trial-by-trial lick precision?
- **Method.** Per animal: scatter of mean_cross_area_corr_DMSDLS and DMSACC against zscored_lick_errors over trials 1:n_trials; lsline; [rho,pval] = corr(x, y, 'Rows','complete') reported in the legend. Saved as SVG per animal (save_to_svg('cross_area_lickerror_animal%d')) in Task; commented out in Control.
- **Inputs.** mean_cross_area_corr_*, zscored_lick_errors
- **Outputs.** cross_area_lickerror_animal*.svg (Task)
- **Statistics.** Pearson correlation per animal per pair, p reported uncorrected; 16 animals × 2 pairs = 32 tests in Task, 5 × 2 = 10 in Control; no across-animal aggregation, no hierarchical model
- **Inferential unit.** trials within animal (each panel), then eyeballed across animals
- **Soundness.** Trial-level correlation within animal is the right unit for a within-session claim, but 32 uncorrected p-values with no combination rule invites cherry-picking; the two predictors are highly collinear (both contain DMS); and the cross-area correlation is itself dominated by shared spatial tuning (see that entry), so a significant rho is not evidence of coupling. Trials are also serially autocorrelated (learning trend in both variables) → Pearson p is anticonservative.
- **Concerns.**
    - 32 uncorrected within-animal tests, no aggregation
    - serial autocorrelation/common learning trend inflates significance
    - collinear predictors
    - x and y both computed from overlapping trial sets in unfiltered index space (animal 13 shift)

#### 2.14 Trial-to-trial stability: per-neuron sliding-window spatial-profile correlation
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 868-1032 (Control: 1069-1234) · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure candidate (stability vs learning) but only with non-overlapping windows or an explicitly autocorrelation-aware test, and identical NaN handling in both conditions*

- **Question.** How stable is each neuron's spatial firing profile from trial to trial, and how does that evolve with learning?
- **Method.** For each neuron and each trial t: window = t-2 : t+2 (window_size = 5, half_window = 2, clipped at edges); data_block = [100 bins × n_trials_in_window]; R = corr(data_block) (Task: no 'Rows' option; Control: 'Rows','complete' for Pearson but plain corr for Spearman); stability = mean of the strict upper triangle extracted as `upper_triangle(upper_triangle ~= 0)`. Both Pearson and Spearman versions computed. TASK HARD-CODES trials = 50 (line 888) regardless of the animal's true trial count; Control uses all trials. Population version: per area, all unique trial pairs in the window scored with corr2(trial_i, trial_j) over the [n_area_units × 100] matrices, averaged.
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_fr_all
- **Outputs.** avg_neuron_corrs, avg_neuron_corrs_spear, avg_population_corrs (workspace only, never saved); per-animal figures (save_to_svg commented out); a cross-animal population-correlation tiled figure that indexes trials 1:50 unconditionally
- **Statistics.** none (descriptive); feeds the rmANOVA/t-test cells below
- **Inferential unit.** neurons × trials nested in animals
- **Soundness.** The metric is reasonable in spirit (windowed profile reliability) but the implementation has three defects. (1) `upper_vals = upper_triangle(upper_triangle ~= 0)` drops any pair whose correlation is EXACTLY 0 and, more importantly, treats 0 as 'absent' — with NaN bins present a fully-NaN pair yields NaN not 0, but a genuine r = 0 is silently deleted, biasing the mean away from zero. (2) Overlapping windows (stride 1, width 5) make consecutive stability values ~80% shared, so any downstream test treating trials as independent is pseudoreplicated. (3) Task's hard-coded trials = 50 both truncates long sessions and, for animals with fewer than 50 usable trials, indexes beyond the tensor (the population plot at line 1040 indexes 1:50 unconditionally; task animals 3, 6, 7 have 71/76/90 trials so survive, but the cross-animal plot assumes ≥50 everywhere). Task's Pearson corr has no 'Rows' handling, so a single NaN bin makes the whole pair NaN — Control differs here, so Task and Control stability values are not computed identically.
- **Concerns.**
    - overlapping sliding windows → severe pseudoreplication downstream
    - `~= 0` filter deletes genuine zero correlations
    - Task hard-codes 50 trials; Control uses all → Task/Control not comparable
    - Task lacks 'Rows','complete' where Control has it → different NaN policy between conditions
    - Task line 1018 mixes sem(avg_corrs(is_acc,1:50)) with mean(avg_corrs(is_acc,:)) in the same shadedErrorBar call
    - triple loop, ~n_neurons × n_trials corr calls (NOTES flags a 10-20× speed-up)

#### 2.15 Trial-to-trial stability of behaviour (lick and occupancy profiles)
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 1084-1168 (Control: 1286-1368) · **🟠 major** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *drop the pooled scatter; keep per-animal stability curves only*

- **Question.** How stable is the animal's spatial lick pattern and its dwell-time profile from trial to trial?
- **Method.** Sliding window over trials (Task: window_size = 10, half 5; Control: window_size = 5, half 2 — different between conditions), on spatial_binned_data.licks and .durations ([n_trials × 100]); R = corrcoef(block); mean of the strict upper triangle via the same `~= 0` filter. Task reads `task_data(ianimal)` (lines 1090, 1095-1096) — a variable that is NEVER defined in ProcessStriatumTask.m; Control reads preprocessed_data. Cross-animal matrices padded with NaN to max_trials; Control hard-codes trials = 50.
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_data.licks, .durations
- **Outputs.** figures only
- **Statistics.** final panel pools ALL animals × all trials into one scatter and reports a single Pearson rho/p for lick-stability vs occupancy-stability
- **Inferential unit.** trials nested in animals — but the pooled scatter treats every (animal, trial) as independent
- **Soundness.** Task's version cannot run: `task_data` is undefined in this file (copy-paste from the integrated pipeline). Where it does run (Control), the pooled lick-vs-occupancy correlation is textbook pseudoreplication: n = 5 animals × 50 overlapping-window trials scored as 250 independent points, and the two variables share the same trial windows and the same denominator (dwell time enters both the lick-rate binning and the occupancy profile), so a positive rho is close to guaranteed.

#### 2.18 Population-level stability vs behavioural performance
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 1386-1463 (Control: 1586-1663) · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary*

#### 2.19 Neural stability across behavioural conditions — rmANOVA (Task) / paired t-tests (Control)
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 1513-1869 (Control: 1713-1865) · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure candidate for the Task version, after making the conditions exhaustive, weighting by trial count, and correcting across areas*

- **Question.** Is neural stability higher on precise trials than on naive or imprecise trials (Task) / on the first 3 trials vs the rest (Control)?
- **Method.** TASK: three conditions from zscored_lick_errors with n_trials pinned to 50 — first_idx = trials 1:3, precise_idx = z <= -2, imprecise_idx = z > -1, both excluding trials 1:3 (non-exhaustive, asymmetric thresholds). Per animal, mean over neurons AND trials within condition (mean(...,'all','omitnan')). fitrm('First3,Precise,Imprecise~1','WithinDesign',within) + ranova + multcompare(...,'ComparisonType','tukey-kramer'), repeated for all neurons, DMS, DLS, ACC (4 rmANOVAs). sigstar uses p_values(i) for i = [1,2,4] mapped onto pairs [1 3; 1 2; 2 3]. CONTROL: two conditions (first 3 vs rest), paired ttest per area, 4 tests, plus a whole-population test.
- **Inputs.** avg_neuron_corrs, zscored_lick_errors
- **Outputs.** figures only; nothing saved
- **Statistics.** Task: 4 repeated-measures ANOVAs + Tukey-Kramer post-hoc, no correction across the 4 area families; n = animals with all conditions present. Control: 4 paired t-tests, n = 5, uncorrected
- **Inferential unit.** animals (means over neurons and trials) — the right unit, unlike the scatter cells
- **Soundness.** This is the most defensible of the stability analyses because it aggregates to one number per animal per condition. But: (1) conditions are defined on the same lick-error data used to label them and 'precise'/'imprecise' do not partition the trials (-2 < z <= -1 is silently discarded), while 'First3' overlaps the learning-onset period; (2) trial counts per condition are wildly unequal (3 vs tens) and unweighted, so the First3 mean is far noisier; (3) the sigstar index mapping i = [1,2,4] onto pairs [1 3; 1 2; 2 3] is a hand-wired guess at multcompare's row order and will mislabel which comparison is significant if that order differs; (4) DMS/DLS/ACC families are not corrected against each other; (5) Task uses rmANOVA over 3 conditions while Control uses paired t-tests over 2, so the two conditions are not tested comparably. Sample sizes are small enough (n = 5 control animals) that a paired t-test p-value has a coarse floor.
- **Concerns.**
    - condition labels and tested quantity both derive from zscored_lick_errors (soft circularity)
    - precise/imprecise thresholds asymmetric and non-exhaustive
    - 3-trial condition compared against tens of trials, unweighted
    - hand-wired multcompare row indices ([1,2,4]) likely mislabel comparisons
    - 4 area families uncorrected
    - Task (3-way rmANOVA) and Control (2-way t-test) designs differ → no clean Task-vs-Control statement

#### 2.20 Behavioural stability vs behavioural performance
`Striatum project/ProcessStriatumTask.m` lines 1873-1899 (Control: 1869-1896) · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *drop (circular by construction)*

- **Question.** Are trials with stable licking also trials with precise licking?
