## 5. Canonical three-group figure script: IntegratedAll_v1.m

*Full domain label:* Canonical three-group figure script: IntegratedAll_v1.m (Task g=1 / Control1-spatial g=2 / Control2-temporal g=3), plus its superseded two-group ancestor legacy/StriatumTaskControl_IntegratedAnalysis.m

**Position in pipeline.** Consumes only preprocessed caches; produces only figures and console text; nothing downstream depends on it. Upstream chain: RawData/Neuropixels_V1_Depth_Data.csv + raw NPx -> OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m -> processed_data/all_data.mat (+ all_data_control.mat, all_data_control2.mat) -> ProcessStriatumTask.m / ProcessStriatumControl.m / legacy PreprocessStriatumControl2.m -> processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat (Task, 2026-05-23), processed_data/preprocessed_data_control2p5cm.mat (Control 1, 2026-05-24), processed_data/preprocessed_data_control2.mat (Control 2, 2025-01-28, STALE). IntegratedAll_v1.m reads those three and writes 20 .svg files into 'Striatum project/' (CWD) plus a stdout summary; it saves NO .mat, so every number and curve must be re-derived by re-running the script. Sibling consumers of the same caches (overlapping analyses, not dependents): SpatioTemporalActivityEvolution.m, MutualInformationStriatum_v2.m, CCA_striatum_spatial_v2.m/v3.m, Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding.m, CrossSpatialBinDecoding.m, Run_TCA_pipeline.m -> ensemble_analysis.m, save_for_cebra.m -> cebra_analysis.py. Superseded ancestor: legacy/StriatumTaskControl_IntegratedAnalysis.m. Not wired into any orchestrator (no Makefile/Snakefile target); run interactively with CWD='Striatum project', and it opens with clearvars so it cannot be invoked as a function.

**Data flow, shapes and units.** Verified directly from the HDF5 caches (h5py dims are reversed relative to MATLAB). TASK preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat: 16 mice, spatial_binned_fr_all = [cells x 100 bins x trials]; cells per mouse 133,193,47,152,467,17,77,33,86,63,193,210,110,80,42,134 (total 2037; 2019 after DG removal); trials 357,469,71,371,501,76,90,331,260,189,299,104,155,257,142,109. Spatial bins are 2.5 cm (cfg.bin_size_au=2 a.u. x 1.25 cm/a.u.) over a 250 cm / 200 a.u. corridor -> 100 bins; landmark xlines land on bin 40 and bin 50, i.e. 100 cm and 125 cm (cfg.visual_zone_cm=80 / reward_zone_cm=100 are a.u., not cm, despite the field names). spatial_binned_data.licks and .durations are [trials x 100], durations in SECONDS (spatial_binning.m:45 = (last-first sample ms)/1000, which underestimates dwell time). zscored_lick_errors = [1 x trials]; change_point_mean scalar (125,225,NaN,100,109,NaN,NaN,92,131,79,182,100,NaN,112,27,51). Per-area unit counts (task, in file order): DMS 57,69,19,16,55,12,13,16,28,20,20,16,8,31,2,19 (sum 401); DLS 42,60,22,83,237,0,2,0,0,20,5,0,6,26,19,0 (522); ACC 34,64,6,53,175,5,62,17,34,16,67,0,7,23,21,115 (699); V1 0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,24,7,67,102,64,0,0,0 (264, 5 mice); CA1 0...,28,81,24,... (133, 3 mice); DG 6,11,1 (18, 3 mice, dropped everywhere). Areas partition the units exactly (401+522+699+264+133 = 2019). LEARNER-ONLY cohort actually entering S6/S7/S9/S11: 14 mice, 1686 units = DMS 366, DLS 522, ACC 584, V1 162 (4 mice with >=5 units), CA1 52 (2 mice). CONTROL 1 preprocessed_data_control2p5cm.mat: 5 mice, [cells x 100 bins x trials], cells 105,474,180,169,192; trials 209,109,132,137,145; fields include is_dms/is_dls/is_acc and final_neurontypes but NO is_v1/is_ca1/is_dg. CONTROL 2 preprocessed_data_control2.mat (2025-01-28): 4 mice, firing_rates_per_bin = [cells x 50 TEMPORAL bins x trials], cells 275,136,50,39; trials 404,403,443,418; only fields {firing_rates_per_bin, is_dms, is_dls, is_acc, trialData} — no spatial_binned_data, no final_neurontypes, no V1/CA1/DG. group_n_bins = [100, 100, 50]; max_n_bins = 100. Epochs: trials_per_epoch=10; Naive 1:10, Intermediate lp-10:lp-1, Expert lp:lp+9. LPs recomputed = 22,44,32,53,54,36,34,14,44,67,84,NaN,23,39,26,NaN -> 14 learners, avg_lp=41 (used verbatim as lp for all 9 control mice). Naive/Intermediate overlap by 7 trials for the LP=14 mouse; Naive/Expert never overlap. Decoder trial budget: task n_tr = min(trials, change_point_mean) = 27..225 (mouse with DP=27 and LP=26 loses its Expert epoch in S7 only); controls n_tr = min(trials, 300). Rolling stability windows: 5 trials (3 at t=1, 4 at t=2). LP-aligned axis in S9: -20:+40 trials (61 points, NaN-padded). Decoder outputs are unitless fractions: RMSE/n_bins (uniform-guess chance ~0.408) and entropy/log2(n_bins) in [0,1].

**Cross-cutting notes.** REPRODUCIBILITY: rng() is never called in IntegratedAll_v1.m, yet three randperm calls drive every null (S6 trial shuffle, S7A template bin shuffle, S7B target permutation). project_cfg.m declares seed=42 and n_shuffles=25 and this script uses neither — the S6 null is a SINGLE unseeded draw plotted as a mean+/-SEM band, so it cannot yield a p-value and is not reproducible run to run. STATISTICS: the only p-values anywhere in the file are the 46 uncorrected Pearson tests in S11; Sections 4.3, 4.4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 present every headline claim (behaviour sharpens, neurons become reliable, decoding improves, ablations matter) as mean+/-SEM curves with no test, no CI and no correction. fdr_correct.m and annotate_ks_panels_fdr.m exist in the repo and are not called. PSEUDOREPLICATION: every 'Pooled' variant (S6 pooled_z, S9 Pooled) uses units nested in mice as independent observations; S11 uses trials nested in mice; S12 uses units for firing-rate SEM. The hierarchical twins are computed alongside in S6/S9 — only those are usable. PERSISTENCE: nothing is saved to .mat/.csv; save_to_svg (line 1638) writes SVG only (no PNG pair, contrary to the project figure convention) into the CWD rather than figures/. STALE OUTPUTS ON DISK, by mtime: current (2026-05-24) = S4/S4.1/S4.2/S4.3/S4.4, S6, S8; STALE = S5 Behavioural_Evolution_3Groups_Yoked.svg and all eight S9 Area_Activity_*.svg (2026-05-14, predating the LP-definition fix, the DG drop and the Control-1 2.5 cm regeneration); VERY STALE = the three S11 Group_*_Cross_Modal_Correlations.svg (2026-05-07, predating the 2026-05-08 CA1 addition entirely). Orphan artefacts that the current code no longer produces but that sit next to the real ones: Stability_AllGroups_{Hierarchical,Pooled}_{Raw,ZScored}_{ByArea,WholePopulation}.svg. STALE CACHE: Control 2 rests on a 2025-01-28 file with no V1/CA1/DG/final_neurontypes and an unverified FR floor, so every three-group claim is unmatched on unit selection; the V1/CA1 knockout conditions and the V1/CA1 stability rows are degenerate (identical to All / empty) in both control groups. CODE HYGIENE with scientific consequences: epoch slicing is inlined six times (S4.3, S4.4, S5, S6, S7, S9) instead of calling epoch_indices.m, and only S7 truncates the task session at the disengagement point, so S6/S9 and S7 do not run on the same Expert cohort; the variables areas/n_areas/epochs/epoch_colors/area_colors are reassigned mid-script (S6 -> S9 -> S11) and min_units leaks from S6 into S7, so the file is strictly sequential and no section can be re-run alone; there is no Section 10 (numbering gap); NOTES.md still documents 7 areas and a No-DG condition, which the code removed on 2026-05-24 (code is authoritative: 6 area rows, 7 decoder conditions). CONCEPTUAL: the S6 'Z-Scored' label is vacuous because Pearson r is invariant to the per-cell affine transform applied; the S7A/S7B leave-one-out models are session-global, so epoch differences partly measure similarity to a template dominated by whichever epoch contributed most trials; the Expert epoch begins exactly at the LP threshold crossing, which biases every Naive->Expert behavioural contrast.

**Scientifically load-bearing constants.**

- IntegratedAll_v1.m:16 mov_avg_window = 10 (behavioural smoothing)
- IntegratedAll_v1.m:17 max_trials = 300 (control trial cap in S7)
- IntegratedAll_v1.m:23 cfg.bin_size_au = 2 (re-set locally, matches cfg)
- IntegratedAll_v1.m:24 n_bins = cfg.corridor_cm/(bin_size_au*1.25) = 100 (landmark scaling reference)

### Analyses (17)

#### 5.1 S11 Cross-modal trial-wise correlation grid (behaviour vs neural stability vs decoding)
`Striatum project/IntegratedAll_v1.m` lines 1318-1443, 1595-1624 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *drop as an inferential figure; if kept, rebuild as a within-mouse (or mixed-effects) analysis with per-epoch fits, one r per animal, and FDR across panels — otherwise supplementary/exploratory with p-values removed*

- **Question.** Do trials with more reproducible licking also have more reliable neural activity and better decoding, and does the relationship differ Naive vs Expert?
- **Method.** corr_epochs=[1,3] (Naive, Expert). For each group, pool over mice and over the 10 trial slots of both epochs: valid_tr = trials where BOTH ep_stab_licks (S4.4) and hier_z(:,:,:,g,all_col=6) (S6) are non-NaN. Vectors pooled: p_lick_stab, p_vel_stab, p_neur_stab [n x 6 areas incl. All], p_dec_space = ep_pos_err(...,cond 1 All), p_dec_lick = ep_lick_corr(...,cond 1), p_epoch_idx. Layout 3 x 6 tiles. Row 1: neural stability per area (6 panels) vs lick stability. Row 2: lick decoding vs lick stability; space decoding vs lick stability; All-units stability vs velocity stability (g<3); lick decoding vs velocity stability (g<3); remaining tiles axis off. Row 3: neural stability per area (5) vs space decoding, plus All-units stability vs lick decoding. Each panel = local_plot_scatter: drops NaN/Inf, returns silently if <5 points, scatters the two epochs in different colours, fits ONE polyfit(x,y,1) line to the POOLED points, then corr(x,y,'Type','Pearson') and prints 'r=..., p=...' in the title; if p<0.05 it thickens the axis box.
- **Inputs.** ep_stab_licks, ep_stab_vel (S4.4), hier_z (S6), ep_pos_err, ep_lick_corr (S7)
- **Outputs.** Group_1_Cross_Modal_Correlations.svg, Group_2_..., Group_3_... (all STALE, 2026-05-07)
- **Statistics.** Pearson r with parametric p per panel. Exact test count: 16 panels for g=1, 16 for g=2, 14 for g=3 (the two velocity panels are skipped for Control 2) = 46 Pearson tests. NO FDR, NO Bonferroni, no correction of any kind (fdr_correct.m exists in the repo and is not called here).
- **Inferential unit.** as coded: a single (mouse, epoch, trial-slot) observation — trials pooled across mice and treated as independent
- **Soundness.** Fatal as an inferential figure. (1) Pseudoreplication: n is (mice x up to 10 trials x 2 epochs) with trials from the same animal treated as independent; the p-values are therefore meaningless as animal-level inference. (2) Autocorrelation: both axes are 5-trial rolling-window statistics, so consecutive points share 4 of 5 trials — the effective df is roughly a fifth of the nominal one, compounding (1). (3) Simpson's-paradox pooling: a single regression is fitted across the pooled Naive and Expert clouds, so a pure between-epoch mean shift (which is exactly the hypothesis of the rest of the script) manufactures a strong 'correlation' with no within-epoch relationship; the per-epoch fits are never computed even though the points are already colour-coded by epoch. (4) 46 uncorrected tests, with significance communicated as a subtle axis-linewidth change — no reader can audit the multiplicity, and the panels are not independent (6 neural variables re-tested against a second x in row 3). (5) x and y are partly the same construction (rolling-window reliability of two signals over the same 5 trials), so shared window artefacts (e.g. a window straddling a disengagement) create correlation without any behaviour-neural coupling. (6) The on-disk figures are the OLDEST in the directory (Group_{1,2,3}_Cross_Modal_Correlations.svg, 2026-05-07): they predate the CA1 addition (2026-05-08), the 2.5 cm rebinning, the DG drop and the LP-definition fix, so they do not correspond to the current code at all. (7) Stale inline comment claims 'All Units (a=4)' while all_col=6.
- **Concerns.**
    - 46 Pearson tests, zero multiple-comparison correction
    - trials pooled across mice as independent observations
    - overlapping rolling windows inflate df
    - single regression over Naive+Expert clouds (between-epoch shift read as correlation)
    - significance encoded only as axis line width
    - panels silently blank when <5 valid points
    - figures on disk predate CA1, 2.5 cm rebinning, DG drop and LP fix

#### 5.4 S6 Single-neuron trial-to-trial reliability by area (hierarchical + pooled)
`Striatum project/IntegratedAll_v1.m` lines 534-728 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure (Hierarchical only), but needs a real permutation null (>=1000 seeded shuffles, p per area/epoch with FDR), the silent-trial r=0 bias fixed, and the CA1 row demoted to supplementary or dropped at n=2*

- **Question.** Do individual neurons become more reliable across trials with learning, and does this differ by area (DMS/DLS/ACC/V1/CA1) and group?
- **Method.** areas={'dms','dls','acc','v1','ca1','all'}; window_size=5 (half_win=2); min_units=5. Per mouse: activity(isnan)=0; DG units dropped via ~is_area_safe(s,'DG'); per-cell z-score over ALL bins x trials (sig=0 -> all zeros). ONE unseeded randperm(n_trials) builds the trial-shuffled tensor. For each trial t, stab_z(:,t)=batch_triu_corr_mean(activity_z(:,:,win_idx)) — vectorised per-cell mean off-diagonal Pearson r over the <=5 windowed trial profiles (z-scores across bins per cell/trial, pagemtimes, /(bins-1)). Same for the shuffled tensor. Epoch extraction as S4.3. hier_z = mean over cells within mouse [animals x 3 x 10 x 3 x 6]; pooled_z = cells concatenated across mice. Two figures (Hierarchical, Pooled), 6 rows (areas) x 3 columns (groups), observed vs shuffle traces, N annotated, all axes y-linked then the top capped at stab_ylim_top=0.5.
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_fr_all / firing_rates_per_bin, is_dms/is_dls/is_acc, is_area_safe(V1,CA1,DG)
- **Outputs.** Stability_AllGroups_Hierarchical_ZScored.svg, Stability_AllGroups_Pooled_ZScored.svg (2026-05-24). Orphan same-day files Stability_AllGroups_{Hierarchical,Pooled}_{Raw,ZScored}_{ByArea,WholePopulation}.svg are from an earlier version of this section and are no longer produced by the code.
- **Statistics.** mean +/- SEM (across mice for Hierarchical; across UNITS for Pooled) with a single-draw trial-shuffle reference. NO test, NO p-value, NO null distribution.
- **Inferential unit.** Hierarchical: animal. Pooled: unit (pseudoreplicated — units nested in mice).
- **Soundness.** Several structural problems. (1) The per-cell z-score is a no-op: Pearson r is invariant to a common affine transform of each variable, so stab_z is mathematically identical to the raw metric except for the sig==0 branch — the figure labelled 'Z-Scored' carries no z-scoring, and the 2026-05-24 decision to 'drop raw' dropped nothing. (2) batch_triu_corr_mean sets sd_S(sd_S==0)=1 and Z(isnan)=0, so a trial in which a cell is silent (constant zero profile) contributes r=0 instead of the NaN the original per-cell calc_triu_corr produced. Sparse-firing trials therefore drag reliability toward 0, and sparseness changes with learning/epoch — a confound that runs in the same direction as the headline effect. (3) The null is a SINGLE unseeded permutation per mouse (rng is never seeded anywhere in the file; cfg.seed=42 and cfg.n_shuffles=25 exist in project_cfg.m and are ignored), plotted as a mean+/-SEM band over cells/mice rather than over shuffles — it is not a null distribution and supports no p-value. (4) Edge-truncated windows (3 and 4 trials) fall in the Naive epoch only. (5) The Pooled figure is pseudoreplication by construction. (6) Cohort: recomputed per-area hierarchical N for the Task column is DMS 13, DLS 10, ACC 14, V1 4, CA1 2 mice (units 366/522/584/162/52); the CA1 row rests on 2 animals and 52 units. V1/CA1 rows are entirely empty for Control 1 and Control 2 (those caches have no such fields), so 4 of the 18 tiles say 'No data'. (7) y-axis hard-capped at 0.5 after linking, so any curve above 0.5 is silently clipped out of view.
- **Concerns.**
    - z-scoring is a no-op for Pearson r; figure label misleading
    - silent-trial profiles score r=0 rather than NaN (learning-correlated bias)
    - single unseeded shuffle; cfg.seed/cfg.n_shuffles unused
    - no statistical test at all
    - Pooled panels pseudoreplicated
    - CA1 = 2 mice / 52 units; V1 = 4 mice / 162 units
    - hardcoded y-cap 0.5 clips data
    - edge-truncated windows only in Naive

#### 5.5 S7A Position/time decoding with area-knockout ablations (Poisson ML, leave-one-trial-out)
`Striatum project/IntegratedAll_v1.m` lines 730-869, 904-916 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure, but the ablation panels cannot be published as-is: restrict each No-X curve to animals that have X, add unit-count-matched ablation controls, and train within epoch (or state plainly that the reference is the session-average template)*

- **Question.** How accurately (and how confidently) does the population encode corridor position (or trial time), how does that change with learning, and which area's removal degrades it?
- **Method.** 7 conditions: All, No-DMS, No-DLS, No-ACC, No-V1, No-CA1, Shuffle (cond_names line 733). min_units is INHERITED from S6 (=5); this section never sets it (legacy used 3). Trial budget: task n_tr=min(n_trials, change_point_mean) (=27..225; NaN DP falls through to n_trials); controls n_tr=min(n_trials, max_trials=300). activity(isnan)=0 applied to the whole tensor before any split; DG units dropped. Knockout = set that area's mask false in active_mask (no unit-count matching, no subsampling). Decoder: for each held-out trial, template lambda_x = mean over the other n_tr-1 trials + 1e-6 (NaN->1e-6); per bin b, r=test(:,b) with r(isnan)=0, LL = r'*log(lambda_x) - sum(lambda_x,1); pred_bin = argmax LL; posterior = softmax(LL); entropy = -sum(p.*log2(p+eps)). Metrics: trial RMSE = sqrt(mean((pred-(1:nb)).^2))/nb (fraction of axis); per-bin |error|/nb; entropy/log2(nb). Shuffle condition: per held-out trial, per cell, lambda_x(cell,:) = lambda_x(cell, randperm(nb)) — unseeded, tuning destroyed, rate distribution preserved.
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_fr_all / firing_rates_per_bin, area masks, learning_points_task, change_point_mean
- **Outputs.** in-memory bin_pos_err, bin_pos_entropy, ep_pos_err, ep_pos_entropy (nothing saved to .mat); consumed by S8 and S11
- **Statistics.** per-animal means, later plotted as mean +/- SEM across animals. NO test, NO CI, NO correction. Chance level not drawn (uniform-guess RMSE would be ~0.408 of the axis).
- **Inferential unit.** animal (task <=14 learners, ctrl1 5, ctrl2 4); trials are averaged within animal first
- **Soundness.** The LOO Poisson ML decoder itself is correctly implemented (no label leakage: the template excludes the test trial; RMSE/entropy normalisation by nb and log2(nb) makes the 100-bin and 50-bin groups comparable, and chance sits at ~0.408 regardless of nb). Three serious interpretive defects. (1) KNOCKOUT DILUTION: the No-X curve is averaged over all animals, including those with zero X units, where No-X is byte-identical to All. From the cache: V1 units exist in only 4 of the 14 task learners and CA1 in only 2; Control 1 and Control 2 have no V1/CA1 at all. So the No-V1 curve equals All in 10/14 task mice and in 9/9 control mice, and No-CA1 equals All in 12/14 task mice — these curves are guaranteed to hug All whatever the true effect. No-DLS is also degenerate in 3 learners (0 DLS units) and No-ACC in 0. (2) CELL-COUNT CONFOUND: conditions remove wildly different numbers of units (e.g. mouse 5 loses 237 DLS vs 55 DMS units) and Poisson ML accuracy scales with N, so No-DMS vs No-DLS differences partly measure how many units were deleted. No unit-count-matched control is computed. (3) SESSION-GLOBAL TEMPLATE: the leave-one-out template averages ALL other trials in the session, so it is dominated by whichever epoch contributes the most trials. Decoder 'improvement' across epochs therefore partly measures each trial's similarity to the session-average tuning curve rather than the emergence of a decodable code; a within-epoch-trained decoder would be the honest version. Also NaN->0 imputation conflates unvisited bins with silence in both the template and the test vector (a constant imputation, so not leakage, but a likelihood misspecification), and the shuffle is unseeded. Cohort mismatch with S6: only S7 truncates the task session at the disengagement point, so mouse 15 (LP=26, DP=27) contributes no Expert epoch here while it does in S6/S9 — the Expert panels of the two figures are not on the same animals.
- **Concerns.**
    - No-V1 identical to All in 10/14 task mice and all controls; No-CA1 in 12/14
    - ablation not unit-count matched
    - LOO template pooled across epochs -> epoch effect partly tautological
    - min_units silently inherited from S6
    - NaN->0 before splitting (imputation, applies to test trial too)
    - unseeded tuning shuffle
    - chance level never drawn
    - task-only DP truncation changes the Expert cohort relative to S6/S9

#### 5.6 S7B Lick-pattern decoding (bin-wise log-link ridge, closed-form PRESS LOO)
`Striatum project/IntegratedAll_v1.m` lines 774-775, 871-902 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary at best; needs lambda chosen by nested CV (or ridge scaled to n), Inf/outlier filtering, and reporting of the All-minus-Shuffle difference rather than raw r*

- **Question.** Can population activity in a bin predict the lick rate in that bin, and does that prediction improve with learning / degrade with area removal?
- **Method.** lambda=1.0 (line 732). Y_lick = licks./durations (g<3) or temporal_binned_licks (g=3); Inf->NaN; winsorised at quantile(Y_lick(:),0.99) computed over ALL trials. Bin-count guard: skipped with a warning if size(Y_lick,2) ~= n_bins_i. Y_lick_log = log(Y+1). For each bin b: X_b = [trials x cells] activity at b; y = Y_lick_log(:,b); y_pred = loo_ridge_press(X_b, y, 1.0) with defaults Standardize=true, Intercept=true (unpenalised); prediction back-transformed exp(.)-1 and negatives clipped to 0. Per trial: Pearson r between the predicted and actual lick profile across bins, gated on >3 valid bins and var>1e-6 on both sides. Shuffle condition permutes Y_lick rows (unseeded) and correlates against the SHUFFLED target.
- **Inputs.** activity tensors + lick rate per bin
- **Outputs.** in-memory ep_lick_corr; consumed by S8 Figure D and S11
- **Statistics.** per-trial Pearson r, averaged per animal per epoch, then mean +/- SEM across animals. No test.
- **Inferential unit.** animal (bins within trial are the observations of each r)
- **Soundness.** Three quantitative problems. (1) p >> n for most animals: lambda=1 on standardised columns is a negligible penalty next to diag(X'X)~n-1, so with cells (17-467) exceeding usable trials (27-225) the hat diagonal approaches 1 and the PRESS identity (y_hat - h*y)/(1-h) amplifies residuals by 1/(1-h). loo_ridge_press guards h at 1-1e-12 only, so predictions can explode; exp() of a large value then gives Inf, and the downstream validity mask checks only isnan, not isinf (line 897) — Inf survives into var() (making it NaN, so the trial is silently dropped) or, when merely huge-but-finite, a single bin dominates that trial's Pearson r. No lambda selection by CV anywhere. (2) The metric is inflated by the stereotyped mean lick profile: the per-bin unpenalised intercepts reconstruct the across-trial mean lick shape, which already correlates strongly with any single trial's shape, so r measures profile stereotypy far more than trial-specific decoding. The Shuffle condition partly controls this (it retains the intercepts) and is the only meaningful reference — the All-vs-Shuffle gap, not the absolute r, is the interpretable quantity. (3) Minor leaks: the 99th-percentile cap and the X standardisation are both computed on all trials including the held-out one (the latter is the documented O(1/n) drift in loo_ridge_press). Improvement over the legacy version: the shuffle null now correlates the prediction against the shuffled target (legacy compared it against the unshuffled licks), which is the correct permutation logic.
- **Concerns.**
    - p>n with lambda=1 -> h_ii->1, exploding LOO predictions
    - isinf not filtered before corr/var
    - r dominated by the stereotyped mean lick profile
    - winsorisation and standardisation computed on all trials
    - unseeded target permutation

`Striatum project/IntegratedAll_v1.m` lines 1445-1593 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods table / Extended Data — must be re-run restricted to the analysed (learner) cohort and written to a .csv*

- **Question.** How many units per area and per putative cell type, how many trials, and what are the mean firing rates, per group?
- **Method.** Per group, over ALL animals (no learner filter): keep_cells = ~is_area_safe(s,'DG'); counts of is_dms/is_dls/is_acc/is_v1/is_ca1 after DG removal; total_units = numel(is_dms). Cell types from final_neurontypes column 5 when >=5 columns (else column 1, else NaN), subset by keep_cells; 1=MSN, 2=FSN, 3=TAN, everything else Unclassified. total_trials = size(fr_tensor,3). mean_fr_per_neuron = mean(fr_tensor,[2 3],'omitnan') then subset by keep_cells, concatenated across animals per area and per type. - **Inputs.** is_* masks, final_neurontypes(:,5), spatial_binned_fr_all / firing_rates_per_bin
- **Outputs.** stdout only (nothing saved)
- **Statistics.** descriptive means +/- SEM; SEM over animals for counts, over UNITS for firing rates
- **Inferential unit.** animal for counts; unit for firing rates
- **Soundness.** Arithmetic is correct (masks and mean_fr_per_neuron are indexed consistently; SEM denominators match the vectors used). Three manuscript-relevant defects. (1) The cohort does not match the analyses: S12 counts all 16 task mice, while every neural section drops the 2 non-learners. Verified from the cache: S12 will report 16 mice / 2019 units after DG removal (DMS 401, DLS 522, ACC 699, V1 264, CA1 133), whereas Figures S6/S7/S9 actually rest on 14 mice / 1686 units (DMS 366, DLS 522, ACC 584, V1 162, CA1 52) — the single largest V1 dataset (102 units) and 81 of the 133 CA1 units belong to a non-learner and never enter any figure. A Methods table copied from this printout would overstate V1 by 63% and CA1 by 156%. (2) Firing-rate SEM is over units pooled across animals (pseudoreplication); the label 'Mean +/- SEM across neurons' is honest but the number is not an animal-level statistic. (3) Output is console text only — nothing is written to disk, so every number in the paper must be hand-transcribed with no provenance. Control 2 has no final_neurontypes, so all its units print as Unclassified and the MSN/FSN/TAN firing rates print NaN +/- NaN (mean of an empty vector).
- **Concerns.**
    - counts include the 2 non-learners excluded from every figure (2019 vs 1686 units; V1 264 vs 162; CA1 133 vs 52)
    - FR SEM over pooled units
    - console-only output, no machine-readable record
    - Control 2 lacks final_neurontypes -> all Unclassified, NaN cell-type FRs
    - unit counts inherit whatever fr_threshold each cache was built with (0.02 Hz for Task/Ctrl1; unknown for the 2025 Ctrl2 cache)

#### 5.11 S3 Control-2 temporal lick binning (on the fly)
`Striatum project/IntegratedAll_v1.m` lines 64-101 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** What is the Control-2 (dark habituation) lick rate per temporal bin, matched to its neural binning?
- **Method.** Per mouse: n_bins_ctrl2 = size(firing_rates_per_bin,2) (=50). Per trial: bin_edges = linspace(0, max(trial_times_zeroed), n_bins_ctrl2+1); bin_duration=(edge diff)/1000 (ms->s); lick_count/bin_duration -> Hz. Branch: if numel(trial_licks)==numel(trial_times) treat licks as a per-sample indicator (sum(licks(idx)>0)); else treat licks as event timestamps (count in [start,end)). Bins with no VR samples get 0 (not NaN).
- **Inputs.** control2_data(i).trialData.{trial_times_zeroed,trial_licks}, firing_rates_per_bin
- **Outputs.** control2_data(i).temporal_binned_licks [trials x 50] (in-memory only)
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** trial x bin
- **Soundness.** Bins are trial-duration-normalised, so bin width varies trial to trial (time-warped) — unlike the Task's fixed 2.5 cm bins. That is defensible for a temporal control but means the x-axes of the g=3 panels are not a fixed physical unit. The length-equality branch silently switches the meaning of trial_licks between indicator and event-time; if a session happens to have numel(licks)==numel(times) by coincidence the wrong branch fires with no warning. Empty bins are coded 0 Hz rather than missing, which biases mean lick rate downward in fast/short bins.
- **Concerns.**
    - ambiguous lick-representation branch
    - 0 vs NaN for unsampled bins

#### 5.14 S4.4 Behavioural stability evolution (lick and velocity pattern reliability)
`Striatum project/IntegratedAll_v1.m` lines 298-422 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure (behavioural counterpart of S6)*

- **Question.** Do lick and running patterns become more reproducible trial-to-trial with learning, in each group?
- **Method.** window_size_beh=5, half_win_beh=2. For each trial t: win_idx=max(1,t-2):min(n_tr,t+2); stability = calc_triu_corr(lr(win_idx,:)') = mean of the off-diagonal upper triangle of corrcoef over the (<=5) trial profiles (bins as observations). Velocity = cfg.bin_size_au*1.25 ./ durations (=2.5 cm/s per bin), Inf->NaN; g=3 has durs=ones so lr is counts and velocity is all-NaN. Epoch extraction as in S4.3. Plot 2x3: lick stability (all 3 groups) and velocity stability (g<3), mean +/- SEM across mice, y-linked per row.
- **Inputs.** spatial_binned_data.{licks,durations}; temporal_binned_licks
- **Outputs.** Behavioral_Stability_AllGroups_Epochs.svg (2026-05-24); ep_stab_licks/ep_stab_vel consumed by S11
- **Statistics.** mean +/- SEM across mice; NO test, NO shuffle control
- **Inferential unit.** animal (task n<=14 learners; ctrl1 n=5; ctrl2 n=4)
- **Soundness.** Metric is well posed (Pearson is scale-invariant so the counts-vs-Hz difference between groups does not matter). Two systematic issues: (i) edge truncation — at t=1 the window has 3 trials (3 pairs) and at t=2 four trials (6 pairs) versus 10 pairs elsewhere, and t=1,2 fall inside the Naive epoch, so Naive stability is estimated from fewer, noisier pairs than Expert by construction; (ii) the 5-trial rolling window makes consecutive values share 4/5 trials, so the 10 points within an epoch are ~2 independent observations, which matters as soon as anyone tests them (and matters for S11, which consumes these values). No shuffle/chance reference is drawn on these panels, unlike the neural version in S6.
- **Concerns.**
    - edge-truncated windows concentrated in the Naive epoch
    - overlapping windows -> autocorrelated points
    - no chance level

## 6. Spatiotemporal activity evolution omnibus

*Full domain label:* Spatiotemporal activity evolution omnibus (SpatioTemporalActivityEvolution.m, 2028 lines) plus the two multiple-comparison helpers it depends on — descriptive spatial/temporal evolution figures, the Increaser/Decreaser/Maintainer modulation classifier, population-skewness profiles, and the KS-test distribution grids, across DMS/DLS/ACC/V1/CA1 (DG dropped) in Task and Control cohorts

**Position in pipeline.** Terminal leaf of the TCA branch — consumes, produces nothing consumed downstream. Upstream chain: OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m -> ProcessStriatumTask.m -> processed_data/preprocessed_data5cm.mat (+ preprocessed_data_control5cm.mat) -> Run_TCA_pipeline.m (processTaskData for learning points, buildCombinedTensor for the 30-slot LP-aligned tensor) -> processed_data/tca_outputs.mat. SpatioTemporalActivityEvolution.m either inherits supermouse_tensor_raw / combined_labels / cfg from a live Run_TCA_pipeline workspace or loads tca_outputs.mat wholesale (lines 7-20). It calls only two repo helpers, fdr_correct.m and annotate_ks_panels_fdr.m, plus two functions that live OUTSIDE this repository: save_to_svg.m (in /Users/theoamvr/Desktop/Experiments/2afcanalysis/) and shadedErrorBar.m (in ~/Documents/MATLAB/External/). It notably does NOT use the project's canonical epoch helper epoch_indices.m, nor find_learning_points.m or is_v1_safe.m. Downstream: nothing. No .mat, .csv or table is written; only 17 save_to_svg calls emitting SVGs into the current working directory. modulation_class — the one quantity another analysis wants (NOTES.md items M2 and 412: the Decreasers-only communication-subspace CCA via the striatum_cca Python loader) — dies with the MATLAB workspace, so that downstream analysis is currently blocked on an export that does not exist. Section 4's Area x Cell-Type grids and Section 16b's MSN/FSN distribution panels are the only parts of this file that look manuscript-ready; the KS p-values on every one of them must be regenerated after fdr_correct.m:54 is fixed.

**Data flow, shapes and units.** Input: processed_data/tca_outputs.mat (1.1 GB, v7.3, saved by Run_TCA_pipeline.m:1179, mtime 2026-05-14 15:35). supermouse_tensor_raw = [1693 units x 50 spatial bins x 30 aligned trials], double. Spatial bins are 5 cm (cfg.plot.zone_params.bin_size = 4 a.u./bin; Run_TCA_pipeline deliberately uses preprocessed_data5cm.mat, NOT the 2.5 cm files project_cfg points at, because 2.5 cm binning leaves NaN gaps that wipe whole mice and with them all V1/CA1). Units are Hz before z-scoring; fr_threshold_hz = 0.02 applied upstream. Trial axis is stitched, not chronological (buildCombinedTensor.m:244-246): slots 1:10 = session trials 1:10; slots 11:20 = LP-10 : LP-1; slots 21:30 = LP+1 : LP+10 (the 'lp1' convention, contradicting project_cfg.expert_starts_at = 'lp'). Task learning points = [22 43 29 54 54 35 33 16 43 65 84 21 37 25], avg_learning_point = 40; mouse 8 (LP=16) has slots 11:15 identical to slots 6:10, so 5 of its 'Intermediate' trials are literally its 'Trials 4-10' trials. Labels in combined_labels: mouse_labels_all (1..14), group_labels_all (1=Task, 2=Control), area_labels_all (cell of strings), neurontype_labels_all (1=MSN, 2=FS, 3=TAN, 4=unclassified, 5=RS). Cache composition: 14 task mice, 0 control mice; areas ACC 584, DLS 522, DMS 366, V1 162, CA1 52, DG 7; types MSN 767, FS 174, TAN 37, unclassified 5, RS 710. Filtering inside the omnibus: DG drop removes 7 units, then the any-NaN filter removes 63, leaving 1623 units — ACC 568, DLS 502, DMS 346, V1 155, CA1 52. Area x type after filtering: DMS MSN 309 / FS 22 / TAN 12; DLS MSN 426 / FS 53 / TAN 21; ACC FS 54 / RS 514; V1 FS 23 / RS 132; CA1 FS 8 / RS 44. Mice per area with >= 5 units (the min_units gate for Sections 3, 4, 14, 15): DMS 12, DLS 9, ACC 13, V1 3, CA1 2 — independently confirmed by the N=... strings in the saved SVGs. Mice per area x type with >= 3 units (min_units_per_mouse for Section 16): DMS MSN 12, DLS MSN 9, DMS FS 4, DLS FS 6, DMS TAN 2, DLS TAN 3, ACC FS 8, ACC RS 13, V1 FS 3, V1 RS 3, CA1 FS 2, CA1 RS 2. Derived tensors: tensor_full_raw [1623 x 50 x 30] and tensor_full_z (same shape, per-unit whole-session z). Epochs: {1:3, 4:10, 11:20, 21:30} labelled {'Trials 1-3', 'Trials 4-10', 'Intermediate', 'Expert'}. Zone overlays: visual [80 100]/4 = bins [20 25], reward [100 135]/4 = bins [25 33.75]. Histogram grid: linspace(-2, 2, 25) = 24 bins of width 0.167; KDE grid: linspace(-1.5, 1.5, 100) 1-D and a 60 x 60 mesh over [-1.5, 1.5] for the 2-D density. Output: SVG only, written to the current working directory.

**Cross-cutting notes.** Z-SCORING (question 1): exactly ONE z-scheme exists — per-unit, whole-session, over all 50 bins x all 30 aligned trials, one scalar mu/sig per unit (sig<=0 -> unit set to 0). There is no per-trial, per-epoch, per-bin or per-group z anywhere. The identical loop is coded out EIGHT times (lines 55, 243, 705, 1118, 1262, 1390, 1529, 1783), each preceded by an identical recomputation of the NaN filter (lines 45, 233, 690, 1108, 1252, 1380, 1513, 1767). All eight produce bit-identical output, so the cost is ~150 redundant lines and 8x runtime, not divergence. The scientific consequence of the choice is severe and pervasive: whole-session z forces each unit's 30-trial mean to exactly 0, so the epoch means satisfy 3*m_naive + 7*m_4to10 + 10*m_int + 10*m_expert = 0. Every naive-vs-expert contrast, every Increaser/Decreaser split, every KS test and every trial-1-vs-trial-21 correlation in the file therefore operates inside an accounting identity. No analysis in the file tests raw firing rate; the 'Raw FR' panels are plotted but never tested.

CELL-TYPE STRATIFICATION (question 5): area-only panel families are Sections 1 (unique(lbls_full.area), currently 5 areas after the DG drop), 14, 15a and 15b (explicit {DMS, DLS, ACC, V1, CA1}). Cell-type-stratified families are Sections 3 and 4 (5 areas x 4 types with anatomy-aware masking: MSN/FS/TAN for DMS/DLS, FS/RS for ACC/V1/CA1), Section 5 (5 areas x 4 types, no masking, so 7 of 20 panels read 'No Units'), Section 16a (4 areas x 3 types) and 16b (5 areas x 4 types). NOTES.md lines 60 and 151 still assert that the cell-type panels are 'intentionally left at 3 areas because V1/CA1/DG have no MSN/FSN/TAN classification' — that documentation is STALE for Sections 3, 4 and 16b, which are now 5-area and add RS specifically to cover non-striatal units. The stated rationale is nonetheless the correct one and is implemented properly only in Sections 3 and 4; Sections 5 and 16 lack the anatomy mask and produce empty tiles instead.

XLINE MARKERS (question 6): 24 xline calls at 6 sites (208-211, 451-454, 660-663, 892-895, 1351-1354, 1484-1487), all hardcoded to 0, 3, 10, 20, all decoupled from epoch_trials = {1:3, 4:10, 11:20, 21:30}. They mark the LAST trial of each epoch, not the first (epoch starts are 1, 4, 11, 21), so they are off by one relative to the epoch definition; xline(0) also sits on the axis boundary since xlim starts at 0. Change epoch_trials and the markers drift silently — this is NOTES.md item 316, still unfixed. Section 14 (spatial skewness) has no xlines. The file never calls the canonical helper epoch_indices.m (which defines 3 epochs of 10, not 4 of 3/7/10/10), so the omnibus's epoch convention is independent of the project's.

SEM PATCH AS A SIGNIFICANCE TEST (question 4): confirmed for both skewness sections. Section 14 displays 50 bins x 4 epochs x 5 areas of bin-wise bias-corrected skewness (skewness(r,0), var>1e-6 gate, min 5 units per mouse) with a mean+/-SEM-across-mice band and no test at all; Section 15b displays 30 trials x 5 areas of movmean-5-smoothed skewness with a SEM band and no test. In both cases panel separation of the bands is the only evidence offered, over hundreds of uncorrected comparisons, with no cluster-based correction and, in 15b, with smoothing-induced autocorrelation that the SEM ignores. V1 rests on N=3 mice and CA1 on N=2 (verified against the saved figure titles), so those two panels' bands are not interpretable.

WHAT IS SAVED (question 7): nothing but SVGs. grep for save(, writetable, csvwrite, exportgraphics returns zero hits in the 2028 lines. save_to_svg is called 17 times and does only print(fig,'-dsvg',[name '.svg']) into the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY — no PNG companion (violating the project's .svg+.png rule), no figures/ subdirectory (the code directory root holds ~85 loose SVGs), no run manifest. modulation_class, every KS p-value and D, every Pearson r, the [mice x epochs x bins] skewness array and the per-mouse PDFs all exist only in the workspace and as text baked into SVG glyphs. ### Analyses (16)

#### 6.1 BH-FDR helper (fdr_correct.m) — monotonicity enforced in the wrong direction
`Striatum project/fdr_correct.m` lines 38-73 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only — but must be fixed and every KS grid regenerated before any corrected p-value is quoted*

- **Question.** Adjust a family of raw p-values for multiple comparisons (used by every KS grid in the omnibus).
- **Method.** Sorts p ascending; 'bh': adj = p_sorted .* n ./ rank; 'by': additionally x sum(1./rank); 'holm': p_sorted .* (n - rank + 1). Then line 54: adj_sorted = min(cummax(adj_sorted, 'reverse'), 1). Unsorts, re-embeds with NaN preservation, h = (p_adj <= q), fdr_thresh = max of raw p whose adjusted value <= q.
- **Inputs.** raw p vector from annotate_ks_panels_fdr
- **Outputs.** p_adj, h, fdr_thresh (never persisted to disk)
- **Statistics.** Benjamini-Hochberg / Benjamini-Yekutieli / Holm step-down, q default 0.05
- **Inferential unit.** tests within a family (here: the 2-5 panels of one figure row)
- **Soundness.** The step-up enforcement is inverted. Correct BH adjusted p is p_adj(i) = min over j >= i of (n/j)*p_j, i.e. a reverse cumulative MINIMUM (MATLAB cummin(...,'reverse')). The code uses cummax(...,'reverse'), which returns max over j >= i — so every test in a family is assigned the LARGEST adjusted p in that family, and the ordering with respect to raw p is inverted. The result is always >= the true BH value, so no false positives are created, but power is destroyed and every p_FDR printed on a figure is wrong. Verified empirically against the saved figures. (a) _Task__MeanDist_Epochs_Hierarchical_MSN.svg: raw p = [1.3e-09, 3.9e-08] -> reported p_FDR = 3.9e-08 for BOTH panels; correct BH = [2.6e-09, 3.9e-08]. (b) _Task__MeanDist_Epochs_Hierarchical_FSN.svg: raw p = [DMS 3.1e-01, DLS 2.4e-01, ACC 4.4e-03, V1 1.7e-02, CA1 1.9e-01] -> reported p_FDR = 3.1e-01 for ALL FIVE panels; correct BH = ACC 2.2e-02 (significant), V1 4.25e-02 (significant), CA1/DLS 3.0e-01, DMS 3.1e-01. Two genuine findings (ACC-FS and V1-FS naive-vs-expert distribution shifts) are being reported as null by the helper. The 'holm' branch has the mirror-image error (it needs a forward cummax over j <= i). fdr_thresh inherits the same corruption.
- **Concerns.**
    - cummax should be cummin for BH/BY (line 54); every reported p_FDR is inflated to the family maximum
    - ACC-FS and V1-FS results are wrongly reported non-significant on the saved figures
    - 'holm' branch also enforces monotonicity in the wrong direction
    - no unit test covers this function (tests/ has no fdr_correct case)

#### 6.2 Data preparation: whole-session per-unit z-scoring + NaN unit filter
`Striatum project/SpatioTemporalActivityEvolution.m` lines 22-65 (repeated at 233-253, 690-715, 1108-1128, 1252-1272, 1380-1400, 1513-1539, 1767-1793) · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** Put all units on a common scale so spatial/temporal profiles can be pooled across areas and firing-rate regimes.
- **Method.** Defensive DG drop (strcmp area=='DG'), then neuron_has_nan = any(isnan(tensor),[2,3]) drops any unit with a single NaN anywhere. Z: per unit, mu = mean(unit_data(:)) and sig = std(unit_data(:)) over ALL 50 bins x ALL 30 trials of the aligned session (one scalar mu/sig per unit); z = (raw-mu)/sig; if sig<=0 the whole unit is set to 0. No per-trial, per-epoch, per-bin or per-group z-scoring anywhere in the file. The identical block is coded out 8 times (8x NaN filter, 8x z loop) and recomputed each time; results are bit-identical, so the repetition is cost, not divergence.
- **Inputs.** processed_data/tca_outputs.mat -> supermouse_tensor_raw [1693 x 50 x 30], combined_labels (mouse/group/area/neurontype), cfg (with cfg.plot, which project_cfg() does NOT provide)
- **Outputs.** tensor_full_z, lbls_full (workspace only; never saved)
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** units (1693 in cache -> 1630 after NaN filter -> 1623 after DG drop; 14 task mice; 0 control units in the cached tca_outputs.mat)
- **Soundness.** The z-choice is the single most consequential decision in the file and it is a whole-session z: it forces sum over all 30 trials of each unit's z to be exactly 0. Every epoch mean is therefore linearly constrained: m_naive = -(7*m_4to10 + 10*m_int + 10*m_expert)/3. Consequences: (a) 'increase from naive to expert' and 'decrease' are two views of one accounting identity, not independent findings; (b) any genuine global rate change (all units up) is invisible by construction; (c) every statistical test in the file runs on this constrained tensor and never on raw FR, so the tests cannot speak to absolute rate changes. The NaN filter is also all-or-nothing per unit (63/1693 = 3.7% dropped) rather than bin-wise.
- **Concerns.**
    - Whole-session z imposes a zero-sum constraint across the 30 trials that the naive-vs-expert contrasts and KS tests then 'discover'
    - 8 identical recomputations of the NaN filter and z loop (lines 45/55, 233/243, 690/705, 1108/1118, 1252/1262, 1380/1390, 1513/1529, 1767/1783)
    - cfg.plot is defined only in Run_TCA_pipeline.m:44-64; the self-sufficient fallback cfg = project_cfg() (line 9) has no .plot field, so that path errors at line 69 unless load() of tca_outputs.mat overwrites cfg
    - load(tca_outputs_file) at line 14 silently overwrites every workspace variable in a 1.1 GB file, including cfg and task_data

#### 6.3 Modulation classifier: Increaser / Decreaser / Maintainer
`Striatum project/SpatioTemporalActivityEvolution.m` lines 255-297 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary (as a descriptive split, with the label trials excluded from the displayed epochs); not defensible as a main figure in its current form*

- **Question.** Do individual units gain, lose, or maintain activity from naive to expert, and do the three subpopulations have different spatial tuning?
- **Method.** delta_act = mean(z over bins,trials 21:25) - mean(z over bins, trial 1). z_thresh = 0.25 (session-z units). class 1 (Increaser) if delta > 0.25; class 2 (Decreaser) if delta < -0.25; class 3 (Maintainer) if abs(delta) <= 0.25. Label trials: naive_label = naive_full(1:floor(end/2)) = TRIAL 1 ONLY (naive_full = 1:3, floor(3/2)=1); expert_label = expert_full(1:floor(end/2)) = 21:25. Held-out sets naive_test = setdiff(1:3, 1) = 2:3 and expert_test = setdiff(21:30, 21:25) = 26:30 are computed at lines 273-274 and NEVER READ ANYWHERE ELSE in the file (grep-verified).
- **Inputs.** tensor_full_z, epoch_trials
- **Outputs.** modulation_class (workspace only — NEVER saved; NOTES.md item M2 asks for it as an exported per-unit label for the Decreasers-only CCA, and that export does not exist)
- **Statistics.** none — no test, no null model, no permutation, no correction; a hard threshold on a difference of means
- **Inferential unit.** units (all 1623 valid units, pooled across 14 mice, both groups)
- **Soundness.** The 2026-05-07 'de-circularisation' is nominal, not real. Labels are defined on trial 1 and trials 21:25; every downstream plot and every panel n uses epoch_trials = {1:3, 4:10, 11:20, 21:30}, which CONTAIN the label trials. The held-out halves exist as variables and are never used, so the train/test halves are NOT disjoint as coded — the label trials are a strict subset of the displayed trials. Quantified on the cached tensor: as coded, Inc 352 / Dec 380 / Main 891 of 1623; classifying on the held-out halves instead gives Inc 338 / Dec 316 / Main 969 with only 67.4% class agreement and corr(delta_label, delta_heldout) = 0.706 — a third of units flip class. Regression to the mean is directly measurable: Decreasers' naive activity is +0.597 z on the label trial but only +0.266 z on held-out trials 2:3 (55% shrinkage); Increasers -0.348 -> -0.258 (26% shrinkage). The effect does not vanish on held-out expert trials (Inc +0.180, Dec -0.111), so the phenomenon is real, but the magnitude shown in the figures is inflated by selection on trial-1 noise. Additional asymmetry: the naive side is estimated from ONE trial and the expert side from FIVE, so the two arms of the difference have ~5x different noise. Near-equal Inc/Dec counts (352 vs 380) are what the whole-session z zero-sum constraint predicts.
- **Concerns.**
    - naive_test/expert_test computed then never used — the disjoint-half design is documented in the comment but not implemented
    - label trials (1 and 21:25) are inside the plotted epochs (1:3 and 21:30) -> selection-on-noise inflates the very difference the figures show
    - naive arm = 1 trial vs expert arm = 5 trials: unequal noise in the two halves of the difference
    - z_thresh = 0.25 is arbitrary, unjustified, and applied to session-z units whose scale depends on session length
    - no statistical test at all — a hard threshold produces three subpopulations with no null

#### 6.8 Section 14: spatial profile of population skewness (hierarchical)
`Striatum project/SpatioTemporalActivityEvolution.m` lines 1104-1245 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary; needs a cluster-based permutation test across bins and a per-mouse unit floor well above 5 before any bin-specific claim*

- **Question.** Does the population activity distribution become more sparse/heavy-tailed at particular corridor locations as learning proceeds?
- **Method.** Per mouse, per area (min_units = 5 units per mouse per area), per epoch: tuning_curves = mean over the epoch's trials -> [units x 50 bins]; then per bin b, skewness(r, 0) (flag 0 = BIAS-CORRECTED sample skewness) of the population vector across that mouse's units, gated on var(r) > 1e-6. Stored as [14 mice x 4 epochs x 50 bins]; plotted as mean across mice with SEM = std/sqrt(sum(~isnan)) per bin, one shaded band per epoch, 5 area panels, y-axes linked, zone patches.
- **Inputs.** tensor_full_z, lbls_full (mouse, area)
- **Outputs.** _<Group>__Spatial_Skewness_Profile_Hierarchical.svg (Task only on disk, 2026-05-24 23:02)
- **Statistics.** none. 200 bin x epoch cells per area are displayed with a SEM band and no test, no cluster correction, no null
- **Inferential unit.** mice (correct hierarchy: N = 12 DMS, 9 DLS, 13 ACC, 3 V1, 2 CA1 — verified against the saved SVG titles)
- **Soundness.** The hierarchy is right (skewness computed within animal, averaged across animals) — this is the best-designed statistic in the file. But the SEM band IS being used as the significance test: any bin where two epochs' bands separate reads as an effect, across 50 bins x 4 epochs x 5 areas with no correction and no cluster-based inference. Second problem: bias-corrected skewness on n as low as 5 units (min_units = 5) has enormous variance and is not even approximately unbiased at that n; V1 rests on 3 mice and CA1 on 2, so 'SEM across mice' with N=2 is not an error bar in any useful sense. Third: because z is whole-session, the per-bin population distribution is already centred per unit, which shapes the skewness in ways that are not independent of the epoch structure.
- **Concerns.**
    - SEM patch used as a de facto significance test over 50 bins x 4 epochs x 5 areas
    - bias-corrected skewness with as few as 5 units per mouse
    - CA1 N=2 mice, V1 N=3 mice
    - mouse_skewness matrix never saved — the numbers behind the figure cannot be recovered without a rerun

Separately, the 5-trial moving average straddles the slot-10/11 stitch (session-early vs pre-LP), blending non-contiguous session trials at trials 8-12, and it induces autocorrelation that the SEM band ignores.

    - two sections both numbered '%% 15.' with different definitions of the same quantity

#### 6.13 KS panel annotation layer (annotate_ks_panels_fdr.m)
`Striatum project/annotate_ks_panels_fdr.m` lines 21-40 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** Stamp D, raw p, and BH-adjusted p on each KS panel of a tiled row.
- **Method.** Family = only the panels with ks_did true; p_adj(ks_did) = fdr_correct(p_raw(ks_did), q, 'bh') with q defaulting to 0.05 (no caller ever passes q). Stars are cascading ifs on p_adj: '*' < 0.05, '**' < 0.01, '***' < 0.001. Text drawn at normalized (0.05, 0.95) showing 'D=%.2f, p=%.1e, p_FDR=%.1e' plus stars.
- **Inputs.** axis handles, p_raw, ks_stat, ks_did, label, q
- **Outputs.** p_adj returned but discarded by all four call sites (lines 1654, 1752, 1919, 2020) — no p-value table is ever written
- **Statistics.** BH-FDR at q = 0.05 within one figure row (2-5 tests)
- **Inferential unit.** panels (areas) within one cell-type row
- **Soundness.** The centralisation is correct and the raw p is shown alongside the adjusted one, which is good practice. Two limitations: the correction family is deliberately narrow — one row of at most 5 panels — while the script fires 128 KS tests overall (48 in 16a + 80 in 16b), so the correction does not cover the comparison structure actually being interpreted (cell types and the epoch-vs-trial contrast are treated as separate experiments without justification). And it silently inherits the fdr_correct cummax bug, so the numbers it prints are wrong. NOTES.md's description of '24-cell KS-test grids' overstates the family size: the actual families are 2-5 tests.
- **Concerns.**
    - FDR family is one row (2-5 tests) out of 128 KS tests in the script
    - inherits the fdr_correct monotonicity bug
    - returned p_adj discarded at all four call sites, so corrected p-values exist only as pixels in an SVG

## 7. MATLAB canonical correlation analysis

*Full domain label:* MATLAB canonical correlation analysis (inter-area communication): DMS/DLS/ACC/V1/CA1/DG spatial CCA, v2 (in-sample + bolt-on held-out, precession index) and v3 (H&H-adapted residual CCA with CV + shuffle null + IFI), plus the shared helpers held_out_canoncorr / loo_ridge_press / batch_triu_corr_mean and the superseded legacy/striatum_cca.m.

**Position in pipeline.** Consumes: processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat (cfg.task_data_file, written by OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m -> ProcessStriatumTask.m; per-animal struct with spatial_binned_fr_all = n_units x n_bins x n_trials, is_dms/is_dls/is_acc/is_v1/is_ca1/is_dg logical masks, zscored_lick_errors, change_point_mean), filtered by filterDataByArea.m and gated by processTaskData.m (learning-point detection; animals without an LP are DROPPED, so is_learner is always all-true downstream). Produces: CCA_Results/Striatum_CCA_Results_<date>.mat (v2; on disk: Striatum_CCA_Results_2026_05_14.mat, 15 pairs x 14 animals, 50 bins) and CCA_Results/Striatum_CCA_v3_<date>.mat (v3; on disk: Striatum_CCA_v3_2026_05_15.mat, cfg.n_position_bins = 50, cfg.bin_size_cm = 5), plus SVG figures in CCA_Results/ (Epoch_Corr_Bars_Split, Epoch_Precession_Bars_Split, Combined_CC_<cc>_Learners, Combined_Prec_<cc>_Learners, Network_Filtered_CC<cc>_Learners, StriatumCCAv3_*). Consumed downstream by: nothing in MATLAB -- no script reads either .mat; the only consumer is CCA_striatum_spatial_v3_plot.m (reads Striatum_CCA_v3_*.mat) and v2's own load-and-replot branch. Superseded by the Python package Striatum project/cca/src/striatum_cca/ (config.py, dataio.py, core.py, pipeline.py, analysis.py, lagged.py, subspace.py, surrogate.py, epoch_stats.py, partial.py, crosspair.py, aggregate.py, sweep.py), which per NOTES.md lines 189 and 409 and ResearchVault Methods/CCA_HH_Adapted.md section 6 is the implementation target; MATLAB CCA_striatum_spatial_v3.m is explicitly legacy-sequestered ("do not extend"). legacy/striatum_cca.m is the first-generation version, superseded by v2 (NOTES.md line 250).

**Data flow, shapes and units.** Per animal: spatial_binned_fr_all = (n_units x n_bins x n_trials) spatial-binned firing rate. Unit inclusion upstream at fr_threshold = 0.02 Hz; per-area floor cfg.min_units = 5 units. CURRENT cfg (project_cfg.m, repointed 2026-05-24): bin_size_au = 2, au_to_cm = 1.25 -> bin_size_cm = 2.5, n_bins_full = 100, max_bin = 60, visual_bin = 40, reward_bin = 50, corridor 250 cm. BOTH SAVED CCA CACHES ARE ON THE OLD GRID: v2 cache all_bins_corr cells are 3 x 50 (50 bins), v3 cache cfg.n_position_bins = 50 and cfg.bin_size_cm = 5. Trials truncated at change_point_mean (disengagement) in v2 and v3. Learning point: first trial t with zscored_lick_error(t) <= -2 AND movsum over [t, t+9] of (z <= -2) >= 7 (cfg.lp_z_threshold = -2, lp_window = 10, lp_min_consecutive = 7); rule itself changed 2026-05-24, after both caches were written. 14 animals with an LP (analysis_lp = [22 43 29 54 54 35 33 16 43 65 84 21 37 25]); is_learner all true; group_results cells filled for 13 (animal 14 empty) and 4 animals empty for DMS-DLS. v2 epochs: early 1:10, pre lp-10:lp-1, post lp:lp+9, gated on lp > 10 and lp+9 <= num_trials. v3 epochs: naive 1:10, pre lp-9:lp, post lp+1:lp+10, gated on n_trials >= 30, lp >= 10, lp+10 <= n_trials (LP trial sits in POST for v2 but in PRE for v3). v2 CCA sample matrices: trial-wise 7 trials x up to 50 valid bins ~ 350 rows (700 under 100-bin cfg) x (nc1, nc2) PC columns, nc = first cumulative-variance index >= 70%, floored at 3; bin-wise 7 bins x valid trials ~ 300-450 rows. v2 held-out split: floor(n/2) train / rest test, row-wise. v2 lag axis: +/-2 bins = +/-10 cm on the cached 5 cm grid, +/-5 cm under current cfg. v3: 10 trials x 50 bins = 500 rows per fit, k = min(min(n_units_x, n_units_y), floor(500/50) = 10, 30) so k <= 10 per side, samples_per_var = 500/(2k) = 25; residualised by subtracting the 10-trial mean PSTH per (bin, unit); 5-fold CV, 50 trial-block shuffles; lags 1-3 bins = 5/10/15 cm on the cached grid.

**Cross-cutting notes.** 1) STALE CACHES ARE THE HEADLINE RISK. Every CCA figure on disk predates two code changes: the 2026-05-24 repoint of cfg.task_data_file to preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat (2.5 cm / 100 bins; caches are 5 cm / 50 bins, verified from the .mat shapes and the saved cfg) and the 2026-05-24 learning-point redefinition in processTaskData.m (first sub-threshold trial rather than window start; the cached analysis_lp values use the old rule). v2 makes this worse by loading the newest Striatum_CCA_Results_*.mat unconditionally and never comparing saved_config with current_config, so a rerun silently replots the old data.
2) IN-SAMPLE vs HELD-OUT. v2's figures are 100% in-sample; the held-out fields exist in the .mat (all_bins_corr_held, trial_corr_*_held and their shuffle twins) and are never plotted or tested. v3 plots cc_cv (out-of-fold) as primary, which is the right choice, but its lagged IFI, projection IFI and principal angles are all in-sample. NOTES.md line 290 ("No held-out CCA ... all in-sample") is now half-stale: the values exist, they are just unused.
3) CV BLOCKING. Both v2 (held_out_canoncorr) and v3 (v5_cca_fit_cv) split over ROWS of a (bin x trial) matrix, so bins from the same trial appear in both train and test. For v3, where residualisation makes the per-trial fluctuation the signal, this means cc_cv is optimistically biased as a generalisation estimate; the sign of cc_excess survives because the null breaks the X-Y trial pairing, but the magnitude should not be quoted as out-of-sample. A trial-blocked CV is the fix and does not exist in either path.
4) LEARNER/NON-LEARNER IS DEAD CODE. processTaskData drops animals without an LP, so is_learner is all-true (confirmed in both .mat files). v2's mean-LP yoking never fires, its Non-Learners figure branch is unreachable, and the anovan LearnerGroup / Epoch x Group terms are fitted on a single-level factor. Any sentence contrasting learners with non-learners cannot be supported by this code as written.
5) STATISTICS. v2: anovan on stacked epochs with no subject term (pseudoreplication of the repeated factor, mis-labelled 'rmANOVA'), plus ~70 uncorrected paired/one-sample t-tests driving figure stars and network edges. v3: no statistical test at all, only a per-cell mean+3sd shuffle criterion. Neither uses the BH-FDR machinery (fdr_correct.m) that the KS panels in this repo already use.
6) NULLS. v2's 25 shuffles use randperm inside parfor with no rng seeding -> not reproducible (NOTES.md item 16 requested this fix; not done), and only the shuffle MEAN is stored so no per-cell z or p can be recovered. v2's precession null bin-permutes one area, which destroys all spatial alignment rather than only the lead-lag asymmetry -- it is not a directionality null. v3's null is properly seeded (shuffle_seed = 0) and permutes trial blocks of Y only, but covers cc_cv only: neither IFI has any null.
7) RUNNABILITY. CCA_striatum_spatial_v3.m calls eight v5_* primitives (v5_residualise, v5_pca_reduce, v5_cca_fit, v5_cca_fit_cv, v5_shuffle_null, v5_lagged_refit_ifi, v5_project, v5_projection_ifi, v5_principal_angles) and NONE exist under StriatumACC; they live in /Users/theoamvr/Desktop/Experiments/TomLearning/HC_V1_Code/, whose headers assert a byte-identical mirror in 'Striatum project/' that is absent. The script only does addpath(pwd). So v3 as committed cannot reproduce its own .mat without the sibling repo on the MATLAB path, and there is no way to verify the primitives have not drifted.
8) NO TESTS. There is no tests/ directory and no run_v5_tests.m anywhere in this repo (contrary to the project CLAUDE.md orientation note), so held_out_canoncorr, loo_ridge_press, batch_triu_corr_mean and both CCA drivers are entirely untested here.
9) SUPERSESSION. NOTES.md lines 189/409 are explicit: CCA work belongs in the Python striatum_cca package (Striatum project/cca/src/striatum_cca/) per ResearchVault Methods/CCA_HH_Adapted.md section 6, and MATLAB v3 is legacy-sequestered ("do not extend"). The Python pipeline header confirms it fixed the v3 principal-angle defect by doing cross-epoch subspace comparison in neuron space. For the manuscript: v3 is provenance, v2 is either regenerated-with-held-out-scoring or demoted to a spatial-tuning-similarity supplement, legacy/striatum_cca.m is dropped.
10) FIGURE CONVENTION. Both drivers emit SVG only (v2 via print -dsvg with a PNG fallback on error, v3_plot via saveas), so the repo-wide "SVG + <=1600 px PNG pair" rule is not met for any CCA figure.
11) A separate gate applies to LFP-derived CCA (NOTES.md 2026-07-12): LFP voltage provenance is unresolved and "downstream learning/position/CCA analyses are therefore gated" -- that concerns the lfp/ package, not these spike-based scripts, but it should not be conflated with them in the manuscript.

**Scientifically load-bearing constants.**

- CCA_striatum_spatial_v2.m:33-34 pca_selection_method='variance', pca_variance_threshold=70 (cumulative % explained)

### Analyses (19)

#### 7.1 v2 epoch statistics (mis-named rmANOVA + real-vs-shuffle t-tests)
`Striatum project/CCA_striatum_spatial_v2.m` lines 431-473 (drivers), 611-726 (plot_grouped_bars_with_rmanova), 728-780 (plot_real_shuff_bars_with_stats), 539-554 (network p-values) · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *must be redone before any epoch/learning claim ships: mixed model or within-subject ANOVA with an animal term, BH-FDR across pairs x CCs, and either real non-learners (i.e. do not drop them upstream) or removal of the learner factor entirely.*

- **Question.** Does inter-area CC1 / precession change with learning, and does it differ between learners and non-learners?
- **Method.** Per-animal epoch value = mean over the 10 trials of the epoch of CC(cc) (extract_animal_means). Test 1 (labelled rmANOVA): Y = [early; pre; post] stacked, anovan(Y, {G_epoch(3 levels), G_group(is_learner)}, 'model','interaction') -- a BETWEEN-subjects two-way ANOVA with each animal contributing three independent rows and no subject term. multcompare post-hoc on Dimension [1 2] if interaction p<0.05 else Dimension 1. Test 2: paired ttest(real, shuffle) for naive and for expert, gated at n>2, star at p<0.05; paired ttest(expert, naive) printed as 'Naive vs Expert'. Test 3 (precession only): ttest(x, 0) per epoch per group, star at p<0.05. Network edges kept only if p_cc < 0.05 and starred if p_ifi < 0.05.
- **Statistics.** anovan (fixed-effects, no repeated-measures term), paired t-tests, one-sample t-tests. No multiple-comparison correction anywhere: 6 pairs x 3 CCs x {naive, expert} x {CC, precession} ~ 72 t-tests plus 6 ANOVAs per metric, all thresholded at 0.05 raw. Elsewhere in this repo the KS grids do use BH-FDR (fdr_correct.m) -- CCA does not.
- **Inferential unit.** animal, but the ANOVA treats the three epochs of one animal as three independent animals -> pseudoreplication of the repeated factor (inflates df from ~13 to ~39).
- **Soundness.** Two structural defects. (1) The function is named ...rmANOVA and prints an ANOVA table, but there is no subject factor and no within-subject error term: it is a between-subjects model on repeated measures, so the Epoch main effect and its post-hoc are anticonservative. (2) The LearnerGroup factor is degenerate: processTaskData DROPS every animal without a learning point (processTaskData.m:43-47), so learning_points_task is never empty, is_learner is all-true (confirmed: is_learner = ones(1,14) in the saved .mat) and mean_lp yoking never fires. The Group and Epoch x Group terms are therefore estimated on a single-level factor, the 'Non-Learners' figure branch is unreachable (sum(mask)==0 -> continue), and any printed Group/interaction p-value is not interpretable. Add uncorrected mass testing and the significance stars on the figures are not trustworthy as they stand.
- **Concerns.**
    - pseudoreplication: repeated epochs treated as independent rows in anovan
    - LearnerGroup factor has a single level because non-learners are dropped upstream -> group/interaction terms meaningless, non-learner panels dead
    - no multiple-comparison correction across 6 pairs x 3 CCs x 2 epochs x 2 metrics
    - significance stars drive which network edges/arrows are drawn

The script then globs CCA_Results/Striatum_CCA_Results_*.mat, takes the newest by datenum, loads group_results/is_learner/analysis_lp (+ saved_config if present) and SKIPS the entire compute block. saved_config is never compared with current_config. pair_name is re-stamped for the first 6 entries after load.

- **Soundness.** Silent staleness. Any parameter edit (n_shuffles, variance threshold, max_shift_bins, pair list) has no effect while any dated .mat exists in CCA_Results/, and nothing warns. So the cached analysis_lp values, epoch boundaries, bin-lag physical units and landmark indices all predate current code. Re-running today reproduces the old figures rather than the current pipeline. Also: the cache holds 15 pairs (cfg.area_pairs order) while the script loops over 6, so CA1/DG results sit unread in the file.

#### 7.3 v3 principal angles across epoch transitions
`Striatum project/CCA_striatum_spatial_v3.m` lines 179-197 (chaining), v5_principal_angles.m:30-60 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `superseded` · manuscript role: *drop. Any subspace-rotation claim must come from the neuron-space computation in the Python package.*

- **Question.** Does the communication subspace rotate between naive, pre-LP and post-LP?
- **Method.** Within a pair, prev_A/prev_B carry the previous epoch's canonical loading matrices; res.principal_angles_A = v5_principal_angles(prev_A, res.A) (QR-orthonormalise both, SVD of Q1'Q2, angles = acos(clipped singular values), degenerate/non-finite columns dropped, NaN if all dropped). Epoch 1 gets NaN. v3_plot plots the top and mean angle for transitions naive->pre-LP and pre-LP->post-LP against reference lines at 0 and pi/2.
- **Outputs.** principal_angles_A/B in the .mat; StriatumCCAv3_PrincipalAngles_*.svg
- **Statistics.** none (bars of means, no test, no null for 'how much rotation is expected by chance')
- **Inferential unit.** animal x pair x transition
- **Soundness.** Structurally invalid as coded: A is a k x r matrix of coefficients in the PC coordinates of ITS OWN epoch, because fit_one refits v5_pca_reduce separately for every epoch. Comparing subspaces spanned by A columns across epochs therefore compares coordinate vectors expressed in two different (and independently sign-/rotation-determined) bases -- the resulting angle mixes real subspace rotation with PCA basis change. The Python successor states this explicitly and does the cross-epoch comparison in NEURON space instead (cca/src/striatum_cca/pipeline.py header: 'Cross-epoch subspace comparison (D10) is therefore done in neuron space'), which confirms this is a known defect of the MATLAB version. There is also no chance level: with k=10 and r=10, random 10-dim subspaces of a 10-dim ambient space are identical by construction, so the ambient/subspace dimensions must be reported for the numbers to mean anything.
- **Concerns.**
    - A compared across epochs despite per-epoch PCA bases (basis-inconsistent)
    - no sign/permutation alignment of PCs
    - no chance level; r may equal k so angles can be trivially 0
    - known-fixed in the Python port (neuron space)

#### 7.5 v2 trial-wise CCA (sliding 7-trial window, in-sample CC1-3)
`Striatum project/CCA_striatum_spatial_v2.m` lines 13-56 (cfg), 168-221 (PCA), 254-306 (loop) · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary at best in its current form; the headline inter-area/learning claim should come from the residual, cross-validated pipeline (v3 / Python striatum_cca). Usable as a descriptive 'shared spatial-tuning similarity' panel if relabelled.*

- **Question.** How does shared variance between two areas evolve trial-by-trial across learning (naive -> pre-LP -> post-LP)?
- **Method.** Per animal: spatial_binned_fr_all (n_units x n_bins x n_trials) truncated at change_point_mean (TRUNCATE_AT_DISENGAGEMENT=true). Per area, pca() on reshape(area_dat, n_units, [])' i.e. samples = ALL (bin x trial) rows of the WHOLE session pooled; n_comps = first index where cumsum(explained) >= 70 (pca_selection_method='variance', pca_variance_threshold=70), floored at num_ccs_analyze=3, capped at size(scores,2); n_components_reduced=3 is dead (only used if method ~= 'variance'). Pairs: 6 hardcoded {DMS-DLS, DMS-ACC, DLS-ACC, V1-DMS, V1-DLS, V1-ACC} (note: the on-disk cache actually holds 15 pairs = cfg.area_pairs, so CA1/DG pairs exist in the .mat but are never plotted). For each trial t: window win = t + (-3:3) clipped to [1,num_trials]; bins with any NaN in either area dropped; samples = (valid_bins x |win|) rows, i.e. up to 7 trials x 50 bins = 350 rows in the cached run (700 under the current 100-bin cfg); x = PC scores of area1 (nc1 cols), y = area2 (nc2 cols); [~,~,r] = canoncorr(x',y'); first min(3,numel(r)) CCs stored. Rank guard is bins-only: `if sum(valid_bins) < max(nc1,nc2)+5, continue`, i.e. it never checks the actual sample count (bins x trials).
- **Inputs.** processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat (cfg.task_data_file) -> filterDataByArea -> processTaskData
- **Outputs.** group_results(ipair).trial_corr_early/pre/post{ianimal} (3 x 10) in CCA_Results/Striatum_CCA_Results_<date>.mat; figures Epoch_Corr_Bars_Split.svg, Combined_CC_<cc>_Learners.svg
- **Statistics.** none at this level (raw CC per trial index). Group tests happen in the plotting section (separate entry).
- **Inferential unit.** one CC value per (animal, pair, CC, trial-index); trial-index values are NOT independent (adjacent t share 6/7 of their samples). Group-level unit is the animal (n=14 with LP; only 13 have any filled cells).
- **Soundness.** The construct measured is not communication but shared position tuning: no residualisation of the trial-averaged spatial PSTH, so the dominant shared signal in a (bin x trial) sample matrix is that both areas ramp with corridor position. CC1 therefore mostly indexes similarity of spatial tuning, not trial-by-trial cross-area coupling. Compounding: (i) unregularised canoncorr on variance-thresholded PC counts (nc can grow large in rich sessions) with a rank guard that only counts bins -> near-rank-deficient regimes inflate CC1 (already flagged in NOTES.md line 308); (ii) the +/-3-trial window makes the 'trial curve' a smoothed, autocorrelated series and bleeds epochs into each other -- the early epoch (1:10) uses trials up to 13, pre (lp-10:lp-1) uses up to lp+2, post (lp:lp+9) uses down to lp-3, so the pre-vs-post paired contrast shares trials; (iii) PCA fitted on the whole session, so epoch-specific fits inherit a basis that saw all epochs.
- **Concerns.**
    - no residualisation: CC1 dominated by shared position tuning
    - rank guard counts bins only, not samples (line 263)
    - PCA basis fitted on all trials (all epochs) before epoch slicing
    - +/-3-trial window bleeds adjacent epochs into the naive/pre/post contrast
    - trial-index curve points are 6/7 overlapping -> autocorrelated, not independent
    - in-sample canoncorr (upward biased); the held-out twin is computed but never used

#### 7.6 v2 held-out CCA (bolt-on, computed + saved, never used)
`Striatum project/CCA_striatum_spatial_v2.m` lines 235-245, 275-276, 296-297, 331-332, 350-351, 366-367, 387-392 · **🟠 major** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *methods-only unless promoted: if v2 is reported at all, the held-out fields (which already exist on disk) should replace the in-sample ones in the figures.*

- **Question.** Is the trial-wise / bin-wise CC1 an artefact of in-sample fitting?
- **Method.** held_out_canoncorr(x', y', 3, seed) with seed = t for trial-wise and seed = n_bins + b for bin-wise; the same seed (hence the same 50/50 split) is reused for the matched shuffle calls. Results go to fields all_bins_corr_held, all_bins_corr_held_shuff, trial_corr_{early,pre,post}_held(+_shuff). Verified present in CCA_Results/Striatum_CCA_Results_2026_05_14.mat.
- **Outputs.** saved in the .mat, plotted nowhere
- **Statistics.** none - no plot, no test, no comparison against the in-sample values anywhere in the script (grep '_held' stops at line 392).
- **Inferential unit.** same as the in-sample analysis
- **Soundness.** The correct instinct, wired to nothing. Every figure and every printed statistic in v2 uses the in-sample fields; the held-out fields are dead weight in the .mat. Additionally the split is row-wise over (bin x trial) samples, so rows from the same trial appear in both halves -> not a trial-level generalisation estimate; and the PC basis was fitted on all rows including the test half, so held_out_canoncorr's docstring claim 'unbiased by construction' is overstated in this call context.
- **Concerns.**
    - computed and saved but never plotted or tested
    - row-wise 50/50 split leaks trial identity across train/test
    - PCA fitted on all rows before the split

#### 7.7 v2 bin-wise CCA (sliding 7-bin window)
`Striatum project/CCA_striatum_spatial_v2.m` lines 311-360, 363-371 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary spatial-profile panel; not defensible as a localisation claim without a bin-level null and correction.*

- **Question.** Where along the corridor (relative to visual cue and reward zone) is inter-area shared variance strongest?
- **Method.** For each spatial bin b: window win = b + (-3:3) clipped to [1,n_bins]; trials with any NaN in either area dropped; samples = (|win| bins x valid_trials) rows, e.g. 7 x ~60 = ~420; in-sample canoncorr on PC scores as above; guard `if sum(valid_trials) < max(nc1,nc2)+5, continue`. Saved as all_bins_corr{animal} (3 x n_bins) plus the shuffle and held-out twins. Cached shape confirms n_bins = 50.
