- **Statistics.** none; the bin-resolved curves are saved but the summary figures only use the trial-epoch fields. No spatial multiple-comparison control anywhere.
- **Inferential unit.** one CC per (animal, pair, CC, bin); bins overlap 6/7 -> heavily autocorrelated
- **Soundness.** Same no-residualisation and rank-guard problems as the trial-wise version. Within a 7-bin window the shared signal is again position tuning plus trial covariation. Because adjacent bin estimates share 6 of 7 bins, any 'CC1 peaks at the reward zone' claim needs a cluster/permutation treatment that does not exist. Landmark annotation is also unsafe: `landmarks = [cfg.visual_bin, cfg.reward_bin]` (line 45) is computed and then never used, and the current cfg landmarks (40, 50) are 2.5 cm indices while the saved results are on a 50-bin (5 cm) grid.
- **Concerns.**
    - 7-bin overlap -> autocorrelated spatial curve, no cluster correction
    - unused `landmarks` variable; cfg landmark indices (40/50 at 2.5 cm) mismatch the 50-bin cached results
    - no residualisation

#### 7.8 v2 shuffle null (bin-permutation trial-wise / trial-permutation bin-wise)
`Striatum project/CCA_striatum_spatial_v2.m` lines 282-305, 338-359 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only; the null needs reseeding, more shuffles, and per-shuffle retention before any 'above chance' sentence rests on it.*

- **Question.** Is the observed CC above chance?
- **Method.** n_shuffles = 25, inside a parfor. Trial-wise: perm_idx = randperm(n_bins_local) applied to dim 2 of area-1 data only (D1_s = D1_local(:,perm_idx,:)), the same permutation for every trial in the window; area 2 untouched. Bin-wise: perm_idx = randperm(n_tr_local) applied to dim 3 of area 1 only. For each shuffle: in-sample canoncorr, held-out canoncorr with the real fit's seed, and calc_precession on the shuffled tensor. Only the MEAN over the 25 shuffles is retained (mean(...,2,'omitnan')); the SD and the per-shuffle draws are discarded.
- **Statistics.** No permutation p-values are formed. The per-cell shuffle mean is later used as a paired comparison value in an across-animal ttest (see the plotting entry). Because only the mean is stored, no per-(animal,pair,bin/trial) z-score or p-value can be recovered from the saved .mat.
- **Inferential unit.** animal (the per-cell shuffle mean becomes one paired observation)
- **Soundness.** randperm inside parfor with no per-worker seeding and no rng call -> the null is not reproducible run-to-run (NOTES.md item 16 asks for exactly this fix and it has not been made). 25 shuffles is thin even for a mean. The trial-wise null (permuting bin order of one area) destroys cross-area bin alignment while preserving each area's spatial profile, which is the right null for 'shared spatial structure' but is a very weak null for 'communication': it also destroys the trial-level covariation that the analysis claims to measure. Conservative direction is unclear, so 'real > shuffle' cannot be read as evidence for trial-by-trial coupling.
- **Concerns.**
    - unseeded randperm inside parfor -> non-reproducible null
    - n_shuffles = 25, mean-only retention (SD discarded)
    - only area 1 is permuted
    - no permutation p-values at all

#### 7.9 v2 precession index (lagged canoncorr over position bins)
`Striatum project/CCA_striatum_spatial_v2.m` lines 918-955 (calc_precession), 278-280, 334-336, 394-406 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main-figure candidate scientifically, but only after re-estimation (lag-symmetric null, denominator floor tied to the null scale, held-out CCs at each lag). As coded it is supplementary/exploratory.*

- **Question.** Does one area's population activity systematically lead the other along the corridor (directionality of the shared signal)?
- **Method.** shifts = -max_shift_bins:max_shift_bins with max_shift_bins = 2 -> lags {-2,-1,0,+1,+2} (n_shifts = 5). For shift<0: s1 = D1(:,1:end+shift,:), s2 = D2(:,1-shift:end,:) -> D1 at bin b paired with D2 at bin b+|shift| (area 1 leads). For shift>0 the mirror. At each lag, samples are re-flattened over (bins x trials) and an in-sample canoncorr is refit; the curve c_curve is 3 CCs x 5 lags. Index: p_idx(cc) = (neg_val - pos_val)/(neg_val + pos_val) where neg_val = mean of lags {-2,-1} and pos_val = mean of {+1,+2}; zero lag excluded; guard `if (neg_val+pos_val) > 0.001` else NaN. Positive index => area 1 (first name in the pair) leads. Lag unit = 1 spatial bin = 5 cm in the cached run, 2.5 cm under the current cfg (max lag = +/-10 cm vs +/-5 cm).
- **Outputs.** trial_precession_{early,pre,post}_idx / _curve (+ _shuff), all_bins_precession_idx / _curve (+ _shuff); figures Epoch_Precession_Bars_Split.svg, Combined_Prec_<cc>_Learners.svg, Network_Filtered_CC<cc>_Learners.svg
- **Statistics.** Per-lag CCs are in-sample maxima (refit at each lag). Group level: ttest against 0 per epoch per group (uncorrected) plus paired ttest vs the shuffle mean; shuffle index = mean over 25 bin-permuted refits.
- **Inferential unit.** animal for the group test; within an animal the index at trial t reuses the +/-3-trial window (autocorrelated)
- **Soundness.** The idea is genuinely informative, the estimator is fragile. (1) It is a ratio of two in-sample CC maxima, each biased upward and each computed on a slightly different sample count (n_bins - |shift|), so lag-dependent bias partly (not exactly) cancels. (2) The denominator guard 0.001 is far too permissive: when both branches are near chance the index is noise/noise and explodes to +/-1 -- which is exactly the regime of the shuffle control, so the shuffle 'index' distribution is heavy-tailed and its mean over 25 draws is unstable. (3) The shuffle null is the wrong null for directionality: bin-permuting area 1 destroys all spatial alignment rather than only the lead-lag asymmetry (a lag-swap / time-reversal null would be the correct comparison). (4) Only +/-2 bins of lag with no interpolation, so the index is a two-point contrast. (5) Direction is inherited by the network figure's arrowheads, so a noisy sign becomes a drawn arrow.
- **Concerns.**
    - ratio of in-sample CC maxima
    - denominator guard 0.001 admits noise/noise ratios
    - shuffle destroys alignment rather than only asymmetry -> not a directionality null
    - only +/-2 bins of lag; physical lag changed from 5 cm to 2.5 cm per bin when cfg was repointed

#### 7.10 v2 network graph (filtered edges, precession-signed arrows)
`Striatum project/CCA_striatum_spatial_v2.m` lines 484-608 (driver), 798-916 (plot_dual_network) · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *schematic/illustrative only; not a defensible connectivity result. If retained, arrows should be drawn only for p_FDR-significant IFI and edges only for corrected CC significance.*

- **Question.** What is the directed inter-area communication network in naive vs expert, per CC?
- **Method.** Per pair: edge weight = mean over animals of the per-animal epoch CC1 (naive = trial_corr_early, expert = trial_corr_post); edge drawn only if the paired real-vs-shuffle p_cc < 0.05 (uncorrected); arrow direction from sign(mean precession index) (>=0 -> area1 -> area2); arrowed digraph drawn only where p_ifi < 0.05; LineWidth = 1 + 8*(cc/global_max_cc); colour ramps grey->blue with |IFI|/global_max_ifi. Node layout hardcoded for 6 areas (DMS 3,4; DLS 7,4; ACC 5,7; V1 5,1; CA1 9,5.5; DG 9,2.5).
- **Outputs.** CCA_Results/Network_Filtered_CC{1,2,3}_Learners.svg (2026-05-14)
- **Statistics.** inherits the uncorrected paired t-tests above; no network-level statistics (no correction for 6-15 edges, no permutation over the graph).
- **Inferential unit.** pair-level mean over animals
- **Soundness.** Purely a rendering of the two statistics above, so it inherits all their problems and adds a presentation risk: a non-significant precession sign still sets the arrow direction of every drawn edge (only the asterisk depends on p_ifi), so the figure asserts directionality that the statistics do not support. Edge presence is thresholded at raw p<0.05 across 6 edges.
- **Concerns.**
    - arrow direction drawn regardless of IFI significance
    - edge threshold uncorrected
    - layout/graph includes CA1/DG nodes but v2 only analyses 6 of the 15 pairs

#### 7.11 v3 per-(animal x pair x epoch) residual CCA with 5-fold CV
`Striatum project/CCA_striatum_spatial_v3.m` lines 27-92 (cfg), 136-206 (loop), 217-273 (tensor), 276-284 (epochs), 287-309 (choose_k), 312-371 (fit_one) · **🟠 major** · status: `superseded` · manuscript role: *methods/provenance only. NOTES.md (lines 189, 409) declares v3 the retired v5 instantiation, sequestered per ResearchVault Methods/CCA_HH_Adapted.md section 6; the live implementation is the Python striatum_cca package. Any figure from it is a preliminary that the Python pipeline must reproduce.*

- **Question.** How much cross-area shared variance (residual, trial-to-trial) exists in each of naive / pre-LP / post-LP, for all 15 area pairs?
- **Method.** One fit per (animal x pair x epoch). Tensor: spatial_binned_fr_all truncated at change_point_mean, first cfg.n_position_bins bins kept (spatial_truncate_at_max_bin=false -> n_position_bins = cfg.n_bins_full), permuted to (trials x bins x units), per-area masks is_<area> with >= cfg.min_units_per_region = 5 units. Epochs (n_trials_per_epoch = 10), gated by n_trials >= 30, lp >= 10, lp+10 <= n_trials: naive = 1:10, pre_lp = (lp-9):lp, post_lp = (lp+1):(lp+10) -- note this puts the LP trial in PRE, whereas v2 puts it in POST. Stage 2: v5_residualise(S, ones(n_trials,1)) -> subtracts the 10-trial mean PSTH per (bin, unit); with a single condition label this is pure PSTH removal. Stage 3: v5_pca_reduce per epoch (SVD, svd_flip sign convention), k identical for X and Y. k rule (k_mode='samples'): k = max(1, min([min(n_units_x,n_units_y), floor(n_samples_smallest/50), 30])) where n_samples_smallest = 10 * n_position_bins, computed from the SMALLEST epoch and held fixed across the three epochs; the 'variance' branch (k_variance_target = 0.80) is present but not selected. In the saved run (n_position_bins = 50) that gives floor(500/50) = 10, so k <= 10 and samples_per_var = 500/(2*10) = 25. Stage 4: flatten to (trials*bins x k) with bins fastest, then v5_cca_fit_cv(X, Y, cv_splits=5, shuffle=true, cca_fold_seed=0): full-sample QR+SVD fit for (A, B, cc) plus 5-fold CV where each fold refits on the training rows, projects the test rows through the fold's (A,B) after subtracting the fold's means, and Pearson-correlates the paired variates; cc_cv = mean over folds (negatives kept; zero-variance folds set to 0).
- **Inputs.** processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat via filterDataByArea + processTaskData (non-learners dropped -> is_learner all true)
- **Outputs.** CCA_Results/Striatum_CCA_v3_<date>.mat (group_results.per_epoch(n_animals x 3) with A, B, cc_full, cc_cv, cc_cv_per_fold, cc_excess, null_*, ifi_*, k_used, var_x/y_at_k, n_samples, samples_per_var, principal_angles_*); saved run is Striatum_CCA_v3_2026_05_15.mat (15 pairs, 14 animals, cfg.n_position_bins = 50, cfg.bin_size_cm = 5)
- **Statistics.** cc_cv (out-of-fold, primary), cc_full (in-sample, retained), cc_excess = cc_cv(1) - null.mean, null threshold = mean + 3*sd of 50 shuffles. NO group-level statistical test anywhere in v3 or v3_plot -- no t-test, no ANOVA, no correction, no p-values.
- **Inferential unit.** one fit per (animal, pair, epoch); group unit = animal (14). Rows within a fit are (bin x trial) samples, not independent.
- **Soundness.** Much better constructed than v2: residualisation removes the position-tuning confound so cc_cv indexes trial-to-trial cross-area covariation; k is fixed across epochs within a pair (so the epoch contrast is not confounded by dimensionality); CV folds are seeded (cca_fold_seed = 0) and the null reuses the identical CV protocol. Remaining structural issues: (1) CV folds are random over ROWS, so other bins of a test trial sit in the training set -- with residualised data the shared signal is precisely the per-trial fluctuation, so cc_cv is optimistically biased relative to a trial-blocked CV (the sign of cc_excess survives because the null breaks the X-Y trial pairing, but the magnitude is not a generalisation estimate); (2) residualising within a 10-trial epoch removes 1/10 of the variance and imposes a sum-to-zero constraint across those 10 trials; (3) the k rule pins samples-per-variable at ~25 by construction (k = n_samples/50 => n_samples/(2k) = 25), i.e. permanently half the H&H stability threshold of 50 that the diagnostics panel draws -- the diagnostic can never be satisfied; (4) not runnable in this repo: v3 calls v5_residualise, v5_pca_reduce, v5_cca_fit(_cv), v5_shuffle_null, v5_lagged_refit_ifi, v5_project, v5_projection_ifi, v5_principal_angles and NONE of these files exist under StriatumACC (they live in /Users/theoamvr/Desktop/Experiments/TomLearning/HC_V1_Code/, whose own headers claim a byte-identical mirror in 'Striatum project/' that is absent), while the script only does addpath(pwd); (5) latent bug at line 144: the catch block formats mouse_id, which is commented out at line 137 and therefore undefined.
- **Concerns.**
    - v5_* primitives absent from this repo -> script cannot run without the TomLearning path; cross-repo hidden dependency
    - row-wise CV folds leak trial identity
    - k rule fixes samples/var at ~25, half the stated H&H threshold
    - no statistical test of any kind at group level
    - epoch definition off-by-one vs v2 (LP trial in pre here, in post there)
    - saved .mat is 50-bin/5 cm, predating the 2026-05-24 repoint to 2.5 cm and the LP-rule fix
    - undefined mouse_id in the failure path (line 144)

#### 7.12 v3 lagged-refit IFI (information-flow index over position lags)
`/Users/theoamvr/Desktop/Experiments/TomLearning/HC_V1_Code/v5_lagged_refit_ifi.m` lines 39-117 (called from CCA_striatum_spatial_v3.m:332-334) · **🟠 major** · status: `superseded` · manuscript role: *supplementary/exploratory; needs its own null before it can carry a directional claim.*

- **Question.** Along the corridor, does area X lead area Y (directionality of the residual shared signal)?
- **Method.** cfg.max_lag_bins = 3, cfg.central_window_bins = 3, cfg.smooth_size = 3, cfg.smooth_sigma = 1.0. Zero lag: one v5_cca_fit on the full flattened PC scores; cc_xy(1) = cc_yx(1) = cc(1). For tau = 1..3: X-leads-Y pairs X(:,1:end-tau,:) with Y(:,tau+1:end,:), reflattened to n_trials*(n_bins-tau) rows, and CCA is REFIT (in-sample, no CV); Y-leads-X is the mirror. Both 4-point curves are Gaussian-smoothed (kernel size 3, sigma 1, reflect padding). cw = min(3,3) = 3, xy_mean = mean(cc_xy_smooth(2:4)), yx_mean likewise; ifi = (xy_mean - yx_mean)/(xy_mean + yx_mean) if the denominator > 1e-15 else 0. Positive => X leads Y. Physical lags = 1..3 bins = 5, 10, 15 cm in the saved run (2.5/5/7.5 cm under the current cfg).
- **Outputs.** res.ifi_lagged, ifi_lagged_curve_{xy,yx}(_smooth) in Striatum_CCA_v3_<date>.mat; figures StriatumCCAv3_IFI_lagged_*.svg, StriatumCCAv3_LaggedCCcurves_*.svg
- **Statistics.** none; ifi is a point estimate per (animal, pair, epoch). No shuffle null for the IFI (the shuffle null is built only for cc_cv), no test, no correction. v3_plot shows bars +/- SEM with per-animal dots.
- **Inferential unit.** animal (one ifi per animal x pair x epoch)
- **Soundness.** Cleaner than v2's precession index (finer lag grid, smoothing, symmetric branches, sane 1e-15 guard) but the same core weakness: every lag CC is an in-sample refit maximum, so the curve is upward-biased and the bias grows as tau removes samples -- symmetric between branches, so it largely cancels in the ratio, but the ratio has no null distribution at all. A directionality claim from it is unsupported until an IFI shuffle (e.g. lag-swap or trial-shuffled) exists.
- **Concerns.**
    - in-sample CC at every lag (no CV)
    - no null distribution for the IFI
    - smoothing across a 4-point curve then averaging 3 of the 4 points
    - sample count shrinks with tau

#### 7.13 v3 projection IFI (per-trial lag-correlation asymmetry)
`/Users/theoamvr/Desktop/Experiments/TomLearning/HC_V1_Code/v5_projection_ifi.m` lines 36-89 (called from CCA_striatum_spatial_v3.m:336-347) · **🟠 major** · status: `superseded` · manuscript role: *supplementary; the pooled-trial histogram must not be used for inference, only the per-animal means.*

- **Question.** Trial by trial, does the leading canonical variate of X precede that of Y?
- **Method.** u = v5_project(P_x_3d, fit_res.x_mean, A(:,1)), v likewise with B(:,1) -- i.e. the FULL-SAMPLE canonical direction of the epoch. Per trial: r(tau) = corr(u_t(1:n-tau), v_t(tau+1:end)) for tau = -3..+3 (cfg.proj_max_lag_bins = 3), lags with fewer than cfg.proj_min_paired_samples = 5 paired points or with std < 1e-15 are left NaN; if ANY of the six non-zero lags is NaN the trial's IFI is skipped. ifi(t) = (sum r(tau>0) - sum r(tau<0)) / (sum|r(tau>0)| + sum|r(tau<0)|), bounded [-1,1], zero lag excluded; denominator guard 1e-15. Positive => u leads v. v3_plot reports mean(ifi_proj_per_trial) per cell and pools all trials for histograms (edges -1:0.1:1).
- **Outputs.** res.ifi_proj_per_trial, ifi_proj_lag_corr; figures StriatumCCAv3_IFI_proj_*.svg, StriatumCCAv3_IFI_proj_distributions_*.svg
- **Statistics.** none. The pooled histogram in v3_plot mixes all trials from all animals.
- **Inferential unit.** trial for the histogram (pooled across animals -> pseudoreplication in that panel), animal for the bar panel
- **Soundness.** Reasonable per-trial descriptor, two flags: (1) the canonical directions come from the full-sample fit of the same epoch, so the per-trial lag correlations are measured on the very trials that defined the projection -- in-sample; (2) the distribution panel (plot_ifi_proj_distributions) pools per-trial values across animals with no animal weighting, which is textbook pseudoreplication if used to claim a non-zero group mean. With 50 bins and 3 lags the per-trial correlations use 47-50 points, so per-trial noise is moderate but the trial-level n (10 per epoch) is what matters for inference.
- **Concerns.**
    - projection weights fitted in-sample on the same epoch
    - trials pooled across animals in the distribution figure (pseudoreplication)
    - no null, no test

#### 7.14 held_out_canoncorr (cross-validated CC helper)
`Striatum project/held_out_canoncorr.m` lines 1-86 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods; would need a trial-blocked / repeated-split variant to support a generalisation claim.*

- **Question.** What is the out-of-sample canonical correlation for a given (X, Y) sample matrix?
- **Method.** Guard: if n < 2*(max(p1,p2)+2) return NaN(1,num_ccs). Split: rng_state = rng(); rng(seed,'twister'); perm = randperm(n); rng(rng_state) (caller RNG restored); train = perm(1:floor(n/2)), test = perm(floor(n/2)+1:end) -> single 50/50 split, deterministic in `seed` (default 0). canoncorr on the TRAIN half only -> (A,B,r_train_full); keep n_keep = min(min(size(A,2),size(B,2)), num_ccs) columns; U_test = X_test*A, V_test = Y_test*B; r_test(k) = corrcoef(U_test(:,k),V_test(:,k)) when both stds > 0, else NaN. Returns [r_test, r_train, A, B]; r_test can be negative and is NOT re-sorted (kept in train-fold canonical order). Callers in v2 pass seed = t (trial-wise) and seed = n_bins + b (bin-wise), and reuse the identical seed for the matched shuffle call, so real and shuffled share the split exactly.
- **Statistics.** no test; returns held-out r (r_test) and in-sample r (r_train) side by side
- **Inferential unit.** rows of X/Y as supplied by the caller = (bin x trial) samples, NOT trials
- **Soundness.** Mechanics are correct (fit on train, project test, correlate; caller RNG preserved; single split, so seeded and reproducible unlike the shuffle loop). Three caveats for the manuscript: (1) 'unbiased by construction' holds only w.r.t. the CCA fit -- in the v2 call path the PC basis was fitted on all rows including the test half, so a residual optimistic bias remains; (2) the split is row-wise, and rows are (bin, trial) pairs, so the same trial contributes to both halves -- there is no trial-blocked option; (3) a single 50/50 split (no repeats, no k-fold) gives a high-variance estimate, and because the seed is a function of t or b only, the same split pattern is reused across animals and pairs.
- **Concerns.**
    - row-wise split leaks trial identity
    - docstring overstates unbiasedness given upstream PCA on all rows
    - single split, high variance; seed shared across animals/pairs
    - no MATLAB tests exist in this repo for it

#### 7.15 v3 trial-shuffle null and cc_excess
`/Users/theoamvr/Desktop/Experiments/TomLearning/HC_V1_Code/v5_shuffle_null.m` lines 42-106 (called from CCA_striatum_spatial_v3.m:329-330) · **🟡 minor** · status: `superseded` · manuscript role: *main-figure supporting statistic if v3 were the reported pipeline; as it stands, methods/provenance for the Python port.*

- **Question.** Is the cross-validated CC1 above what independent trials would give?
- **Method.** cfg.n_shuffles = 50, seed = cfg.shuffle_seed = 0 (rng(seed,'twister') once, then 50 successive randperm draws; caller RNG restored via onCleanup). Permutation unit = TRIAL BLOCK of Y only: samples_per_trial = n_pos_bins, block_idx = (perm-1)*spt + (1:spt), so within-trial bin order is preserved and X is untouched. Each shuffle is refit through the identical v5_cca_fit_cv(X, Y_shuf, 5, true, fold_seed=0). Outputs: cc_cv (50 x r), cc1_null (50 x 1), mean, threshold = mean(cc1_null) + 3*sd(cc1_null) (sd with ddof=1). v3 stores null_mean, null_threshold, null_cc1 and cc_excess = cc_cv(1) - null_mean.
- **Statistics.** Parametric 3-sigma criterion on 50 shuffles (not a percentile, so no 1/(n+1) p-floor, but it assumes an approximately normal null). No p-values are computed; no correction across 15 pairs x 3 epochs x 14 animals; the criterion is applied per (animal, pair, epoch) cell and then only eyeballed in the scatter plot.
- **Inferential unit.** trial (the permuted unit) within an animal; the 3-sigma decision is per cell, so 630 implicit tests with no correction
- **Soundness.** Correct and well-constructed null: it destroys the X-Y trial correspondence while preserving each area's within-trial spatial profile, it is properly seeded and reproducible, and it reuses the exact CV protocol of the real fit so the row-wise-CV bias is present in both. Weaknesses: only 10 trials per epoch means just 10! orderings are available but more importantly a 10-element permutation with n=10 trials gives a coarse null; mean+3sd substitutes normality for a percentile; and cc_excess (a difference of two CV estimates) is reported per animal but never tested at group level.
- **Concerns.**
    - 3-sigma threshold assumes normal null; no p-values
    - no correction across the 630 (animal x pair x epoch) cells
    - only 10 trials per epoch to permute
    - cc_excess never tested at group level

#### 7.16 v3 k-selection and rank/conditioning diagnostics
`Striatum project/CCA_striatum_spatial_v3.m` lines 287-309 (choose_k), 366-369 (var_x/y_at_k, samples_per_var); CCA_striatum_spatial_v3_plot.m:330-371 · **🟡 minor** · status: `superseded` · manuscript role: *supplementary methods panel; state plainly that samples/var ~ 25 by construction.*

- **Question.** Is each CCA fit adequately sampled and well conditioned?
- **Method.** k reported per fit (k_used), samples_per_var = n_samples/(2k), var_x_at_k = sum of the retained explained-variance ratios. Diagnostic figure: histogram of k; histogram of samples/var with reference lines at 50 ('H&H stability threshold') and 25 ('below 25 = sample-limited'); scatter of variance explained vs k per side. Conditioning is only guarded inside v5_cca_fit (warning if cond(Rx) or cond(Ry) > 1e10; pinv instead of mldivide for the loading solve; cc clamped to [0,1]).
- **Outputs.** StriatumCCAv3_Diagnostics_*.svg
- **Statistics.** descriptive only
- **Inferential unit.** fit (animal x pair x epoch)
- **Soundness.** Good practice to save and plot these, but the diagnostic is self-defeating: because k_mode='samples' sets k = floor(n_samples/50), samples_per_var is algebraically pinned near 25 for every fit, so the 50-line can never be met and the 25-line is always straddled. The honest reading of the saved run is that every fit sits at the sample-limited boundary (10 trials x 50 bins = 500 rows, k <= 10 per side). The cond > 1e10 warning plus pinv means ill-conditioned fits degrade quietly to small loadings rather than erroring, which is safer numerically but means rank problems are not recorded in the output struct (no cond number is saved).
- **Concerns.**
    - samples/var pinned at ~25 by the k rule -> threshold unreachable
    - conditioning warnings not persisted to the results struct

#### 7.18 loo_ridge_press (closed-form LOO ridge; decoder helper, not CCA)
`Striatum project/loo_ridge_press.m` lines 1-100 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods (decoding sections); the standardisation leak should be stated with its ~0.3-0.5% magnitude rather than left implicit.*

- **Question.** What is the leave-one-out prediction of a ridge model without refitting n times?
- **Method.** Drops rows with NaN in y or any X column BEFORE fitting (no NaN imputation, so no fill-before-split leakage); returns early if n < 3 or m == 0. Standardize (default true): mu_X = mean(Xv,1), sig_X = std(Xv,0,1) with zeros mapped to 1, applied to all valid rows. Intercept (default true): a leading ones column is appended AFTER standardisation and is left unpenalised via L = diag([0; lambda*ones(m,1)]); without an intercept L = lambda*eye(m). Solve: A = X'X + L, A_inv = A\eye, beta = A_inv*X'y, y_hat = X*beta. Hat diagonal computed as h_ii = sum((Xv*A_inv).*Xv, 2) (vectorised, no n x n matrix), clamped to [0, 1-1e-12]. PRESS identity used: y_loo = (y_hat - h.*y)./(1 - h), which is algebraically the textbook form (equivalently y_hat + h/(1-h)*(y_hat - y)); both forms in the comment are correct and equivalent. Second output beta is the AUGMENTED, STANDARDISED coefficient vector despite the comment at lines 96-97 implying re-expression in original units. Callers: Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding.m:126,138 and CrossSpatialBinDecoding.m:99,136 with cfg.ridge_lambda = 1.0; IntegratedAll_v1.m:888 with a local lambda.
- **Statistics.** n/a (produces LOO predictions consumed by the decoding scripts)
- **Inferential unit.** observation/row as supplied by the caller
- **Soundness.** PRESS identity correct for a fixed lambda and a fixed standardisation. The documented leak: the z-scoring uses full-sample mu/sigma rather than per-fold statistics, so the 'held-out' row contributed to its own scaler; the docstring calls this an O(1/n) correction 'well below the noise floor' at n = 200-300 trials, and NOTES.md quantifies it as ~0.3-0.5% at n ~ 200-300 and accepts it as documented. Second-order caveats: lambda is applied to standardised features so its effective strength depends on the full-sample sigma (also a full-sample quantity); the intercept is correctly unpenalised and the hat matrix includes it, so the LOO formula is exact for the intercept model; the h clamp silences near-singular rows rather than reporting them; and the stale comment about beta's coordinates could mislead a caller (no current caller uses beta).
- **Concerns.**
    - standardisation fitted on all rows including the held-out one (O(1/n), ~0.3-0.5% at n~200-300)
    - lambda scaled by full-sample sigma
    - beta returned in standardised/augmented coordinates contrary to its comment
    - no tests in this repo

#### 7.19 batch_triu_corr_mean (vectorised trial-pair stability; stability helper, not CCA)
`Striatum project/batch_triu_corr_mean.m` lines 1-48 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods (stability section)*

- **Question.** How similar are a cell's spatial profiles across the trials of a window (representational stability)?
- **Method.** Input (n_cells x bins x w). Returns NaN(n_cells,1) if w < 2 or bins < 2 or n_cells == 0. Z-scores along bins per (cell, trial) with mean/std omitnan, zero sd mapped to 1, then NaN -> 0. Computes per-cell R = pagemtimes(permute(Z,[3 2 1]), permute(Z,[2 3 1]))/(bins-1) (w x w x n_cells), takes the strict upper triangle (triu(...,1)) and returns the mean over pairs; cells whose entire upper triangle is NaN return NaN. Called from IntegratedAll_v1.m:609-610 for stab_z and stab_z_shuff.
- **Statistics.** n/a (descriptive statistic feeding the stability analysis)
- **Inferential unit.** cell (per window), so downstream stability claims are unit-level and nested in animals
- **Soundness.** Correct vectorisation of a mean pairwise Pearson r, with one silent behaviour worth documenting: NaN bins are replaced by 0 AFTER z-scoring, so a partially-NaN trial profile is treated as having mean-valued bins rather than being excluded -- this biases r toward 0 for cells with missing bins instead of dropping the pair (the docstring only claims to match the old per-cell loop for fully-NaN cells). Also the divisor (bins-1) assumes the z-scoring used the same bins for every pair, which holds here. No leakage or circularity. Pseudoreplication risk lives in the caller (cells pooled across animals), not here.
- **Concerns.**
    - NaN->0 after z-scoring biases r toward 0 for partially-missing profiles rather than excluding them
    - no tests in this repo

## 8. MATLAB decoding and information-theoretic analyses

*Full domain label:* MATLAB decoding and information-theoretic analyses (cross-spatial-bin behaviour decoding, Shannon MI, MMI/PID bound, position decoders, cell-type classification, descriptive summaries)

**Position in pipeline.** All of this domain sits at the terminal (figure-producing) end of the chain. Upstream: RawData/<mouse>_raw.mat + <mouse>_V1_raw.mat + <mouse>_neurontype2025.mat + RawData/Neuropixels_V1_Depth_Data.csv -> OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m (assigns areas by depth, applies the MSN/FSN/TAN rules at lines 104-107, writes processed_data/all_data.mat) -> ProcessStriatumTask.m / ProcessStriatumControl.m (fr_threshold_hz = 0.02 gate, spatial binning, change_point_mean, zscored_lick_errors; writes processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat and processed_data/preprocessed_data_control2p5cm.mat). decode_position.m and decode_position_mld.m are the exception: they are called from INSIDE ProcessStriatumTask.m:459/481 and ProcessStriatumControl.m:753/775, so they are part of preprocessing, and decode_position's outputs are written back into preprocessed_data(.decoded_positions, .decoding_options, .decoding_performance) and saved as preprocessed_data.mat (note: NOT preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat - a provenance fork); the decode_position_mld write-back is commented out, so MLD results are plotted and discarded. Downstream consumers of the four analysis scripts: NONE - Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding.m writes processed_data/{ridge,gpr}_epoch_decoding_results.mat, CrossSpatialBinDecoding.m writes processed_data/cross_spatial_decoding_results.mat, MutualInformationStriatum_v2.m writes processed_data/shannon_mi_results.mat plus cross_spatial_mi_results.mat, cross_area_mi_results.mat and pid_shared_info_results.mat at the CWD ROOT (path inconsistency), and nothing in the repository reads any of these files. summary_numbers.m and neurontype_classification.m produce console text and unsaved figures only. Materialised state on disk: ONLY processed_data/cross_spatial_decoding_results.mat (424 MB, 14 May) exists, and it predates processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat (23 May) and the 2026-05-24 repoint of cfg.task_data_file to the 2.5 cm data - every other output of this domain is absent, i.e. the MI v2 and epoch-decoding analyses have never been run to completion since the 2026-05 refactor and the CA1/DG area additions.

**Data flow, shapes and units.** Neural input everywhere is preprocessed_data(ianimal).spatial_binned_fr_all, [n_units x n_spatial_bins x n_trials], spatially binned firing rate in Hz at 2.5 cm/bin, n_spatial_bins = 100 over a 250 cm corridor (project_cfg: bin_size_au = 2, au_to_cm = 1.25, corridor_au = 200, n_bins_full = 100). Landmarks in 2.5 cm bin indices: visual_bin = 40, reward_bin = target_rz_bin = 50. Spatial truncation cfg.max_bin = 60 is applied by Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding (n_bins_actual = min(100, 60) = 60) and by MutualInformationStriatum_v2 (same 60), but NOT by CrossSpatialBinDecoding, which uses all 100 bins (line 44) - so its cross-bin matrices are 100x100 while the epoch decoder's are 60x60 and they are not directly comparable. decode_position_mld consumes z_spatial_binned_fr_all (z-scored, same shape). Behaviour: spatial_binned_data.licks and .durations are [n_trials x n_spatial_bins]; durations == 0 replaced by eps; lick_rate = licks./durations [licks/s]; velocity = (4*1.25)./durations, i.e. a hardcoded 5 cm numerator in all three scripts (Nonlinear:37, CrossSpatial:33, MI v2:52) while cfg.velocity_factor = bin_size_cm = 2.5 - so reported velocity is 2x too large in absolute units (Pearson r is scale-invariant so the decoders are unaffected, but any quoted cm/s is wrong; velocity is never exactly zero, which is what makes the 2-bin zero-aware MI degenerate). Both behaviour matrices are transposed to [bins x trials] inside clean_data. Trials are truncated at n_trials = min(n_trials_raw, change_point_mean) (behavioural disengagement). Epochs are 10 trials each: naive = 1:10, pre-LP = lp-10:lp-1, post-LP = lp+1:lp+10, with cfg.trials_per_epoch = 10; the two decoders use find_learning_points with lp_window = 7 / lp_min_consecutive = 7 and the START-of-window convention, MI v2 uses lp_window = 10 / lp_min_consecutive = 7 and then shifts to the END of the window (lp = lp_start + 9), so the same dataset yields different LPs and therefore different epoch trials between the decoding and MI analyses. Decoder design matrices: X = [n_epoch_trials x n_units] (one spatial bin, so n = 5-10 rows against tens-to-hundreds of unit columns in the epoch decoder; n = full session, typically 150-350 trials, in CrossSpatialBinDecoding). MI sample vectors: 5 pooled spatial bins x n_epoch_trials flattened (>= 40 samples typical), discretised to 2 levels, so the joint table is 2x2 with N ~ 40-50 - exactly the regime where the Miller-Madow term (R_xy - R_x - R_y + 1)/(2N ln2) is a non-trivial fraction of the estimate. MI window grid: 56 windows (pool_win = 5, shift = 1, over 60 bins), centres at win_start + 2, lag ranges mi_max_lag = 15 (neural->behaviour), area_max_lag = 10 (cross-area plotting), pid_max_lag = 10 (MMI). Position decoders flatten to (n_pos_bins * n_trials) samples with target = bin_index * options.bin_size = bin_index * 5, i.e. labelled 'cm' but scaled for the retired 5 cm binning. Areas: 6 (DMS, DLS, ACC, V1, CA1, DG) in project_cfg; MI v2 covers all 6 for single-unit MI but only 6 hand-listed pairs (ACC-DMS, ACC-DLS, DMS-DLS, V1-DMS, V1-DLS, V1-ACC) for cross-area MI/MMI, excluding CA1 and DG; both decoding scripts only populate is_dms/is_dls/is_acc/is_v1 into clean_data and therefore crash on CA1; decode_position/decode_position_mld can only select dms/dls/acc (everything else falls through to 'all units').

**Cross-cutting notes.** TOP FINDINGS, in order of consequence for the manuscript.

1. The 2-bin zero-aware discretiser silently zeroes three of the four MI analyses. discretize_zero_aware puts only |x| < 1e-8 in bin 1 and, with n_bins = 2, everything else in bin 2. Any stream without exact zeros therefore becomes a CONSTANT and its MI is identically 0.000 with no warning: (a) velocity = (4*1.25)./durations is strictly positive, so every velocity MI panel in sections 4-7 is structurally zero; (b) extract_pc1 returns continuous mean-centred PC scores, so the entire cross-area information-flow analysis (sections 8-9) and the MMI/PID bound (sections 10-12) compute matrices of zeros for both behavioural targets. Only single-unit firing rate (genuinely zero-inflated) and lick_rate (zero whenever the animal does not lick in a bin) are non-degenerate. The file's own header comment claims the 2-bin scheme is 'the smallest non-degenerate scheme for sparse signals' - which is true, and is exactly why it must not be applied to dense signals. Nothing downstream detects the degeneracy because no p-values are computed and only the null MEAN (also zero) is overlaid.

2. Both cross-spatial decoding scripts cannot be run against the current configuration. cfg.regions = cfg.areas = 6 areas, but clean_data is populated with only is_dms/is_dls/is_acc/is_v1 (Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding.m:55-58, CrossSpatialBinDecoding.m:49-52) while the region loops index clean_data.(['is_' lower(region)]) for all 6 (lines 87 and 70 respectively) - a non-existent-field error on CA1. Corroborating evidence: no {ridge,gpr}_epoch_decoding_results.mat exists on disk. CrossSpatialBinDecoding only survives because it short-circuits on a cached .mat.

3. Every published number from CrossSpatialBinDecoding rests on a stale cache. Line 56 loads processed_data/cross_spatial_decoding_results.mat whenever it exists, with no parameter fingerprint (MI v2 has check_cache/cache_meta; this script has nothing). The file is dated 14 May; preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat is dated 23 May and cfg.task_data_file was repointed to the 2.5 cm data on 2026-05-24. The cache therefore encodes a different bin width, a different bin count and a pre-CA1/DG region list. Any figure or claim derived from it must be regenerated before it goes into a manuscript.

4. 25 shuffles are computed; single-shuffle nulls are plotted. Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding stores r_shuff_mean, r_shuff_std and empirical_p, but every plotting section (4, 5, 5A, 5B, 5C) forms delta r = r_mat - r_shuff, where r_shuff is the FIRST permutation only (line 154, 'first sample (compat)'). CrossSpatialBinDecoding likewise stores shuff_mean/shuff_std/empirical_p and then plots raw moving_r with no null at all. The 2026-05-07 upgrade from 1 to 25 shuffles is thus invisible in every figure.

5. The permutation nulls are not matched to the statistic they null. In both decoders the shuffle path fits the ridge/GPR on permuted Y but scores the prediction against the UNpermuted Y (Nonlinear:136-142, CrossSpatial:133-146). The real statistic and the null statistic are computed by different procedures, so real - shuffle is not a permutation contrast and the LOO negative bias present in the real r is absent from the null.

6. Empirical p-values have a floor of exactly 0 and are never used. Both decoders compute p = mean(shuffle >= real) with no (count+1)/(n+1) correction, so with 25 shuffles the smallest reportable p is 0 and the resolution is 0.04. CrossSpatialBinDecoding additionally divides by a fixed 25 while NaN comparisons count as false, so cells with an undefined null report p = 0. Neither p-matrix is read by any plot, no FDR is applied anywhere in this domain, and the tested space is large (up to ~1800 lower-triangle cells x 3 epochs x 6 areas x 2 targets for the epoch decoder; 56 x 16 lag cells for the MI lag analysis). Contrast the project convention documented in CLAUDE.md, where KS grids use BH-FDR via fdr_correct.m.

7. Reproducibility is split. MI v2 seeds correctly (rng(cfg.seed) globally plus rng(cfg.seed + ianimal) per parfor worker, so nulls are worker-count independent) but reuses the SAME per-animal seed in all four of its analyses, so the permutation sequences in sections 4, 6, 8 and 10 are identical rather than independent. Both decoders and both position decoders never call rng at all, so their permutation nulls and neuron-subsample bootstraps are irreproducible.

8. Epoch definitions are partly circular, in opposite directions in the two families. With the START-of-window LP used by the decoders (lp_window = 7, lp_min_consecutive = 7), the Post-LP/'Expert' epoch lp+1:lp+10 contains the 7 consecutive criterion trials that DEFINED lp. With MI v2's END-of-window LP (lp = lp_start + 9), the Pre-LP/'Intermediate' epoch lp-10:lp-1 coincides almost exactly with the qualifying window. In both cases one of the three epochs is selected on the same behavioural variable that is being decoded or informed about. A clean design would exclude the criterion window from all epochs.

9. loo_ridge_press's documented leak is much larger in the epoch decoder than its docstring assumes. The helper standardises with full-fit rather than per-fold statistics, an O(1/n) effect, and its docstring justifies this at 'n = 200-300 trial sizes'. Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding calls it with n = 5-10 trials per epoch, where the leak is ~5-10%, not 0.3-0.5%, and where LOO r over <= 10 points is itself a very high-variance statistic. NOTES.md line 121 records the leak but not the n-dependence.

10. GPR's try/catch does not fall back to chance, it falls back to r = -1. local_gpr_loo substitutes mean(Y(train_mask)) on failure; the leave-one-out mean is a strictly decreasing linear function of the held-out value, so a cell where fitrgp fails on all folds returns a Pearson r of exactly -1, and partial failures interpolate toward it. Failures are never counted. NOTES.md line 395 flags that the fallback should be logged; the sign of the artefact is worse than that note implies.

11. Position-decoder accuracy is reported optimistically and against the wrong chance level. decode_position sets negative predictions to NaN twice and then drops NaNs before computing RMSE/MAE/R2, which selectively removes the largest negative-side errors in a position-dependent way. decode_position_mld's chance line is drawn at 1/50 = 0.02 because ProcessStriatumTask passes the neuron count (100) into the second positional argument and n_pos_bins silently defaults to 50, while the data has 100 position bins (true chance 0.01); no test against chance is performed either way. Both scripts also multiply bin indices by options.bin_size = 5 while the current data is 2.5 cm/bin, so all reported cm errors are 2x too large. decode_position's 'gpr' branch is dead code that would error at beta = mdl.Beta.

12. There is no Poisson decoder in this domain, despite the naming expectation. decode_position is ridge/least-squares regression; decode_position_mld is a Gaussian naive-Bayes maximum-likelihood classifier on z-scored rates with a 1e-6 variance floor that lets degenerate low-variance cells dominate the log-likelihood. The only Poisson ML decoders in the repository are inside IntegratedAll_v1.m (section 7) and decode_ensemble_ablation.m, i.e. a different domain.

13. The MSN/FSN/TAN scheme is applied to cortex. The rules at OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m:104-107 run over all probe-1 units, and probe 1 spans DMS, DLS and ACC, so ACC units receive striatal cell-type labels; neurontype_classification.m then plots non-zero ACC MSN/FS/TAN bars and summary_numbers sums them into cohort totals, while printing a caveat (line 134) that the classification is striatum-only. Probe-2 areas (V1/CA1/DG) are correctly NaN. Units matching no rule get label 0 and are dropped by the plots but counted as Unclassified by summary_numbers, so the two scripts disagree on totals.

14. Stale/incomparable cached data feeding descriptive claims. summary_numbers prints control2 numbers from processed_data/preprocessed_data_control2.mat (28 Jan 2025), which has no 2.5 cm variant and predates the 2026-05-07 alignment of fr_threshold to 0.02 Hz - so its unit counts and firing rates were computed under a different inclusion threshold and bin width yet appear in the same table as the task/control 2.5 cm numbers. neurontype_classification reports the CONTROL cohort's cell-type composition, not the task cohort's.

15. Pseudoreplication in the descriptive layer. summary_numbers reports firing-rate mean +/- SEM with std/sqrt(n_units) over units pooled across animals (lines 196-215, 334-341, 459-467) while using std/sqrt(n_animals) for count metrics in the same table; neurontype_classification pools units across animals for its per-area proportions. The MI and decoding analyses handle this correctly (unit -> animal mean, then SEM across animals).

16. Hard runtime break in summary_numbers: sem() is called at lines 23-50 but no sem.m exists in the repository (the only definition is a local function inside CCA_striatum_spatial_v3_plot.m:416, not visible from this script), so the script errors at line 23 on a clean path. The values it would compute are never printed anyway - lines 20-51 are dead relative to the fprintf blocks that recompute everything inline.

17. Figure-layout breakage from the 6-area expansion. Fixed tiledlayouts are still sized for 3 areas or 3 pairs while the loops now issue 6: Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding sections 5 and 5A (tiledlayout(3,3), 18 nexttile calls), section 5B (tiledlayout(1,3), 6 calls), section 5C (hardcoded nan(3,3,n_animals) and i_reg = 1:3, silently dropping V1/CA1/DG while legend(cfg.regions) supplies 6 labels); CrossSpatialBinDecoding section 4 (tiledlayout(2,4), 12 calls); MI v2 section 12 (tiledlayout(2,3), 12 calls).

18. Output-path and geometry inconsistencies worth fixing before a manuscript run: MI v2 writes one cache into processed_data/ and three into the CWD root; its zone definitions (bins 10-15 / 20-25 / 25-30) and the legacy script's max_bin = 30 / target_rz_bin = 25 are 5 cm-era constants, so the panel labelled 'Reward Zone (Bins 25-30)' no longer contains the reward zone (bin 50 at 2.5 cm); CrossSpatialBinDecoding ignores cfg.max_bin while the epoch decoder applies it, making their cross-bin matrices non-comparable; cfg.ntype_col = 5 exists but every consumer hardcodes 5; cfg.velocity_factor exists but all three scripts hardcode 4*1.25.

### Analyses (12)

#### 8.1 Epoch-resolved cross-spatial-bin behaviour decoding (Ridge)
`Striatum project/Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding.m` lines 61-165 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure if fixed (predictive-horizon claim), currently drop - cannot be run and no outputs exist*

- **Question.** Does population activity at spatial bin s predict lick rate / velocity at a later bin t (predictive horizon), and does that horizon lengthen across learning (Naive vs Pre-LP vs Post-LP)?
- **Method.** Per animal x area x behav target x epoch, for every (target_b, source_b) with source_b <= target_b (lower triangle only, n_bins = min(100, cfg.max_bin=60)): X = single-bin population FR [trials x units] at source_b, Y = behaviour at target_b [trials x 1]. Ridge via closed-form PRESS LOO (loo_ridge_press, cfg.ridge_lambda = 1.0, Standardize=true, unpenalised intercept). Score = Pearson r(Y_pred_LOO, Y). Epochs: naive = trials 1:10, pre-LP = lp-10:lp-1, post-LP = lp+1:lp+10; LP from find_learning_points with lp_z_threshold=-2, lp_window=7, lp_min_consecutive=7 (START-of-window convention). Trials truncated at change_point_mean (disengagement). Cells skipped if epoch has <5 trials or Y is flat. Saved: r_mat, r_shuff (FIRST shuffle only), r_shuff_mean, r_shuff_std, empirical_p, n_shuffles to processed_data/ridge_epoch_decoding_results.mat.
- **Inputs.** processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat -> spatial_binned_fr_all [units x 100 bins x trials], spatial_binned_data.licks/.durations [trials x bins], zscored_lick_errors, change_point_mean, is_dms/is_dls/is_acc/is_v1
- **Outputs.** processed_data/ridge_epoch_decoding_results.mat (ABSENT on disk); 3 figure families per behav target: delta-r approach-to-RZ curves, delta-r heatmaps (raw + imgaussfilt sigma=0.5), spatial-lag profiles (lags 0:20), instantaneous-vs-predictive summaries. No figures saved to file.
- **Statistics.** Trial-label permutation null, cfg.n_shuffles = 25 per cell; empirical_p = mean(r_shuffle >= r_real) (one-sided, NO +1 correction, so p can be exactly 0 and resolution is 0.04). No multiple-comparison correction across ~1800 lower-triangle cells x 3 epochs x 6 areas x 2 targets. empirical_p is saved but NEVER read by any plot or test. Group level: mean +/- SEM across animals only, no test.
- **Inferential unit.** trials within an epoch for the LOO r (n = 5-10); animals for the SEM across the plotted curves (n <= n_animals)
- **Soundness.** Method is appropriate in principle (held-out LOO r, lower-triangle-only so no anti-causal cells) but the implementation is not runnable and the figures do not use the null that was computed. (1) FATAL RUNTIME BUG: cfg.regions = cfg.areas = 6 areas incl. CA1/DG, but clean_data only receives is_dms/is_dls/is_acc/is_v1 (lines 55-58); line 87 does clean_data(ianimal).(['is_' lower('CA1')]) -> reference to non-existent field is_ca1 -> the compute block errors on the first animal. No ridge_epoch_decoding_results.mat or gpr_* exists on disk, consistent with the script never having completed since CA1/DG were added (2026-05-08). (2) Every plotted quantity (sections 4, 5, 5A, 5B, 5C) uses delta r = r_mat - r_shuff where r_shuff is a SINGLE permutation sample (line 154 comment 'first sample (compat)'), so all figures rest on a single-shuffle null despite 25 shuffles being computed and stored. (3) The null is not matched to the statistic: the shuffle path fits on permuted Y (Y_shuff_s) but scores against the UNpermuted Y_ep (line 142), so real and null statistics differ in construction and their difference is not a clean permutation contrast. (4) No rng seeding anywhere in the script (cfg.seed=42 is never used), so nulls are not reproducible. (5) n = 5-10 trials per LOO r: r is estimated from <=10 points, and LOO ridge with p = n_units >> n trials is deep in the interpolation regime. (6) loo_ridge_press standardises with full-fit statistics -> documented O(1/n) leak, but at n=10 (not the n=200-300 the helper's docstring assumes) the leak is ~5-10%, not 0.3-0.5%. (7) Post-LP epoch (lp+1:lp+10) overlaps the 7 consecutive criterion trials that DEFINED lp -> the 'expert' epoch is partly selected on the behaviour being decoded. (8) Figure-layout breakage with 6 areas: section 5 and 5A use tiledlayout(3,3) but issue 3x6=18 nexttile calls; 5B uses tiledlayout(1,3) with 6; 5C hardcodes nan(3,3,n_animals) and i_reg=1:3, silently dropping V1/CA1/DG while legend(cfg.regions) lists 6 labels.

#### 8.2 Epoch-resolved cross-bin decoding, Gaussian-process variant
`Striatum project/Nonlinear_Epoch_Decoding.m` lines 13, 120-141, 479-495 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `gated` · manuscript role: *drop (or supplementary robustness check only after the fallback is replaced by NaN and failures are logged)*

- **Question.** Same as the ridge version, but does a nonlinear (GPR) decoder reveal predictive structure that linear ridge misses?
- **Method.** Toggle cfg.decoder_type = 'GPR' (default is 'Ridge', so this path is off by default). X_ep is jittered with randn*1e-6 before fitting (line 121). local_gpr_loo refits fitrgp per held-out trial: KernelFunction='squaredexponential', Standardize=true, PredictMethod='exact', explicit n-fold LOO loop (no PRESS shortcut). Same 25-shuffle null, same lower-triangle sweep. Saves to processed_data/gpr_epoch_decoding_results.mat.
- **Inputs.** same as ridge path
- **Outputs.** processed_data/gpr_epoch_decoding_results.mat (ABSENT on disk)
- **Statistics.** Identical to the ridge path: 25 trial permutations, empirical_p = mean(shuffle >= real), no correction, unseeded.
- **Inferential unit.** trials within epoch (n = 5-10)
- **Soundness.** Same fatal is_ca1 bug and same single-shuffle plotting as the ridge path, plus a specific and severe fallback artefact: the try/catch at lines 486-493 substitutes Y_pred(test_t) = mean(Y(train_mask)) when fitrgp fails. The leave-one-out mean is (sum(Y) - y_i)/(n-1), a strictly DECREASING linear function of y_i, so a cell where GPR fails on all folds yields r = -1 exactly, not r ~ 0. Partial failures pull r toward -1. Failures are never counted or logged, so an area/epoch with poor conditioning (few trials, many units - exactly the naive epochs) can produce systematically negative r that then propagates into delta r = real - shuff with arbitrary sign. GPR with p = n_units features and n = 5-10 training points is also not identifiable in any case. cfg.seed unused.

#### 8.3 Trial-resolved cross-spatial-bin ridge decoding (moving-window r)
`Striatum project/CrossSpatialBinDecoding.m` lines 55-180 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary (trial-resolved companion to the epoch decoder) - currently drop: the only existing output is a stale cache from a superseded preprocessing*

- **Question.** How does the predictive (source bin < target bin) decodability of lick rate / velocity from single-bin population activity evolve trial-by-trial, and does it change around the learning point?
- **Method.** Per animal x area x behav target: for every (target_b, source_b) with source_b <= target_b over the FULL bin range (n_bins = size(neural,2) = 100 for the 2.5 cm data; cfg.max_bin is NOT applied here), fit one PRESS-LOO ridge across ALL session trials (loo_ridge_press, lambda = 1.0, Standardize=true) giving Y_pred [target_b x source_b x trials]. 'Trial-resolved' = a centred moving-window Pearson r: cfg.corr_window = 9, half_win = floor(9/2) = 4, window = max(1,t-4):min(n_trials,t+4), computed only if window length > 3, giving moving_r(target_b, source_b, t) per trial index t. Trials truncated at change_point_mean. LP via find_learning_points(lp_z_threshold=-2, lp_window=7, lp_min_consecutive=7). Saved: moving_r, moving_r_shuff (first shuffle), shuff_mean, shuff_std, empirical_p, n_shuffles to processed_data/cross_spatial_decoding_results.mat.
- **Inputs.** processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat (same fields as the epoch decoder; neural NOT clipped to cfg.max_bin)
- **Outputs.** processed_data/cross_spatial_decoding_results.mat (PRESENT, 424 MB, dated 14 May - predates the current 2.5 cm data file); cross-spatial r heatmaps and LP-aligned predictive-power curves. No figures saved.
- **Statistics.** cfg.n_shuffles = 25 whole-session trial permutations; online mean/var aggregation; empirical_p = shuff_above / 25 (one-sided, no +1, p can be 0). Bug: shuff_above accumulates double(moving_r_s >= moving_r) with NaN comparisons counting as false and the denominator fixed at 25, so cells where the null is undefined report p = 0 rather than NaN. empirical_p / shuff_mean / shuff_std are saved but NEVER used by any plot. Section 5 plots mean +/- SEM across animals with a >=3-mice gate, no test.
- **Inferential unit.** trials in the 9-trial window for each r(t) (windows overlap by 8 trials, so successive r(t) are strongly dependent); animals for the LP-aligned SEM
- **Soundness.** The held-out scoring is legitimate (PRESS LOO over the whole session, moving-window r evaluated on held-out predictions), but the analysis as published rests on a stale cache and the same null mismatch as the epoch decoder. (1) STALE CACHE: line 56 loads processed_data/cross_spatial_decoding_results.mat unconditionally whenever the file exists - there is no cache-key check (contrast MI v2's check_cache). The on-disk file is dated 14 May, while preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat is dated 23 May and project_cfg was repointed to the 2.5 cm data on 2026-05-24. Every figure from this script therefore describes an earlier preprocessing (different bin width, different bin count, and a regions list that predates CA1/DG), not the current data. (2) Recomputation is impossible as written: lines 49-52 populate only is_dms/is_dls/is_acc/is_v1 while line 70 indexes clean_data.(['is_' lower(region)]) for all 6 cfg.areas -> non-existent field is_ca1. (3) Null mismatch: Y_pred_shuff_s is fitted on permuted Y but moving_r_s correlates it against the UNpermuted Y_all (line 146). (4) No rng seeding; cfg.seed unused. (5) Cost/feasibility: with 100 bins the sweep is ~5050 ridge fits x (1 + 25 shuffles) x a 100x100xn_trials correlation triple loop per animal/target/area - the cached result cannot have been produced at this bin count. (6) Section 4 plots raw mean moving_r with no null subtraction and no significance mask; section 5's LP-aligned curve averages the strictly-lower-triangle mean over ALL (target,source) pairs including anti-causal-in-time-but-causal-in-space pairs far from the reward zone, diluting the effect. (7) Overlapping 9-trial windows are treated as independent samples along the trial axis. (8) Figure breakage: section 4 uses tiledlayout(2,4) but issues 2 targets x 6 regions = 12 nexttile calls.

#### 8.4 Single-unit Shannon MI between activity and behaviour (pooled spatial windows)
`Striatum project/MutualInformationStriatum_v2.m` lines 95-206, 960-1010 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure for lick_rate (spatial information profile across learning) once p-values/FDR are added; velocity panels must be dropped entirely*

- **Question.** How much information does each unit's firing carry about lick rate / velocity at each corridor location, and how does that spatial information profile change across learning?
- **Method.** Per animal (parfor) x behav target x area x epoch x spatial window x unit: pool cfg.mi_pool_win = 5 adjacent spatial bins, step cfg.mi_pool_shift = 1, window centre = win_start + floor(5/2) = win_start+2, over n_bins = min(100, cfg.max_bin = 60) -> 56 windows. Flatten [5 bins x n_epoch_trials] to a sample vector, discretise both streams with discretize_zero_aware (bin 1 = |x| < 1e-8 exact zeros; the remaining n-1 bins are equipopulated quantiles of the non-zeros, with randn*1e-10 tie-breaking jitter), cfg.mi_neural_bins = cfg.mi_behav_bins = 2 -> strictly binary zero/non-zero. MI via compute_mi_mm: plug-in joint histogram (accumarray), I_raw = sum p_xy log2(p_xy/(p_x p_y)), minus the Panzeri-Treves / Miller-Madow asymptotic bias (R_xy - R_x - R_y + 1)/(2*N*log(2)) where R_* are counts of OCCUPIED bins, then I_corrected = max(0, I_raw - bias). Epochs from epochs_from_lp with the v2 END-of-window LP convention (lp = lp_start + cfg.lp_window - 1 = lp_start + 9; project cfg lp_z_threshold=-2, lp_window=10, lp_min_consecutive=7). Saved per (animal, area, target, epoch): real, shuffle_mean, shuffle_p95 [n_units x 56] to processed_data/shannon_mi_results.mat with a cache_meta parameter fingerprint.
- **Inputs.** processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat; area masks via is_area_safe so CA1/DG flow through automatically
- **Outputs.** processed_data/shannon_mi_results.mat (ABSENT); per-target figures of mean corrected MI vs window centre for 3 epochs, dashed shuffle-mean overlay
- **Statistics.** cfg.n_shuffles = 25 trial-label permutations of the behaviour, pre-generated per (window, epoch) and REUSED across all units in that window (nulls correlated across units). Null summarised only as mean and prctile(null_vals, 95) over 25 values (the 95th percentile of 25 samples is an interpolation between the top two draws - very high variance). NO p-value is computed or saved anywhere in the script, no FDR, no test of real vs null. Plots overlay the null mean as a dashed line. Seeded: rng(cfg.seed = 42) globally and rng(cfg.seed + ianimal, 'twister') per parfor worker, so nulls are reproducible.
- **Inferential unit.** units for the within-animal mean (n = units in area); animals for the plotted SEM (sqrt(sum(~isnan)) across animals). Samples entering each MI estimate are (5 bins x n_epoch_trials) flattened pseudo-independent observations - the 5 pooled bins from one trial are not independent draws.
- **Soundness.** The estimator is defensible (plug-in + Miller-Madow with occupied-bin counts is the standard small-N correction, and the zero-aware binning is a reasonable choice for sparse spike data), and this is the only non-degenerate MI analysis in the file - but only for the lick_rate target. FATAL for velocity: velocity = (4*1.25)./durations with durations(durations==0) = eps, so velocity is strictly positive and never within 1e-8 of zero; with mi_behav_bins = 2 every velocity sample lands in bin 2, Y is CONSTANT, R_y = 1, and I_raw = 0 with bias = 0 -> MI(unit; velocity) is identically 0.000 for every unit, window, epoch and area. All velocity MI panels are structurally zero, not empirically null. Other concerns: max(0, I_raw - bias) rectifies both real and null at zero, so the null mean is positively biased and 'MI > 0' is vacuous; min_valid_trials = 8 is applied inconsistently (as a TRIAL count at the epoch gate, line 146, but as a flattened SAMPLE count inside the window/unit loops, lines 166/179, where 5 bins x 8 trials = 40 samples makes the check nearly always pass); no min_units gate at all (only sum(idx_reg) == 0), so an area contributing 1 unit is averaged in with equal weight; the v2 END-of-window LP makes the 'Pre-LP' epoch (lp-10:lp-1) coincide almost exactly with the qualifying window that DEFINED lp, i.e. the intermediate epoch is selected on the behaviour being predicted (circular); parfor broadcasts the full clean_data neural tensors to every worker; no output exists on disk (processed_data/shannon_mi_results.mat is ABSENT), so nothing has been materialised since the 2026-05 refactor.

#### 8.5 Cross-area MI between PC1 traces (information flow)
`Striatum project/MutualInformationStriatum_v2.m` lines 464-581, 1012-1044 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *drop - the computed quantity is identically zero; if resurrected it needs equipopulated (non-zero-aware) binning with >=4 bins and a directed measure*

- **Question.** How much information is shared between two areas' population activity, and is the sharing asymmetric in space (which area leads)?
- **Method.** Per animal, extract_pc1 per area: reshape [units x bins x trials] to [(bins*trials) x units], coeff = pca(X2D, 'NumComponents', 1, 'Rows', 'pairwise'), score = (X2D - nanmean) * coeff, reshaped to [bins x trials]; PC1 fitted ONCE on all trials so epochs share a coordinate system. Then for each ordered window pair (wA, wB) over all 56 x 56 windows, MI(discretised PC1_A in wA; discretised PC1_B in wB) with the same compute_mi_mm estimator and mi_neural_bins = 2. Pairs are a script-local override at line 471: ACC-DMS, ACC-DLS, DMS-DLS, V1-DMS, V1-DLS, V1-ACC (6 of the 15 pairs in project_cfg; CA1 and DG are excluded from all cross-area MI). Plotted as lag profiles over diag(mat, -lag) for lag = -10:10 (cfg.area_max_lag = 10).
- **Inputs.** clean_data neural tensors -> extract_pc1 per area
- **Outputs.** cross_area_mi_results.mat at CWD root (ABSENT); cross-area lag-profile figure (3 epochs x 6 pairs)
- **Statistics.** 25 trial permutations of area B; shuffle_mean and shuffle_p95 only; no p-values, no correction. Seeded per worker.
- **Inferential unit.** animals (one MI matrix per animal per pair per epoch); the MI itself is estimated from (5 bins x n_epoch_trials) samples
- **Soundness.** FATAL BY CONSTRUCTION: discretize_zero_aware assigns bin 1 only to samples with |x| < 1e-8 and, with n_bins = 2, assigns every non-zero sample to bin 2. PC1 scores are continuous mean-centred projections that are never numerically zero, so both discA and discB are CONSTANT vectors -> R_x = R_y = 1, I_raw = 0, bias = 0, and MI is identically 0.000 for every window pair, lag, epoch, pair and animal. The entire cross-area information-flow analysis (and its 'which area leads' asymmetry read-out) computes a matrix of zeros. The file's own header comment (lines 10-14) states the 2-bin scheme is 'the smallest non-degenerate scheme for sparse signals' - it is degenerate for any dense/continuous signal, which PC1 is. Secondary issues even after fixing the binning: PC1 is a 1-D summary that discards the subspace structure the CCA analyses target; PC1 is fitted on all trials including the epochs later compared (a shared-coordinate choice that is defensible but is fit on test data); MI(A;B) is symmetric, so 'directionality' rests entirely on the spatial-lag asymmetry of a symmetric quantity, not on any directed measure (no transfer entropy / Granger); n = 25 shuffles with no test. Output cross_area_mi_results.mat is written to the CWD root and is ABSENT on disk.

#### 8.6 MMI redundancy upper bound (PID proxy)
`Striatum project/MutualInformationStriatum_v2.m` lines 659-956 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *drop - degenerate as computed, and the MMI bound cannot support the directionality claim even when non-zero*

- **Question.** How much behavioural information is redundantly shared between two areas (upper bound on the shared/redundant PID atom), and is the redundancy spatially asymmetric (which area's activity leads the behaviour)?
- **Method.** Minimum-MI bound: SI(wA, lag) = min(I(PC1_A at w_source; behaviour at w_targ), I(PC1_B at w_targ; behaviour at w_targ)), with w_source = w_targ - lag over lag = -cfg.pid_max_lag(10):+10, for the 6 script-local area pairs and both behav targets. All three streams discretised with discretize_zero_aware at mi_neural_bins = 2 (A, B) and mi_behav_bins = 2 (behaviour). Result [56 windows x 21 lags] per (animal, pair, target, epoch). Plotted as NaN-aware imgaussfilt (sigma = 0.8) heatmaps and as an 'information dominance' bar chart contrasting mean SI over lag<0 vs lag>0.
- **Inputs.** clean_data neural tensors -> extract_pc1; lick_rate / velocity
- **Outputs.** pid_shared_info_results.mat at CWD root (ABSENT); MMI heatmaps and asymmetry bar charts per pair x target
- **Statistics.** 25 permutations of the behaviour trial labels; shuffle_mean and shuffle_p95 stored; no p-values, no correction; asymmetry bars are mean +/- SEM across animals with no test. Seeded per worker.
- **Inferential unit.** animals for the plotted bars/curves; the underlying MI estimates come from (5 bins x n_epoch_trials) flattened samples
- **Soundness.** FATAL BY CONSTRUCTION on both inputs: (a) A and B are PC1 traces, which the 2-bin zero-aware discretiser collapses to a constant (see cross-area MI), so I_A_F = I_B_F = 0; (b) for the velocity target the behaviour stream is also constant, so the bound is zero regardless. Every si_mat is therefore a matrix of zeros and the 'information dominance' bars compare 0 with 0. Beyond the degeneracy, the measure itself is only an UPPER bound on redundancy (MMI/Imin), which is known to conflate redundancy with the smaller of the two univariate informations and cannot separate redundancy from synergy - the figures are titled 'Redundancy Upper Bound' but the summary panels interpret asymmetries in that bound as directed information dominance, which the quantity does not license. Note also that I_B_F is evaluated at w_targ for every lag while only I_A_F moves with the lag, so the min is dominated by whichever stream is smaller and the lag axis is not symmetric between A and B. Section 12 also issues 12 nexttile calls into a tiledlayout(2,3) (6 tiles). Output pid_shared_info_results.mat written to CWD root, ABSENT on disk.

- **Question.** Over what spatial lag does single-unit activity carry information about future behaviour (predictive horizon, information-theoretic analogue of the ridge decoder)?
