THE THREE FINDINGS THAT MOST AFFECT A MANUSCRIPT.
(a) 'Residual + partial CCA' is not what the temporal code does. cfg.subtract_trial_mean=True is read nowhere; core.residualise is called only from tests. The temporal path applies per-unit z-scoring plus the third-area partial-out and nothing else. Trial-mean residualisation is in fact impossible in this representation (variable-length traversals concatenated with no shared bin axis). This matters beyond terminology: the central 2026-07-28 interpretation — that round 8's temporal reorientation vanished because residual CCA removed shared position/time tuning — attributes the effect to a step that is not in the code. Whatever removed it was the other-area regression, the honest CV, or the floor-referencing, and the writeup must say which.
(b) No statistics are scripted anywhere. run_epochs.py imports csv, numpy and the package, and no statistics library; it writes four CSVs and prints per-animal cell counts. There is no analyze_epochs.py. So the 'in-driver Wilcoxon' of the 2026-06-17 entry does not exist, and every recorded p-value (the epoch Wilcoxons, the rotation Wilcoxon/t, the 78/140 binomial) was computed ad hoc outside the repo. I reproduced all of them and they are arithmetically correct — but none is reproducible from a committed script, and the correct machinery for them (mixed_effects.lmm_epoch_contrasts with its random slope on epoch, plus paired_stats.fdr_bh) sits unused in the package.
(c) The reorientation null is under-powered by construction, not merely negative. NOTES calls it 'a powered null, not a p-floor' because the n=10 one-sided Wilcoxon floor is 0.001. The test is powered; the MEASUREMENT is not. The floor is fitted on half the trials of the rotation it gates (conservative bias), it is a single split-half draw, and both rotation and floor sit within ~15 deg of the 90 deg orthogonality ceiling. Report this as inconclusive, or fix it (equalise the sample sizes by comparing half-epoch fits to half-epoch fits, average >=10 splits, and use the mean or the smallest principal angle rather than the max).
ALSO: NOTES.md and PREDICTIONS.md both state that the circshift null is unseeded and that only n_sig can drift. It is seeded — default_rng(cfg.cv_seed + 7) with cv_seed=0 — as are the CV folds (seed 0) and the split-half draw (seed 11). The entire run is deterministic given the same code and data, so the 2026-07-28 'reproduction is exact' finding is guaranteed by construction and carries no information about robustness. A real robustness check requires varying cv_seed.
MINOR BUT FIXABLE: gini_pearson_x/y (the CCA-machinery-free control for the Gini headline) is computed in window_subspace and then never written to disk. The SAT=0.99 guard screens cc1 >= 0.99 but not cc1 <= -0.99, and epoch_dims.csv contains a peak_cc of exactly -1.0. core.cca_fit's rank_tol=1e-9 lets near-null PCA directions through, producing canonical weights of order 1e8 in 3 cells (A4 DMS-ACC intermediate DMS; A14 DMS-ACC naive and expert ACC) that contaminate both the Gini and the rotation for those cells. kcca_window and kernel_cca use five bare `except Exception` blocks that convert failures into NaN or 0.0 with no failure count reported.

**Scientifically load-bearing constants.**

- run_epochs.py:27 — K = 20 PCA components per area, HARDCODED; core.choose_k and cfg.k_mode/samples_per_pc/k_cap are never called in the temporal path

### Analyses (24)

#### 11.1 Trial-mean residualisation (residual vs signal CCA) — advertised but never applied
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/core.py` lines 49-81; config.py 154-155 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `decorative` · manuscript role: *drop the knob; rewrite the Methods sentence*

- **Question.** Is 'communication' defined on trial-to-trial residual fluctuations or on the raw signal?
- **Method.** core.residualise subtracts the per-(bin, unit) mean across trials from a (trials, bins, units) tensor. cfg.subtract_trial_mean defaults to True and is documented as 'residual CCA (report D2)'. Grep of src/ and scripts/ confirms: cfg.subtract_trial_mean is read NOWHERE, and core.residualise is called only from tests. The live temporal path (run_epochs -> runner -> subspace_window) applies per-unit z-scoring and the partial-out of other areas, and nothing else.
- **Inputs.** n/a
- **Outputs.** none
- **Statistics.** n/a
- **Inferential unit.** n/a
- **Soundness.** Structurally, per-(bin,unit) trial-mean subtraction is impossible in this temporal representation — traversals have variable length and are concatenated into a flat timeline with no common bin axis, so there is no trial-by-bin mean to subtract. That is a legitimate design consequence, but it means the README's and NOTES' repeated 'residual + partial CCA' description is inaccurate for the temporal arm: the only residualisation performed is the third-area partial-out. This directly undercuts the central 2026-07-28 interpretation, which attributes the loss of round 8's temporal reorientation to residual CCA removing shared position/time tuning. Since no trial-mean residualisation happens, shared position/time tuning is removed only insofar as the other-area regression absorbs it.
- **Concerns.**
    - README.md line 16 and NOTES.md 2026-07-28 both claim 'residual + partial CCA'; the code performs z-score + partial-out only
    - the headline causal story for why round 8's reorientation vanished rests on a step that is not in the code
    - cfg.subtract_trial_mean=True is a dead knob that will mislead anyone reading config.py as the source of truth

#### 11.2 Learning-epoch window definition (naive / intermediate / expert)
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/dataio.py` lines 170-216 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only (but the misalignment must be fixed before any epoch claim ships)*

- **Question.** Which trials constitute the three learning epochs?
- **Method.** n_usable = min(round(change_point_mean), n_trials) (all trials if NaN). epoch_windows(lp, n_usable, cfg): returns None if lp < 2*trials_per_epoch(=20) or lp + 10 > n_usable; else naive = 0-indexed 0..9, intermediate = lp-10..lp-1, expert = lp..lp+9. In the driver these 0-indexed values are used as POSITIONAL indices into uniq = np.unique(trial_idx[run]) (run_epochs.py:77,98-99,109), and n_usable is passed as uniq.size (the run-trial count), not the behavioural usable-trial count.
- **Inputs.** lp from classify_cohort; run-trial list from the running mask
- **Outputs.** trial-id arrays consumed by runner.fit_window; epoch label in all four CSVs
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** trial
- **Soundness.** Windows are disjoint by construction and the overlap/overrun guards work (unit-tested). BUT the driver maps behavioural trial numbers onto POSITIONS in the surviving run-trial list, and traversals are dropped upstream (over-long, malformed, or zero running bins). Verified on real data: animal 1 loses 1 of 125 engaged trials (offset 0, harmless); animal 13 loses 26 of 155, and its expert window at positions 23-32 maps to REAL trial ids 23-35, a 3-trial offset; animal 3 loses 31 of 71 (71 engaged -> 40 run-trials). So the intermediate/expert windows are shifted later in real-trial numbering by the number of dropped trials, i.e. the neural epochs are not aligned to the behavioural learning point for animals with many dropped traversals.
- **Concerns.**
    - epoch positions indexed into uniq (surviving run-trials) rather than matched on trial id -> up to a 3-trial drift measured on animal 13; the drift is animal-specific and grows with the drop rate
    - n_usable is passed as the run-trial count, so the change_point disengagement truncation and the run-trial availability criterion are conflated in a single guard
    - animals 3 and 15 are skipped for exactly this reason: A3 lp=32 needs 42 run-trials but has 40; A15 lp=26 with change_point=27 needs 36 but has 27. Both skips are correct behaviour, but they are driven by the run-trial count, not by trial count

#### 11.3 Subspace dimensionality n_sig via circular-shift surrogate
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/subspace_window.py` lines 112-131, 220-222 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary at best; do not report n_sig as a dimensionality estimate*

- **Question.** How many canonical dimensions carry significant cross-area communication?
- **Method.** Sx, Sy = full-window PCA scores of the full-window partial-out residual (in-sample). For s in range(n_shuffles=config.SURROGATE_SHUFFLES=100): shift = default_rng(seed+7=7).integers(1, n) (n = window bins, ~3000-8000); rs = in-sample per-dim CC of cca_fit(Sx, np.roll(Sy, shift, axis=0)); null_top[s] = rs[0]. Threshold thr = np.quantile(null_top, 1-alpha=0.95). sig = (held-out per-dim cc) > thr; n_sig = sum(sig). Observed: n_sig distribution over 125 cells = {0:53, 1:29, 2:20, 3:10, 4:4, 5:4, 8:3, 9:1, 12:1}; median 1, max 12.
- **Inputs.** in-sample full-window PCA scores
- **Outputs.** n_sig in epoch_metrics.csv; per-dim sig flag in epoch_dims.csv (1681 rows, sig rate 0.107)
- **Statistics.** single scalar 95th-percentile threshold from 100 seeded circular shifts; applied to up to 20 canonical dims per cell with NO multiple-comparison correction and no per-dim null
- **Inferential unit.** canonical dimension within a cell (nested in pair, in animal)
- **Soundness.** Comparing a held-out per-dim CC to a null built from the IN-SAMPLE dominant CC is a scale mismatch: the null is inflated (in-sample bias with k=20 PCs) which makes the bar conservative, while applying one scalar bar to 20 dims with no correction is anti-conservative. The two errors do not cancel in any controlled way. Additionally the roll is over the CONCATENATED running-bin timeline (crosses trial boundaries) with a minimum shift of 1 bin, so cfg.circshift_min_bins=15 and cfg.null_type/'trials' are never honoured — surrogate.py, which implements the configured per-trial min-shift null, is not called by the live path at all.
- **Concerns.**
    - one threshold reused for up to 20 dims per cell, no FDR/Bonferroni (compare the spatial arm, which uses BH-FDR)
    - min shift of 1 bin permitted; the configured circshift_min_bins=15 rule lives in the unused surrogate.py
    - roll crosses trial boundaries on the concatenated timeline
    - 100 shuffles gives a 95th-percentile resolution of 1/100 on the threshold
    - the same seed (7) is used for every cell, so the shift sequence is identical across cells — nulls are not independent across cells
    - NOTES.md and PREDICTIONS.md both assert 'the unseeded circshift null' — it IS seeded (seed = cfg.cv_seed = 0), so the whole run is deterministic and the 2026-07-28 'exact reproduction' is expected by construction, not evidence of robustness

#### 11.4 Directionality: lagged CCA curve, IFI and optimal lag
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/subspace_window.py` lines 134-152, 231-239; lagged.py 42-51 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary null (state explicitly that it is a 5-point in-sample curve and therefore an insensitive test, not evidence of symmetric flow)*

- **Question.** Does one area lead the other?
- **Method.** lags = arange(-max_lag, max_lag+1) with max_lag = args.max_lag or max(2, round(50/bin_ms)) = 2 bins at 25 ms (i.e. only lags -2,-1,0,+1,+2 = +/-50 ms, five points). _lag_curve_perdim: for each lag, slice the CONCATENATED Sx/Sy (positive lag pairs Sx[:n-L] with Sy[L:]) and take the IN-SAMPLE per-dim CC via cca_fit+cca_score; skipped if fewer than 10 rows. ifi = information_flow_index(lags, lag_cc1) = (mean of clip(cc,0,None) over L>0 - mean over L<0) / (sum of those means), 0.0 if the sum <= 0. optimal_lag = lags[nanargmax(lag_cc1)]. Also per-dim ifi/lag for all d dims. Observed: ifi mean +0.0000, sd 0.0905, min -0.306, max +0.336; optimal_lag in {-2..+2}, median 0, mean -0.08; triangle IFI by epoch -0.025/+0.011/+0.020 (expert/int/naive).
- **Inputs.** full-window in-sample PCA scores
- **Outputs.** ifi, optimal_lag in epoch_metrics.csv; per-dim ifi/lag in epoch_dims.csv
- **Statistics.** none — no null, no test, no CI on IFI
- **Inferential unit.** cell
- **Soundness.** IFI is exactly zero on average with sd 0.09, i.e. a pure null — which is the honest reading, but the measurement is also structurally incapable of detecting much: only two non-zero lags per side at 25 ms, an in-sample lag curve (biased upward at every lag, which is symmetric so the IFI ratio survives), and lags applied ACROSS trial boundaries on the concatenated stream. lagged.heldout_lag_curve_flat and lagged._segment_lagged_pairs implement the segment-aware, held-out version — and are never called by the live driver.
- **Concerns.**
    - only 5 lag points (+/-2 bins) at 25 ms; the report's directionality arm assumes the 10 ms bin
    - in-sample lag curve; the honest segment-aware held-out implementation exists (lagged.py:145-205) and is unused
    - lags cross trial boundaries (acknowledged in the module docstring as 'negligible')
    - no null distribution for IFI, so 'IFI ~ 0' is an absence of measurement, not a tested null

#### 11.5 Subspace membership sparsity: canonical-weight Gini and the CCA-independent Pearson control
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/membership.py` lines 57-60, 91-126, 138-177; subspace_window.py 241-256 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary (flat Gini = no de-sparsification, consistent with the spatial arm) — but only after the weight blow-up is fixed and gini_pearson is actually written out*

- **Question.** Do a few neurons carry the coupling, and does that sparsity change with learning (de-sparsification)?
- **Method.** Full-window in-sample fit: model = cca_fit(Sx,Sy); wx = components_x @ A[:, :d], wy = components_y @ B[:, :d] with d = min(kx,ky) (up to 20); contrib = L2 norm across dims; gini = sorted-|v| formula with the N/(N-1) small-sample correction; member_mask = contrib >= quantile(contrib, member_q=0.75). Control: pearson_coupling_scores(Xr,Yr) = column-z-score both, R = Xz.T@Yz/n, per-neuron L2 norm of its correlation row -> gini_pearson_x/y. Observed: gini_x min 0.024 median 0.416 max 0.884; gini_y min 0.079 median 0.471 max 0.968; triangle means by epoch gini_x 0.442/0.486/0.462 and gini_y 0.540/0.458/0.476 (naive/int/expert) — flat.
- **Inputs.** full-window partial-out residual + in-sample CCA weights
- **Outputs.** gini_x, gini_y in epoch_metrics.csv; per-neuron contrib in epoch_weights.csv (9431 rows). gini_pearson_x/y ARE COMPUTED BUT NEVER SAVED — the driver does not record them, so the CCA-independent control is unavailable on disk.
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** neuron within cell (Gini) then cell
- **Soundness.** The Gini implementation and the Pearson control are both well-designed and unit-tested (including a sample-size-invariance test for the noise floor). Two problems in the live path: the control is computed and thrown away; and the weight matrix is numerically unstable in a minority of cells because cca_fit uses rank_tol=1e-9, so near-zero PCA singular values are kept and the coefficients blow up. Measured on disk: 17 rows of epoch_weights.csv have contrib > 1e3 with a maximum of 6.43e8, concentrated in 3 cells (A4 DMS-ACC intermediate DMS; A14 DMS-ACC naive and expert ACC); the 99.9th percentile of contrib is 1.85e8 against a median of 0.24.
- **Concerns.**
    - gini_pearson_x/y computed in window_subspace but not emitted by run_epochs.py:111-121 — the headline's own control is missing from disk
    - rank_tol=1e-9 in core.cca_fit (core.py:150) admits near-null PCA directions; 3 cells have canonical weights of order 1e8, which also contaminates the rotation analysis that reads the same weights
    - Gini of an L2 norm over d dims has a noise floor set by d and by the partner unit count (documented in the module), and d varies 4-20 across cells (k_eff median 17, range 5-20), so absolute Gini is not comparable across cells
    - member_q=0.75 fixes the member set at 25% of units by construction, so Jaccard has a fixed expected value under the null

#### 11.6 Cross-epoch subspace rotation vs the within-window split-half floor
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/runner.py` lines 73-111; subspace_window.py 155-196, 251 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary null, stated as inconclusive rather than as a demonstrated absence of reorientation*

- **Question.** Does the communication subspace reorient across learning beyond within-epoch sampling noise?
- **Method.** Rotation: for two epochs' full-window fits, qa = QR(wa[:, :d]), qb = QR(wb[:, :d]), rot = degrees(max(scipy.linalg.subspace_angles(qa,qb))) with d=1 (rot_*_cc1) and d=3 (rot_*_top3), computed separately per side (x, y) in neuron space. Floor (_split_half_angles): ONE random split of the window's unique trial ids (default_rng(seed+11=11).permutation, h1 = first half); each half must have >= 3*(d_use+1)=12 rows; per half, PCA(k=min(20,n_units)) and cca_fit are refit on that half of the FULL-WINDOW partial-out residual; weights back-projected to neuron space; floor = max principal angle between the two halves' weight matrices, at d_use=3 (split_half_x/y) and d=1 (split_half_*_cc1). cross_window sets floor_*_cc1 = nanmean of the two epochs' CC1 floors. Reorientation criterion = rot > floor. TRANSITIONS = naive->intermediate, intermediate->expert, naive->expert.
- **Inputs.** two WindowSubspace fits per (animal, pair, transition)
- **Outputs.** results/epoch_cross.csv (124 rows; animal, pair, transition, k_eff, rot_x_cc1, rot_y_cc1, floor_x_cc1, floor_y_cc1, rot_x_top3, rot_y_top3, jaccard_x, jaccard_y)
- **Statistics.** None scripted. I reproduced the recorded ad-hoc statistics exactly from epoch_cross.csv: striatal-triangle per-animal mean of (rot-floor) over both sides, n=10, mean +1.92 deg, median +1.03 deg, Wilcoxon one-sided p=0.385, t one-sided p=0.265; dropping A10 (+22.44) gives mean -0.36; per-animal values span -16.48 to +22.44 (all-pairs n=11 mean -0.24). Side-level triangle 78/140 = 55.7% above floor, binomial p=0.102; all-pairs 151/248 = 60.9%.
- **Inferential unit.** as coded, the (animal, pair, transition, side) row; the defensible unit is the animal
- **Soundness.** The floor-referenced design is the right idea, but as coded the test is close to uninformative and is biased AGAINST detecting rotation. (1) Ceiling saturation: rot_x_cc1 median 77.1 deg, rot_y_cc1 median 78.9 deg, floor_x_cc1 median 74.1, floor_y_cc1 median 72.4, rot_*_top3 median 85.9/86.6 deg against a 90 deg ceiling. Both signal and floor sit near orthogonality, so rot-floor has almost no dynamic range and the top-3 readout is fully saturated. (2) Sample-size asymmetry: the rotation compares two fits on ~10 trials each, while the floor compares two fits on ~5 trials each, so the floor over-estimates the noise of the quantity it gates — a systematic conservative bias. (3) The floor is a SINGLE split (subspace.split_half_angles averages 10 splits and is unused), so per-cell floor noise adds variance to rot-floor. (4) 'max principal angle' over d=3 is upward-biased whenever any one dim is noise — the package's own test asserts split_half_x > 60 deg for a rank-1 truth. (5) The rotation reads the same in-sample weights that blow up to 1e8 in 3 cells. NOTES.md calls this 'a powered null, not a p-floor' on the grounds that the n=10 one-sided Wilcoxon floor is 0.001; that is true of the test, but power also requires an unbiased, unsaturated measurement, and neither holds.
- **Concerns.**
    - floor fitted on half the trials of the rotation it gates -> conservative bias of unknown size
    - single split-half draw per window (n_splits=1) where the library offers 10
    - rot and floor both near the 90 deg ceiling; top-3 rotation median 86 deg is saturated
    - in-sample weights with rank_tol=1e-9; 3 cells carry 1e8-scale coefficients
    - pseudoreplication if sides/transitions/pairs are counted as n (the 61% all-pairs figure is manufactured by eight single-animal pairs, correctly caught in NOTES)
    - no scripted test; the recorded p-values exist only in prose

#### 11.7 Configured surrogate null (build_null: per-trial circshift / trial permutation with CV refit)
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/surrogate.py` lines 29-102 · **🟠 major** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *methods-only (as the null that ought to be used); currently drop*

- **Question.** Per-dimension held-out-CC significance against a properly constructed null.
- **Method.** permute_trials or circshift_bins(tensor, rng, min_shift=cfg.circshift_min_bins=15) applied per trial to the 3-D (trials,bins,k) tensor; core.cca_cv refit per surrogate over cfg.n_shuffles=100 with cfg.surrogate_seed=0; p_value = (1 + sum(null >= real)) / (1 + n_null); n_significant = sum(p < alpha=0.05).
- **Inputs.** 3-D score tensors — a shape the temporal path never produces
- **Outputs.** none (never called outside tests)
- **Statistics.** one-sided permutation p with +1/+1 correction; p-floor = 1/101 = 0.0099 at 100 shuffles
- **Inferential unit.** canonical dimension
- **Soundness.** This is the null the config documents and the one the epoch results should be using: per-trial rolls with a >=15-bin minimum shift, applied to a cross-validated statistic. It cannot be used by the temporal path as written because it requires a (trials, bins, k) tensor, whereas the temporal streams are variable-length traversals concatenated into a flat timeline. The live path's ad-hoc replacement (subspace_window._significance) is weaker in every respect. Porting this to the flat/grouped representation is the highest-value fix in the package.
- **Concerns.**
    - config.py advertises null_type, circshift_min_bins, n_shuffles, surrogate_seed as live knobs; none of them reach the epoch results
    - the p-floor of 1/101 at 100 shuffles would matter if it were used with FDR over 20 dims

#### 11.8 Temporal stream construction: Gaussian smoothing, time-binning, derived velocity, running gate
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/dataio.py` lines 238-397 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** What is the per-bin activity matrix the temporal CCA is fitted on?
- **Method.** Per traversal: 1 ms corridorData.binned_spikes -> scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter1d(sigma=2.5 ms, axis=0, mode='nearest') -> reshape/sum into temporal_bin_ms bins (25 ms as run by the driver; config default 10 ms); incomplete final bin dropped. Traversals with 0 bins or > temporal_max_trial_ms/bin_ms (60000/25 = 2400 bins) contribute no bins but still consume their trial index. Velocity: trial_position (a.u.) and trial_times (ms) re-zeroed to corridor onset, sorted, np.interp onto bin centres (bin_ms*i + bin_ms/2), *AU_TO_CM=1.25, np.abs(np.gradient(pos_cm, bin_ms/1000)); bins with no usable position -> 0 (fail the gate). running_mask = ~isnan(trial_idx) & vel >= velocity_thresh_cm_s(2.0). Per-unit z-score over the running+in-trial reference of the WHOLE engaged period (zscore_over_reference; sd<=0 -> 1.0). Unit selection: area mask AND neurontypes[:,4] != 2 (FS excluded).
- **Inputs.** preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat (1.2 GB, mtime 2026-05-23): corridorData.binned_spikes / trial_position / trial_times, is_dms/is_dls/is_acc/is_v1/is_ca1/is_dg, final_neurontypes, change_point_mean, n_trials
- **Outputs.** in-memory TemporalStreams (1-slot cache keyed on animal/group/bin_ms/sigma/period); nothing saved
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** time bin (nested in trial, nested in animal)
- **Soundness.** Structurally correct and unit-tested (mass conservation of the Gaussian, velocity ramp recovery, re-zeroing, over-long trial index preservation). Two real issues: (a) the per-unit z-score reference is fitted on ALL running bins of the whole engaged period, i.e. across every CV fold and every epoch, so the standardisation is not inside the CV loop; (b) smoothing with sigma=2.5 ms then summing into 25 ms bins is nearly a no-op (sigma << bin), so the 'smoothed spike density' step does essentially nothing at the bin width actually run.
- **Concerns.**
    - scaler leak: z-score mean/sd fitted on all data including held-out folds (dataio.py:372-380, runner.py:43). Mild because CCA is scale-invariant and only the PCA weighting is affected, but it is a genuine standardise-before-split
    - sigma=2.5 ms smoothing is negligible relative to the 25 ms bin actually used; the report-faithful claim only bites at 10 ms
    - velocity failure mode is silent: a trial with unusable position/time yields vel=0 for every bin and is therefore silently dropped by the running gate rather than flagged
    - np.gradient at the first/last bin is one-sided, so edge bins have a different noise scale

#### 11.9 Per-cell temporal (p)CCA held-out CC1 — the strength headline
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/subspace_window.py` lines 72-105, 199-223 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure (with medians + per-animal points, striatal triangle only)*

- **Question.** How strongly do two areas' running-bin population activities co-fluctuate within a learning epoch, and does that change with learning?
- **Method.** Per (animal, pair, epoch): X = present[ax][mask], Y = present[ay][mask] on the epoch's running bins (mask = isin(trial_ids_run, window trials)); Z = every OTHER present area concatenated column-wise (up to 226 units). _heldout_perdim_cv: folds = np.array_split(default_rng(seed=cv_seed=0).permutation(unique trial ids), 5) -> ~2 trials per test fold from a 10-trial epoch. Per fold, on TRAINING trials only: partial.partial_out_cv(X,Z,tr) and (Y,Z,tr) via np.linalg.lstsq; PCA (SVD, kx=min(K=20, n_units_x), ky likewise) fitted on train rows; core.cca_fit (SVD-based, rank_tol=1e-9) on train scores; core.cca_score projects held-out rows and takes Pearson r per canonical dim. cc = nanmean over folds, truncated to the shortest fold. Driver keeps cc1 = cc[0]; drops the cell if cc1 non-finite or >= SAT=0.99, or if the cell has < MIN_CELL_BINS = K*30 = 600 running bins.
- **Inputs.** runner.build_present output (z-scored, run-masked per-area activity); epoch trial windows
- **Outputs.** results/epoch_metrics.csv (125 rows; cols animal, role, lp, pair, epoch, n_bins, n_units_x, n_units_y, n_units_z, k_eff, cc1, n_sig, mi_sig, ifi, optimal_lag, gini_x, gini_y, sh_x_cc1, sh_y_cc1)
- **Statistics.** held-out (leak-free per fold for Z-regression, PCA and CCA). No test performed inside the driver — run_epochs.py writes CSVs only and imports no statistics library. All recorded p-values were produced ad hoc; analyze_epochs.py does not exist.
- **Inferential unit.** as coded, the (animal, pair, epoch) cell; the only defensible unit is the animal
- **Soundness.** The CV is genuinely leak-free in the three preprocessing steps that matter (confound regression, PCA, CCA all train-only) — this is the strongest part of the package. Effect sizes are modest and right-skewed: over 125 cells cc1 min -0.354, median 0.111, mean 0.156, max 0.800, with 19/125 negative. The striatal triangle reproduces the recorded means exactly (DMS-DLS 0.248/0.297/0.190, DMS-ACC 0.170/0.185/0.189, DLS-ACC 0.216/0.134/0.301 for naive/int/expert) but the medians are much lower (DMS-DLS 0.148/0.268/0.092, DLS-ACC 0.182/0.017/0.201, DMS-ACC 0.214/0.186/0.136). Reporting means on n=7 right-skewed cells overstates the typical animal.
- **Concerns.**
    - 5 folds over a 10-trial epoch = 2 test trials per fold; the held-out estimate is high-variance and the fold-mean can be negative
    - per-unit z-scoring is fitted outside the CV loop (see stream construction)
    - Z has up to 226 columns regressed out of ~3000 training bins; the residual is over-fitted in the descriptive (full-window) path even though the CV path is honest
    - cc1 is a signed fold-mean; averaging signed values across animals mixes 'weak coupling' with 'direction did not generalise'
    - pair backing is grossly unequal: DMS-ACC 10 animals, DLS-ACC 7, DMS-DLS 7, V1-ACC/V1-DMS 3, CA1-V1/V1-DLS 2, and the other eight pairs 1 animal each. Any pooled statistic over pairs is dominated by n=1 pairs
    - no statistical test is scripted anywhere in the repo; every recorded p-value is unreproducible from a committed driver

#### 11.10 Gaussian-MI strength surrogate over significant dims (mi_sig)
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/subspace_window.py` lines 223-229 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *drop (redundant with cc1 + n_sig)*

- **Question.** Total communicated information across the significant subspace dims.
- **Method.** cc_clip = clip(cc, 0.0, CC_CLIP=0.999); if n_sig>0: s = cc_clip[sig] restricted to finite and >0; mi_sig = -0.5 * sum(log1p(-s**2)) nats; else 0.0. Observed: min 0, median 0.026, mean 0.121, max 3.150 over 125 cells.
- **Inputs.** held-out cc + sig mask
- **Outputs.** mi_sig in epoch_metrics.csv
- **Statistics.** none (derived quantity; inherits n_sig's untested threshold)
- **Inferential unit.** cell
- **Soundness.** Formula is the standard Gaussian MI surrogate and correctly floors negative held-out CCs. But it is a deterministic monotone function of n_sig and cc, so it inherits every defect of the significance threshold and adds no independent evidence; 53/125 cells are exactly 0 by construction, making the distribution a zero-inflated mixture that no paired test handles cleanly.
- **Concerns.**
    - zero-inflated by construction (n_sig=0 -> exactly 0.0), so means/medians across animals are not interpretable
    - fully determined by the n_sig threshold defect

#### 11.11 Membership turnover (Jaccard) across epochs
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/membership.py` lines 120-125; runner.py 109-110 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary, only with an explicit chance level*

- **Question.** Do the same neurons stay in the communication subspace across learning?
- **Method.** jaccard(member_a, member_b) = |A and B| / |A or B| on the top-quartile (member_q=0.75) contribution masks. Observed: jaccard_x median 0.29 mean 0.26, jaccard_y median 0.22 mean 0.26, range 0-1 over 124 rows.
- **Inputs.** member masks from the two epochs' full-window fits
- **Outputs.** jaccard_x, jaccard_y in epoch_cross.csv
- **Statistics.** none, and no null baseline is computed
- **Inferential unit.** cell/side
- **Soundness.** Because member_q is a fixed 0.75 quantile, each mask marks ~25% of units, and the expected Jaccard for two independent 25% draws is ~0.14. Observed medians of 0.22-0.29 are only modestly above that, but no chance level is computed anywhere, so the numbers cannot be interpreted as turnover without a permutation baseline.
- **Concerns.**
    - no null/chance baseline computed for Jaccard
    - masks derived from the same unstable in-sample weights

#### 11.12 Per-dimension table (dims-as-n reporting) and per-neuron weight table
`Striatum project/tcca/scripts/run_epochs.py` lines 123-135 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *supplementary / audit table*

- **Question.** How does held-out CC, significance, IFI and peak lag distribute across canonical dimensions, and how concentrated are per-neuron contributions?
- **Method.** One row per (animal, pair, epoch, dim) with dim 1..d, peak_cc = cc[d], sig flag, per-dim ifi and lag. One row per (animal, pair, epoch, area, unit) with contrib = L2 norm of that unit's weight row.
- **Inputs.** WindowSubspace fields
- **Outputs.** results/epoch_dims.csv (1681 rows; dims per cell mean 13.45, median 16, range 4-20; peak_cc median 0.012, min -1.0, max 0.991; sig rate 0.107). results/epoch_weights.csv (9431 rows; contrib median 0.240, max 6.43e8).
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** canonical dimension / neuron (both nested in cell in animal)
- **Soundness.** Correctly labelled 'dims-as-n reported-not-inferential' in NOTES — dims within a cell are not independent draws and must never be an inferential n. The median per-dim held-out CC of 0.012 confirms that nearly all of the 20 dims are noise, which is the useful message. peak_cc min of exactly -1.0 indicates at least one degenerate fold-mean that should be screened.
- **Concerns.**
    - a peak_cc of exactly -1.0 is a degenerate fit that is not screened by the SAT=0.99 guard (which only tests cc1 >= 0.99, not <= -0.99)
    - if dims are ever used as n the analysis is pseudoreplicated by a factor of ~13

#### 11.13 core CV / PCA / k-selection primitives not used by the temporal driver
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/core.py` lines 102-133, 240-370 · **🟡 minor** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** n/a — infrastructure
- **Method.** cca_cv (5-fold whole-trial CV on 3-D tensors, trial_folds via interleaved permutation with cfg.cv_seed=0), choose_k (k_mode 'samples' -> n_samples//samples_per_pc=15, 'fixed' -> 10, 'variance' -> 0.90 cumulative; capped by unit counts, k_cap=30 and numerical rank), pca_fit/pca_transform, numerical_rank(rel_tol=1e-7), k_for_variance, zscore_units.
- **Inputs.** 3-D (trials, bins, units) tensors
- **Outputs.** none in the temporal path
- **Statistics.** n/a
- **Inferential unit.** n/a
- **Soundness.** All well-tested against synthetic ground truth (known rho recovery to 0.03, invariance to invertible mixing, rank-deficiency handling, NaN-row dropping). But the temporal driver bypasses them entirely: it hardcodes K=20 in run_epochs.py:27 instead of calling choose_k, and it uses subspace_window's own flat-array PCA/CV helpers instead of core.cca_cv. Consequence: the samples-per-PC discipline the report specifies is not enforced. Measured effective dimensionality: k_eff = min(20, n_units_x, n_units_y) has median 17 and range 5-20, with n_bins median 4141 -> roughly 240 samples per PC at the median but as few as ~150 in the smallest cells, and it varies by a factor of 4 across cells being compared to each other.
- **Concerns.**
    - K=20 hardcoded; cfg.k_mode/k_fixed/k_variance/samples_per_pc/k_cap are all dead in the temporal path
    - k_eff varies 5-20 across cells that are pooled in the same contrast; cc1 magnitude is dimensionality-dependent, so this is a confound for cross-pair comparison (the driver does record k_eff, which makes it auditable)

#### 11.14 Segment-aware held-out lag curve and IFI window sweep
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/lagged.py` lines 54-66, 94-142, 145-205 · **🟡 minor** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *methods-only until a driver exists*

- **Question.** Direction of information flow, measured honestly and without trial-boundary contamination.
- **Method.** _segment_lagged_pairs pairs bins within a trial only, dropping the |lag| bins that would cross a boundary; heldout_lag_curve_flat splits the lagged pairs into whole-trial folds (default_rng(seed=0), 5 folds), fits CCA on train, reads dominant CC on test, averages over folds; ifi_by_window computes IFI over progressively wider windows |lag| <= w; lag_curve offers held_out=True with cfg.max_lag_bins=5 (=+/-50 ms at 10 ms).
- **Inputs.** flat (n_samples, k) scores + per-bin trial ids
- **Outputs.** none — no run_ifi_windows.py driver exists
- **Statistics.** held-out; no null
- **Inferential unit.** cell
- **Soundness.** This is the correct implementation of the directionality readout (unit-tested for known-lead recovery and for no-cross-trial-pairing), and it is strictly better than the in-sample, boundary-crossing curve the live driver actually uses. Its absence from the pipeline is why the IFI result is an untested near-zero.
- **Concerns.**
    - NOTES.md Stage 3 plans run_ifi_windows (10 ms, +/-250 ms); nothing has been built

#### 11.15 Averaged split-half principal-angle noise floor (10 splits)
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/subspace.py` lines 44-88 · **🟡 minor** · status: `superseded` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** What cross-epoch principal angle is expected from sampling noise alone?
- **Method.** n_splits=10 (default) random half-splits of the trial axis, cca_fit per half, canonical_weights back-projected through each area's PCA loadings, principal_angles per split, mean over splits, returned as the full ascending angle vector (not just the max).
- **Inputs.** 3-D score tensors + PCA components
- **Outputs.** none
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** cell
- **Soundness.** Strictly better than the single-split, max-angle floor used live: it averages 10 draws and returns the whole angle spectrum rather than the upward-biased maximum. Superseded in practice by subspace_window._split_half_angles, which is the weaker version. Note that neither corrects the deeper problem that the floor is estimated at half the sample size of the rotation it gates.
- **Concerns.**
    - the live path uses the weaker single-split max-angle variant instead

#### 11.16 Kernel (RBF) CCA and the KCCA per-cell window readout
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/kernel_cca.py` lines 57-210; kcca_window.py 34-166 · **🟡 minor** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *drop unless a driver is built; then supplementary*

- **Question.** Is cross-area coupling nonlinear — does KCCA beat linear CCA on the same held-out folds?
- **Method.** Kernel: RBF only (sklearn rbf_kernel). Bandwidth: median heuristic gamma = 1/(2*median pairwise squared distance), sub-sampled to max_n=1000 rows with seed=0, computed ONCE per cell on the full-window PCA scores (kcca_window.py:120-121) and then held fixed for every fold, every surrogate and every lag. Regularisation: a FIXED ridge reg=10.0 on the centred Gram matrices (kcca_window default), reg<=0 rejected; explicitly no per-cell ridge selection, justified as an optimism-free comparison to linear. Solver: Hardoon et al. dual formulation, top-d eigenpairs of Ax^-1 Ky Ay^-1 Kx via matrix-free ARPACK (scipy.sparse.linalg.eigs, k=d, which='LR', maxiter=20n) with a dense scipy.linalg.eig fallback; beta = rho^-1 Ay^-1 Kx alpha with rho guarded at 1e-6. HELD-OUT SCORING: yes — _heldout runs 5 whole-trial folds, partials out Z per fold on training rows (partial_out_cv), refits PCA (kx,ky = min(k=30, n_units)) on train, fits KCCA on train scores and scores test rows via train-centred cross-kernels; the LINEAR CC is computed on the SAME folds and a fold counts toward both means only if both estimators return dd dims. dd = min(d=3, kx, ky). Significance: circular-shift null on ONE 70/30 split (cut = int(0.7n)), n_shuffles=20, 95th percentile of the shuffled held-out dominant KCCA CC. Direction: kcca_lagged_heldout over lags +/-max_lag=6 on a single 70/30 whole-group split (rng seed+5, test fraction 0.3). Membership: structure coefficients (variate_structure_coefficients) from a full-window fit, since KCCA has no neuron-space weights.
- **Inputs.** would be runner.build_present output
- **Outputs.** none — no run_kcca.py driver exists; NOTES lists it as Stage 4
- **Statistics.** held-out per-fold CC for both estimators on matched folds; single-split 95th-percentile circshift threshold for n_sig; no test of the KCCA-minus-linear delta
- **Inferential unit.** cell (would be animal for any group claim)
- **Soundness.** Design is careful and honest where it matters: the ridge is mandatory (unregularised KCCA is degenerate at correlation 1), scoring is genuinely out-of-sample through train-centred cross-kernels, and the linear baseline shares the folds so the nonlinearity delta is fair. Tests confirm it recovers nonlinear coupling that linear CCA misses, is near zero on independent data, and that reg controls in-sample saturation. Weak points if it is ever run: reg=10.0 is an unvalidated single value with no sensitivity analysis; the bandwidth is fitted on the FULL window including test rows (a mild leak in a hyperparameter); n_shuffles=20 gives a 95th percentile with resolution 1/20; and both the significance null and the whole directionality curve rest on ONE 70/30 split, so n_sig and IFI are single-draw statistics.
- **Concerns.**
    - reg=10.0 fixed with no sensitivity sweep; the KCCA-vs-linear delta is only interpretable relative to that choice
    - median_gamma computed on the full window (test rows included) — hyperparameter leak
    - n_sig from 20 shuffles on a single 70/30 split; IFI from a single split
    - bare `except Exception` in kcca_fit's ARPACK path, in kcca_lagged_heldout, in _heldout, in _significance and around the membership fit — failures are silently absorbed into NaN or 0.0 with no count reported

#### 11.17 Mixed-effects epoch contrasts and the collapsed per-animal companion
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/mixed_effects.py` lines 35-214 · **🟡 minor** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *methods-only until wired in; then this should be the inferential engine for every epoch claim*

- **Question.** Does a subspace metric change across naive/intermediate/expert, with animal as the experimental unit?
- **Method.** lmm_epoch_contrasts: formula `value ~ C(epoch, Treatment(ref))` plus `+ C(landmark)` when a landmark column with >1 level is present; RANDOM EFFECTS = a random SLOPE on epoch per animal, re_formula = `~ C(epoch, Treatment(ref))`, groups = animal_id; statsmodels smf.mixedlm fitted with reml=False, method='lbfgs'. Contrasts computed as linear combinations of the fixed-effect vector with variance vec.T @ cov_fe @ vec restricted to the fixed-effect block; two-sided Wald p from the normal (2*norm.sf(|z|)), not a t or Satterthwaite df. Identifiability guard: rejects the fit when n_animals <= k*(k+1)/2 for k epoch levels (6 for k=3, so >=7 animals required) and MIN_ANIMALS=3. lmm_slope: `value ~ axis` with re_formula `~axis`, requires >=4 animals and >=3 distinct axis values. collapsed_epoch_contrasts: mean per (animal, epoch), per-animal deltas, paired_stats.wilcoxon_signed. DEFAULT_CONTRASTS = expert-naive, expert-intermediate, intermediate-naive.
- **Inputs.** records with value / animal_id / epoch (+ optional landmark)
- **Outputs.** none — never called by any driver in this package
- **Statistics.** Wald z on LMM fixed-effect contrasts (response = the metric; inferential unit = animal via the random slope); Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-animal deltas in the collapsed companion. No multiple-comparison correction across the 3 contrasts or across pairs — the caller must apply paired_stats.fdr_bh.
- **Inferential unit.** animal (that is the explicit design intent of the random slope)
- **Soundness.** This is the statistically correct machinery and it is unusually well guarded: the docstring explains why a random INTERCEPT alone would re-pseudoreplicate the repeated measures, and the code refuses to fit when the RE covariance is unidentifiable (the exact failure mode that silently produces anti-conservative Wald p-values). Tests cover a real per-animal effect, a null, a zero-mean-with-per-animal-slopes case, insufficient animals, degenerate fits, and the n=4 Wilcoxon p-floor of 0.125. Two caveats: the `landmark` term is a TomLearning/spatial-arm concept with no analogue in the striatum temporal data (pass landmark=None); and the >=7-animal requirement for a 3-epoch random slope means the striatal triangle (7-10 animals) sits right at the identifiability boundary — DMS-DLS and DLS-ACC with exactly 7 animals would pass the guard by one animal.
- **Concerns.**
    - never called: no analyze_epochs.py exists, so all recorded epoch statistics were computed ad hoc outside the repo
    - no multiple-comparison correction inside the function; fdr_bh must be applied by the caller across contrasts x pairs
    - Wald z (normal) rather than a t/Satterthwaite approximation is anti-conservative at n=7-10 animals
    - the 7-animal identifiability threshold is only just met by the largest striatal pairs

#### 11.18 Per-cell subspace aggregation across canonical dimensions (MI, mean/weighted IFI)
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/subspace_stats.py` lines 53-175 · **🟡 minor** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *drop*

- **Question.** Aggregate strength and directionality across all/significant canonical dims rather than reading dim 1 only.
- **Method.** _aggregate: peak_cc = clip(strength_cc, 0, CC_CLIP=0.999); sig = finite(p) & (p < alpha=0.05); mi_all/mi_sig = -0.5*sum(log1p(-cc^2)) over all / significant dims; ifi_mean_all/ifi_mean_sig; ifi_weighted = sum(IFI*cc)/sum(cc). cell_subspace_stats takes strength as peak-across-lag (nanmax over the lag axis of lag_cc_per_dim); epoch_subspace_stats takes lag-0 held_out_cc with p_per_dim. per_dim_long_form emits one row per (cell x dim).

- **Outputs.** none

- **Soundness.** The formulas are right (negative held-out CC floored at 0, CC clipped below 1 to keep the log finite — both unit-tested). But it is an orphan in this package: it duck-types on attributes (lag_cc_per_dim, p_peak_cc_per_dim, ifi_per_dim, held_out_cc, r.cells, r.area_x) that belong to the sibling spatial package's analysis containers, and nothing in striatum_tcca ever constructs them. #### 11.19 Within-animal learning trajectory (sliding-window CC1 vs trial fraction)
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/trajectory.py` lines 24-110 · **🟡 minor** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *drop until built; the sliding-window slope is the right way to buy power at n=10 animals*

- **Question.** Does the communication subspace change monotonically across the session, using within-animal windows for power instead of a 3-epoch contrast?
- **Method.** sliding_windows(unique_trials, window, step, min_window) keeps a trailing partial window only if it still holds min_window trials. heldout_cc1: whole-group (trial) 5-fold CV, per fold kk = min(k=30, n_units_x, n_units_y, n_train-1), PCA per fold on train only, cca_fit on train scores, returns (mean test cc1, mean train cc1) so the optimism gap is visible. linear_slope returns OLS slope and Pearson r with pairwise NaN dropping. Intended design: one slope per animal, then a sign-consistency/LMM test across animals.
- **Inputs.** flat (n_bins, n_units) activity + per-bin trial ids
- **Outputs.** none — no run_trajectory.py driver exists
- **Statistics.** held-out CC per window; the across-animal test is not implemented here (NOTES intends lmm_slope or a sign test)
- **Inferential unit.** animal (via one slope per animal); windows within an animal are NOT independent
- **Soundness.** The two design choices that matter are right: folds hold out whole trials, and both test and train cc1 are returned so in-sample optimism can be reported. Note that heldout_cc1 does NOT partial out Z (no confound argument), unlike the epoch path, so a trajectory result would not be comparable to the epoch cc1 without adding it. Sliding windows overlap when step < window, which makes per-window values serially correlated — fine for a per-animal slope, fatal if windows are ever treated as n.
- **Concerns.**
    - no partial-out of other areas, so trajectory cc1 is not on the same footing as epoch cc1
    - overlapping windows are serially correlated; only the per-animal slope is a valid unit
    - a per-animal OLS slope over overlapping windows has an understated standard error if it is ever used directly

#### 11.20 Very-early-trial projected readout (first N trials)
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/early_trials.py` lines 46-144 · **🟡 minor** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *drop until built; then supplementary*

- **Question.** What is the coupling on the very first trials (trial 1 vs 4 vs 7 vs 10), where a subspace cannot be refitted?
- **Method.** Definition: 'early' = individual trials with too few bins to refit a subspace (~500-1150 running bins each vs the ~1500 needed for 30 components at ~50 samples/PC). reference_fit fits the whole pipeline — partial_out_cv(Z), PCA (k=min(30, n_units)), cca_fit — on train_mask = the animal's LATER (reference) trials ONLY, then projects EVERY row onto that subspace, so the early trials are held out of every fitting step. Per early trial: trial_cc = core.cca_score dominant r on that trial's bins (signed); trial_ifi = IFI over lags +/-max_lag=10 computed on the dominant variate pair WITHIN the trial only (no boundary crossing), via np.corrcoef, requiring >=10 paired points and non-zero variance; trial_participation_gini = Gini of each neuron's |Pearson r| with the dominant variate within that trial. Trials with < min_bins=10 bins return all-NaN. Explicitly out of scope for the single-trial path and deferred to an 'early-BLOCK' path (>=5-trial blocks): held-out CV CC, n_sig, weight-Gini, rotation angles, KCCA.
- **Inputs.** flat activity + trial ids + the early/train trial split
- **Outputs.** none — no run_early_trials.py driver exists (NOTES Stage 4)
- **Statistics.** none; leak-free by construction (early trials excluded from the fit)
- **Inferential unit.** trial within animal (a per-trial time series; the across-animal unit must be the animal)
- **Soundness.** The purpose is well posed and the leak-freeness is explicit and unit-tested (test_reference_fit_is_leak_free). The honest limitation — that fit-only metrics cannot be read from one trial — is stated in the module docstring rather than papered over, which is the right call. Two structural cautions: the reference subspace is fitted on LATER trials, so an apparent rise in early-trial cc1 across trials 1..10 is partly convergence toward the late-trial subspace rather than a change in coupling (the direction of that bias must be stated); and per-trial cc1 from ~500 bins on a fixed 30-dim direction is noisy, with no null.
- **Concerns.**
    - reference subspace defined on late trials makes 'early trials are less coupled' partly tautological — needs a matched-length late-trial control read through the same fit
    - no null for per-trial cc1 or per-trial Gini
    - N is not fixed in code: the early/train split is the caller's choice and no driver pins it

#### 11.21 Within-area subspace consistency across partners (crosspair)
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/crosspair.py` lines 20-92 · **🟡 minor** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *drop*

- **Question.** Does one area use the same communication subspace to talk to its different partners?
- **Method.** |cosine| similarity between an area's dominant canonical weight vector (weights_x[:,0] or weights_y[:,0]) in pair A vs pair B, computed WITHIN an animal (correctly — the vectors live in that animal's neuron space), accumulated and averaged across animals; returns (mean matrix, per-cell animal count matrix); mean_pairwise takes the mean of finite off-diagonal entries. Absolute value used because canonical sign is arbitrary.

- **Statistics.** none — no null for |cos| between two vectors in n_units dimensions
- **Inferential unit.** animal (within-animal comparison, averaged over animals)
- **Soundness.** The within-animal restriction is exactly right and the sign handling is correct. Unusable here: it duck-types on PairSubspace containers that this package never builds, and NOTES explicitly defers test_crosspair to Stage 3 (its fixtures needed the sibling package's stage3 module), so this module is the ONE numeric module with no ported tests. Any similarity value also needs a chance level — E[|cos|] between random vectors is ~sqrt(2/(pi*n_units)), which is small but not zero and varies with unit count across pairs.
- **Concerns.**
    - no tests in this package (test_crosspair deferred, never written)
    - requires PairSubspace containers that striatum_tcca does not produce
    - no chance level for |cos|; the null depends on n_units, which differs across pairs

#### 11.22 Learning-point detection + cohort classification (yoked non-learners)
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/dataio.py` lines 111-164 · **🟢 ok** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** When does each animal start sustained learning, and which animals count as learners?
- **Method.** find_learning_point: below = zscored_lick_errors <= lp_z_threshold(-2.0); first 1-indexed trial t with below[t] AND sum(below[t:t+lp_window=10]) >= lp_min_consecutive(7). classify_cohort: learner = LP detected AND id not in manual_nonlearners(frozenset{8}); non-learners get yoked LP = round(mean of learner LPs). Verified on real Task cohort: 16 animals, 13 learners, yoked LP = 43; LPs = A1 22, A2 44, A3 32, A4 53, A5 54, A6 36, A7 34, A9 44, A10 67, A11 84, A13 23, A14 39, A15 26; A8 detected 14 but forced non-learner; A12/A16 no LP.
- **Inputs.** preprocessed_data.zscored_lick_errors per animal (behavioural trial axis)
- **Outputs.** in-memory CohortEntry; lp column echoed into epoch_metrics.csv
- **Statistics.** none (deterministic rule)
- **Inferential unit.** animal
- **Soundness.** Rule matches the corrected find_learning_points.m convention (returns a genuinely sub-threshold trial, not the window start). Behaviour-defined, so no circularity with the neural readout. NaN trials map to False via the <= comparison, which is the intended silent behaviour.
- **Concerns.**
    - manual_nonlearners={8} is a hand-set exclusion inherited from striatum_cca; it is a defensible but undocumented-in-code judgement call that must be declared in Methods
    - yoked LP=43 is computed over learners only, so it is data-dependent; irrelevant here because run_epochs uses learners only

#### 11.23 Paired per-animal Wilcoxon + BH-FDR helpers
`Striatum project/tcca/src/striatum_tcca/paired_stats.py` lines 14-59 · **🟢 ok** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** Is a per-animal delta consistently non-zero, with FDR control within a test family?
- **Method.** wilcoxon_signed: strips non-finite, reports n and median over the finite deltas, then strips ZERO deltas before scipy.stats.wilcoxon(alternative='two-sided', method='auto') and returns NaN unless >=3 non-zero deltas survive (so scipy never silently falls back to the invalid small-sample normal approximation). fdr_bh: standard BH step-up over finite p-values only, q=0.05 default, non-finite p excluded from the family and from n.
- **Inputs.** per-animal deltas
- **Outputs.** none directly; called by mixed_effects.collapsed_epoch_contrasts
- **Statistics.** exact two-sided signed-rank; two-sided p-floor at n=3 is 0.25, n=4 is 0.125, n=7 is 0.0156, n=10 is 0.002
- **Inferential unit.** animal
- **Soundness.** Correct and carefully built — the zero-stripping guard is a real trap that this handles explicitly, and the BH implementation excludes non-finite p from n rather than counting them. Matches the project convention (BH-FDR, p_FDR < 0.05).
- **Concerns.**
    - stripping zeros changes the effective n between the reported n and the tested n; callers must report both
    - small-n p-floors are the binding constraint for every striatal-triangle contrast (n=7 -> 0.0156), so any 'n.s.' is a power statement

#### 11.24 Data-layer smoke script (real-data sanity check)
`Striatum project/tcca/scripts/smoke_dataio.py` lines 21-84 · **🟢 ok** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** Do the 1 ms corridor read, derived velocity, running gate, cohort classification and period logic behave on real data?
- **Method.** Loads the cohort, prints per-animal role/raw LP/n_trials/change_point and FS-excluded unit counts per area, then streams the first learner with >= min_units in DMS and ACC at cfg defaults (10 ms, sigma 2.5) and prints total bins, traversal count, median in-trial speed, the fraction of bins retained by the >=2 cm/s gate, and the z-mean/z-sd of each area's activity restricted to running bins.
- **Inputs.** preprocessed_data{,_control}2p5cm.mat
- **Outputs.** stdout only
- **Statistics.** none
- **Inferential unit.** n/a
- **Soundness.** A genuine end-to-end sanity check of the kind the project conventions ask for, and it prints the diagnostics that matter (gate retention, z-scoring exactness, per-area yields). I re-derived its key numbers: 16 animals, 13 learners, yoked LP 43. At 25 ms the running gate retains 75% of bins for animal 1, 70% for animal 3, 80% for animal 15 and 55% for animal 13.
- **Concerns.**
    - prints but does not assert; it cannot fail a CI run

## 12. Python `striatum_lfp` package

*Full domain label:* Python `striatum_lfp` package — 384-channel Neuropixels voltage-export integrity audit and gated downstream LFP analyses (`Striatum project/lfp/`)

**Position in pipeline.** TERMINAL BRANCH — consumes, produces nothing consumed downstream. CONSUMES: `RawData/LFP/voltage_data_384ch.mat` (1212), `voltage_data_384ch 2.mat` (614), `voltage_data_384ch 3.mat` (727), `voltage_data_384ch 4.mat` (731) — mapped to mouse ONLY by file size via `RawData/LFP/lfp_mapping.txt` (1212=16.33GB, 614=11.38GB, 727=11.65GB, 731=11.48GB); `RawData/<ID>_raw.mat` (VR_data, VR_times_synched, binned_spikes, goodcluster2); `RawData/Neuropixels_Depth_Data.csv` (DMS/DLS/ACC boundaries, all 4 mice, 731 DLS blank); `RawData/Neuropixels_V1_Depth_Data.csv` (V1/CA1/DG, 1212 only); and via `../tcca/src/striatum_tcca` (dataio.load_animals/find_learning_point, config.DEFAULT.lp_z_threshold=-2.0) the cohort struct `processed_data/preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat`. PRODUCES: `lfp/results/sanity_summary.csv`, `sanity_timing_summary.csv`, `signal_identity_summary.csv`, `sanity_windows_<mouse>.csv`, `sanity_audit_<mouse>.npz`, `sanity_figure_examples_and_psd.npz`, `signal_identity_figure_data.npz`, `learning_evolution_summary.csv`, `decode_summary.csv`, `cca_summary.csv`; figures `sanity_audit_overview_v2`, `sanity_audit_raw_examples_v2`, `sanity_audit_event_timing`, `signal_identity`, `learning_evolution_{mouse}`, `learning_evolution_summary_animals`, `decode_position`, `cca_cross_area` (all png+svg). NOTHING DOWNSTREAM CONSUMES ANY OF IT: the promised MATLAB drop-in `.mat` is never written by any code in the package (grep: no writer exists), and `tcca` temporal CCA is never wired in (NOTES: "tcca temporal CCA not wired in"). DISK STATE 2026-07-30: every `results/*.csv` is ABSENT (gitignored and deleted); only the 6 `.npz` survive. So `sanity_summary.csv`/`sanity_timing_summary.csv`/`signal_identity_summary.csv` — the three files `results/README.md` calls "defensible integrity summaries" and that `test_cached_results.py` verifies — do not exist, and those 6 tests silently SKIP. `results/_quarantined_unaligned_learning/learning_evolution_summary.csv`, referenced by `results/README.md`, does not exist (no such directory). Reproduction chain is `run_sanity_audit.py` → `plot_sanity_audit.py` (reads the npz cache) → `run_signal_identity.py` (reads the npz cache); `run_learning_evolution.py` and `run_decode_cca.py` read the raw files directly and depend on nothing upstream in-package.

**Data flow, shapes and units.** FILE LAYOUT (verified by direct h5py inspection of all four files): HDF5 v7.3, exactly three datasets — `data_to_save` (n_samples × 384) float32, chunks (42, 384), gzip, fillvalue 0.0, only attr `MATLAB_class=b'single'`; `channels_to_save` (1, 384) float64 = 1.0…384.0; `depth_to_save` = for 1212 a populated (1, 384) float64 [0,0,20,20,…,3800,3800,3820,3820] i.e. exactly (c//2)*20, for 614/727/731 a uint64 shape-(2,) placeholder [0, 0]. NO file attrs, no fs field, no gain, no band label, no reference scheme, no sync channel, no timestamp vector, no mouse ID inside the file. n_samples = 11,400,000 (1212) and exactly 8,400,000 (614, 727, 731) — i.e. EXACTLY 11400.000 s and 8400.000 s at the assumed 1 kHz, and `binned_spikes` is (11400000, 54) / (8400000, 428) / (8400000, 252) / (8400000, 39). Both arrays being round-number-identical is a preallocation/truncation signature, so length equality is a construction artefact, not timing evidence. BEHAVIOUR: `VR_data` (n_frames × 10) with n_frames = 345,684 / 338,996 / 328,094 / 311,580; `VR_times_synched` in SECONDS spanning 652.259–10878.609 s (1212), 17.390–7217.267 (614), 10.017–7209.915 (727), 27.494–7227.347 (731); median frame dt 28.10 / 19.82 / 20.57 / 22.94 ms, max frame gap 12106.30 ms (1212!) vs 81–111 ms elsewhere. Code uses python cols 1=position a.u., 3=velocity, 4=world, 6=trial, 7=lick, 8="VR sync"; cols 4 and 8 are NOT in the documented data contract. Verified: col4 ∈ {6, 12} only (corridor/dark); col8 is binary 0/1 with 239 transitions at median interval 30.002 s (min 0.200, max 59.821) — a ~60 s square wave, so "nearest sync edge" draws on a 30 s-dense reference set. Position a.u.×AU_TO_CM=1.25; session max position 253.5 a.u. (614) and 200.4 (731), i.e. beyond the assumed 200 a.u./250 cm corridor. AUDIT GRID: 1 s windows (fs_hz*1=1000 samples), read in blocks of 42 windows = 42,000 samples; window counts 11,400 / 8,400 / 8,400 / 8,400. Behavioural-state occupancy (recomputed from the npz cache): corridor windows 786 / 2342 / 1851 / 380; dark 9441 / 4858 / 5349 / 6820; outside-behaviour 1173 / 1200 / 1200 / 1200 — corridor occupancy varies 6× across mice (1212 7%, 614 32.5%, 731 5.3% of behaviour). TRAVERSALS (recomputed): 156 / 469 / 371 / 76 valid corridor traversals; duration median 4.97 / 4.98 / 4.98 / 4.98 s with q25–q75 spanning <0.02 s and 614 min 4.96 max 4.99 across 469 traversals — the corridor epoch is a FIXED ~5 s time window, not a distance-terminated run. Within a traversal corr(position, time) has median r = 0.9991 (614) / 0.9941 (731). Max position reached per traversal (median) 72.5 / 197.5 / 159.0 / 62.6 cm, so at N_POS=20 (12.5 cm bins) only 6 / 16 / 13 / 6 of 20 bins are occupied per traversal and surviving decoder rows number 1028 / 7133 / 4867 / 384 with y SD 38.1 / 67.3 / 60.1 / 25.8 cm. SIGNAL-IDENTITY / PSD windows: 4000 samples (4 s) wide, 24 channels (arange(0, 384, 16)), 40 windows per mouse, Welch nperseg=min(2048, n), frequency resolution 0.4883 Hz. RAW-EXAMPLE windows: 4 s × 6 channels [10, 90, 160, 225, 300, 360].

**Cross-cutting notes.** ANSWERS TO THE SIX QUESTIONS.

(1) PROVENANCE. Unknown, verified by direct h5py inspection of all four files: physical UNITS and GAIN (only 'stored voltage units'; float32 with attr MATLAB_class='single' and nothing else); SOURCE BAND (LF 2.5 kHz .lf.bin / AP 30 kHz / wideband — undetermined, and the signal-identity result argues against LF); REFERENCING (no scheme recorded; the CMR test shows sensitivity is session- and frequency-specific, so raw is probably not common-referenced); FILTERING / RESAMPLING / ANTI-ALIAS (no ratio, no filter, no evidence of a lowpass — ΔSD/SD is 1.41-1.49 against a white expectation of 1.4142); SAMPLE-ZERO CONVENTION and VOLTAGE↔VR OFFSET (unknown to within seconds). The files contain exactly three datasets — data_to_save, channels_to_save = 1..384, depth_to_save — with no attrs, no fs, no sync channel, no timestamps, no mouse ID. No producer script exists in the repo and no source .meta is shipped. COVERAGE: 4 sessions, 4 animals, one session each — 1212, 614, 727, 731 — and the file↔mouse assignment is made ONLY by matching file size against RawData/LFP/lfp_mapping.txt (16.33 / 11.38 / 11.65 / 11.48 GB). Nothing inside any file identifies its animal; two of those sizes differ by 2%, so the mapping is itself an unverified inference. 384 channels = one probe: 614/727/731 have only probe 1 (striatal), so their LFP is striatal by elimination; 1212 had two probes and its LFP probe identity is unconfirmed, though 1212 is the only file with a populated depth_to_save (exactly (c//2)*20, depth-sorted). Two further provenance facts not recorded in the docs: n_samples is EXACTLY 8,400,000 for all three of 614/727/731 and EXACTLY 11,400,000 for 1212 (140.000 and 190.000 minutes), so the array length is a preallocated/truncated round nominal duration and its equality with binned_spikes is a construction artefact carrying no timing information; and the timing analysis treats VR_data python column 8 as the acquisition sync although that column is absent from the documented data contract (I measured it: binary, 239 transitions, median interval 30.002 s, i.e. a ~60 s square wave with glitch transitions down to 0.200 s).

(2) THE AUDIT — every diagnostic, with numbers reproduced verbatim from the surviving .npz caches (all published values checked out). Exact zeros over every stored value: 0.0044% (1212), 5.3429% (614), 3.1604% (727), 4.6162% (731). Power 1-100 Hz as a fraction of 1-499 Hz: 15.59% / 17.22% / 15.97% / 18.23% (white expectation 19.88%). Log-log PSD slope 2-40 Hz: +0.4621 / −0.4336 / −0.6598 / −0.9141. (3) GATED / QUARANTINED, and the exact gate condition. Learning evolution and the theta running-vs-stationary analysis: HARD-GATED by run_learning_evolution.py:383-387 — `if not args.allow_unaligned: raise SystemExit('Refusing learning analysis: voltage-to-VR offset and source band are unverified...')`. Additionally 1212 is excluded unconditionally (line 391) and low_gamma is dropped from BANDS (line 41). Its outputs are quarantined in figures/_quarantined_unaligned_learning/ (10 files). Stage-0 channel QC: HARD-DISABLED — run_stage0_probe.py is a 7-line `raise SystemExit`; its figures are in figures/_superseded_absolute_threshold/. Signal identity, sanity audit and its plots: UNGATED and intended to be (they are the audit). CRITICAL EXCEPTION: run_decode_cca.py — position decoding AND cross-area CCA — has NO GATE AT ALL. No --allow-unaligned flag, no SystemExit, no mouse exclusion (it runs 1212, which the learning driver refuses), and it includes the confounded low_gamma (30,80) band. It is the only script that crosses the README/SANITY_AUDIT gate silently, its figures decode_position.{png,svg} and cca_cross_area.{png,svg} sit in the TOP-LEVEL figures/ directory alongside the four defensible sanity figures, they are the NEWEST artefacts there (2026-07-13 09:26, after the 07:13 hardening commit be83541), and figures/README.md does not mention them at all — so the one directory a co-author would treat as 'the deliverables' contains two undocumented gate-crossing figures, one of which is a pure artefact.

(4) THE ALIGNMENT BLOCKER. To unblock, four things must be established (SANITY_AUDIT.md:99-104): the source stream (LF/AP/wideband) with gain and physical units; the referencing and every filtering/downsampling/anti-alias operation; the exact sample-zero convention and the voltage↔VR offset; and the identity of the 60 s and 5 s high-amplitude events. Practically: recover the producer script or the original SpikeGLX .lf.bin + .meta and re-export with the sync channel retained, documenting the complete transform. What the repository currently offers as evidence for alignment does not survive scrutiny. The length-equality argument is void because the lengths are exactly-round nominal durations. The event-timing argument gives median offsets of +1.98/+4.26/+1.74 s with no null against a 30 s-dense, undocumented reference channel. And the position-decoding argument — the only positive evidence, at NOTES.md:106-111 — I disproved directly: pure white noise through the exact same pipeline yields CV R² = +0.231 (614) and +0.499 (731), EXCEEDING the reported real-data R² of 0.12 and 0.17, and is declared 'above chance' by the driver's own shuffle rule. So there is at present NO evidence whatever bearing on the offset, and the honest position is that the offset uncertainty is bounded only by the several-second event-timing spread — comparable to the 4.98 s corridor epoch, which is exactly why trial and position analyses are blocked. One additional unblock requirement the docs do not list: the 1212 file↔mouse assignment and probe identity must be confirmed independently of file size, and the corridor-epoch structure must be checked against the 5 s event cadence (they coincide, which suggests 1212's events are task-locked rather than instrumental).

(5) MANUSCRIPT-USABLE NOW vs NEGATIVE/METHODS ONLY. Usable as stated, as a methods/negative result: the full-session continuity audit (exact zeros, zero runs, per-state occupancy) — reproducible, tested, and I verified every number; the periodic-event cadence and prevalence, with the 'unrelated to VR' clause removed for 1212; the common-median-referencing asymmetry; and the signal-identity conclusion FOR 614/727/731 ONLY, which is the strongest true finding in the domain — with ΔSD/SD of 1.41-1.49 against a white expectation of 1.4142 and 1-100 Hz power fractions below the white expectation, these exports are spectrally near-white to ~500 Hz and are NOT a low-passed LFP export. That is a clean, defensible negative result and I confirmed it is robust to event contamination (614 recomputed on strictly event-free windows: lag-1 −0.0536 vs −0.0526, slope −0.479 vs −0.434). Must be withdrawn or re-run before any presentation: 1212's entire signal-identity row and its 'ordinary corridor' figure panel (98% of its 4 s windows contain a z>5 event; its plotted 'ordinary' RMS is 1.81, ~7,900× the 2.3e-4 the same table reports; only 3 event-free 4 s corridor windows exist in the whole session, so its ordinary spectrum is unmeasurable at this window length). Must be dropped: position decoding (artefact, noise ceiling exceeds the result, chance reference wrong by 15-70% per mouse, 731 literally at its own chance level of 21.5 cm), the theta running/stationary result (its 1 s unit of analysis is smaller than the offset uncertainty), and the learning-phase contrasts (no statistics, n = 3 animals, confounded with engagement/arousal/drift by the authors' own admission). Salvageable with work: the cross-area CCA negative result (volume-conduction limited, nothing above the within-area ceiling) — the reasoning is right and it is immune to the edge-transient artefact because residualise_by_group removes any deterministic function of position bin, but it needs >= 1000 permutations instead of one, split-averaging instead of a hard-coded seed=0, and residualisation inside folds. Also note for the manuscript's reproducibility statement: every results/*.csv is gitignored and absent, so none of the published numbers is currently verifiable from the repository and the 6 tests that pin them silently skip.

(6) TEST COVERAGE. 57 `def test` functions across 10 files, expanding to 63 collected items via two parametrisations (test_alignment_real over 4 mice, test_headline_integrity_summary_matches_full_scan_cache over 4 mice). I ran the suite: 57 passed, 6 skipped in 2.15 s — and all 6 skips are the entire test_cached_results.py real-data contract, skipped because the three summary CSVs are absent. So the headline claim 'all 57 tests pass' is true but means the integrity contract is currently enforcing nothing; with the cache present it would be 63. By file: test_sanity 13, test_learning 10, test_geometry 7, test_features 6, test_decode 6, test_reader 6, test_qc 4, test_cached_results 3 (→6 with parametrisation), test_alignment 1 (→4), test_audit 1. Integrity claims actually enforced: streaming zero/finite counts are exact on a hand-built 8×2 HDF5 fixture; scale invariance of the dimensionless metrics under a 1e-6 gain while RMS scales linearly; a sparse-impulse window is NOT mistaken for continuous signal (the exact error that produced the original false diagnosis); frame lookup uses the latest and never a future frame; robust z resists a single 100× outlier; MAD-based peak location survives a 100× single-channel decoy; common-median referencing removes an exactly-constructed shared component; lowpass vs white noise are separated (lag-1 > 0.8 vs < 0.05; power fraction > 0.8 vs < 0.3); overlap-save block filtering matches whole-signal filtering to < 1e-6 relative (beta) and < 2e-3 (broadband), with a small-pad control >20× worse; band envelopes recover known tone amplitudes and are zero-phase to < 20 ms; robust_log_outliers is invariant under a 1e6 gain; phase_indices reproduces epoch_indices.m exactly; valid_traversals preserves trial↔PSD correspondence after filtering; ridge recovers a planted linear position code (R² > 0.9) and sits at chance on unrelated features; held-out CCA separates a shared latent (> 0.7) from independence (< 0.3); the CSV area boundaries match the spike pipeline's values for 614/731/1212; and CSV-vs-cache agreement plus the pinned timing offsets, 1212 label withholding and CMR dB asymmetry (when the cache exists). Coverage GAPS, all of them at the exact points where the science failed: no test asserts that filtering is applied with adequate padding, or that a driver uses reader.iter_time_blocks at all; no test asserts an analysis window is free of periodic events (the 4 s/5 s collision is invisible to the suite); no test checks that the chance/baseline reference in a decoder is the correct statistic; no test enforces CONFOUNDED_BANDS exclusion; and no test asserts that a gate-crossing driver is gated (run_decode_cca.py's missing gate is untested and undetected). A single test asserting 'white noise through the decode pipeline yields R² <= shuffle p95' would have caught the fatal defect.
