### Analyses (18)

#### 12.1 Robust spectral shape: ordinary corridor windows versus high-amplitude events
`scripts/plot_sanity_audit.py:64-122 (read_centred_windows, normalised_psd, build_spectral_cache) + src/striatum_lfp/sanity.py:147-171 (median_welch_psd)` lines plot_sanity_audit.py 64-122, 202-215; sanity.py 147-171 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *Supplementary figure for 614/727/731 after re-selection on strictly event-free windows. The 1212 row must be dropped or replaced by an explicit statement that its ordinary spectrum is unmeasurable at this window length.*

- **Question.** Does ordinary corridor voltage have LFP-like spectral shape, and how does it differ from the periodic events?
- **Method.** Selects 1 s windows that are corridor & non-zero & isfinite(artefact_z) & |artefact_z| < 1 ('ordinary') or artefact_z > 5 ('event'); takes 40 of each by `np.linspace` over the candidate index set; reads a 4 s (4000-sample) window CENTRED on each selected 1 s bin, 6 channels [10,90,160,225,300,360]; median Welch PSD (nperseg = min(2048, 4000)) across windows and channels; normalises each curve by its 1–200 Hz trapezoid area so only shape is compared.
- **Outputs.** results/sanity_figure_examples_and_psd.npz (PRESENT — exact plotted arrays) → figures/sanity_audit_overview_v2 panel D, sanity_audit_raw_examples_v2
- **Statistics.** none — median-pooled spectra, shape-normalised. Median at both the window and channel level is the right robustness choice.
- **Inferential unit.** 4 s windows × 6 channels, nested in session.
- **Soundness.** FATAL FOR 1212, sound for the others. The selection criterion is applied to a 1 s bin but the data read is a 4 s window, and 1212's events recur every 5.00 s. I reproduced the selection and find 39/40 (98%) of 1212's 'ordinary corridor' windows contain a z>5 event bin, versus 5/40 (12%), 3/40 (8%), 3/40 (8%) for 614/727/731. Direct confirmation from the saved figure source data: 1212's plotted 'Ordinary corridor' example has per-channel RMS 1.66–1.98 stored units, ~7,900× the 2.30e-4 that the SAME document (SANITY_AUDIT.md:23) reports as 1212's ordinary median RMS. Worse, only 3 strictly event-free 4 s corridor windows exist in 1212's entire 190-minute session, so 1212's ordinary spectrum is not measurable at 4 s resolution at all. The raw-example figure standardises every channel by its own robust SD before plotting (plot_sanity_audit.py:233-236), which visually erases the amplitude discrepancy — a reader cannot see that the 1212 'ordinary' trace is artefact-dominated. For 614/727/731 the 8–12% contamination is largely suppressed by the double median, and I verified this directly (see the signal-identity entry).

#### 12.2 Theta power: running versus stationary (speed-split)
`scripts/run_learning_evolution.py:84-91 (frame_speed), 145-166` lines run_learning_evolution.py 84-91, 145-166 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `gated` · manuscript role: *Drop. Cannot be presented in any form until the offset is established, because its unit of analysis is 1 s and the offset uncertainty is seconds.*

- **Question.** Is striatal/ACC theta modulated by locomotion?
- **Method.** 400 one-second windows at `np.linspace(0, n - FS, 400)` over the WHOLE array; a window is dropped if max|v| > art_thr, or if fewer than 3 VR frames fall in [s, s+1000) ms, or if mean speed is non-finite. Speed per frame = |diff(position)|*1.25 / diff(t) with jumps > 50 cm masked as trial resets; running iff mean speed >= RUN_SPEED = 2.0 cm/s. Reports the ratio of the MEDIAN theta band power (running) to the MEDIAN (stationary) per area; n_run / n_sta are computed but never written to the CSV. Reported values (NOTES.md:136-147): 727 0.46-0.57, 731 0.33-0.36, 614/1212 ≈ 1; area-averaged 727 0.52, 731 0.35, 614 0.94, 1212 1.07.
- **Outputs.** learning_evolution_summary.csv column theta_run_over_stationary (ABSENT) → figures/learning_evolution_* row-3 panel and summary_animals panel 3, both quarantined
- **Statistics.** NONE — a ratio of two medians. No test, no CI, no null, no correction across 3 areas × 4 mice; the two sample sizes are discarded.
- **Inferential unit.** One-second windows within a session (<= 400, fewer after three exclusion filters), nested in animal. Effect claimed as consistent in 2 of 4 animals.
- **Soundness.** This is the analysis most damaged by the unresolved offset, and NOTES.md:146-147 promotes it as 'the one semi-consistent effect' without noting that. It matches a 1 s voltage window to VR frames whose timestamps fall in the same 1 s interval — i.e. it assumes the voltage-to-VR offset is ZERO, which is precisely the quantity the audit says is unknown to within several seconds (median event-peak offsets +1.98/+4.26/+1.74 s). At a 2-4 s offset the running/stationary labels on 1 s windows are scrambled, so the measurement cannot be interpreted at all. Separately: no statistics, sample sizes discarded, an n=2-of-4 'consistency' claim on 4 animals, and the ratio is of medians of absolute power (dimensionless, so at least scale-safe). The zero-padded tail is correctly excluded, but by accident rather than design — padding survives the artefact test (max|v| = 0 < art_thr) and is removed only by the >= 3-VR-frame requirement. Note the sign is opposite to hippocampal running-theta, which is the kind of surprising-but-plausible result that most needs a clean timebase before it is believed.

#### 12.3 Position decoding from LFP band power, run as an ALIGNMENT TEST
`scripts/run_decode_cca.py:48-111 (collect, decode_analysis) + src/striatum_lfp/decode.py:27-68 (bin_by_position, ridge_cv_decode)` lines run_decode_cca.py 48-111, 165-189; decode.py 27-68 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *Drop entirely, and retract the alignment inference in NOTES.md. Not salvageable as a supplementary figure. The white-noise ceiling is itself worth keeping as a methods cautionary control.*

- **Question.** Can corridor position be decoded from LFP band power — and, by the driver's own argument, does that prove the export's time offset is roughly correct?
- **Method.** NOT GATED — this script has no --allow-unaligned flag and no SystemExit; it runs all four mice (including 1212, which the learning driver excludes) and all three bands including the confounded low_gamma (30,80). Per corridor traversal (min_frames=20, requires b-a >= 500 ms): `seg = lf[a:b, :]` read as a BARE segment, then `features.band_envelope(seg, SOS[bd])` per band, then `bin_by_position` into N_POS = 20 bins over pos_max = CORRIDOR_CM = 250 cm (12.5 cm bins) with sample position from `np.interp(samp_ms, frame_ms, pos_au) * 1.25`. Artefact exclusion `robust_log_outliers(traversal peak, z=4.0)`. Rows = traversal × position bin; features = area-median band power (3 areas × 3 bands = up to 9 columns). Decoding: `Ridge(alpha=1.0)` under `GroupKFold(n_splits=min(5, n_groups))` grouped by trial, `StandardScaler` fit on each TRAIN fold only; pooled CV R² and MAE. Null: 15 draws of `rng.permutation(y)` (global permutation, seeded `default_rng(0)`); verdict `above_chance = r2 > shuffle p95`. Plotted chance reference = CORRIDOR_CM / sqrt(12) = 72.17 cm.
- **Outputs.** results/decode_summary.csv (ABSENT on disk) → figures/decode_position.{png,svg} — PRESENT IN THE TOP-LEVEL figures/ DIRECTORY, timestamped 2026-07-13 09:26, i.e. AFTER the 07:13 hardening commit, and NOT mentioned anywhere in figures/README.md
- **Statistics.** Group-k-fold cross-validated R²/MAE versus a 15-draw global-y-permutation null; `above_chance` thresholded at the 15-draw 95th percentile. Best attainable p is ~1/16 = 0.0625; no exact permutation p is reported. Reported result (NOTES.md:106-111): R² 0.12/0.14/0.17 and MAE 53/46/20 cm for 614/727/731, 1212 at chance.
- **Inferential unit.** (traversal × position bin) rows: 1028 / 7133 / 4867 / 384 for 1212/614/727/731, grouped by trial (156/469/371/76 groups). Single animal per fit; no cross-animal inference.
- **Soundness.** FATAL — the result is an artefact of insufficient filter padding, and I demonstrated this directly. Mechanism, in order. (a) Each traversal is filtered as a bare segment, bypassing reader.py's 3,000-sample overlap-save pad; `band_envelope` passes no padlen, so scipy's default of 3*(2*n_sections+1) = 27 samples applies to a 4-8 Hz bandpass whose transient is ~1 s. (b) I measured the corridor epoch to be a FIXED ~4.98 s window (614: 469 traversals, min 4.96 s, max 4.99 s), and within a traversal corr(position, time-within-traversal) has median r = 0.9991. So a deterministic filter edge transient IS a position code. (c) GroupKFold by trial gives no protection: the transient is identical in every traversal, so it generalises perfectly across folds. (d) The global-y-permutation null cannot detect it, because permuting y destroys the very ramp the artefact predicts — hence the reported shuffle p95 ≈ 0. PROOF: I ran PURE WHITE NOISE (rng.standard_normal((b-a, 384)), no LFP, no brain, no timebase) through the exact driver pipeline with the real traversals and positions: 614 gives CV R² = +0.2311, MAE 49.8 cm; 731 gives CV R² = +0.4998, MAE 14.9 cm — both declared 'above chance' by the driver's own rule. THE NOISE CEILING EXCEEDS THE REPORTED REAL RESULT IN BOTH MICE (real: 614 R² 0.12 / MAE 53; 731 R² 0.17 / MAE 20). Mechanism control: re-running the same noise with padlen = 2999 collapses R² from +0.2311 to +0.0047 (614) and +0.4998 to +0.0828 (731). Therefore the claim at NOTES.md:106-111 — 'You cannot decode position from mis-timed data ⇒ the export offset is roughly correct' — is void, and with it the only evidence offered anywhere for the offset. Three further independent defects. (i) The plotted chance MAE of 72.17 cm is CORRIDOR_CM/sqrt(12), which is the SD of a uniform, not the MAE of the optimal constant predictor. I computed the true median-predictor MAE from the actual surviving y: 30.7 (1212), 56.9 (614), 50.0 (727), 21.5 (731) cm. Every reported MAE is within ~10% of its own mouse's chance level and 731's reported 20 cm is BELOW its 21.5 cm chance — the headline 'MAE 20 cm vs ~72 cm uniform-chance' compares a mouse whose traversals reach a median of only 62.6 cm against a fixed 250 cm reference. (ii) This also resolves the arithmetic impossibility in the logged numbers: R² 0.17 with MAE 20 cm is inconsistent for a 250 cm range but consistent once y's SD is 25.8 cm. (iii) alpha = 1.0 is fixed with no inner CV, and the confounded low_gamma band is included as a feature.

#### 12.4 Event-peak timing versus VR sync edges (the alignment probe)
`scripts/plot_sanity_audit.py:252-341 (timing_summary_and_plot) + src/striatum_lfp/sanity.py:54-112 (distance_to_nearest, signed_distance_to_nearest, robust_synchronous_peak_sample)` lines plot_sanity_audit.py 252-341; sanity.py 54-112 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *Methods/negative result only. The offset numbers may be quoted as descriptive, but not as evidence of a shared clock without a jitter null and without establishing what column 8 is.*

- **Question.** Do the deterministic high-amplitude events provide a marker that pins the voltage-to-VR sample offset?
- **Method.** For each event run, re-reads voltage over [run_start_s, run_stop_s + 1 s) on 24 channels (arange(0, 384, 16)) and locates the peak at 1 ms resolution by `robust_synchronous_peak_sample`: per-channel median-centre and 1.4826*MAD scale (std then 1.0 fallback), median |z| ACROSS channels, argmax — so no single electrode can set the event time and multiplicative channel gains are irrelevant. Signed offset to the nearest VR sync edge, where edges = frame times of `np.diff(VR_data[:, 8]) != 0`. Reports median/q25/q75 signed peak-to-sync offset, median absolute event-start-to-sync distance, fraction of event starts within 2 s of a sync edge, and event prevalence per behavioural state. Published values (test-pinned at atol 0.002): median signed peak↔sync = +1.983 s (614), +4.256 s (727), +1.740 s (731); 1212 reported with a ~30 s IQR and no usable marker.
- **Outputs.** results/sanity_timing_summary.csv (ABSENT on disk) → figures/sanity_audit_event_timing.{png,svg}
- **Statistics.** none — medians and IQRs of offsets. No test that the offset distribution is tighter than chance given the reference-edge density.
- **Inferential unit.** Event runs within a session (n = 120/121/120 events; 2049 for 1212).
- **Soundness.** The peak-localisation primitive is well built and correctly unit-tested against a planted shared transient with a 100× single-channel decoy (test_sanity.py:124-129), and the conclusion drawn — that a several-second offset uncertainty comparable to a traversal blocks position/trial analyses — is the right conclusion. But the quantitative claim is weaker than it reads. I verified VR_data col 8 has 239 transitions at median interval 30.002 s (min 0.200 s, max 59.821 s): it is a ~60 s square wave, so 'nearest edge' is drawn from a 30 s-dense reference and any event lands within ±15 s by construction; a median offset of +1.98 s therefore needs a null (e.g. offsets of jittered event times) to be interpretable, and none is computed. The min 0.200 s interval shows the channel also has glitch transitions that contaminate nearest-edge distances. And col 8 is undocumented — the entire timing probe rests on assuming an unlabelled binary VR column is the acquisition sync.

#### 12.5 Signal-identity diagnostics: lag-1 autocorrelation, 1-100 Hz power fraction, difference-to-signal SD ratio, 2-40 Hz log-log slope
`src/striatum_lfp/sanity.py:174-203 (temporal_identity_metrics) + scripts/run_signal_identity.py:37-188` lines sanity.py 174-203; run_signal_identity.py 37-188 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *Main figure of the negative/methods result for 614/727/731. 1212 must be withheld, not merely 'kept separate'.*

- **Question.** Is the exported voltage a low-passed LFP-band signal, or broadband/wideband data?
- **Method.** 40 ordinary corridor windows (corridor & exact_zero_fraction < 0.99 & isfinite(artefact_z) & |artefact_z| < 1, sampled by np.linspace), each 4000 samples read from `second*FS - 1500`, 24 channels (arange(0, 384, 16)). Per window×channel: mean-centre, lag-1 correlation = sum(x[:-1]*x[1:]) / sum(x[:-1]^2), and std(diff(x))/std(x); medians over the window×channel pool. Median Welch PSD (nperseg 2048, Δf = 0.4883 Hz) → power_fraction = trapz(psd, 1–100 Hz) / trapz(psd, 1–499 Hz); slope = polyfit of log10 psd on log10 f over 2–40 Hz. White-noise references plotted explicitly: lag-1 = 0, power fraction = 99/498 = 0.1988, ΔSD/SD = sqrt(2) = 1.4142. VERIFIED VERBATIM from the npz: 1212 lag-1 −0.0698, fraction 0.1559, ΔSD/SD 1.4629, slope +0.4621; 614 −0.0526, 0.1722, 1.4509, −0.4336; 727 −0.1078, 0.1597, 1.4884, −0.6598; 731 +0.0085, 0.1823, 1.4083, −0.9141.
- **Outputs.** results/signal_identity_summary.csv (ABSENT), results/signal_identity_figure_data.npz (PRESENT) → figures/signal_identity.{png,svg} panels A/B
- **Statistics.** none — descriptive medians against analytic white-noise expectations. Using the closed-form white-noise reference in place of a resampling null is legitimate and cheap here.
- **Inferential unit.** Window × channel measurements within a session (40 × 24 = 960 per mouse), all nested in one animal.
- **Soundness.** The measurement is the correct one and its verdict is the most important true finding in the domain: with ΔSD/SD of 1.41–1.49 against a white-noise expectation of 1.414, and 1–100 Hz power fractions of 15.6–18.2% against a white expectation of 19.9%, these exports are essentially spectrally white to ~500 Hz. That is a decisive refutation of 'this is an LFP-band export'. The primitive is properly discriminated in test (butter-lowpassed noise gives lag-1 > 0.8 and fraction > 0.8; white gives |lag-1| < 0.05 and fraction < 0.3). Two defects. (1) Same 4 s / 5 s window–cadence collision: 39/40 of 1212's windows contain a z>5 event, so 1212's whole row — and with it the 'rising 2–40 Hz spectrum, qualitatively different' conclusion (NOTES.md:46-48) — is measured on artefact-dominated data. Its median 4 s RMS is 1.807, not 2.3e-4. (2) I ran the control the audit did not: recomputing 614 on strictly event-free 4 s windows gives lag-1 −0.0536 vs −0.0526, fraction 0.1753 vs 0.1722, ΔSD/SD 1.4517 vs 1.4509, slope −0.4792 vs −0.4336, median RMS 2.99e-6 vs 3.01e-6. So 614/727/731 are robust and their rows stand; 1212's does not.

#### 12.6 Band-power feature extraction (theta / beta / low-gamma / broadband Hilbert envelopes)
`src/striatum_lfp/features.py:23-63` lines features.py 23-63 · **🟠 major** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *Methods only, and only after the padding defect is fixed. Should expose an explicit pad/`padlen` parameter.*

- **Question.** Infrastructure: extract the LFP analogue of a unit's firing rate.
- **Method.** `butter(order=cfg.filt_order=4, [lo, hi], btype='band', fs=1000, output='sos')` per band; `sosfiltfilt` (zero-phase) then `abs(hilbert(...))`, or optionally sqrt of a boxcar-smoothed square (cfg.smooth_ms = 0.0 → off). Bands theta (4,8), beta (15,30), low_gamma (30,80), broadband (1,100).
- **Outputs.** none — library only; consumed by run_decode_cca.py
- **Statistics.** n/a. Ground-truth tested: a 2.0-amplitude 6 Hz tone recovers envelope 2.0 ± 0.15 in theta and > 10× the beta envelope; a two-tone splits correctly; an AM envelope peaks within 20 ms of the modulation peak (zero-phase, no causal lag).
- **Inferential unit.** n/a
- **Soundness.** The primitive itself is correct and properly validated on known ground truth. The problem is entirely in how it is called. `band_envelope` takes no padding argument and passes nothing to `sosfiltfilt`, so a caller who hands it a short bare segment silently gets scipy's default padlen — which for an order-4 SOS bandpass is 3*(2*n_sections+1) = 27 samples. I measured this. That is two orders of magnitude below the 3,000 samples that `config.pad_samples` documents as necessary for a 1-4 Hz edge. The module docstring warns about the alignment offset but not about this, and the API offers no way to request adequate padding. This is the mechanism of the fatal decoding artefact. Also: `low_gamma` (30,80) remains a first-class band in BANDS even though `CONFOUNDED_BANDS` marks it invalid, and nothing enforces the exclusion — run_decode_cca.py duly uses it as a decoding feature.

#### 12.7 LFP band-power evolution across learning phases (naive / intermediate / expert / disengaged)
`scripts/run_learning_evolution.py:94-333 + src/striatum_lfp/learning.py` lines run_learning_evolution.py 94-333; learning.py 26-149 · **🟠 major** · status: `gated` · manuscript role: *Drop as a result. Retain only as an audit-trail appendix. Cannot become a figure without provenance, a statistical model with animal as a random effect, and n >> 3.*

- **Question.** Does striatal/ACC LFP band power change across learning?
- **Method.** GATED — `main()` raises SystemExit unless `--allow-unaligned` is passed (lines 383-387); 1212 excluded unconditionally (line 391); low-gamma excluded (BANDS = theta (4,8), beta (15,30) only). Per corridor traversal (world == 6, min_frames = 20, clipped to the array and requiring min_samples = 500): Welch (nperseg = min(1024, len)) on the bare segment, band power = trapz over [lo, hi), median over the area's channels. Areas from channel_depths() = (c//2)*20 µm and the inclusive CSV boundaries. Artefact exclusion: `robust_log_outliers(traversal peak |v|, z_threshold=4.0)` (median/MAD z on log10). Power → log10 → z-scored using mean/SD of CLEAN traversals only. Learning point from `tcca.dataio.find_learning_point(zscored_lick_errors, lp_z_threshold=-2.0)`; mouse→animal_id by POSITION in TASK_MOUSE_IDS (614→2, 727→4, 731→6), validated by `abs(a.n_trials - n_corr) > 1 → raise`. Epochs via `learning.phase_indices(trials_per_epoch=10)` = naive 1:10, intermediate lp-10:lp-1, expert lp:lp+9 (0-indexed), matching epoch_indices.m; plus 'disengaged' = change_point-1 to end. Evolution lines are a MA_WINDOW = 10 centred rolling mean ± within-window SEM.
- **Outputs.** results/learning_evolution_summary.csv (ABSENT), figures/learning_evolution_{614,727,731}.{png,svg} + learning_evolution_summary_animals.{png,svg} — all QUARANTINED under figures/_quarantined_unaligned_learning/ (10 files, dated 2026-07-12, i.e. produced BEFORE the 2026-07-13 hardening; the 1212 figures in that directory come from the pre-exclusion code path)
- **Statistics.** NONE. Epoch means ± within-window SEM, and an expert/naive fold-change. No test, no null, no correction across 2 bands × 3 areas × 4 epochs × 3 mice, no cross-animal test. NOTES.md:143-147 correctly reports the conclusion as no robust group-level effect.
- **Inferential unit.** Corridor traversals within a session (469 / 371 / 76 valid after the >=500 ms filter, n_clean fewer). Traversals are nested in animal; the cross-animal panel averages 3 animals with no test.
- **Soundness.** Correctly quarantined, and the gate is real (a hard SystemExit, not a comment). The scientific hygiene is good: the learning point comes from lick behaviour and is therefore not circular with the LFP; the mouse→animal mapping was fixed from a brittle nearest-trial-count rule to a positional index with a hard trial-count assertion; phase indices were fixed to match epoch_indices.m and are unit-tested against the MATLAB convention (test_learning.py:77-83); z-scoring uses clean traversals only; and `valid_traversals` returns filtered objects specifically so a later index cannot associate a PSD with the wrong trial (test_learning.py:31-38). Substantive remaining problems if it is ever ungated. (1) The per-traversal Welch is computed on a bare ~5 s segment with nperseg = min(1024, len), giving ~4 Welch segments and a very noisy per-traversal PSD; the resulting theta estimate has few degrees of freedom. (2) `art_thr = 10**(median(log10(peaks[clean])) + 3)` is an arbitrary 3-decade constant. (3) No statistics at all, so 'expert/naive 0.92-1.26' has no uncertainty attached. (4) The slow rise/fall is acknowledged to co-vary with engagement, arousal, running and electrode drift and cannot be attributed to learning — the honest reading, and it means the analysis as designed cannot answer its own question. (5) The quarantined figures on disk predate the corrections, so any number read off them is stale relative to the current code.

#### 12.8 Cross-area LFP-LFP CCA versus within-area volume-conduction ceiling versus trial shuffle
`scripts/run_decode_cca.py:114-131 (cca_analysis) + src/striatum_lfp/decode.py:71-107 (residualise_by_group, heldout_cca)` lines run_decode_cca.py 114-131, 192-217; decode.py 71-107 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *Supplementary/methods negative result at best, after replacing the single shuffle with >= 1000 permutations, averaging over splits, and residualising within folds. The qualitative conclusion (volume-conduction limited, no area-specific coupling on one probe) is likely to survive.*

- **Question.** Is there area-specific inter-areal LFP coupling (DMS-ACC, DMS-DLS, DLS-ACC) above what shared volume-conducted field explains?
- **Method.** NOT GATED. Rows = traversal × position bin, per-channel band power (384 columns) for theta and beta only (CCA_BANDS). `residualise_by_group(M, posbin)` subtracts the per-position-bin mean ACROSS ALL rows → trial-to-trial residual fluctuations. Then `heldout_cca(A, B, k=5, seed=0)`: drop non-finite rows, require n >= 8, split-half by `np.random.default_rng(0).permutation(n)`, PCA to k = min(5, p, n_train-1) fit on TRAIN only, `CCA(n_components=1, max_iter=1000)` fit on train, |corr| of the projections on the HELD-OUT half. Three quantities per pair×band: `cross` (area A vs area B channels); `within` = the VC ceiling, A's channels split as cx[:half] vs cx[half:]; `shuffle` = A vs row-permuted B (a SINGLE draw). Reported (NOTES.md:112-117): cross CC1 0.6-0.9, shuffle 0.02-0.14, within-area ceiling 0.88-0.99, cross falls with area separation.
- **Outputs.** results/cca_summary.csv (ABSENT on disk) → figures/cca_cross_area.{png,svg} — PRESENT in the top-level figures/ directory, 2026-07-13 09:26, undocumented in figures/README.md
- **Statistics.** Split-half held-out CC1 against a within-area ceiling and a SINGLE-DRAW shuffle. No permutation distribution, no p-value, no correction across 3 pairs × 2 bands × 4 mice = up to 24 comparisons.
- **Inferential unit.** (traversal × position bin) rows, n = 1028/7133/4867/384; channels within an area are the features. One animal per fit.
- **Soundness.** The best-reasoned analysis of the two gate-crossers, and its conclusion is probably right, but the inference machinery is too weak to support it. Genuine strengths: the design correctly identifies that cross-area LFP-LFP CCA is offset-robust (both sides share the file's single offset), correctly insists on a within-area split-half VC ceiling rather than testing against zero, uses held-out rather than in-sample CC (PCA and CCA both fit on the train half only — no leakage there), and reaches the conservative conclusion that nothing exceeds the ceiling, i.e. no area-specific coupling. It is also largely immune to the edge-transient artefact that kills the decoder, because `residualise_by_group` removes any deterministic function of position bin — which the transient is. Defects. (1) SINGLE-DRAW shuffle null per pair/band: one permutation cannot bound a null distribution and no p-value is derivable. (2) `seed=0` is hard-defaulted in `heldout_cca`, so the identical split-half partition is reused for every pair, band and mouse — the 'independent' comparisons share one split, and no split-averaging is done. (3) `residualise_by_group` is computed over ALL rows before the split-half, so the per-bin means are estimated using held-out rows — an O(1/n_traversals) leak of the same family as the documented loo_ridge_press leak, small for 614 but material for 731 (76 traversals, 384 rows). (4) `abs(r)` folds the null upward, which is why the shuffle baseline sits at 0.02-0.14 rather than 0. (5) The VC ceiling splits area channels as contiguous depth-ordered halves rather than interleaved, so the two halves are maximally proximal — this biases the ceiling high, which is conservative for the conclusion drawn, but it should be stated. (6) 731 has no DLS at all (blank CSV cell), so only DMS-ACC exists for it, and n = 384 rows is thin for k = 5 PCA per side.

#### 12.9 Cached-result integrity contract (real-data regression tests)
`tests/test_cached_results.py:1-94` lines test_cached_results.py 1-94 · **🟠 major** · status: `gated` · manuscript role: *Methods/reproducibility statement. Either commit the three small summary CSVs (they are kilobytes, not data) or make the drivers regenerate them as a test fixture — otherwise the paper's numbers have no in-repo provenance.*

- **Question.** Do the published summary CSVs still agree with the full-scan cache, and are the headline claims pinned against silent drift?
- **Method.** Skips entirely unless sanity_summary.csv, sanity_timing_summary.csv, signal_identity_summary.csv AND all four sanity_audit_<mouse>.npz exist. Then asserts per mouse: window count == n_samples // 1000; mean(channel_exact_zero_fraction) == the CSV's global zero fraction; zero-window fraction matches; corridor/dark window counts match; `not zero[corridor].any()` and `not zero[dark].any()`; median ordinary RMS matches; and boolean_runs over the zero mask gives 0 runs for 1212, exactly 1 terminal run otherwise. Pins the timing claims (614 +1.983, 727 +4.256, 731 +1.740 s at atol 0.002), the 1212 area-label withholding, and the CMR asymmetry (614 strongest < −4.0 dB; all other peaks |Δ| < 0.2 dB). Also asserts every current figure has machine-readable source arrays of the exact expected shapes ((4000, 6) raw examples; matching PSD shapes).
- **Outputs.** n/a
- **Statistics.** n/a — regression assertions on real cached results.
- **Inferential unit.** n/a
- **Soundness.** Excellent design, currently INERT. This is the right way to stop a documented claim from silently drifting — it pins the exact published numbers, and it enforces the scientifically load-bearing structural facts (zeros absent from corridor and dark, exactly one terminal run) rather than just recomputing. But all three CSVs it depends on are gitignored (`results/*.csv`) and absent from disk, so `_CACHE_PRESENT` is False and all 6 parametrised tests SKIP. I confirmed: `57 passed, 6 skipped`, with all 6 skips from this file. The consequence is that every number in SANITY_AUDIT.md and NOTES.md is currently unverifiable from the repository — I had to reconstruct them from the surviving .npz files (they all checked out). This also makes NOTES.md:20-21 and SANITY_AUDIT.md:114 ('57 pytest tests pass') ambiguous: 57 is now the pass count with the contract disabled, whereas at audit completion with the cache present it would have been 63.

#### 12.10 Zero-gap occupancy by behavioural state (corridor / dark-ITI / outside behaviour)
`scripts/run_sanity_audit.py:29-38 (behaviour_at_windows) + src/striatum_lfp/sanity.py:206-226 (frame_values_at_samples)` lines run_sanity_audit.py 29-38, 100-127; sanity.py 206-226 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *Methods + supplementary figure panel.*

- **Question.** Are the zero regions task-locked (i.e. ITI/dark periods stripped at export, which would break corridor analyses) or purely terminal padding?
- **Method.** Window centre = window_start_sample + FS//2 = start+500. `frame_values_at_samples` assigns each centre the value of the LATEST preceding VR frame (searchsorted side='right' minus 1, NaN before the first frame) — deliberately avoiding the future-frame error of a bare side='left' lookup. world = VR_data col 4 (== 6 → corridor, == 12 → dark); centres outside [frame_ms.min(), frame_ms.max()] are set NaN → 'outside behaviour'. Reports zero-window fraction separately per state.
- **Outputs.** sanity_summary.csv columns corridor_window_count, dark_window_count, corridor_zero_window_fraction, dark_zero_window_fraction (CSV ABSENT; values reproducible and reproduced from npz) → figures/sanity_audit_overview_v2 panel C
- **Statistics.** none — descriptive fractions per state.
- **Inferential unit.** 1 s windows, nested within session/animal (n corridor = 786/2342/1851/380).
- **Soundness.** Sound, and the decisive result of the whole audit: corridor and dark zero fractions are exactly 0.0000 in all four sessions, which falsifies the 'export stripped the ITI' hypothesis directly rather than by inference. The piecewise-constant frame hold is the correct interpolation for a categorical state variable and is unit-tested against hand-computed ground truth (test_sanity.py:48-56). Two caveats worth stating in a methods section: `world` is VR_data python column 4, which is NOT in the documented data contract (NOTES.md:80-81 lists only rows 2/4/7/8 = cols 1/3/6/7), so the corridor/dark semantics rest on an undocumented column that happens to be binary {6, 12}; and for 1212 the maximum VR frame gap is 12.1 s, over which the held value is asserted rather than observed.

#### 12.11 Periodic high-amplitude event detection and cadence
`scripts/run_sanity_audit.py:41-49 (classify_windows) + src/striatum_lfp/sanity.py:115-124 (robust_zscore) + scripts/plot_sanity_audit.py:53-54 (event_mask)` lines run_sanity_audit.py 41-49, 109-112; sanity.py 115-124; plot_sanity_audit.py 53-54 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *Main or supplementary figure (the negative/methods result). The 1212 'unrelated to VR' sentence must be retracted or tested against corridor onsets.*

- **Question.** Is there a deterministic non-physiological high-amplitude mode, at what cadence, and how prevalent is it?
- **Method.** log10 of per-window median-channel RMS over non-zero windows → median/MAD robust z (scale 1.4826*MAD, std fallback); event = isfinite(z) & z > 5. Prevalence also reported at z > 3, 5, 8, 10. `boolean_runs` gives contiguous event runs; intervals = diff of run-start times. VERIFIED VERBATIM: event bins 2049 / 120 / 121 / 120; runs 2049 / 120 / 121 / 120 (every run is a single 1 s bin); median interval 5.00 s (1212, min 5.0 max 10.0) and exactly 60.00 s (614, min 60.0 max 60.0; 727 median 60.00 with one 5.0 s minimum; 731 min=max=60.0); prevalence z>5 = 17.974% / 1.429% / 1.440% / 1.429%, and IDENTICAL at z>3, z>8 and z>10 for 1212/614/731 (727 rises to 4.262% at z>3) — the mode is >10 MAD separated. Event fraction by state: corridor 0.1985/0.0184/0.0184/0.0132, dark 0.2000/0.0159/0.0161/0.0169, outside 0.0043/0.0000/0.0008/0.0000.
- **Outputs.** sanity_windows_<mouse>.csv column log_rms_robust_z (ABSENT), sanity_audit_<mouse>.npz key artefact_z (PRESENT), sanity_summary.csv artefact_fraction_z_gt_{3,5,8,10} (ABSENT) → figures/sanity_audit_overview_v2 panel A, sanity_audit_event_timing
- **Statistics.** Robust z-score threshold, not a hypothesis test. Prevalence stability across z ∈ {3,5,8,10} substitutes for a formal separation test — a reasonable substitute given a bimodal amplitude distribution.
- **Inferential unit.** 1 s windows within session.
- **Soundness.** Method is right: log-then-robust-z is scale-invariant (a gain change shifts the log by a constant and cancels in the z), and the invariance of prevalence from z>3 to z>10 is genuine evidence of a separated mode rather than a tail. The 1 s bin resolution is honestly declared as prevalence, not duration (SANITY_AUDIT.md:30-31). The gap that matters: the audit never tests the 1212 5 s cadence against the corridor-epoch structure, and I find the corridor epoch is itself a fixed 4.97 s window (156 traversals, q25–q75 = 4.96–4.97 s). A 5.00 s event cadence coinciding with a 4.97 s trial epoch is prima facie evidence that 1212's events are task/VR-locked (world reload, valve, screen event) rather than 'instrument-like and unrelated to VR' as SANITY_AUDIT.md:66-67 asserts. That inference is unsupported by the analysis as coded.

#### 12.12 Narrowband peak detection, 40-180 Hz
`scripts/run_signal_identity.py:79-90` lines run_signal_identity.py 79-90 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *Supplementary panel + the methods justification for excluding 30-80 Hz.*

- **Question.** Is there line-noise or other narrowband contamination inside the planned analysis bands?
- **Method.** `scipy.signal.find_peaks(np.log10(psd[40 <= f <= 180]), prominence=0.15)`; peaks ranked by prominence; the two strongest retained. VERIFIED VERBATIM by re-running the detector on the saved PSDs: 614 → 153.81 and 74.22 Hz; 727 → 150.88 and 74.22 Hz; 731 → 150.88 and 73.73 Hz; 1212 → NO peaks detected at all (empty array, hence the 'none sharply resolved' in SANITY_AUDIT.md:40). Δf = 0.4883 Hz.
- **Outputs.** signal_identity_summary.csv columns strongest_peak_40_180hz, second_peak_40_180hz (ABSENT on disk; reproduced) → figures/signal_identity panel A
- **Statistics.** none — prominence threshold 0.15 log10 units on the median PSD. No significance test against local spectral background.
- **Inferential unit.** Frequency bins of one median-pooled spectrum per session; n = 1 spectrum per animal.
- **Soundness.** Correct conclusion, incompletely scoped. The finding that ~74 Hz sits inside the planned 30–80 Hz low-gamma band and therefore invalidates that band as specified is right and load-bearing, and is properly propagated into `config.CONFOUNDED_BANDS = ("low_gamma",)`. Three scoping gaps. The search band starts at 40 Hz, so 50 Hz mains and any sub-40 Hz harmonic is never looked for — an odd omission given that ~150 Hz is being read as a mains harmonic. It stops at 180 Hz, so the 250 Hz region is unexamined despite the export being white to ~500 Hz. And the ~74 Hz / ~151 Hz pair is not 50 Hz-harmonic-consistent (2×74.2 = 148.4 ≠ 153.8 for 614), which is a substantive clue about the events' origin that the analysis notes but does not pursue. Prominence 0.15 is an unjustified magic constant, and 1212's 'no peaks' is at least partly a consequence of its event-contaminated (hence flatter, broadband-dominated) spectrum rather than a property of its ordinary voltage.

#### 12.13 Within-nominal-depth-band channel correlations (raw, theta, beta, low-gamma)
`scripts/run_signal_identity.py:32-34 (median_pairwise_correlation), 96-123` lines run_signal_identity.py 32-34, 96-123 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *Supplementary panel at most, or drop. Cannot support the 'physiological LF structure may be embedded in the broadband voltage' sentence without a distance-matched null.*

- **Question.** Is there shared low-frequency structure within striatal depth bands, i.e. any physiological LF signal embedded in the broadband voltage?
- **Method.** Of the 24 loaded channels, those falling inside each area's inclusive [start, end] µm band; requires >= 2 such channels. Per 4 s window: `sosfiltfilt(butter(4, band, 'bandpass', fs=1000))` for theta (4,8), beta (15,30), low_gamma_confounded (30,80), plus raw; median of the upper-triangle of `np.corrcoef` across channels; then the median over the 40 windows. 1212 gets `masks = {}` and area_mapping_status = 'withheld_probe_identity_unverified'. VERIFIED VERBATIM (theta, beta, low-gamma): 614 DMS 0.072/0.370/0.182, DLS 0.123/0.378/0.188, ACC 0.046/0.387/0.178; 727 DMS 0.149/0.328/0.182, DLS 0.003/0.113/0.093, ACC 0.103/0.355/0.167; 731 DMS 0.131/0.432/0.330, DLS all NaN (blank CSV cell), ACC −0.061/0.242/0.229; 1212 all NaN.
- **Outputs.** signal_identity_summary.csv columns {area}_{band}_median_r (ABSENT; reproduced), signal_identity_figure_data.npz key <mouse>_nominal_depth_band_correlations (PRESENT) → figures/signal_identity panel C
- **Statistics.** none — median Pearson r, no null, no CI, no correction across 3 areas × 4 bands × 3 mice = 36 reported values.
- **Inferential unit.** Channel pairs within an area within a window — deeply nested and non-independent (with 24 channels at 320 µm spacing, most areas contribute only 2-5 channels, i.e. 1-10 pairs).
- **Soundness.** Honestly framed and correctly de-scoped — the code and both READMEs call these 'nominal depth-band diagnostics', not connectivity, and withhold 1212's labels entirely. That framing is the right one and the r values are too low (theta 0.00-0.15) to support any claim regardless. Real limitations: with arange(0, 384, 16) only 2-5 channels land in each ~300-700 µm area, so each r is a median over as few as one pair; there is no null (channel pairs share volume-conducted field, so the correct baseline is a distance-matched or across-area pair set, not zero); no multiple-comparison handling across 36 values; and the 8-12% event-contaminated windows enter these correlations too, which would inflate them (a shared transient correlates all channels). Note the internal tension: beta r (0.11-0.43) exceeds theta r (0.00-0.15) throughout, which is the opposite of what shared LF structure predicts and is more consistent with the broadband/narrowband contamination the same script documents.

#### 12.14 Structural grid-compatibility guard (length equality + VR range containment)
`src/striatum_lfp/align.py:32-54` lines align.py 32-54 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *Methods sentence only. Should be strengthened to state that the round-number lengths make length equality uninformative.*

- **Question.** Are the voltage array, the spike bin grid and the VR timestamps mutually compatible in length/range?
- **Method.** `ok = (lfp_n_samples == spike_n_bins) and (round(max(VR_times_synched)*1000) <= lfp_n_samples)`. Deliberately makes no offset claim; `describe()` prints 'GRID-COMPATIBLE (offset unverified)'.
- **Outputs.** nothing written to disk; used by tests/test_alignment.py only
- **Statistics.** none — a boolean assertion.
- **Inferential unit.** One check per session (4 sessions).
- **Soundness.** The module is scrupulously honest — the docstring, the dataclass message and the test comment ('equal length is necessary, not sufficient') all state that this cannot detect an offset, which is a correction of the earlier '1 kHz spike-grid lock' error that NOTES.md:236-239 records. But the check is weaker still than the code concedes, for a reason not noted anywhere: I verified n_samples is EXACTLY 11,400,000 (1212) and EXACTLY 8,400,000 (614/727/731), i.e. exactly 190.000 and 140.000 minutes, and binned_spikes matches to the sample. Three independent recordings of three different animals cannot all be exactly 8400.000 s long. Both arrays are therefore preallocated or truncated to a round nominal duration, so their length equality carries essentially zero information about a shared time base — it is a property of the export convention, not of the data. VR containment is also trivially satisfied given that padding (614: last VR frame at 7217 s, zeros only from 7952 s, so 735 s of unexplained non-zero voltage after behaviour ends).

#### 12.15 Out-of-core overlap-save block reader
`src/striatum_lfp/reader.py:30-107` lines reader.py 30-107 · **🟡 minor** · status: `scaffold` · manuscript role: *Methods sentence if band power is ever computed; otherwise drop. Flag for reuse before any re-analysis.*

- **Question.** Infrastructure: can a 12-16 GB array be filtered block-wise without injecting seam artefacts into band power?
- **Method.** `block_spans(n, block_samples, pad_samples)` returns (read0, t0, t1, read1) with cores tiling [0, n) exactly once and each read window padded by up to pad_samples per side, clipped to [0, n). Defaults block_samples = 100,800 = 2400 × 42 (whole HDF5 chunk rows, ~101 s at 1 kHz) and pad_samples = 3,000 ('>= 3 s: covers the 1-4 Hz filter transient'). Data upcast to float64; channel selection applied in numpy after the chunk-aligned row read.
- **Outputs.** none — library only
- **Statistics.** n/a — infrastructure. Correctness is established by test against whole-signal filtering: beta 15-30 Hz max error < 1e-6 relative, broadband 1-100 Hz < 2e-3 relative, and a pad=50 control is >20× worse.
- **Inferential unit.** n/a
- **Soundness.** Well designed, well tested, and NOT USED BY ANY LIVE DRIVER. `iter_time_blocks` appears in no script: run_sanity_audit/plot_sanity_audit/run_signal_identity read raw h5py slices, and both gate-crossing drivers read bare per-traversal segments. This is the single most consequential piece of dead infrastructure in the package, because the padding discipline it encodes (pad_samples = 3000) is exactly what run_decode_cca.py omits, and that omission is what produces the fatal decoding artefact documented below. The pad-vs-band tolerance is also documented with unusual care (the broadband 1 Hz edge is called out as the worst case at ~5e-4 relative residual).

#### 12.16 Full-session exact-continuity audit (every stored value read once)
`src/striatum_lfp/audit.py:34-104 (audit_voltage_file) + src/striatum_lfp/sanity.py:127-144 (summarise_fixed_windows) + scripts/run_sanity_audit.py:91-147` lines audit.py 34-104; sanity.py 127-144; run_sanity_audit.py 91-147 · **🟢 ok** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *Methods + supplementary figure. This is the one analysis in the domain that is publication-ready as stated.*

- **Question.** Are the four voltage exports continuous during behaviour, or ~99% empty as the earlier absolute-threshold analysis claimed?
- **Method.** Streams the whole (n_samples × 384) float32 array in blocks of window_samples*block_windows = 1000*42 = 42,000 rows; counts exact zeros (raw == 0.0) and finite values globally and per channel; reshapes complete 1 s windows to compute per-window exact_zero_fraction, median-over-channels RMS (mean-centred within window), median |v|, and max |v|. A window is called a gap only at exact_zero_fraction >= 0.99. No amplitude threshold anywhere. VERIFIED VERBATIM from the surviving npz: global exact-zero fraction 0.0044% (1212), 5.3429% (614), 3.1604% (727), 4.6162% (731); >=99%-zero windows 0.000% / 5.333% (448 win) / 3.155% (265) / 4.607% (387); boolean_runs over the zero mask gives 0 runs for 1212 and EXACTLY 1 terminal run for each of 614 [7952,8399], 727 [8135,8399], 731 [8013,8399]; corridor_zero_window_fraction == 0.0000 and dark_zero_window_fraction == 0.0000 for all four; median RMS over non-zero windows 2.3013e-4 / 2.6192e-6 / 2.5700e-6 / 2.0708e-6 stored units; max |v| 130.9 / 55.2 / 54.87 / 55.38.
- **Outputs.** results/sanity_summary.csv (ABSENT on disk), results/sanity_windows_<mouse>.csv (ABSENT), results/sanity_audit_<mouse>.npz (PRESENT, 4 files) → figures/sanity_audit_overview_v2.{png,svg}
- **Statistics.** none — descriptive per-session exact counts. No test, no null, correctly so.
- **Inferential unit.** 1 s windows within a session (n = 11400/8400/8400/8400); 4 sessions, 4 animals, one session each. Explicitly declared repeated measurements, not biological replicates (SANITY_AUDIT.md:118-120).
- **Soundness.** Structurally the right instrument for the question. Exact-zero counting and finite-counting are scale-free, which is exactly what an undocumented-gain export demands, and reading every value (rather than sampling windows) removes the sampling error that produced the original false '99% empty' verdict. The >=0.99 gap criterion is a defensible convention rather than a tuned threshold, and the terminal-padding structure (single run ending at the last window) is a strong, falsifiable prediction that the data satisfy. I reproduced every published number to the digit from the cache.

#### 12.17 Common-median-referencing sensitivity per spectral peak
`src/striatum_lfp/sanity.py:86-91 (common_median_reference) + scripts/run_signal_identity.py:62-90` lines sanity.py 86-91; run_signal_identity.py 62-90 · **🟢 ok** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *Supplementary panel; the methods justification that low-gamma cannot be recovered by re-referencing.*

- **Question.** Are the narrowband peaks common-mode (removable by re-referencing) or local, i.e. is the contamination fixable at the reference stage?
- **Method.** For each 4 s window the ACROSS-CHANNEL median is subtracted at every sample using ALL 384 channels (`common_median_reference(full_window)`) and only then subsampled to the 24 analysis channels; median Welch PSD recomputed; change at each detected peak reported as 10*log10(referenced_psd[i] / psd[i]). VERIFIED VERBATIM: 614 → 153.81 Hz changes by −4.536 dB, 74.22 Hz by −0.064 dB; 727 → 150.88 Hz +0.004 dB, 74.22 Hz −0.023 dB; 731 → 150.88 Hz −0.063 dB, 73.73 Hz +0.027 dB.
- **Outputs.** signal_identity_summary.csv columns strongest_peak_common_median_change_db, second_peak_common_median_change_db (ABSENT; reproduced) → figures/signal_identity panel A (dashed overlay)
- **Statistics.** none — per-peak dB deltas, single estimate each, no CI across windows.
- **Inferential unit.** One median spectrum per session; peaks within it.
- **Soundness.** Sound, and a good example of the project self-correcting: it overturned an earlier blanket '<0.2 dB' claim (NOTES.md:11-13) and replaced it with a session- and frequency-specific result. Referencing across all 384 channels before subsampling is the correct order of operations (subsampling first would give a 24-channel median, a different and worse estimator). The primitive is unit-tested against an exactly-constructed shared component (test_sanity.py:132-138), and the numeric claims are pinned in test_cached_results.py:72-76 (614 strongest < −4.0 dB, all others |Δ| < 0.2 dB). The scientific reading is also correct and conservative: the persistent ~74 Hz peak is NOT common-mode, so re-referencing will not rescue the low-gamma band. Limitations to state: no uncertainty on the dB deltas (a single median-spectrum ratio), only the top-2 peaks are tested, and 1212 contributes nothing because no peaks were detected in it.

#### 12.18 Legacy single-window channel QC (flat-spectrum + high-std)
`src/striatum_lfp/qc.py:58-104 + scripts/run_stage0_probe.py` lines qc.py 58-104; run_stage0_probe.py 1-7 · **🟢 ok** · status: `superseded` · manuscript role: *Drop. Mention in a methods/error-record appendix at most.*

- **Question.** (Retired) Which channels are good or dead?
- **Method.** One 60 s window starting at qc_probe_start_s = 1000 s; per-channel std and hf_frac = trapz(psd, f >= qc_hf_lo=300 Hz) / trapz(psd, all f) from Welch (nperseg = min(4096, dur)); reject if hf_frac > qc_hf_frac_max = 0.05 ('flat-spectrum', checked first) else if std > median + qc_std_mad_k=4.0 * MAD within its own area ('high-std'); channels in no area labelled 'not-in-area'.
- **Outputs.** nothing — `run_stage0_probe.py` is a 7-line `raise SystemExit` stub; the old figures/stage0_qc_614.* are deleted.
- **Statistics.** Threshold classification. No null, no test.
- **Inferential unit.** Channels within one 60 s window of one session.
- **Soundness.** Correctly and explicitly retired, and the retirement is honestly documented as an error record: the module docstring, README.md:35-36 and test_qc.py:1-5 all state that passing these thresholds is not a quality verdict, and NOTES.md:200-218 preserves the false 'ACC 0/52 dead' conclusions it produced. This is good scientific hygiene — the wrong answer is kept as a record, the entry point is hard-disabled, and the numerical primitives are retained only under regression test. The retained real-data test (test_qc.py:62-70) is carefully reframed to assert only that the diagnostic has dynamic range on 614, explicitly 'not that either side is physiological'. Nothing to fix; do not describe it as live.

## 13. Python `rl_model` package

*Full domain label:* Python `rl_model` package — belief-state two-timescale actor-critic RL model of VR-corridor behaviour, per-mouse MAP fitting, parameter/latent recovery, nested model ladder, per-epoch validation, and per-neuron encoding of model latents in ACC/DMS/DLS/V1/CA1/DG

**Position in pipeline.** CONSUMES exactly one upstream artefact: "Striatum project/processed_data/preprocessed_data5cm.mat" (1.32 GB, v7.3/HDF5), the 5 cm-binned task-mouse product of the MATLAB chain OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1 -> ProcessStriatumTask. It reads spatial_binned_data.{licks,durations}, change_point_mean, zscored_lick_errors, z_spatial_binned_fr_all and the is_{acc,dms,dls,v1,ca1,dg} cell masks. It reimplements two MATLAB helpers in Python rather than calling them — find_learning_points.m (lp_z_threshold -2, lp_window 10, lp_min_consecutive 7) and epoch_indices.m (trials_per_epoch 10, Naive 1:10, Intermediate lp-10:lp-1, Expert lp:lp+9) — both ports verified faithful, but they will silently diverge if the .m files change. It uses no other repo code and no other .mat (notably NOT preprocessed_data2p5cm.mat, tca_outputs.mat, or any *_control*.mat).

PRODUCES, in dependency order: results/real_fits_v6_{interleaved,forward}/M01..M16.npz (fit_real_data.py) -> results/rl_latents.mat + results/rl_latents.npz (plot_real_data.py, from the interleaved dir by default) -> results/encoding_v6/M01..M16.npz (run_neural_encoding.py, reading rl_latents.npz) -> figures/fig_encoding_stats.png, fig_encoding_examples.png (plot_encoding_detail.py). Side branches: results/recovery_v*.npz + results/fits_v*/ (run_parameter_recovery.py, self-contained synthetic), results/ladder_{real,synth}/ (run_model_ladder.py, NEVER MATERIALISED), figures/fig_epoch_validation_{lick,vel}.png (plot_epoch_validation.py, reading the real_fits dir + the .mat).

DOWNSTREAM CONSUMERS: none in MATLAB. results/rl_latents.mat is written specifically so "existing MATLAB plotting / neural-regression code consumes them unchanged" (UNDERSTANDING.md), but a grep for `rl_latents` across every .m file in the repository returns no hits — the export is currently a dead end. The only real consumers are the two Python scripts run_neural_encoding.py and plot_encoding_detail.py, both via results/rl_latents.npz. The package is a leaf: nothing else in StriatumACC depends on it, and the separate MATLAB belief-state code (simulatePOMDP_striatum.m, beliefMDP.m, calculate_nll.m, Run_DMS_ACC_Model.m) is listed in NOTES.md among the legacy/superseded scripts and is unrelated to this package.

ORCHESTRATION: there is no Snakemake/Make wiring. Every script is an incremental, idempotent, time-budgeted (RLMODEL_TIME_BUDGET) module intended to be re-invoked until it prints DONE, coordinating through per-mouse .npz files and git-tracked DONE_* marker files in results/. Because the markers are tracked while the .npz outputs are gitignored (*.npz in the repo .gitignore), DONE_v7 and DONE_ladder_synth are present on this machine while their actual outputs are not — the marker protocol cannot distinguish "completed here" from "completed in some container".

**Data flow, shapes and units.** INPUT (single file): "Striatum project/processed_data/preprocessed_data5cm.mat", 1,316,706,605 bytes, MATLAB v7.3 = HDF5, read via h5py with object-reference dereferencing. Fields used: preprocessed_data.n_trials (16 animals -> n_animals inferred from its first dim), .spatial_binned_data{i}.licks (bins x trials, lick COUNTS, occasional NaN) and .durations (bins x trials, seconds), .change_point_mean{i} (scalar disengagement trial), .zscored_lick_errors{i} (1 x n_trials), .z_spatial_binned_fr_all{i} (trials x bins x cells, already z-scored in MATLAB over the whole session), .is_{acc,dms,dls,v1,ca1,dg}{i} (per-cell boolean).

GEOMETRY (config.py, mirrors project_cfg.m): corridor 0-200 a.u.; BIN_SIZE_AU = 4.0 -> N_BINS = 50; AU_TO_CM = 1.25 -> BIN_SIZE_CM = 5.0 cm/bin; bin centres (arange(50)+0.5)*4 = 2, 6, ..., 198 a.u.; VZ = 80.0 a.u. (bin 19, centre 78 / bin 20 centre 82); RZ = 100.0-135.0 a.u. -> RZ_MASK true for bin indices 25-33 inclusive (9 bins). io_real transposes to (trials x bins).

BEHAVIOURAL PREPROCESSING (io_real.py): validity = isfinite(licks) & isfinite(durations) & (durations > 0); licks set to 0.0 where invalid; velocity = 5.0 cm / max(duration, 1e-9), CLIPPED to VEL_CLIP_CM_S = (2.0, 150.0) cm/s; logv = log(clipped velocity), 0.0 where invalid. Sessions truncated at change_point_mean (kept trials n_keep = min(cp, n_total), min 1); mice with non-finite cp keep all trials.

COHORT AS FIT (n_total -> n_kept trials): M01 357->125, M02 469->225, M03 71->71, M04 371->100, M05 501->109, M06 76->76, M07 90->90, M08 331->92, M09 260->131, M10 189->79, M11 299->182, M12 104->100, M13 155->155, M14 257->112, M15 142->27, M16 109->51. Total 1725 fitted trials across 16 mice; per-mouse arrays (n_kept x 50) float64.

FITTING TENSORS: sessions zero-padded to a bucketed length of 256 (n_kept<=256) or 512 trials so mice share a JIT compilation; padded rows have mask 0 in both score and learn masks. Interleaved CV holds out trial indices arange(4, nt, 5) (25, 45, 14, 20, 21, 15, 18, 18, 26, 15, 36, 20, 31, 22, 5, 10 test trials for M01..M16); forward CV holds out arange(round(0.75*nt), nt) (31, 56, 18, 25, 27, 19, 22, 23, 33, 20, 46, 25, 39, 28, 7, 13 test trials). Fit metric normalised per VALID held-out bin (nats/bin).

LATENTS (per mouse, (n_kept x 50) float64): value (dimensionless, w_crit.b), rpe = delta_actor (reward units), precision = 1/max(sigma_post, 1e-3) (a.u.^-2), lick_rate = expected COUNT mu_lick = lam*dt (licks/bin, NOT licks/s), v_mean = exp(log_v_mean) (cm/s, log-normal median), belief_mean (a.u.), sigma (a.u.^2). Exported as MATLAB cell arrays (1 x 16 object arrays) in results/rl_latents.mat (4,844,928 bytes) and as dtype=object arrays in results/rl_latents.npz (4,028,942 bytes), both 2026-06-02 15:39, both derived from results/real_fits_v6_interleaved. test_idx is +1-shifted to MATLAB 1-based on export.

NEURAL TENSORS (neural_encoding.load_neural): fr per mouse (n_total_trials x 50 x n_cells), truncated to [:n_kept] in the encoding script. Cell counts by area, pooled over 16 mice: ACC 699, DMS 401, DLS 522, V1 264, CA1 133, DG 18 = 2037 cells total (per-mouse totals 133, 193, 47, 152, 467, 17, 77, 33, 86, 63, 193, 210, 110, 80, 42, 134). Every cell receives an area label (none left as "none").

ENCODING DESIGN MATRIX: rows = valid (trial x bin) cells (up to n_kept*50, e.g. 11,250 for M02); columns = 3 interest regressors (value, rpe, precision) + 2 behavioural nuisances (observed lick count, observed velocity in cm/s) + 5 DCT drift cosines over trials = 10 columns. Ridge lam = 1.0, 5 trial-wise folds, 50 trial-shuffles and 50 bin-shuffles per (latent, model), p-floor 1/51 = 0.0196, alpha 0.05. Mean cross-validated full-model R2 = 0.0718 ('beh') and 0.0439 ('beh_spatial'); mean unique dR2 per latent +0.0004 to +0.0016 (value/rpe) and +0.005 to +0.040 (precision under 'beh').

EPOCH ARM: learning points (0-based) M01 21, M02 43, M03 31, M04 53, M05 53, M06 35, M07 32, M08 15, M09 43, M10 66, M11 83, M12 NA, M13 22, M14 38, M15 25, M16 NA; epochs are 10-trial windows (Naive trials 0-9, Intermediate lp-10..lp-1, Expert lp..lp+9). Only 13/16 mice yield a valid Expert epoch (M12 and M16 non-learners; M15 lp+10 > n_kept=27).

ANALYST-COMPUTED DIAGNOSTICS (not repo artefacts; run against on-disk fits + current latents):
A. Exposure-matched null test on the lick channel. Replacing the coded per-bin COUNT null with a per-bin RATE null (train-trial licks-per-second x observed dt, identical 50-parameter budget) collapses the headline gain: interleaved +0.604 -> +0.109 nats/bin (16/16 -> 11/16 mice positive); forward +0.454 -> +0.091 (15/16 -> 10/16). Per-mouse the residual gain is negative for M01/M05/M08/M11/M15 (interleaved) and M04/M05/M08/M09/M10/M16 (forward). ~80% of the reported fit-quality advantage is dwell-time exposure.
B. RPE-regressor confound. After per-bin demeaning, the rpe latent is R2=0.467 (cohort mean) explained by the analysis's own nuisance set (licks, velocity, 5 drift cosines); per mouse it reaches 0.983 (M03), 0.934 (M06), 0.991 (M12) with r(rpe, licks) = -0.986, -0.966, -0.995. Adding dt=5/v and cumulative RZ licks raises the mean to 0.558 and, for M07, to 1.000 (r(rpe, dt) = -0.999). Because the nuisance set contains velocity but not 1/v, dwell-time-tuned neurons can be credited as RPE-encoding.
C. Spatial-demean retained variance (spatial_demean_var_ratio, current latents): value mean 0.194 (range 0.056-0.331); rpe mean 0.746; precision median 0.000, mean 0.048 — driven entirely by M16 (0.727), all other mice 0.000-0.035. The doc's "~6%" for precision is a cohort mean inflated by one animal; the median is zero.
D. Real fitted parameters lie far outside the tested recovery region: mean |u_fit - u0| in units of the recovery jitter SD (0.35) = kappa_v 10.7, Q 9.2, v_slope 8.9, rho 8.3, eta_a 7.8, theta 6.5, R0 6.0, beta 4.0, eta_w 4.1, gamma 3.9, w_init 3.7, R_slope 3.2, lambda_max 3.0, iti_inflation 2.8, log_sigma_v 2.3, v_base 1.3. No parameter hits the +/-12 box, but natural-space extremes are implausible (lambda_max up to 2.63e4 licks/s, iti_inflation up to 1126, R0 up to 469, beta up to 466, gamma down to 0.0011).

PSEUDOREPLICATION SUMMARY: the only analysis with an animal-level inferential unit is the fit-quality "x/16 mice positive" count and the per-epoch "x/16 mice with delta-r>0.5" count — and neither carries a statistical test. Everything neural is at the neuron level (2037 neurons across 16 mice, one mouse contributing 467), with a binomial test that assumes independence. No mixed model, no per-mouse aggregation, no BH-FDR anywhere in the package despite the project convention (fdr_correct.m).
