### Analyses (13)

#### 13.1 Real-data fit + cross-validated fit quality vs a saturated per-bin null
`Striatum project/rl_model/scripts/fit_real_data.py` lines 52-246 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure (Fig 1E fit quality) as currently framed — but the headline number must be recomputed against an exposure-matched null before it can be claimed*

- **Question.** Does the RL agent predict held-out behaviour better than a spatial-profile-only null?
- **Method.** 16 task mice from ../processed_data/preprocessed_data5cm.mat, sessions truncated at change_point_mean (disengagement). Two CV schemes, each in its own results dir (env RLMODEL_CV): 'interleaved' = every 5th trial held out (TEST_EVERY=5); 'forward' = trailing FORWARD_FRAC=0.25 of trials held out. score mask zeroes test trials; learn_mask = full validity mask so test trials STILL drive teacher-forced learning. Sessions zero-padded to 256 or 512 trials for JIT bucketing. N_RESTARTS=4, seed=int(mouse[1:]), maxiter 250 if nt>200 else 400. Null: per-bin Poisson COUNT rate lam_b = train-trial mean lick count in bin b, plus per-bin log-normal N(mu_b, sd_b) on log-velocity from train trials (~150 free parameters). Metric: held-out total log-likelihood divided by number of valid held-out bins (nats/bin), reported separately for lick and velocity channels, as model minus null.
- **Inputs.** processed_data/preprocessed_data5cm.mat (spatial_binned_data.licks, .durations, change_point_mean)
- **Outputs.** results/real_fits_v6_interleaved/M01..M16.npz and results/real_fits_v6_forward/M01..M16.npz (each: u_fit, params, nll, test_idx, train_idx, model/null lick+vel test+train LL/bin, lat_{value,rpe,precision,lick_rate,v_mean,belief_mean,sigma}); markers results/DONE_real_v6_{interleaved,forward}
- **Statistics.** no test at all — only cohort mean gain and a count of mice with positive gain. No paired test across mice, no CI, no correction.
- **Inferential unit.** mouse for the count (n=16); (trial x bin) for the nats/bin normalisation
- **Soundness.** The CV mask split is correct and TDD-pinned, and the null is estimated on train trials only — both good. Two serious problems. (1) THE NULL IS NOT EXPOSURE-MATCHED. The model predicts lick COUNT as Poisson(rate*dt) using the observed same-bin dwell time; the null predicts a fixed count per bin with no dt term. Re-running the same held-out evaluation against an exposure-matched null (per-bin licks-per-second from train trials x observed dt, same 50 parameters) collapses the headline gain: interleaved +0.604 -> +0.109 nats/bin and 16/16 -> 11/16 mice positive; forward +0.454 -> +0.091 and 15/16 -> 10/16. ~80% of the reported lick-channel advantage is dwell-time exposure, not RL structure. (2) Because learn_mask includes the held-out trials, the model's prediction at bin b of a held-out trial is conditioned on that same trial's earlier bins (w_crit updated within-trial from observed licks) — a filtering/one-step-ahead likelihood, whereas the null has no within-trial adaptation. Defensible if described as one-step-ahead, but it is not a trial-level hold-out and the asymmetry favours the model.
- **Concerns.**
    - FATAL for the headline claim: null lacks the dwell-time exposure term the model uses. Analyst-computed exposure-matched null reduces mean lick gain from +0.604 to +0.109 (interleaved) and +0.454 to +0.091 (forward)
    - held-out trials drive learning (by design), so the 'held-out' LL is conditioned on earlier bins of the held-out trial itself; the null is not allowed the same adaptivity
    - velocity channel is negative under interleaved CV: mean gain -0.064, only 3/16 mice positive (forward: +0.057, 7/16) — the velocity claim is not supported
    - no statistical test on the cohort gain (no paired signed-rank, no CI); 'x/16 mice positive' is the only inference
    - severe trial attrition from disengagement truncation, undocumented in the fit-quality figure: M05 501->109, M04 371->100, M01 357->125, M08 331->92 trials kept
    - UNDERSTANDING.md still lists these refits as 'Open ... pending' although both dirs completed on 2026-06-02; the actual on-disk numbers are recorded nowhere

#### 13.2 Per-neuron ridge encoding of RL latents (dR2 with shuffle nulls)
`Striatum project/rl_model/rl_model/neural_encoding.py` lines 102-188 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure (Fig 4A/B) — but the RPE panel cannot be claimed until dt and cumulative-RZ-lick nuisances are added, and per-neuron significance needs FDR*

- **Question.** Do neurons in ACC/DMS/DLS/V1/CA1/DG encode the model's value, RPE and precision beyond observed behaviour, slow session drift, and stationary spatial tuning?
- **Method.** Per mouse, design matrix rows = valid (trial x bin) cells. Interest regressors: value, rpe, precision (z-scored). Nuisance: observed lick count, observed velocity, and 5 DCT cosine drift functions over trials (_drift_basis n=5). Two preprocessing models: 'beh' = global demean; 'beh_spatial' = subtract each spatial bin's across-trial mean (so a latent is credited only for trial-by-trial modulation). Ridge with FIXED lam=1.0 (no tuning), solved vectorised over all neurons. CV: trial-wise 5 folds (fold_of_row = (arange(T) % 5) shuffled with default_rng(0)), so all 50 bins of a trial share a fold. Readout per latent = unique CV dR2 = R2(full) - R2(full minus that latent). Nulls: n_shuffle=50 (default, used for all real data) trial permutations of that latent (destroys trial alignment, keeps spatial profile) and 50 bin permutations; p = (#(null >= observed) + 1)/(50 + 1), so the p-value FLOOR is 1/51 = 0.0196. Null seeds are deterministic (seed + 101*(j+1) and seed + 211*(j+1), seed=0).
- **Inputs.** z_spatial_binned_fr_all (already z-scored in MATLAB over the whole session), is_{acc,dms,dls,v1,ca1,dg} masks, behavioural licks/velocity/mask, and results/rl_latents.npz
- **Outputs.** results/encoding_v6/M01..M16.npz per mouse: area, r2_{beh,beh_spatial}, dR2_/pval_/pvalbin_{model}_{latent}
- **Statistics.** Per-neuron one-sided permutation p from 50 shuffles (floor 0.0196), tested at alpha=0.05. NO multiple-comparison correction across the 2037 neurons, the 3 latents, the 2 models, or the 2 nulls. R2 is cross-validated (good), but the standardisation and demeaning are fit on ALL rows before the CV split.
- **Inferential unit.** neuron (2037 neurons pooled across 16 mice); rows are (trial x bin) cells nested within neuron within mouse
- **Soundness.** The scaffolding is careful (trial-wise folds so no within-trial leakage, unique-contribution dR2, behaviour and drift as nuisances, deterministic seeds, and a synthetic ground-truth gate that passes). Three real problems. (1) LEAKAGE: _zscore, _demean_global and _demean_bin are computed over all rows including the test folds, and _cv_r2's SST uses the full-data Y.mean(0) — per-bin means in particular leak the test fold's own mean into its prediction. Mild but systematic and trivially fixable. (2) THE RPE REGRESSOR IS PARTLY OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR. delta_actor contains -C_LICK*lick - rho*dt and a reward term built from observed cumulative RZ licks. Measured on the current latents after per-bin demeaning: rpe is on average R2=0.467 explained by the nuisance set already, and for M03/M06/M12 it is 0.98/0.93/0.99 (r(rpe, licks) = -0.99, -0.97, -0.995). Critically the nuisance set contains VELOCITY but not dt = 5/v, and rpe depends on 1/v: for M07 r(rpe, dt) = -0.999 and adding dt + cumulative RZ licks to the nuisance set raises R2 to 1.000. So a neuron with hyperbolic dwell-time (rather than linear velocity) tuning can be credited as 'RPE-encoding'. (3) The 'beh_spatial' model tests only the residual after per-bin demeaning: measured retained-variance fraction is ~0.19 mean for value (range 0.056-0.331) and ~0.000 median for precision (mean 0.048, driven entirely by M16 at 0.727) — so value is judged on ~19% of its variance and precision cannot be tested there at all (correctly documented, and quantified by spatial_demean_var_ratio).
- **Concerns.**
    - FATAL for the RPE claim: `rpe` is an explicit function of the same-bin observed lick count and dwell time; nuisance set includes velocity but NOT dt=5/v, so the 1/v component is uncontrolled (M07: r(rpe,dt)=-0.999, R2->1.000 once dt is added)
    - mean R2 of rpe on the existing nuisance set = 0.467; for M03/M06/M12 it is 0.93-0.99, so 'RPE encoding' rests on a 1-7% residual for those mice
    - no multiple-comparison correction over 2037 neurons x 3 latents x 2 models x 2 nulls; the project convention (BH-FDR via fdr_correct.m) is not applied here
    - leakage: z-scoring, global demeaning and per-bin demeaning are fit on all rows including the test folds; SST uses the full-data mean
    - n_shuffle=50 gives a p-value floor of 0.0196 — only ~2.5x below alpha=0.05, so per-neuron p-values have almost no resolution
    - ridge lam=1.0 fixed, never tuned or cross-validated; no intercept column
    - bin-shuffle null IS computed but never used in the headline; measured pass rates (19-59%) sometimes EXCEED the trial-shuffle rates, and no conjunction is required
    - value is tested on only ~19% of its variance under beh_spatial (retained-variance fraction 0.056-0.331); precision's is ~0 for 15/16 mice
    - neural fr is z-scored upstream over the whole session before any split

#### 13.3 Per-mouse MAP fitting engine
`Striatum project/rl_model/rl_model/fitting.py` lines 17-114 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only, but the parameter table it produces should not be interpreted per-parameter without an identifiability analysis at the fitted point*

- **Question.** Can the 16 subjective parameters be estimated per mouse from behaviour alone?
- **Method.** Minimise negative teacher-forced log-likelihood + 0.5*sum(((u-u0)/prior_sd)^2) — i.e. MAP with an isotropic Gaussian prior of SD prior_sd=4.0 (default, used everywhere) centred on u0 = the `typical` parameter vector. Optimiser: scipy L-BFGS-B on exact JAX value_and_grad, bounds +/-12.0 per coordinate, maxiter default 400 (real fits use 250 if n_trials>200), ftol=1e-10. Restarts: restart 0 starts exactly at u0; restarts 1..n-1 at u0 + 0.5*N(0,1) per coordinate, seeded by `seed`. Returns the MINIMUM-nll restart (order statistic over inits). `fixed={name: unconstrained_value}` pins a parameter by collapsing its box bound to a point (used by the model ladder).
- **Inputs.** (n_trials x 50) licks, logv, score mask, learn mask
- **Outputs.** dict{u_fit, params (natural space), nll, success, restart_nlls}; persisted per mouse as results/real_fits_v6_{mode}/M??.npz
- **Statistics.** none reported per fit beyond nll and restart_nlls; no Hessian/standard errors, no profile likelihoods, no identifiability diagnostics at the fitted point
- **Inferential unit.** one mouse = one fit; no pooling, no hierarchy
- **Soundness.** Mechanically sound (exact gradients, generous box, MAP regularisation of flat directions). But: (a) the prior centre, the optimiser start, and the synthetic ground-truth centre are all the SAME vector u0, which makes the recovery experiment optimistically biased; (b) reported nll is a min-over-restarts order statistic (4 restarts real, 1 synthetic/ladder) so nll is not comparable across runs with different restart counts; (c) no curvature-based identifiability check at the real fitted parameters, and the real fits land 1.3-10.7 recovery-jitter-SDs away from u0 (measured: Q 9.2, kappa_v 10.7, v_slope 8.9, rho 8.3, eta_a 7.8, theta 6.5, R0 6.0 SDs), i.e. outside the region where recovery was ever tested. Several fitted natural values are physiologically implausible (R0 up to 469, iti_inflation up to 1126, lambda_max up to 2.6e4 licks/s, beta up to 466, gamma down to 0.0011) yet none hit the +/-12 box, so they are sloppy-direction drift the weak prior does not restrain.
- **Concerns.**
    - prior centre == optimiser start == synthetic ground-truth centre (u0), so recovery is measured under maximally favourable initialisation
    - reported nll = min over restarts (order statistic); 4 restarts for real fits, 1 for recovery and 1 for every ladder cell
    - no standard errors / Hessian / profile likelihood; parameter-level claims are unsupported at the fitted point
    - real fitted parameters sit 1.3-10.7 jitter-SDs from u0 — outside the tested recovery region; several natural values implausible (lambda_max 2.6e4 licks/s, iti_inflation 1126, R0 469)
    - fitting.recovery_table (lines 117-134) is dead code — never called by any script or test

#### 13.4 Parameter recovery on a synthetic cohort
`Striatum project/rl_model/scripts/run_parameter_recovery.py` lines 49-161 · **🟠 major** · status: `superseded` · manuscript role: *supplementary (methods validation) — but must be re-run with jitter spanning the real fitted range before it can support any per-parameter claim*

- **Question.** Are the 16 subjective parameters identifiable from simulated behaviour of known ground truth?
- **Method.** make_cohort(n_mice=12, n_trials=120, seed=2026, jitter=0.35): each synthetic mouse's u_true = u0 + 0.35*N(0,1) per coordinate in UNCONSTRAINED space; agent rolled out generatively (simulate_session, own sampled licks/velocities, PRNGKey(seed*7919+m)). Fit with fit_mouse(n_restarts=1, seed=100+m, prior_sd=4.0, maxiter=400) — i.e. a single start, exactly at u0. Recovery metric = Pearson r of true vs fitted across the 12 mice, computed in NATURAL space (per parameter), plus RMSE via the unused recovery_table. Pass flag hard-coded at r>=0.6 (params) and r>=0.9 (latents).
- **Inputs.** none (self-generating; deterministic given seed=2026)
- **Outputs.** CONFIGURED: results/fits_v7/mouse_00..11.npz, results/recovery_v7.npz, results/DONE_v7, figures/fig_param_recovery.png, fig_latent_recovery.png, fig_behaviour.png, fig_example_latents.png. PRESENT ON DISK: only up to recovery_v6.npz + fits_v6/ (2026-05-24); v7 outputs absent.
- **Statistics.** Pearson r across n=12 synthetic mice per parameter; no CI, no p-value, no bootstrap. n=12 means r>=0.6 is roughly the 5% two-sided critical value — the 'OK' threshold is barely above chance.
- **Inferential unit.** synthetic mouse (n=12) for parameter r; (trial x bin) pooled within mouse for latent r
- **Soundness.** The right gate to have, but as configured it is a weak test of identifiability. (a) Ground truth is drawn around exactly the prior centre and the optimiser's only start — the fit begins at the mean of the truth distribution with n_restarts=1, so recovery measures local sensitivity, not global identifiability. (b) The tested range (SD 0.35 in unconstrained space) is 3-11x narrower than where the real fits actually land (measured mean |u_fit-u0|/0.35 = 1.3 to 10.7 per parameter), so the recovery result does not license parameter interpretation on real data. (c) STALE/ABSENT ARTEFACT: the script is configured for v7 (FITSDIR=results/fits_v7, RESULTS_NPZ=recovery_v7.npz, DONE_v7) but neither fits_v7/ nor recovery_v7.npz exists on this machine — only the tracked DONE_v7 marker. The newest recovery on disk is recovery_v6.npz (2026-05-24) and figures fig_param_recovery.png / fig_latent_recovery.png date from that run, i.e. they predate the 2026-06-02 velocity-gradient correction. The v7 numbers quoted in UNDERSTANDING.md are not reproducible from local artefacts.
- **Concerns.**
    - single restart from u0 = prior centre = centre of the ground-truth distribution: recovery is measured under the most favourable possible initialisation
    - jitter SD 0.35 (unconstrained) vs real fits 1.3-10.7 SDs from u0 — identifiability never tested where the real parameters live
    - n=12 mice: r>=0.6 'OK' threshold is approximately the 5% critical value for n=12; no CIs
    - configured v7 outputs (fits_v7/, recovery_v7.npz) do not exist locally; on-disk recovery is v6, predating the velocity-gradient fix; the tracked DONE_v7 marker falsely signals completion
    - natural-space Pearson r over exp/sigmoid-transformed parameters is dominated by the largest few values (e.g. iti_inflation, lambda_max) — a rank correlation would be more honest

#### 13.5 Nested model-comparison ladder
`Striatum project/rl_model/scripts/run_model_ladder.py` lines 62-195 · **🟠 major** · status: `gated` · manuscript role: *main figure if run on real data (the component-necessity panel); currently cannot be cited at all*

- **Question.** Does each learning channel (critic learning, actor learning) earn its place by improving held-out prediction?
- **Method.** Four nested models, each reduced by pinning learning rates to the unconstrained lower bound OFF=-12.0 (sigmoid(-12)=6e-6): full (nothing pinned); no_value_learning (eta_w off -> critic frozen at flat w_init); no_actors (eta_a off -> lick/velocity are pure critic read-outs); fixed_agent (both off). Held-out evaluation is FORWARD/blocked CV only (FORWARD_FRAC=0.25); learn mask full, score mask zeroes the held-out block. Each cell fit with n_restarts=1, maxiter 150 (synth) / 250 if nt>200 else 400, seed=hash(mouse_id)%10000. Metric: held-out (lick+vel) log-likelihood per valid bin; reported as mean over mice, delta(full - reduced), and a count of mice where full wins. Comparison is on HELD-OUT likelihood — no AIC/BIC anywhere in the package.
- **Inputs.** real: preprocessed_data5cm.mat via load_real_cohort; synth: make_cohort(n_mice=3, n_trials=120, seed=2027, jitter=0.3)
- **Outputs.** CONFIGURED: results/ladder_{real,synth}/{mouse}__{model}.npz, figures/fig_model_ladder_{real,synth}.png, results/DONE_ladder_{real,synth}. PRESENT: only results/DONE_ladder_synth (git-tracked marker); no cell files, no figure.
- **Statistics.** none — cohort mean delta and 'mice full>this' count only. No paired test (signed-rank/t), no CI, no correction for the 3 comparisons.
- **Inferential unit.** mouse (n=3 synthetic; n=16 intended for real)
- **Soundness.** The design is the right one (nested, held-out, forward CV so it tests learning-curve generalisation rather than spatial profile). BUT: THE REAL LADDER HAS NEVER BEEN RUN. Neither results/ladder_real/ nor results/ladder_synth/ exists on this machine, and figures/fig_model_ladder_*.png is absent; only the tracked marker results/DONE_ladder_synth exists, so the synthetic ladder numbers quoted in UNDERSTANDING.md were produced in a container and are not reproducible locally. There is no DONE_ladder_real. The .mat the real ladder needs IS present here (../processed_data/preprocessed_data5cm.mat), so the blocker recorded in UNDERSTANDING.md ('need the .mat, not in this container') no longer applies. Methodological weaknesses even once run: n_restarts=1 per cell means a model-comparison delta can be optimiser luck, and it disadvantages `full` (most free parameters, hardest landscape); the seed uses Python's hash() on a str, which is PYTHONHASHSEED-salted and therefore NOT reproducible across processes (harmless only because with n_restarts=1 the seed is never used); the synthetic demonstration has n=3 mice, so '3/3 mice' is uninformative; no statistical test on the deltas.
- **Concerns.**
    - real ladder never run — no ladder_real/ dir, no DONE_ladder_real, no figure; the .mat is available so the recorded blocker is stale
    - synthetic ladder artefacts absent locally too; its numbers survive only as prose in UNDERSTANDING.md
    - n_restarts=1 per (mouse, model) cell: deltas may reflect optimiser basin rather than model capacity, and the bias runs against the full model
    - seed=hash(str)%10000 is PYTHONHASHSEED-salted — non-reproducible if n_restarts is ever raised
    - no paired statistical test and no multiple-comparison handling over the 3 nested contrasts
    - n=3 mice in the synthetic demonstration

#### 13.6 Per-epoch (Naive/Intermediate/Expert) validation of the learning-curve change
`Striatum project/rl_model/scripts/plot_epoch_validation.py` lines 34-154 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure (the redesign's success criterion) — but must be re-framed as an in-sample conditional-intensity match, with the denominator corrected to n=13 and a null added*

- **Question.** Does the model reproduce the epoch-to-epoch CHANGE in the spatial lick and velocity profiles, not merely the session average?
- **Method.** Learning point (LP) recomputed in Python from preprocessed_data.zscored_lick_errors: first trial that is itself <= -2.0 AND whose forward 10-trial window contains >= 7 sub-threshold trials — a faithful port of find_learning_points.m (lp_z_threshold -2, lp_window 10, lp_min_consecutive 7) and epoch_indices.m (trials_per_epoch 10, Naive = first 10 trials, Intermediate = lp-10..lp-1, Expert = lp..lp+9). For each epoch, mask-weighted trial-average spatial profile (50 bins) of observed licks vs model lat_lick_rate, and of observed exp(logv) vs model lat_v_mean. Validation statistic: Pearson r between the observed Naive->Expert difference profile and the model's Naive->Expert difference profile (50 bins). Reported as count of mice with delta-r > 0.5 and the cohort nanmean. Reads results/real_fits_v6_interleaved by default (env RLMODEL_REALDIR).
- **Inputs.** preprocessed_data5cm.mat (zscored_lick_errors, spatial_binned_data) + results/real_fits_v6_interleaved/*.npz
- **Outputs.** figures/fig_epoch_validation_lick.png, fig_epoch_validation_vel.png (2026-06-02); nothing saved to disk as data
- **Statistics.** Pearson r over 50 spatial bins per mouse (bins are nested/serially correlated within mouse — no correction, no CI, no null); cohort summary = count above an arbitrary 0.5 threshold + nanmean. No hypothesis test anywhere.
- **Inferential unit.** mouse for the count; spatial bin (n=50, autocorrelated) for each per-mouse r
- **Soundness.** This is the intended headline learning-curve check and it does test the right thing qualitatively — but it is essentially IN-SAMPLE. Under interleaved CV, 80% of every epoch's trials were in the fitting objective, and the model profile is a teacher-forced conditional intensity (it uses the observed velocity for dt and the observed licks for its within-trial learning), so it is a one-step-ahead fit, not a free-running simulation of the epoch change. Verified empirically: recomputing on real_fits_v6_forward (where the fit never saw the trailing 25%) gives essentially identical numbers (lick mean delta-r 0.708 vs 0.704; vel 0.351 vs 0.361), which shows the metric is insensitive to what was held out — i.e. it is not measuring generalisation. DENOMINATOR ERROR: only 13/16 mice have a usable Expert epoch (M12 and M16 are non-learners, LP=NA; M15 has 27 trials post-truncation with LP=25 so lp+10>nt), yet the figure reports 'x/16 mice' while the mean is a nanmean over 13. So '11/16' is really 11/13. Actual on-disk numbers (interleaved): lick delta-r > 0.5 for 11/13 valid mice, mean +0.704 (M01 .57, M02 .72, M03 .49, M04 .75, M05 .80, M06 .71, M07 .66, M08 .84, M09 .95, M10 .85, M11 .24, M13 .64, M14 .92); velocity 6/13, mean +0.361, with 3 mice negative (M05 -0.21, M07 -0.04, M08 -0.41).
- **Concerns.**
    - in-sample: 80% of every epoch's trials were in the fitting objective under interleaved CV, and the model curve is a teacher-forced conditional intensity, not a simulation
    - forward-CV fits give near-identical delta-r (0.708 vs 0.704 lick), proving the metric does not test generalisation
    - denominator inconsistency: 'x/16 mice' printed, but only 13 mice have a valid Expert epoch; mean is a nanmean over 13
    - delta-r > 0.5 is an arbitrary threshold with no null distribution; 50 spatial bins are strongly autocorrelated so the per-mouse r has far fewer than 48 effective df
    - model velocity is exp(log_v_mean) (log-normal median) compared against the observed mean velocity — small systematic bias
    - potential NameError if a mouse has nt < 10 (n_obs/n_mod referenced before assignment when the Naive epoch is None)
    - LP is computed on the FULL session but epochs are indexed into the disengagement-truncated session, so mice whose LP falls after truncation silently drop out

#### 13.8 Publication statistics for the encoding result (Wilson CI + binomial test)
`Striatum project/rl_model/scripts/plot_encoding_detail.py` lines 29-221 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure (Fig 4B) — needs an animal-level test (mixed model or per-mouse fractions), FDR across the 18 area x latent tests, and per-neuron FDR*

- **Question.** Is the fraction of encoding neurons per area above chance, and what do example RPE neurons look like?
- **Method.** Pools per-neuron records across mice. Per-latent model choice is fixed: MODEL_BY_LATENT = {value: beh_spatial, rpe: beh_spatial, precision: beh} — precision is deliberately reported under the weaker model because it retains ~0 variance after per-bin demeaning. Per area x latent: fraction with p<0.05, Wilson 95% CI (z=1.96), and scipy.stats.binomtest(k, n, 0.05, alternative='greater'). Bin-shuffle pass rate is printed as a text column only, never plotted or tested. Example figure: top-2 significant RPE neurons per DMS/DLS/ACC by dR2, excluding neurons whose per-bin-demeaned RZ-window residual has nanstd < 0.15; shows z-firing raster, RPE latent raster, and the trial-by-trial RZ-window residual scatter with a Pearson r.

- **Outputs.** figures/fig_encoding_stats.png, figures/fig_encoding_examples.png (both 2026-05-25 08:08); printed text table; nothing saved as data
- **Statistics.** binomial test of the observed significant count against p0=0.05, one-sided greater, per (area, latent) = 18 tests. NO correction across the 18 tests. Wilson 95% CI. Example-neuron Pearson r reported with no p-value and after selecting those neurons for having the largest dR2.

- **Soundness.** Group-level inference against chance is the right instinct and the precision caveat is honestly documented in the code. But the binomial test treats 2037 neurons pooled across 16 animals as independent Bernoulli draws, which is textbook pseudoreplication: a single mouse contributing 467 cells (M05) can drive an area's result, and shared per-mouse latents induce exactly the dependence the test assumes away. There is no mixed-effects or per-mouse aggregation anywhere. Actual on-disk numbers (encoding_v6, headline models): ACC n=699 value 140 (20%, binom p=1.3e-44), rpe 158 (23%, p=1.9e-57), precision 24 (3%, p=0.98 ns); DMS n=401 value 20%, rpe 29%, precision 9%; DLS n=522 value 21%, rpe 33%, precision 8%; V1 n=264 value 30%, rpe 32%, precision 10%; CA1 n=133 value 21%, rpe 41%, precision 6% (ns); DG n=18 value 6% (ns), rpe 17% (ns), precision 6% (ns). Mean unique dR2 is tiny throughout: +0.0004 to +0.0016 for value/rpe (mean full-model CV R2 = 0.044 under beh_spatial, 0.072 under beh). The example-neuron panel is selected-on-the-statistic (top dR2) and then reports a raw correlation on the same data — circular as a display, acceptable only if labelled as illustrative.
- **Concerns.**
    - pseudoreplication: binomial test pools 2037 neurons across 16 mice as independent; one mouse contributes 467 cells
    - no correction across the 18 (area x latent) binomial tests, nor per-neuron FDR (the project standard fdr_correct.m/BH is not used)
    - effect sizes are minute (mean unique dR2 +0.0004 to +0.0016) while significance is enormous (p~1e-57) — a pure n effect that must be reported alongside dR2
    - precision is reported under a DIFFERENT model ('beh') than value/rpe ('beh_spatial'); the bars in one panel are therefore not comparable, and this is only explained in the title text
    - the bin-shuffle null is computed but excluded from the headline; its pass rates (19-59%) do not corroborate the trial-shuffle result
    - example neurons are chosen by max dR2 then shown with a raw r on the same data — selection-on-the-statistic
    - figures date from 2026-05-25 and rest on latents superseded on 2026-06-02

#### 13.9 Belief-state two-timescale actor-critic (generative model + likelihood)
`Striatum project/rl_model/rl_model/agent.py` lines 104-387 (core scan 217-342) · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure (Fig 1E model schematic + methods); the parameter table and the two-TD-error construction are methods-critical*

- **Question.** Can a single generative agent with subjective parameters reproduce, per mouse, the spatial lick and running-speed profiles of the VR corridor task AND their within-session change, so that its internal variables become neural regressors?
- **Method.** State/obs space: 1-D corridor 0-200 a.u., BIN_SIZE_AU=4 -> N_BINS=50 (AU_TO_CM=1.25 -> 5 cm/bin). No discrete action set; two continuous emission channels. Belief = Kalman filter over scalar position, rendered as a 50-bin probability vector via softmax(-0.5*(centres-mu)^2/max(sigma,1e-3)) (NOT a true Gaussian pmf; a softmax of that quadratic). Predict mu+=4.0, sigma += Q*(1+kappa_v*v)*4.0; observe with R(x)=R_slope*|x-80|+R0, gain K=sig/(sig+R); sigma carried across trials and inflated by iti_inflation each trial; sigma0=400 fixed. Value = linear on belief, V=w_crit.b, w_crit initialised FLAT at w_init (not 0). Learning: TWO TD errors — delta_critic=r+gamma*V'-V drives w_crit (eta_w); delta_actor=(r-C_LICK*lick-rho*dt)+gamma*V'-V drives both actors (eta_a). Lick actor = 3-factor rule w_lick += eta_a*delta_actor*lick*b. Velocity actor = DETERMINISTIC gradient ascent w_vel += eta_a*g_vel*b with g_vel = closed-form d/dlogv of expected per-bin advantage (agent._vel_logv_grad, pinned to jax.grad(_vel_advantage) by test). Policies: lick rate lam=lambda_max*sigmoid(beta*V + w_lick.b - theta)+1e-9 licks/s, per-bin count ~ Poisson(lam*dt) with dt=5cm/clip(v,1e-3,1e4); velocity log-normal, log_v_mean=v_base+v_slope*V+w_vel.b, SD exp(log_sigma_v). Reward graded/saturating: r = 1.0*(exp(-cum_rz/10) - exp(-cum_rz_new/10)), cum over RZ licks only (RZ = bins with centre in [100,135] -> indices 25-33, 9 bins). 16 free parameters, all box-bounded +/-12 in unconstrained space, transforms: exp {Q .6, R0 2.0, R_slope .2, iti_inflation 5.0, kappa_v .03, w_init .35, beta 7.0, lambda_max 10.0, rho .15}; sigmoid {eta_w .09, gamma .80, eta_a .02}; identity {theta .28, v_base 3.30, v_slope -0.9, log_sigma_v -1.4} (values = `typical`, used both as optimiser start AND as prior centre AND as synthetic ground-truth centre). C_LICK=0.025 and K_REWARD=10.0 are FIXED constants, not fitted (C_LICK pinned because it degenerates with eta_a). Fitting is teacher-forced: at bin b the agent scores the observed lick given the OBSERVED same-bin velocity (dt), and learning is driven by observed actions. Dual masks: score_mask gates the log-likelihood, learn_mask gates the weight updates.
- **Inputs.** per-mouse (n_trials x 50) observed lick counts, log-velocities, validity mask
- **Outputs.** in-memory latent dict: value, rpe(=delta_actor), rpe_critic, precision, sigma, belief_mean, lick_rate(=expected count mu_lick), v_mean(=exp(log_v_mean)), a_lick, a_vel, reward, dt, lick, logv, loglik, loglik_lick, loglik_vel. Only value/rpe/precision/lick_rate/v_mean/belief_mean/sigma are ever persisted; rpe_critic, a_lick, a_vel, reward, dt are computed and discarded (a_lick/a_vel were promised as exported latents in UNDERSTANDING.md — doc drift).
- **Statistics.** none at this level; emission log-likelihood only (Poisson for licks, Normal on log-velocity). Joint per-bin LL = ll_lick + ll_vel, both multiplied by score_mask.
- **Inferential unit.** per (trial x spatial bin) observation within one mouse; model instance per mouse
- **Soundness.** Architecturally coherent and the two-timescale story is genuinely implemented (unlike the pre-2026-05-24 version). Two structural caveats. (1) The lick likelihood is conditioned on the same-bin OBSERVED velocity through dt; the factorisation P(v_b|hist)*P(lick_b|v_b,hist) is a valid joint likelihood, but it means the lick channel is an exposure-conditioned intensity, and any comparison to a null that lacks dt is not like-for-like (see the fit-quality analysis). (2) The exported `rpe` latent = delta_actor contains -C_LICK*lick and -rho*dt explicitly, plus r built from the observed cumulative RZ lick count, so `rpe` is by construction a function of the same-bin observed behaviour, not a purely internal variable. Belief vector is a softmax not a normalised Gaussian, so `precision`=1/sigma_post is a filter statistic rather than the actual spread of the belief vector used to read out V. Minor: C_LICK/K_REWARD fixed by fiat, so the reward/cost scale is not identified from data.
- **Concerns.**
    - Lick likelihood conditions on same-bin observed velocity via dt=5/v — inflates any comparison against a null without an exposure term
    - `rpe` regressor is an explicit linear function of the same-bin observed lick count and dwell time (C_LICK=0.025, rho) plus observed cumulative RZ licks
    - belief_vector uses softmax(-0.5*(x-mu)^2/sigma), not a normalised Gaussian; `precision`=1/sigma_post is the Kalman variance, not the spread of the vector actually dotted with w_crit
    - C_LICK=0.025 and K_REWARD=10.0 hard-fixed; reward magnitude fixed at 1.0 — absolute cost/reward scale unidentified
    - v_mean exported as exp(log_v_mean) (log-normal median) but compared against observed MEAN velocity in the epoch figures; bias factor exp(sigma_v^2/2) ~ 1.03 at typical log_sigma_v
    - sigma0=400 and iti_inflation mean that perceptual variance is re-inflated every trial including zero-padded trials (harmless, masked, but the carry is not reset)

#### 13.10 Latent recovery (the neural regressors)
`Striatum project/rl_model/scripts/run_parameter_recovery.py` lines 121-135, 194-216 · **🟡 minor** · status: `superseded` · manuscript role: *supplementary (justifies using latents despite sloppy parameters)*

- **Question.** Even where individual parameters are sloppy, are the per-(trial x bin) latents that will be handed to the neural analysis recovered?
- **Method.** For each synthetic mouse, run session_latents twice on the SAME simulated behaviour — once with u_true, once with u_fit — and Pearson-correlate the two (trial x bin) latent maps for value, rpe, precision, lick_rate, v_mean; report the cohort mean.
- **Inputs.** synthetic cohort + fitted u
- **Outputs.** latent_r array inside recovery_v*.npz; figures/fig_latent_recovery.png
- **Statistics.** Pearson r over 120*50 = 6000 (trial x bin) cells per mouse, then averaged over 12 mice. No null, no CI. The within-mouse r pools 6000 nested observations (pseudoreplication) but is used only descriptively.
- **Inferential unit.** (trial x bin) within mouse, averaged over 12 synthetic mice
- **Soundness.** A sensible sufficiency argument (sloppy parameters can still yield correct latents) and the on-disk v6 numbers are strong. But it is a self-consistency check on the same teacher-forcing data, so much of the correlation is inherited from the observed behaviour that drives both runs — a latent that is largely a function of the observed licks/dt (as `rpe` is) will correlate near 1 almost regardless of parameter error. On-disk recovery_v6.npz: value mean r=0.9964 (min 0.9895), rpe 0.9941 (min 0.9823), lick_rate 0.9992, v_mean 0.9988, precision 0.9153 (min 0.5858).
- **Concerns.**
    - latents on both sides are teacher-forced by the same observed behaviour, so recovery is partly tautological for latents that depend strongly on observed licks/dt
    - precision recovery is the weakest and most variable (mean 0.915, min 0.586) — and precision is the latent with essentially no across-trial variance
    - numbers on disk are v6 (pre-velocity-gradient-fix); v7 numbers exist only as text in UNDERSTANDING.md

#### 13.11 Latent export + real-data fit-quality figures
`Striatum project/rl_model/scripts/plot_real_data.py` lines 33-233 · **🟡 minor** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure (Fig 1E panels) + the export that feeds Fig 4*

- **Question.** Package the fitted per-mouse latents for the neural analysis and show session-level fit quality.
- **Method.** Reads results/real_fits_v6_interleaved (env RLMODEL_REALDIR), builds: held-out LL-gain bar chart (model minus null, lick and velocity channels); cohort observed-vs-model spatial lick profile (mask-weighted trial average; shaded band is +/- std/4, an arbitrary non-standard interval); per-mouse profile grid; value and rpe (trial x bin) latent grids; an example-mouse panel for M02 whose 'RZ-window' learning curve uses slice(22,31) (bins 22-30). Exports 7 latents per mouse (value, rpe, precision, lick_rate, v_mean, belief_mean, sigma) plus params, param_names, n_trials and test_idx (converted to MATLAB 1-based) to results/rl_latents.mat and .npz.
- **Inputs.** results/real_fits_v6_interleaved/*.npz + preprocessed_data5cm.mat
- **Outputs.** results/rl_latents.mat (4.8 MB) and results/rl_latents.npz (4.0 MB), both 2026-06-02 15:39; figures fig_real_fit_quality.png, fig_real_lick_profiles.png, fig_real_latents_value.png, fig_real_latents_rpe.png, fig_real_example.png
- **Statistics.** none — descriptive figures only
- **Inferential unit.** mouse (n=16) for the bar chart; (trial x bin) for the profiles
- **Soundness.** Functionally the hand-off point of the whole package and it works. Two defects. (1) The 'RZ window' used for the learning curve is bins 22-30 (88-124 a.u.), whereas the model's actual reward zone RZ_MASK is bins 25-33 (100-135 a.u.) — a 3-bin offset that includes 3 pre-RZ bins and excludes 3 real RZ bins. The same offset appears in run_parameter_recovery._fig_behaviour and in tests/test_recovery.py, so the offset is consistent but wrong relative to config. (2) The error band on the cohort profile is std/4, which corresponds to no standard interval (not SEM: SEM would be std/4 for n=16 only by coincidence of sqrt(16)=4 — so it IS the SEM here, but it is written as std/4 rather than std/sqrt(n) and will silently be wrong if n changes). rl_latents.mat is exported for MATLAB but NO MATLAB file in the repository reads it — the only consumers are the two Python encoding scripts (via the .npz).
- **Concerns.**
    - 'RZ window' slice(22,31) is offset by 3 bins from the model's own RZ_MASK (bins 25-33) — same offset in run_parameter_recovery.py:221 and tests/test_recovery.py
    - error band written as std/4 rather than std/sqrt(n) — correct only because n=16
    - rl_latents.mat is written for MATLAB consumption but nothing in the MATLAB codebase reads it (grep over all .m files: no hits)
    - belief_mean and sigma are exported but never used by any downstream analysis
    - the export takes the interleaved fits by default; the forward fits (arguably the better generalisation model) are exported only if RLMODEL_REALDIR is set

#### 13.13 Test suite (TDD gates)
`Striatum project/rl_model/tests/test_recovery.py, tests/test_encoding.py` lines test_recovery 1-228; test_encoding 1-76 · **🟢 ok** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only*

- **Question.** Are the model's numerical and inferential mechanics correct?
- **Method.** 11 tests. Notable: test_velocity_grad_matches_autodiff pins the closed-form _vel_logv_grad against jax.grad(_vel_advantage) over 25 random physiological states (logv in log(3)..log(60), kappa_v 0..0.2, rtol 1e-5); test_learn_mask_decouples_learning_from_scoring proves a trial dropped from the score mask contributes exactly zero likelihood yet, if kept in learn_mask, leaves the later value trajectory bit-identical (and perturbs it if dropped from both); test_fit_mouse_pins_fixed_params validates the ladder's pinning mechanism; test_true_params_beat_wrong_params checks the likelihood peaks at truth against 5 random perturbations; test_agent_localises_licking_within_session is a behavioural-realism check; test_parameter_recovery_small is an end-to-end 3-mouse / 160-trial recovery with thresholds median|u error| < 0.5 on 6 well-identified params and latent mean r > 0.85; test_encoding duplicates the synthetic encoding gate (n_shuffle=200) and checks spatial_demean_var_ratio flags stationary latents (<0.05) vs trial-varying (>0.8).
- **Inputs.** self-generating synthetic data
- **Outputs.** none persisted
- **Statistics.** assertion thresholds only; no statistical inference
- **Inferential unit.** n/a (unit tests)
- **Soundness.** Unusually strong for a research codebase — the two correctness fixes of 2026-06-02 are both pinned by tests, and the encoding gate is a genuine false-positive control. Gaps: nothing tests the exposure-matched-null issue, nothing tests that the encoding preprocessing is leak-free, and nothing tests recovery outside the narrow jitter=0.3 neighbourhood. test_parameter_recovery_small uses n=3 mice with an assertion on the median error, so it would pass even with 1 of 3 mice badly mis-fit.
- **Concerns.**
    - no test covers the null-model construction in fit_real_data.py (where the headline claim's weakness lives)
    - no test covers CV leakage in neural_encoding preprocessing
    - recovery test uses n=3 mice and a median-based assertion — tolerant of a single bad fit

## 14. Python 'popsim' simulation/validation package + CEBRA pipeline

*Full domain label:* Python 'popsim' simulation/validation package + CEBRA pipeline (StriatumACC)

**Position in pipeline.** TWO SEPARATE POSITIONS — popsim sits BESIDE the analysis chain as a validator; CEBRA sits at the END of it as a manual dead-end branch.

POPSIM (validator, no real data in or out).
- Consumes: nothing from the recording pipeline. Its only external dependency is the sibling analysis package 'Striatum project/cca/src/striatum_cca' (modules core.py, lagged.py, partial.py, config.py), imported lazily by popsim/src/popsim/bridge.py via auto-discovery of ../../../cca/src or the STRIATUM_CCA_SRC env var; needs h5py because striatum_cca.dataio imports it. I verified the package is importable in this checkout and the API matches what the bridge calls.
- Produces: 'Striatum project/popsim/data/generated/recovery_benchmark.json' (committed; the only persisted quantitative record, and I confirmed it reproduces bit-for-bit to ~1e-14); 'Striatum project/popsim/data/generated/{no_coupling,zero_lag,lagged,mediated,epoch_varying}/metadata.json' (committed ground-truth configs — only 5 of 10 scenarios); 'Striatum project/popsim/data/generated/<scenario>/{neural,latents,loadings}_{A,B,C}.npy' (gitignored and currently ABSENT from disk); 'Striatum project/popsim/figures/<scenario>.png' (directory does not exist — never generated here). The striatum_cca bridge results, which are the scientifically load-bearing output, are printed to stdout by scripts/striatum_cca_demo.py and persisted NOWHERE.
- Consumed downstream by: nothing, in code. No file in 'Striatum project/cca/' or elsewhere imports popsim, and popsim is not mentioned in the repo-level NOTES.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or PREDICTIONS.md — only in its own popsim/README.md and popsim/NOTES.md. The intended consumer is a human writing the Methods/validation section for the CCA communication-subspace claims (CCA_striatum_spatial_v2.m on the MATLAB side, striatum_cca on the Python side).

CEBRA (terminal manual branch off the MATLAB preprocessing chain).
- Upstream chain: OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1.m -> all_data.mat -> ProcessStriatumTask.m -> processed_data/preprocessed_data.mat (project_cfg().task_data_file).
- Consumes: 'Striatum project/save_for_cebra.m' reads preprocessed_data (pd.spatial_binned_fr_all, pd.spatial_binned_data.licks, pd.spatial_binned_data.durations, pd.zscored_lick_errors, is_dms/is_dls/is_acc/is_v1, final_neurontypes, mouseid, n_trials) plus project_cfg() and the shared helper find_learning_points.m.
- Produces (stage 1): 'Striatum project/cebra_data/cebra_mouse1..16_data.mat' (v7.3, all dated 2026-05-07 — PREDATES the 2026-05-08 CA1/DG addition; NOTES.md rerun step 3 outstanding).
- Produces (stage 2, cebra_analysis.py): 'Striatum project/cebra_results/cebra_results.npz' (19 KB: single_decoder_r2 16x5, single_decoder_rmse 16x5, consistency_scores 240, consistency_pairs 240x2, dataset_ids, label_keys, area_subsets), 'Striatum project/cebra_results/cebra_results.mat' (2.9 MB: same payload minus consistency_pairs, plus embedding_mouse1..16 each (n_retained, 3)), 'Striatum project/cebra_results/cebra_config.json'. All dated 2026-05-08 02:54. 'cebra_multisession_embeddings.png' is documented but NOT produced (plot_summary fails silently).
- Produces (stage 3, cebra_plot_results.py, dated 2026-05-08 10:04-10:14): 11 top-level PNGs in cebra_results/ — fig_decoder_r2_heatmap, fig_decoder_r2_summary, fig_decoder_rmse_summary, fig_decoder_r2_paired, fig_decoder_r2_distribution, fig_headline_composite, fig_consistency_matrix, fig_consistency_vs_decoding, fig_embedding_grid_by_position, fig_embedding_density_by_epoch, fig_decoding_error_per_bin, fig_decoder_confusion — plus cebra_results/embedding_panels/fig_emb_mouse1..16.png (16 files).
- Consumed downstream by: NOTHING. cebra_results.mat is written explicitly 'for the MATLAB plotting code' but no .m file in the repository reads it (grep over all .m files returns zero consumers). save_for_cebra.m is likewise called by no .m file — it appears only as a manual step in the NOTES.md / CLAUDE.md rerun recipe (OrganiseStriatumDataIncV1 -> ProcessStriatumTask -> save_for_cebra -> TCA -> downstream), so CEBRA is a hand-run side branch whose outputs re-enter no analysis.
- Superseded siblings: 'Striatum project/legacy/{cebra_test,cebra_multianimal,cebra_single_multi_comparison}.py' (orphaned per NOTES.md; cebra_test.py still points at a filename, cebra_mouse2data.mat, that the current exporter no longer writes).

**Data flow, shapes and units.** POPSIM (all synthetic, no real data touched).
- Units: dt = 1.0 throughout, so every tau, lag and cross-correlogram axis is in BINS, not seconds. Latents are standardised to ~unit marginal variance; loadings have unit-norm columns; population 'activity' is dimensionless (a.u.) for the gaussian model and integer counts for poisson.
- Continuous path (simulate): per area, latents (n_timesteps, n_latents) -> neural (n_timesteps, n_neurons). Default n_timesteps = 3000 (SimConfig and generate_datasets.py), 6000 in the recovery benchmark, 4000 in plot_scenarios.py, 8000-9000 in several ground-truth tests.
- Areas are fixed at A/B/C with n_latents 4/5/3 and n_neurons 60/80/40, snr = 3.0, tau = 20.0 bins, dynamics 'ar1', observation 'gaussian' (scenarios.default_areas, scenarios.py:108-115). AreaSpec hard-rejects n_latents outside 3-5.
- Trial path (simulate_trials): per area (n_trials, n_bins, n_neurons) with burn_in = max(20, max_edge_lag + 10) generated and discarded per trial. Bridge/demo operating point: n_trials = 80, n_bins = 60, k = 4 PCs, max_lag = 25 bins -> 51 lag values. Bridge default k = 5. striatum_cca.config.DEFAULT.max_lag_bins = 10.
- Configured coupling magnitudes: gains 1.0 (zero_lag), 1.2 (lagged, bidirectional), 1.4 then 0.7 (epoch_varying epochs 1/2 then 3), 1.6 (rotated_subspace scale, partial_mediation both channels), 2.0 (mediated each link, common_input each link); SharedNoise strength 0.6 with tau 15.0. Lags in bins: 0 (zero_lag, mediated, common_input, rotated_subspace, partial_mediation), 10 and 25 (lagged), 2 (all three epoch_varying edges), 5 and 12 (bidirectional). Epoch boundaries at T/3 and 2T/3.
- Benchmark operating point: n_timesteps 6000, k = 5 PCs per area, max_lag 50 -> 101 lag candidates, strong_threshold 0.3, CCA ridge reg 1e-6, eigenvalue clip 1e-12.
- Recovered magnitudes (in-sample, population level, k=5): population CCA1 ranges 0.150 (no_coupling, i.e. the floor) to 0.9988 (noise_correlation, the false positive); latent CCA1 tracks it within ~0.02 except for noise_correlation where latent CCA1 = 0.197 against population 0.9988. Held-out (bridge, k=4, 80 trials): 0.16 / 0.68 / 0.47 / 0.85 / 0.76 for no_coupling / zero_lag / lagged / mediated / partial_mediation; partial CC1 0.08 (mediated) and 0.78 (partial_mediation).

CEBRA (real recordings).
- 16 mouse files in cebra_data/, 0.17-8.1 MB each, MATLAB v7.3 (HDF5), all dated 2026-05-07.
- Per file: neural_data [N x B x T] spatially binned firing rates; lick_rate [T x B]; lick_errors [1 x T]; position [1 x B]; velocity [T x B]; learning_point, change_point, group_id (=1, task), mouse_id, bin_size_cm scalars; area_labels {1 x N}; neuron_types [N x 1].
- Geometry: B = 50 spatial bins in EVERY mouse; bin_size = 4 VR a.u. x au_to_cm = 1.25 -> bin_size_cm = 5.0 cm, i.e. a 250 cm corridor. position label is the integer bin index 0..49 (constructed in Python as np.tile(arange(50), T), not read from the saved 'position' field). Hardcoded landmark zones in the plotting script: visual bins 20-25 (100-125 cm), reward bins 25-33 (125-165 cm).
- Unit counts N per mouse: 133, 193, 47, 152, 467, 17, 77, 33, 86, 63, 159, 118, 85, 80, 42, 134 (mouse1..16). Trial counts T: 357, 469, 71, 371, 501, 76, 90, 331, 260, 189, 299, 104, 155, 257, 142, 109.
- Flattening: neural_data [N,B,T] -> transpose to (T,B,N) -> reshape to (T*B, N), so one CEBRA sample = one (trial, bin) timepoint. labels = column_stack([position(bin index), lick_rate, lick_errors repeated per bin]) -> (T*B, 3).
- NaN drop (rows with a NaN in neural OR any label column): 120,765 of 189,050 timepoints retained = 63.9% overall. Per mouse retained: 72.4, 60.3, 97.5, 49.6, 36.6, 96.2, 96.4, 40.3, 84.4, 61.8, 68.2, 94.7, 92.5, 61.2, 87.7, 73.6 percent. Dominant cause is NaN zscored_lick_errors on whole trials (NaN-lick-error trials per mouse: 95/357, 182/469, 1/71, 184/371, 314/501, 2/76, 2/90, 195/331, 37/260, 67/189, 91/299, 4/104, 10/155, 97/257, 16/142, 27/109); neural NaN rows are 2-72 per mouse and lick_rate NaN rows 40-232 (the top-1% cap).
- Embeddings: output_dimension = 3, distance = 'cosine'. Saved multi-session embedding row counts per mouse: 12928, 14132, 3461, 9209, 9175, 3655, 4336, 6663, 10966, 5844, 10196, 4924, 7169, 7867, 6230, 4010 (= the retained-sample counts, confirming they are all-data embeddings).
- Training: batch_size 512, learning_rate 3e-4, time_offsets 10, temperature_mode 'auto', conditional 'time_delta', architecture 'offset10-model', hybrid False, max_iterations 15000 for BOTH single- and multi-session, seed 42. 80 single-session fits (16 mice x 5 area subsets, subsets with <5 units skipped) + 1 multi-session fit.
- Split: whole trials, test_frac 0.25, n_test = max(1, round(0.25 * n_unique_trials)), rng seed 42 + mouse_id; same split reused across a mouse's 5 area subsets. Decoder Ridge(alpha=1.0).
- Result magnitudes: single_decoder_r2 (16,5) mean per area [all 0.049, DMS 0.050, DLS -0.001, ACC 0.008, V1 0.111] with n [16, 15, 10, 15, 5]; single_decoder_rmse (16,5) mean per area [14.13, 14.11, 14.51, 14.43, 13.65] bins; marginal SD of position over retained samples ~14.5 bins; 22 of 71 non-NaN R^2 cells negative; per-cell R^2 range -0.117 to +0.269. consistency_scores (240,) = 16x15 ordered pairs, min 0.697, median 0.955, mean 0.924, max 0.995.
- Epoch tagging for the density figure: window w = 10 trials; Naive = trial < 10; Pre-LP = [LP-10, LP); Expert = [LP, LP+10); LP from find_learning_points with lp_z_threshold -2, lp_window 10, lp_min_consecutive 7, START-of-window convention, NaN for non-learners.

**Cross-cutting notes.** SCOPE VERDICT. Two independent bodies of work with opposite health profiles.

(A) popsim IS the method-validation arm for the CCA communication-subspace claims — that is unambiguous from the code, not just the docs: bridge.py imports the real striatum_cca package (I verified it is importable at 'Striatum project/cca/src' and that the API matches: core.cca_cv -> CVResult.held_out_r/in_sample_r, lagged.lag_curve(held_out=True) -> cc_per_dim, partial.partial_cca_cv -> held_out_r) and drives it on trial-structured simulations with known latent-level coupling. The generative model is two-to-three coupled populations whose communication lives entirely at the latent level (z_target(t) += gain * M @ z_source(t-lag), optionally epoch-gated), projected to populations by unit-norm loadings plus private noise at snr=3.0, so the true communication subspace is exactly colspace(W_target @ M). Ten scenarios establish, respectively: independence, instantaneous coupling, lagged directionality (+10 / +25 bins), full mediation, epoch-varying direction/orientation/strength, reciprocal coupling at different lags, common-input confound, rank-2 rotated subspace, graded partial mediation, and observation-level noise correlation without communication. The internal benchmark is fully reproducible (I reran it and got the committed JSON back to ~1e-14) and reports 10/10 PASS.

(B) CEBRA is a real, completed, but scientifically null side-branch. It IS wired end-to-end (save_for_cebra.m -> cebra_data/ -> cebra_analysis.py -> cebra_results/ -> cebra_plot_results.py) and results HAVE been produced (16 mice, 80 single-session fits, 1 multi-session fit, 2026-05-08). It is NOT wired into any orchestrator: no .m file calls save_for_cebra (it appears only as a manual step 3 in the NOTES.md rerun recipe), and no .m file reads cebra_results.mat despite that file being written explicitly for MATLAB. So CEBRA is a manual, dead-ended branch.

THE THREE THINGS THAT MOST MATTER FOR A MANUSCRIPT.

1. popsim's most valuable result is not the 10/10 headline — it is a null-calibration number that is recorded nowhere. Running the bridge myself: for THREE GENUINELY UNCOUPLED populations at n_trials=80, n_bins=60, k=4, striatum_cca's 5-fold whole-trial HELD-OUT CC1 is 0.16, and the lagged directionality peak pins to the edge of the search window (-25 of +-25). That is a floor and a warning that belong in the paper. The internal in-sample benchmark measures the same floor as 0.150 for no_coupling. Any real held-out CC1 near 0.16 at comparable n is not evidence of communication, and any peak lag near the window edge is not evidence of direction.

2. The '10/10 scenarios recover as configured' summary hides two genuine failures. (i) noise_correlation: latents independent (latent CCA 0.197) yet POPULATION CCA1 = 0.9988 and partial CCA(A,B|C) = 0.9988. Shared observation-level noise fools population CCA essentially completely and partialling a third area does not rescue it. The scenario's PASS predicate deliberately never inspects cca1, so a maximal false positive is scored as success. This is the single most important thing popsim demonstrates about the real analysis and the report format buries it. (ii) epoch_varying epoch 3 is configured as A1->B2 at lag +2 (A leads B) and recovers -8 — wrong sign — but the predicate only checks epochs 1 and 2. Both should be re-reported as failures/limits, not folded into a 10/10.

3. Every CEBRA decoding number is near chance, and the reason is a decoder/geometry mismatch rather than biology. Saved held-out position-decoding R^2 (16 mice x 5 area subsets): all 0.049, DMS 0.050, DLS -0.001, ACC 0.008, V1 0.111 (n=5); RMSE 14.13/14.11/14.51/14.43/13.65 bins against a position SD of ~14.5 bins over 50 bins; 22 of 71 non-NaN cells are negative. The embedding is 3-D with distance='cosine' (hyperspherical) and position on a repeatedly traversed 50-bin corridor is a ring, so a LINEAR ridge cannot read a monotonic 0..49 variable off it. CEBRA's canonical evaluation is a kNN decoder in embedding space; cebra_README.md wrongly calls the linear ridge 'the canonical CEBRA evaluation'. Until the decoder is swapped for kNN with a shuffled-label null, the CEBRA null is uninterpretable and must not be reported as an absence of position coding in DMS/DLS/ACC/V1.

LEAKAGE / CIRCULARITY LEDGER.
- CLEAN: fit_single_session (cebra_analysis.py:338-407). Whole-trial split, scaler fit on train only, CEBRA fit on train only, ridge fit on train embedding and scored on test embedding. No scaler leak. This is the honest arm and its answer is ~0.
- FATAL LEAK: plot_per_bin_decoding / fig_decoding_error_per_bin.png / fig_decoder_confusion.png (cebra_plot_results.py:825-990). The ridge's 'held-out' trials were seen by the EMBEDDING: fit_multisession trains on 100% of every mouse's data with position as a contrastive label and does no split. Both figures are titled 'held-out trials'. Invalid as written.
- CIRCULAR-BY-CONSTRUCTION: the consistency score (mean 0.924, median 0.955, range 0.697-0.995 over 240 ordered pairs from 16 mice) is computed on the same all-data samples and the same position labels used to train a model whose objective explicitly optimises cross-session alignment, with no null and no held-out fold.
- IN-SAMPLE: all popsim benchmark CCA/partial-CCA/PCA (metrics.py) is whole-sample in-sample; only bridge.py uses held-out estimators.

UNFLAGGED DATA LOSS (a finding in its own right). Including lick_errors as a contrastive label deletes 36% of all timepoints: 120,765 of 189,050 (trial,bin) samples retained across the 16 mice. The drop is driven almost entirely by zscored_lick_errors being NaN for WHOLE trials, not by neural NaNs — mouse5 retains 36.6% (314/501 trials NaN), mouse4 49.6%, mouse8 40.3%, mouse2 60.3%. The loss is therefore trial-structured and behaviour-dependent (trials where lick error was undefined), i.e. a non-random, behaviourally biased sample, and it is a pure cost of a label choice that contributes nothing to the position-decoding question. Dropping lick_errors from label_keys would recover roughly a third of the data.

MULTIPLE COMPARISONS / SELECTION. CEBRA: 80 mouse x area R^2 cells with no correction and no test against zero; the headline 'V1 R^2 = 0.111' is the maximum of five area means on n=5 mice; areas are compared across non-overlapping animal subsets (V1 5/16, DLS 10/16, DMS 15/16, ACC 15/16). popsim: 10 simultaneous PASS/FAIL verdicts each from n=1 seeded realisation, with hardcoded thresholds (0.3/0.4/0.5, +-3/+-4 bins) never calibrated against the 0.150 null floor the benchmark itself measures; peak-lag is an argmax over 101 candidates with no null.

PSEUDOREPLICATION. The decoder R^2 figure family is correctly animal-level (SEM over mice, n annotated, per-mouse dots shown). Two exceptions: fig_decoder_confusion.png pools every mouse's held-out timepoints into one histogram with no animal weighting (retained counts vary 3.5-fold, 3,461 to 14,132), and the consistency-vs-decoding scatter treats 16 per-mouse consistency values as independent when each is a mean over 15 pairs from one shared model.

DOCUMENTED-BUT-NOT-IMPLEMENTED (doc/code drift to fix before writing Methods).
- cebra_analysis.py docstring item 5 claims 'Multi-session model + Procrustes-aligned single-session models in one pass'. The Procrustes arm does not exist: OrthogonalProcrustesAlignment is imported at line 76 and never used. Only legacy/cebra_single_multi_comparison.py ever implemented it. Without it the consistency number has no comparison condition.
- sklearn.model_selection.GroupKFold imported at line 94 and never used — the group-aware CV that was the right tool here.
- cebra_README.md lists cebra_multisession_embeddings.png as an output; it does not exist. plot_summary (cebra_analysis.py:469-491) colours a NaN-dropped embedding with full-length labels (e.g. mouse2: 14,132 embedding rows vs 23,450 label rows), fails, and the failure is swallowed by a broad except.
- cebra_README.md troubleshooting refers to cfg.min_units_per_mouse; no such field exists — the gate is a hardcoded 'col_mask.sum() < 5' at line 352.
- hybrid=False is fixed in config, so the active pipeline trains only the CEBRA-Behavior variant; the Time / Behavior / Hybrid comparison exists only in legacy.

STALE-CACHE DEPENDENCIES.
- Every CEBRA result depends on cebra_data/*.mat dated 2026-05-07, which PREDATES the 2026-05-08 CA1/DG addition. NOTES.md lists 'save_for_cebra (regenerates cebra_data/ with CA1/DG label rows)' as required rerun step 3 and it has not been done. So area_labels contain only DMS/DLS/ACC/V1(+Unknown), cfg.area_subsets omits CA1 and DG, and no CEBRA number in the repo speaks to the two newest areas. Regenerating cebra_data/ also silently invalidates every embedding figure, because cebra_plot_results re-derives the fit-time NaN mask from those files and guards only with a length-equality check.
- popsim data/generated/ holds only 5 of the 10 scenarios (no_coupling, zero_lag, lagged, mediated, epoch_varying); the five Phase-2 scenarios were added after the last generate_datasets.py run. figures/ and .venv do not exist, so plot_scenarios.py has never been run in this checkout.
- The bridge numbers (the ones that actually validate the real pipeline) are printed to stdout and persisted nowhere: no JSON, no figure, no log.

PROVENANCE / INTEGRATION GAP. popsim is documented only inside its own README.md and NOTES.md — it is mentioned nowhere in the repo-level NOTES.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or PREDICTIONS.md, and the cca subproject's own notes never mention popsim. The dependency is one-directional (popsim -> striatum_cca). Git history shows seven dedicated commits (10f153f through a857674) but the validation is not referenced from the analysis it validates, so a reader of the CCA work would not know a ground-truth test-bed exists.

MINIMUM FIXES BEFORE EITHER BRANCH CAN CARRY A CLAIM.
popsim: (1) persist the bridge results and promote the 0.16 held-out null floor to a reported quantity; (2) run noise_correlation through the bridge — the confound scenario is the one the real claims most need and it is the one the demo omits; (3) repeat every scenario over >=20 seeds and report distributions, not n=1 verdicts; (4) re-report noise_correlation as a false-positive demonstration and epoch_varying epoch 3 as a failure; (5) add a permutation null for the lag curve so peak lags are testable; (6) lift the 3-5 latent cap and add a low-SNR / low-unit-count regime matching the real data (some mice have 17-47 units).
CEBRA: (1) replace the linear ridge with a kNN decoder in embedding space plus a shuffled-label null; (2) refit the multi-session model with test trials excluded before any per-bin or confusion figure; (3) drop lick_errors from label_keys to recover ~36% of the timepoints, or impute rather than delete; (4) rerun save_for_cebra to include CA1/DG and add them to area_subsets; (5) either implement the Procrustes comparison arm or delete the claim; (6) fix or delete plot_summary and the cebra_README output list.

### Analyses (19)

#### 14.1 Per-spatial-bin decoding error and pooled confusion matrix
`Striatum project/cebra_plot_results.py` lines 825-990 · **🔴 fatal** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *drop as-is; it can only become a figure after the embedding itself is refit with the test trials excluded (or the per-bin analysis is run on the single-session train/test fits)*

- **Question.** Where along the corridor is position decoding from the CEBRA embedding accurate, and how does error relate to the visual and reward zones?
- **Method.** _per_mouse_held_out_predictions: for each mouse take the SAVED MULTI-SESSION embedding, split by whole trials with _trialwise_split(trial_id, test_frac=0.25, seed=42+mouse_idx) (the same rule and seed arithmetic as fit_single_session), standardise the embedding using train-fold mean/std only, fit Ridge(alpha=1.0) from embedding -> bin_id on train, predict on test; require >=5 test and >=10 train rows. Figure (a): per-mouse mean |pred-true| per true bin as light grey traces, mean +- SEM across mice, chance baseline = |bin - mean(mean true position across mice)|, axvspan for a hardcoded visual zone (bins 20-25) and reward zone (bins 25-33), secondary top axis in cm via BIN_CM=5.0. Figure (b): pooled 2-D histogram of true bin vs round(pred) clipped to [0, n_bins-1] over ALL mice's held-out timepoints, row-normalised to P(pred|true), magma, with the identity line and the two zones shaded.
- **Inputs.** cebra_results/cebra_results.mat (multi-session, all-data embeddings) + cebra_data/*.mat
- **Outputs.** cebra_results/fig_decoding_error_per_bin.png, cebra_results/fig_decoder_confusion.png
- **Statistics.** mean +- SEM across mice for the error curve; a naive 'predict the global mean position' chance line. No test at any bin, no cluster-based correction over the 50 bins, no permutation null. The confusion matrix pools timepoints across mice with no animal-level weighting.
- **Inferential unit.** mice (n<=16) for the error curve; POOLED timepoints across mice for the confusion matrix
- **Soundness.** This is the one CEBRA analysis with an outright fatal validity problem. The 'held-out' trials are held out only from the RIDGE, not from the embedding: the multi-session CEBRA model was fit on 100% of every mouse's data with position as one of its contrastive labels (fit_multisession does no split), so every test timepoint's position label was already used to shape the representation the ridge then reads. The figure titles and axis labels nonetheless say 'held-out trials', and fig_decoder_confusion.png's caption asserts held-out pooled decoding. Any accuracy above the honest single-session numbers (mean R^2 0.049) in this figure is attributable to that leak, not to generalisation. Two further problems. (a) The confusion matrix pools every mouse's timepoints into one histogram, so mice with more retained samples (mouse2 14132 rows vs mouse3 3461) dominate, and bins nested in trials nested in animals are treated as independent draws — textbook pseudoreplication. (b) The corridor landmarks (visual zone bins 20-25, reward zone bins 25-33) and BIN_CM=5.0 are hardcoded in the plotting script rather than read from project_cfg.m / bin_size_cm in the data files, so they can silently desynchronise from the geometry the data were binned with. Also, the seed coupling (base_seed 42 + mouse_idx, where mouse_idx is the embedding key = list position, while fit_single_session used 42 + mouse_id) only reproduces the training split because mouse_id happens to equal list position for all 16 mice; if that ever stops holding, the 'same split' claim in the docstring silently becomes false.
- **Concerns.**
    - FATAL: the embedding was trained on all trials with position as a contrastive label, so the ridge's 'held-out' trials were seen by the representation — the held-out framing in both figure titles is invalid
    - pooled confusion matrix treats timepoints from all mice as independent; sample counts vary 3.5-fold across mice, so large-n mice dominate
    - no per-bin statistics and no cluster-based correction over 50 bins; only a naive predict-the-mean chance line
    - visual zone (20,25), reward zone (25,33) and BIN_CM=5.0 hardcoded in the plotting script rather than read from project_cfg.m or the exported bin_size_cm
    - split-seed reproduction depends on mouse_id coinciding with list position; true today, silently fragile

#### 14.2 Validation metrics layer (cross-correlogram, CCA, partial CCA, PCA reduce)
`Striatum project/popsim/src/popsim/metrics.py` lines 35-191 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *methods-only (should not be the estimator behind any published recovery claim; the bridge estimators should be)*

- **Question.** Do lightweight standard estimators read back the configured coupling from simulated data?
- **Method.** cross_correlation(x,y,max_lag): z-scores both 1-D signals, corr(x[t], y[t+k]) for k in -max_lag..max_lag, so positive peak means x leads y. lag_of_peak_xcorr returns lags[nanargmax(|corr|)] — argmax of the ABSOLUTE correlation over 2*max_lag+1 candidates. cca(X,Y,reg=1e-6): centres, builds Cxx/Cyy with reg*I added, symmetric inverse square roots via eigh with eigenvalues clipped at 1e-12, SVD of the whitened cross-covariance, corrs = clip(s,0,1). Whole-sample, IN-SAMPLE, no cross-validation, no shrinkage beyond reg=1e-6. canonical_variates refits cca on all data and returns the component-th variate pair. regress_out: lstsq residuals after centring both. partial_cca(X,Y,Z) = cca(regress_out(X,Z), regress_out(Y,Z)) on the SAME samples used to fit the regression. pca_reduce(X,k): centre, SVD, project onto top-k right singular vectors (in-sample basis).
- **Statistics.** none — no null model, no permutation, no significance, no CV. Every number is in-sample.
- **Inferential unit.** time bins of one simulated session
- **Soundness.** Appropriate as a lightweight self-check of the generator, and the docstring is explicit that striatum_cca is the real analysis library. But because benchmark.py builds PASS/FAIL verdicts on top of these estimators, their in-sample bias and their lack of a null propagate into the headline validation claim. Concretely visible in the recorded output: no_coupling — three genuinely independent areas — yields in-sample CCA1 = 0.150 with k=5 PCs and 6000 samples, and lag_of_peak_xcorr returns a spurious peak at +5 bins. So the estimator's own floor is ~0.15 and its peak-lag is an unregularised order statistic over 101 lag candidates with no correction and no null. Partial CCA regresses Z out on the same samples it then tests, which is the standard construction but is in-sample and will under-partial at small n.
- **Concerns.**
    - in-sample CCA with no cross-validation: nonzero floor (0.150 for truly uncoupled areas)
    - peak lag is argmax|corr| over 2*max_lag+1 = 101 candidates with no null and no correction; returns +5 for uncoupled data
    - PCA basis and partial-CCA regression are both fit on all samples then scored on the same samples
    - reg=1e-6 is essentially no regularisation; eigenvalue clip at 1e-12 can silently invert near-null directions

#### 14.3 Coupling-recovery benchmark over all ten scenarios
`Striatum project/popsim/src/popsim/benchmark.py + Striatum project/popsim/scripts/recovery_benchmark.py` lines benchmark.py 53-221; script 31-65 · **🟠 major** · status: `active` · manuscript role: *main figure IF re-reported honestly (noise_correlation reframed as the false-positive demonstration and epoch 3 marked as a failure); as currently summarised ('10/10 recover as configured') it should not go in a paper*

- **Question.** Do lag-0 CCA, lagged CCA and partial CCA applied to POPULATION activity recover the coupling that was dialled in at the latent level?
- **Method.** For each of the 10 scenarios: simulate at n_timesteps=6000 (script default; module default also 6000), pca_reduce each of A/B/C to k=5 PCs (never touching latents), then compute cca1 = top in-sample CCA(A_pcs, B_pcs); n_strong = count(corrs >= strong_threshold=0.3); partial_cca1 = top partial CCA(A,B|C_pcs); drop_frac = (cca1-partial_cca1)/cca1; peak_lag and peak_lag2 = lag_of_peak_xcorr of the 1st and 2nd canonical variate pairs over max_lag=50; latent_cca1 = in-sample CCA on the hidden latents (ground-truth reference); pop_corr = |corr(mean_A(t), mean_B(t))|; epoch_lags = per-epoch peak lag of the top variate pair using config.epoch_boundaries. Verdicts are hardcoded threshold predicates (_expectations, lines 104-154), e.g. no_coupling cca1<0.3; zero_lag cca1>0.4 and |peak_lag|<=3; lagged cca1>0.4 and |peak_lag-10|<=4; mediated/common_input cca1>0.3 and drop_frac>0.5; epoch_varying len(epoch_lags)==3 and epoch_lags[0]>0 and epoch_lags[1]<0; bidirectional cca1>0.3 and peak_lag*peak_lag2<0; rotated_subspace n_strong>=2; partial_mediation cca1>0.4 and drop_frac<0.3 and partial_cca1>0.4; noise_correlation latent_cca1<0.25 and pop_corr>0.3. Script exits 1 unless all pass; writes data/generated/recovery_benchmark.json.
- **Inputs.** scenarios.SCENARIOS builders only
- **Outputs.** Striatum project/popsim/data/generated/recovery_benchmark.json (committed); stdout fixed-width table via format_table
- **Statistics.** no statistics at all — verdicts are hardcoded thresholds on point estimates from ONE seeded realisation per scenario. No permutation null, no repeats over seeds, no CI, no correction for the 10 simultaneous verdicts.
- **Inferential unit.** one simulated session per scenario (n=1 realisation per verdict)
- **Soundness.** I reran the script: it reproduces the committed JSON to ~1e-14 (BLAS float noise only), so it is genuinely deterministic and the recorded numbers are trustworthy AS point estimates. Recorded values (dynamics=ar1, n_timesteps=6000, k=5): no_coupling cca1 0.150 / pcca1 0.157 / lag +5 / latCC 0.155; zero_lag 0.720 / 0.721 / lag 0 / n_strong 4 / latCC 0.738; lagged 0.463 / 0.459 / lag +10 / lag2 -24 / latCC 0.473; mediated 0.866 / 0.239 / drop 0.724 / latCC 0.884; epoch_varying 0.563 / 0.563 / epoch_lags [+2, -2, -8] / latCC 0.577; bidirectional 0.566 / 0.564 / lag +5 / lag2 -12 / n_strong 2; common_input 0.739 / 0.192 / drop 0.740 / popRho 0.322; rotated_subspace 0.841 / 0.841 / n_strong 2 / latCC 0.860; partial_mediation 0.820 / 0.812 / drop 0.010; noise_correlation cca1 0.9988 / pcca1 0.9988 / latCC 0.197 / popRho 0.993. Verdict: 10/10 PASS. THREE structural problems with reading that as 'the method works'. (1) The headline 10/10 is misleading for noise_correlation: the latents are independent (latCC 0.197) yet population CCA1 = 0.9988 and partial CCA(A,B|C) = 0.9988 — i.e. shared observation-level noise fools population CCA essentially completely, and partialling a third area does NOT rescue it. The predicate for that scenario deliberately never inspects cca1, so a maximal false positive is scored as a PASS. This is the single most manuscript-relevant number in the package and the report format buries it. (2) epoch_varying epoch 3 is configured as A1->B2 at lag +2 (A leads B) but recovers -8 — wrong sign — and the predicate only checks epochs 1 and 2, so a real recovery failure passes silently. (3) Every verdict is n=1: one seed, one session length, one k. There is no distribution over realisations, so 'recovers as configured' has no error bar, and the thresholds (0.3/0.4/0.5, +-3/+-4 bins) are post-hoc and uncalibrated against the 0.150 in-sample floor the benchmark itself measures.
- **Concerns.**
    - '10/10 recovered' conceals that noise_correlation yields population CCA1 = 0.9988 with independent latents and partial CCA does not fix it — a maximal false positive scored as PASS
    - epoch_varying epoch 3 recovers lag -8 against a configured +2 (wrong direction) and is not checked by the predicate
    - n=1 seeded realisation per scenario; no repeats, no CI, no permutation null, no correction across 10 verdicts
    - all CCA/partial-CCA/PCA in the benchmark are in-sample (see metrics.py), so cca1 has a ~0.15 floor at this n and k
    - peak_lag is argmax over 101 lags; for no_coupling it returns +5 and for the bridge it returns the window edge
    - verdict thresholds are hardcoded magic numbers with no calibration to the measured null floor
